report.title: "Roll Tide, and I Mean That as a Threat": MK Strickland Hosts Homecoming
report.byline: Our debutante with a coach's brain introduces herself and previews No. 13 Alabama vs. Texas A&M.
report.text:
Mary-Kathryn 'MK' Strickland · Alabama Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Roll Tide, darling, and I mean that as a greeting. Mostly. I'm Mary-Kathryn Strickland, but everyone from the Quad to the press box calls me MK. I rode for the Tide equestrian team, I read blitz pickups the way some girls read Southern Living, and I can quote a legendary coaching maxim for every situation, perfectly, usually at dinner. My family has asked me to stop. I will not stop. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a little belle-of-the-ball polish. When we win, you'll hear "Roll Tide" in seventeen different tones, each more satisfied than the last. When we lose, I'll say "We will not speak of it," and I will not speak of it. This week, I'll make an exception.

The School in 60 Seconds
Alabama claims 18 national championships, 13 of them wire-service titles from the poll era. Paul "Bear" Bryant won six from 1958 to 1982, and Nick Saban won six more between 2007 and 2023. The Tide's Heisman winners are Mark Ingram II (2009), Derrick Henry (2015), DeVonta Smith (2020) and Bryce Young (2021). Alabama has 30 SEC championships, an NCAA-record 79 bowl appearances and 46 bowl wins, also a record, plus a record 16 straight 10-win seasons from 2008 through 2023. Bryant-Denny Stadium seats 101,821 and opened in 1929. Coach Bryant has a maxim for this, and I'll save it for dinner.

The Coach and the Scheme
Kalen DeBoer was hired Jan. 12, 2024, and his first two Tide teams went 9-4 and 11-4. This season's offense started like a debutante's waltz: 48, 45, 50, 49 and 56 points in the first five wins. Then came 17 against Georgia and 10 at Tennessee. Overall, Alabama scores 39.3 points a game (12th) and throws for 252.7 yards (48th). The defense allows 107 rushing yards a game (30th) and is plus-5 in turnovers (15th), with 16 takeaways. The weak spots are pass defense, 230.9 yards allowed (101st), and red zone defense, where opponents score 95.7% of the time (134th). Every ball gown has a loose thread, darling. We sew.

Players to Know
QB Keelon Russell: 129 of 191, 1,746 yards, 12 TD, 4 INT. At Tennessee he was 19 of 29 for 147 yards with two interceptions and scored on a 19-yard run.
RB Trae'shawn Brown: 313 yards on 57 carries, 5 TD.
WR Ryan Coleman-Williams: 23 catches, 415 yards, 4 TD. He missed Tennessee with several injuries, including a concussion, per AP, and an aggregator lists him out with a knee injury as of Oct. 17. Status for Saturday: not official.
LB Caleb Woodson: a team-high 53 tackles. LB Yhonzae Pierre: 3.5 sacks. DB Bray Hubbard: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Alabama is 5-2 and 3-2 in the SEC, 3-1 at home, and No. 13 in both polls. The losses were 20-17 to Georgia and 26-10 at Tennessee. We have lost back-to-back regular-season games for the first time since 2007. After this game comes an open date, then a Nov. 7 trip to LSU. Homecoming against an SEC visitor is precisely the right occasion to straighten our pearls.

This Week: Texas A&M (4-3) at No. 13 Alabama (5-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Bryant-Denny Stadium · ABC. Homecoming.
Last week: we lost 26-10 at Tennessee with 201 yards, 54 rushing, and four turnovers. "The key was they were able to run the football," Coach DeBoer said. Texas A&M beat The Citadel 41-0.
Our offense vs. their defense: the Aggies are good on defense, 17.1 points allowed (27th), 164.1 passing yards allowed (10th) and 29.8% on third down (11th). Their pass rush has just 5 sacks, which should give Russell time.
Their offense vs. our defense: Texas A&M averages 356.9 yards (97th) and 195.7 passing (103rd). In two SEC road games, it scored 6 points each time. Marcel Reed has 7 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. Our run defense, 30th, wants to make him throw.
Series: Alabama leads 13-3 and is 7-1 against the Aggies from 2016 through 2025. The last meeting was a 26-20 win in College Station in 2023. The only Aggie win in Tuscaloosa came in 2012, and we've won five straight at home since.
Availability: per an aggregator dated Oct. 17, Coleman-Williams (knee) and WR A.J. Walker are out and TE Jay Ford is questionable (arm). For A&M, WRs Mario Craver and A.J. Bethel-Roman are questionable. The SEC's first official report comes Oct. 21.
What decides it: (1) Ball security: four turnovers at Tennessee can't happen twice. (2) Red zone defense, our weakest number. (3) Whether our receivers are healthy enough to stretch a top-10 pass defense.
And Colt Wendeborn, Texas A&M's insider: Howdy right back, sugar. Bryant-Denny is lovely this time of year. Roll Tide.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
In Tuscaloosa for homecoming? Brown's Corner on University Boulevard is a nice place for brunch before the parade.

report.byline: Our insider (archetype: ozark hog-calling dork) introduces the Arkansas Razorbacks during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Bubba Fayette-Dorsey · Arkansas Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Woooo, Pig, here comes the data! I'm Bubba Fayette-Dorsey, and I'm your Arkansas insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm an ozark grade-school science teacher who calls the Hogs before every stat. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. Fair warning about my habit: calls the Hogs before every stat, even negative ones. On the podcast, my segment is called Hog Call. The show card describes it like this: calls the Hogs, then reads the stat. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Razorbacks have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Razorback Stadium in Fayetteville, AR, built in 1938 with a listed capacity of 80,000. The playing surface is Frank Broyles Field, per Wikipedia. The fight song is "Arkansas Fight", per Wikipedia. The band is the Best in Sight and Sound, per Wikipedia. The program claims national titles from 1964, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 9-4, 7-6, 4-8, 7-6 and 2-10, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Texas A&M (1-9 in 10 meetings), Ole Miss (4-6 in 10 meetings), Auburn (2-8 in 10 meetings), LSU (1-9 in 10 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 46 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about Calling the Hogs; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Ryan Silverfield leads the Razorbacks; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Nov. 30, 2025. Through 7 games, Arkansas scores 21.0 points a game and allows 26.7. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 49% of its plays, gaining 111.6 rushing yards and 231.4 passing yards a game. That's a balanced menu. On third down, Arkansas converts 42.4% of the time and opponents convert 42.9%. The defense has 10 sacks and 27 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 8 giveaways against 9 takeaways. Penalties cost 52.7 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 34 points against Tulsa on Sept. 27, 2026, and 1 of the 7 games was decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, opponents have outscored Arkansas by a combined 40 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB KJ Jackson (passing leader): 131/215, 1444 yards, 7 TD, 4 INT.
RB Braylen Russell (rushing leader): 58 carries, 205 yards, 2 TD.
WR Chris Marshall (receiving leader): 43 catches, 633 yards, 2 TD.
On defense, LB Ja'Quavion Smith leads with 48 tackles; DL Quincy Rhodes Jr. has 3 sacks; DB Miguel Mitchell has 2 interceptions.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Arkansas is 3-4 overall, 2-2 at home and 1-2 away. In SEC play the Razorbacks are 1-3, which sorts them No. 14 of 16 by record. Georgia sits on top at 4-1 in league games. Right around us: Texas A&M (1-3) and South Carolina (1-3). The top of the table: Georgia (4-1), Kentucky (4-1), Tennessee (3-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Arkansas this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Razorbacks beat Vanderbilt on the road, 31-21. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, vs. Missouri, in Fayetteville, with a flex kickoff window of 2:30 to 7 p.m.; it is also Homecoming. Missouri comes in at 5-2. From 2016 through 2025, Arkansas went 1-9 against Missouri in 10 meetings. After that, CFBD lists at Auburn (Nov. 7), vs. South Carolina (Nov. 14), at Texas (Nov. 21), vs. LSU (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Razorbacks come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Woooo, Pig, here comes the data!

report.title: "War Eagle, Bless Their Hearts": Lacey Bellamy Welcomes LSU After the Georgia Upset
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, hey there, Auburn family, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Lacey Bellamy. I'm a proud former sorority president on the Plains, and I can recite every Iron Bowl down by heart. Ask me anything. I mean it. I'll even act them out, and in my reenactments, I always play the hero. Every single time. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm sweet as sweet tea, and I'll have the sharpest take in the room, all wrapped in a nice Alabama drawl. When we win, I roll an imaginary oak in imaginary toilet paper and shriek "War Eagle!" When we lose, I sip my lemonade with great dignity and say "bless their hearts" about absolutely everybody. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a little Southern charm. "War Eagle, bless their hearts."

The School in 60 Seconds
Auburn has a national championship from 2010, the season Cam Newton led the Tigers. Home is Jordan-Hare Stadium, listed at 87,451, and last Saturday's result would have rolled every tree on the Plains: Auburn beat No. 1 Georgia 27-24 on a field goal as time expired. The series with LSU goes back 57 games, and it's been full of nail-biters, including LSU wins of 22-21 in 2018 and 23-20 in 2019. Auburn has won some big ones in this series too, like 48-11 in 2020.

The Coach and the Scheme
Alex Golesh came to Auburn from South Florida. He was hired on Nov. 30, 2025. The 2026 numbers say Auburn runs a balanced offense, with about 55% runs at 4.71 yards a carry. It averages 26.8 points and 393.7 yards a game. The defense is the real belle of the ball: it allows 21.8 points a game and just 3.56 yards a carry, with 16 sacks. Auburn has forced 11 turnovers and lost 9. The one thing we need to fix: 23 sacks allowed.

Players to Know
QB Byrum Brown: 1,202 passing yards and 8 TD. At Georgia he went 15 of 26 for 150 yards and a touchdown and ran 26 times for 115 yards and another score. That's a hero's performance, and I'll be reenacting it at the tailgate.
WR Keshaun Singleton: a team-high 32 catches for 367 yards and 2 TD, including a touchdown at Georgia.
LB Elijah Melendez: a team-high 52 tackles, 4 sacks and an interception. At Georgia he had 9 tackles, a sack and that interception.
K Alex McPherson: made the 34-yard field goal at the horn to beat Georgia.

The Conference Picture
Auburn is 4-2 overall and 2-2 in the SEC, 2-1 at home and 1-1 on the road, plus a neutral-site win over Baylor. The Tigers aren't ranked yet. They lost 44-39 at home to Florida and 24-14 at Tennessee, then beat Vanderbilt and Georgia. Beating a ranked LSU team at home would put Auburn right back in the SEC conversation. This team plays close games and wins most of them: it's 3-1 in one-score games, and the only one-score loss was to Florida by five. That's pressure-proof, sugar.

This Week: No. 18 LSU (5-2) at Auburn (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 11 a.m. CT (noon ET) · Jordan-Hare Stadium. The network (ABC or ESPN) was not final as of my research. The forecast says 68 and sunny. A perfect day on the Plains.
Last week: Auburn beat No. 1 Georgia 27-24. Georgia tied it late, then fumbled, and Auburn recovered to set up McPherson's kick. LSU shut out No. 16 Mississippi State 31-0.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is a tough one, darlin'. LSU allows only 2.82 yards a carry and 15.9 points a game, and it has 24 sacks. Brown's legs will matter a lot.
Their offense vs. our defense: LSU averages 40.4 points and 504.0 yards a game. QB Sam Leavitt threw four touchdowns against Mississippi State, and RB Dilin Jones has 567 yards. One thing in our favor: LSU is 0-2 on the road this season.
Series: LSU leads 33-23-1 as played, 30-23-1 officially. LSU won the last listed meeting, 48-18 in 2023.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 16 sacks and has allowed 23, with 11 takeaways against 9 giveaways, and it has 8 rushing and 10 passing touchdowns.
Availability: an unofficial injury page lists nobody for Auburn. I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can we protect Brown? We've allowed 23 sacks, and they have 24. (2) Can our defense slow down Leavitt? (3) Can we carry the Georgia energy into a second straight big game?
And to Cece Thibodeaux, LSU's insider: welcome to the Plains, sugar. Bring your beignets. We'll bring the toilet paper.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Auburn? Southern Greens on North College Street for a game-day lunch, a mighty fine one.

report.title: "Pedigree Tells": Rhett Abernathy-Coyle Welcomes the Commodores to Kroger Field
report.byline: Our Keeneland-country horse-farm kid introduces himself and previews No. 12 Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt.
report.text:
Rhett Abernathy-Coyle · Kentucky Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Pedigree tells. Good evening, friends, I'm Rhett Abernathy-Coyle. I grew up on a horse farm out past Keeneland, mucking stalls before school and watching yearlings run in the morning mist. I learned early that you can tell a great deal about a horse from its bloodlines, and I grade football players the same way a Derby breeder grades a foal. I travel with the Wildcats and I live with the Wildcats, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a Southern gentleman's flourish. When we win, you'll hear my best Derby announcer: "And down the stretch they come!" When we lose, I'll say, "Even the best horses stumble," and adjust my hat. Now, pull up a chair, and let's talk bloodlines.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Wildcats represent the University of Kentucky in the SEC. Home is Kroger Field in Lexington, opened in 1973 and listed at 61,000 seats. The last five seasons: a fine 10-3 in 2021, then 7-6, 7-6, 4-8 and 5-7. So friends, this 6-1 start is a horse that broke slow last year and is now running at the front of the field.

The Coach and the Scheme
Will Stein is our first-year head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 1, 2025. And what a debut. This team wins by taking care of the ball and taking it away. We've lost only 5 turnovers and taken away 16, good for a plus-11 margin, 3rd in FBS. That's a thoroughbred that never breaks stride. We score 32.7 points a game (46th) and run for 166.1 (56th). We play clean, 44.4 penalty yards a game (23rd). We have 18 sacks. Now, every horse has a flaw: we convert just 29.1% of third downs, last in FBS, and our pass defense allows 249.7 yards a game (116th).

Players to Know
QB Kenny Minchey: 141 of 206 for 1,552 yards, 13 TD and just one interception. At Oklahoma he went 21 of 28 for 158 yards and two scores. Pure pedigree.
RB C.J. Baxter: 484 yards on 87 carries and 8 TD. Against Oklahoma, Jason Patterson led our backs with 38 yards on 12 carries, and I haven't seen an official report on Baxter's status this week.
WR Kenny Darby: 34 catches, 436 yards, 3 TD. WR Nic Anderson: five catches for 48 yards at Oklahoma.
LB Grant Godfrey: team-high 67 tackles. DL Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace: 4 sacks. DB Jordan Castell: 4 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Kentucky is 6-1 and 4-1 in the SEC, ranked No. 12 by both the AP and the coaches. We beat Youngstown State 45-13, won at Texas A&M 31-21, beat South Alabama 45-21, won at South Carolina 35-34, beat LSU 35-34 and won at Oklahoma 21-13. The one loss: Alabama, 45-17. We're 3-0 on the road. After Vanderbilt, we have a week off, then go to No. 11 Tennessee on Nov. 7. I won't do standings math, friends. I'll only say this horse is in the race.
Down the stretch: two one-point wins in a row, at South Carolina and against LSU. That's a photo finish twice. Champions win those.
Bloodlines, friends: a first-year coach, a quarterback with one interception in seven games and a defense that keeps taking the ball away. When I see a yearling with that kind of balance, I call the farm manager and say, keep an eye on that one. The Alabama loss? Even the best young horses get beat in their first big race. What matters is how they run the next one, and this team has won five straight since. Three of those wins came on the road, in hostile barns.

This Week: Vanderbilt (3-4) at No. 12 Kentucky (6-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kroger Field, Lexington · SEC Network.
Last week: we won 21-13 at Oklahoma. Vanderbilt lost 31-21 to Arkansas.
The history: CFBD shows Kentucky won seven of the 10 meetings from 2016 through 2025.
Their offense vs. our defense: Vanderbilt throws for 235.1 yards a game (63rd), and receiver Junior Sherrill has 628 receiving yards. Our 116th-ranked pass defense must keep him in front. But Vanderbilt has thrown 7 interceptions, and Jordan Castell has 4 of ours. That's a fine matchup for a ball hawk.
Our offense vs. their defense: Vanderbilt's run defense allowed 196 yards to Ole Miss and 170 to Arkansas. That's an open lane on the rail.
Third downs: our weak spot, last in FBS. Vanderbilt's defense has allowed 29.7 points a game (115th).
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our turnover habit, plus-11. (2) Running the ball at a defense that's struggled to stop it. (3) Keeping Sherrill in check.
To Pippa Ashcroft, Vanderbilt's insider: a song about every game? Charming. Write me one about a horse, and I'll come to the show.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
In Lexington for the game? Joe Bologna's on West Maxwell Street is a longtime family pizza spot.

report.title: "That's a Whole Roux of a Defense, Cher": Cece Thibodeaux Takes the Tigers to the Plains
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, bonjour, Tiger fans, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Celestine Thibodeaux, but darlin', everybody calls me Cece. I'm a Baton Rouge girl through and through. I'll out-scout any coordinator in the SEC between two trays of crawfish, and I'll do it in heels. I travel with this team and live with this team. I also rank every defense on a spice scale. It starts at "bland," which is a sad, sad plate, and goes all the way up to "Saturday night in Death Valley," which is as hot as it gets. When we win, I lead a brass-band parade around the room and hand out imaginary beignets to everybody in reach. When we lose, I declare a "gumbo of grief" and list every ingredient that went wrong. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, seasoned just right.

The School in 60 Seconds
LSU plays in Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, listed at 102,321. When that place gets rocking at night, you can feel it in your bones, cher. The 2019 Tigers won the national championship, and quarterback Joe Burrow won the Heisman Trophy that season. LSU is 5-0 at home this year and has outscored those visitors 225-44. That's a spice level of "Saturday night in Death Valley," no question. The series with Auburn goes back a long way: 57 meetings, and LSU leads 33-23-1 as played (officially 30-23-1).

The Coach and the Scheme
Lane Kiffin came over from Ole Miss to take the LSU job, hired on Nov. 30, 2025. The 2026 numbers say this offense cooks with gas. LSU averages 40.4 points and 504.0 yards a game, with 307.9 passing yards and 16 passing touchdowns. It mixes in the run on about 54% of plays, with 20 rushing touchdowns. Now let's talk about the defense, which is a whole roux. LSU allows 15.9 points and 256.6 yards a game, and opponents gain only 2.82 yards a carry. The Tigers have 24 sacks. The one ingredient I'd change: 11 turnovers lost against 9 forced.

Players to Know
QB Sam Leavitt: 1,784 yards and 14 TD. Against Mississippi State he went 31 of 38 for 289 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions. Ooh, that's a spicy plate.
RB Dilin Jones: 567 yards and 5 TD. He had 84 rushing yards and 8 catches against the Bulldogs.
LB T.J. Dottery: a team-high 54 tackles, 12 of them last week.
Availability notes: an unofficial injury page lists DB Tre' Brown as back from a lower-body issue and Jackson Harris with an ankle injury. I found no official LSU report as of Oct. 18, 2026.

The Conference Picture
LSU is 5-2 overall and 2-2 in the SEC, perfect at home and 0-2 on the road. The Tigers are No. 18 in the AP poll and No. 17 in the Coaches Poll. Both losses came on the road: 32-24 at Ole Miss and 35-34 at Kentucky. So if you're wondering what LSU has to prove this week, it's winning away from home. Both of those were one-score games, and the Kentucky loss was by a single point. A little more seasoning in the fourth quarter and this is a 7-0 team. That's not a complaint, cher, it's a recipe card.

This Week: No. 18 LSU (5-2) at Auburn (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET (11 a.m. CT) · Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn. The network (ABC or ESPN) had not been finalized as of my research. The forecast calls for 68 degrees and sunny. Lovely day for a road trip.
Last week: LSU shut out No. 16 Mississippi State 31-0. Auburn knocked off No. 1 Georgia 27-24 on a 34-yard field goal as time expired. Big respect, y'all.
Our offense vs. their defense: Auburn allows 21.8 points a game and 228.0 passing yards. LB Elijah Melendez has 52 tackles, 4 sacks and an interception, and he intercepted a pass at Georgia.
Their offense vs. our defense: Auburn QB Byrum Brown can hurt you with his legs. He ran for 115 yards and a touchdown at Georgia, and he has 1,202 passing yards. Our run defense allows 2.82 a carry. Auburn has allowed 23 sacks, and we have 24. Mmm-hmm.
Series: LSU leads. The last six meetings listed: LSU won in 2018 (22-21), 2019 (23-20), 2022 (21-17) and 2023 (48-18), and Auburn won in 2020 (48-11) and 2021 (24-19).
Availability: see Players to Know. Nothing official found for Auburn as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can we win on the road, finally? (2) Can our pass rush get to Brown before he takes off? (3) Leavitt's ball security in a loud stadium.
And to Lacey Bellamy, Auburn's insider: bless your heart, sugar. Congratulations on Georgia. Now pass the beignets.

report.title: "Ring It If You Mean It": Wade Pettus Welcomes the Sooners to Starkville
report.byline: Our cowbell-carrying insider introduces himself and previews the first-ever Oklahoma-Mississippi State game.
report.text:
Wade Pettus · Mississippi State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Ring it if you mean it. (ding.) Howdy, Bulldog people. I'm Wade Pettus, poultry-science graduate, and I chart Air Raid concepts on the back of feed-store receipts. I have a drawer full of them. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I will tell you plainly that my cowbell has better football sense than most of the analysts on television. It has never once been wrong about a third down. Every week I'll bring you the players, the matchup, the history and a little gentle Starkville deadpan. When we win, I ring the cowbell exactly once for every point we scored, no matter how long it takes. When we lose, the cowbell goes in a sock, out of respect. I believe football is best explained slowly, the way you'd explain a good hen house. I'm glad you're here.

The School in 60 Seconds
Mississippi State plays in the SEC and won the league championship in 1941, plus a division title in 1998. The Bulldogs have made 27 bowl appearances and produced 38 All-Americans, 171 All-SEC selections and 124 NFL players, 11 of them first-round draft choices. Our home, Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field, is the second-oldest stadium in FBS; CFBD dates it to 1914 and lists capacity at 61,337. The last few years have been lean, 2-10 in 2024 and 5-8 in 2025, and that makes this 4-2 start feel like the first warm morning in March. I wrote that on a receipt, too. The Bulldogs have never played Oklahoma before this week, so every snap Saturday is a first for the record books.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jeff Lebby was hired Nov. 26, 2023. He came from Oklahoma, where he was offensive coordinator for Brent Venables's first two seasons, 2022 and 2023. His first two years in Starkville went 7-18. This offseason he brought back Zach Arnett as defensive coordinator, Arnett's second stint in that job here. The 2026 numbers show an offense that can move: 454.3 yards a game (22nd), 277.8 passing (22nd) and 176.5 rushing (50th), for 32.5 points a game. The run game averages 4.6 yards a carry, 1,059 yards on 229 tries. The defense is better against the run (114.7 a game, 36th) than the pass (264.8, 127th). Penalties need cleaning up: 70.7 yards a game ranks 118th.

Players to Know
QB Kamario Taylor: 102 of 154, 1,450 yards, 17 TD, 4 INT. A foot injury slowed him against Missouri and Alabama, and he did not play at LSU. No official status for Saturday as of Oct. 18.
RB Da'Marion "Fluff" Bothwell: 403 yards on 74 carries, 3 TD. He was also unavailable at LSU.
WR Anthony Evans III: 47 catches, 614 yards, 5 TD.
LB Tyler Lockhart: a team-high 38 tackles. DL Will Whitson: 2 sacks. LB Jalen Smith: an interception.
QB Puckett: made his first career start at LSU, 16 of 26 for 121 yards. AP lists him as Parker Puckett and SI as Billy Puckett, so I'm showing you both until the school confirms.

The Conference Picture
Mississippi State is 4-2 overall and 2-2 in the SEC. Wins: UL Monroe 62-13, at Minnesota 38-13, at South Carolina 41-34 and Missouri 31-24. Losses: Alabama 56-23 and at LSU 31-0. That's two SEC wins through four league games, already the most of Lebby's tenure in conference play. We are unranked. Next up after this is a trip to Texas on Oct. 31.

This Week: Oklahoma (3-3) at Mississippi State (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Davis Wade Stadium · SEC Network. First meeting ever.
Last week: we lost 31-0 at LSU, with turnovers and failed fourth-down tries hurting the offense. Oklahoma lost 21-13 at home to Kentucky; Mateer threw three interceptions.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the hard part. Oklahoma allows 260.7 yards a game (5th), 151.3 passing yards (6th) and just 25.6% on third down (2nd). Its red zone defense is 6th.
Their offense vs. our defense: Oklahoma's offense ranks 126th in yards and 136th in rushing, and the Sooners are minus-8 in turnover margin. Our run defense, 36th, gets a chance to make them one-dimensional.
The storyline: Coach Lebby against the program where he called plays two seasons ago. My cowbell has thoughts. It's keeping them to itself.
Availability: Taylor (foot) and Bothwell both missed LSU; neither has an official status for Saturday. For Oklahoma, Venables said left tackle Michael Fasusi was close to returning. No SEC availability report as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Whether Taylor plays, and how well he moves. (2) Turnovers: Oklahoma has 14 giveaways this season. (3) Whether our pass offense, 22nd in FBS, can find room against the nation's 6th-best pass defense.
And to Savannah Redbird-Lowe, Oklahoma's very gracious insider: welcome to Starkville. I'll ring once for you. Politely.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
In Starkville for the game? Thai Siam on Martin Luther King Jr. Drive East makes a good, quiet supper after all that ringing.

Delphine Arceneaux-Moss · Missouri Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Show me the tape! I'm Delphine Arceneaux-Moss, and I'm your Missouri insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a mizzou-J-school style beat reporter who breaks news and blitz tendencies. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. Fair warning about my habit: 'Breaks news' on obvious things, live, with a fake news ticker sound. On the podcast, my segment is called Breaking News. The show card describes it like this: breaks obvious news with a fake ticker. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Tigers have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Memorial Stadium in Columbia, MO, built in 1927 with a listed capacity of 71,168. The playing surface is Faurot Field, per Wikipedia. The Coach and the Scheme
Eli Drinkwitz leads the Tigers; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 9, 2019. Through 7 games, Missouri scores 31.1 points a game and allows 19.6. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 53% of its plays, gaining 164.4 rushing yards and 265.9 passing yards a game. That's a balanced menu. The Conference Picture
Missouri is 5-2 overall, 4-0 at home and 1-2 away. In SEC play the Tigers are 2-2, which sorts them No. 8 of 16 by record. Georgia sits on top at 4-1 in league games. Right around us: LSU (2-2) and Auburn (2-2). The top of the table: Georgia (4-1), Kentucky (4-1), Tennessee (3-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. The Tigers are No. 22 in the latest AP poll in our data. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Missouri this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Tigers lost to Ole Miss on the road, 31-3. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, at Arkansas, in Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, with a flex kickoff window (2:30 to 3:30 or 5 to 7 p.m.). Arkansas comes in at 3-4. From 2016 through 2025, Missouri went 9-1 against Arkansas in 10 meetings. After that, CFBD lists vs. Texas (Nov. 7), at Georgia (Nov. 14), vs. Kentucky (Nov. 21), vs. Oklahoma (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Tigers come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Show me the tape!

report.title: "Boomer! (You Say Sooner.)": Savannah Redbird-Lowe Rides Into Starkville

report.text:
Savannah Redbird-Lowe · Oklahoma Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Boomer! (You say Sooner.) Louder, Norman, I can't hear you over the Schooner wheels. I'm Savannah Redbird-Lowe, former Oklahoma rodeo princess, and I read a defense the way I used to read a barrel pattern: clean turn, tight pocket, no tipped barrels. I travel with this team, I live with this team, and I will make you do the "Boomer!" "Sooner!" call-and-response at least once in every single report. That is my one rule, and I'm sweet about it. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the storylines and the history, told straight with a little Plains-state sass. When we win, you'll hear me holler "Boomer!" and wait for you. When we lose, I'll lift my chin and tell you we'll roll the Schooner again. Saddle up, y'all.

The School in 60 Seconds
Oklahoma football started in 1895. The program claims seven national championships (1950, 1955, 1956, 1974, 1975, 1985 and 2000), 50 conference titles and seven Heisman Trophy winners. Its 963 wins and.723 winning percentage both rank sixth all-time. The Sooners also hold the Division I record for consecutive wins, 47 straight, and Oklahoma is the only program where four different coaches have won more than 100 games. Home is Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, listed at 86,112 seats in the CFBD venue file. These days we're an SEC program; the move came for the 2024 season, after 2021-2023 in the Big 12. Last season the Sooners went 10-3. That is a lot of trophies to dust, and I do it in boots.

The Coach and the Scheme
Brent Venables is the head coach; the CFBD coaches file dates his hire to Dec. 5, 2021, and he has led the program since 2022. The 2026 numbers tell you exactly who this team is. The defense is the barrel racer that never knocks one over: 260.7 yards allowed a game, 5th in FBS, 151.3 passing yards allowed, 6th, and 18.2 points allowed, 30th. Opponents convert only 25.6% of their third downs, 2nd-best in the country, and our red zone defense ranks 6th. The defense has 18 sacks in six games. The offense is still finding its gait. Oklahoma averages 311.5 yards (126th) and 92.5 rushing yards a game (136th), on 555 rushing yards across 197 carries. The turnover column is the sore spot: 14 giveaways and a minus-8 margin that ranks 134th.

Players to Know

report.title: "Hotty Toddy, and Pass the Footnotes": Langston Fairbanks Writes His Way to Austin
report.byline: Our seersucker-suited literature lover introduces himself and previews No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas.
report.text:
Langston Fairbanks · Ole Miss Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hotty Toddy, and pass the footnotes. Good evening, gentle readers. I am Langston Fairbanks, a man of seersucker and sweet tea, a student of literature who has read every word Mr. Faulkner wrote and every snap the Rebels have played this season, often on the same afternoon in the Grove. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I will bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. Be warned: my takes tend to run three paragraphs. I can't help it. Football, like a good novel, deserves a proper beginning, middle and end. But I always land on a hard number. When we win, I recite a celebratory monologue under the nearest chandelier. When we lose, I murmur, "The past is never dead," and sip my sweet tea in silence.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Rebels represent the University of Mississippi, which everyone calls Ole Miss, and play in the SEC. The program was founded in 1893 and has won six SEC titles: 1947, 1954, 1955, 1960, 1962 and 1963. Ole Miss has been recognized as national champion three times by major selectors. Home is Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on campus, opened in 1915 and listed at 64,038 seats. And the recent chapters read like an epic: 10-3, 8-5, 11-2, 10-3, and last year a 13-2 season that AP describes as a playoff team. Since 2023, the Rebels are 25-1 at home.

The Coach and the Scheme
Pete Golding is the head coach in his first full season; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 30, 2025. Under him, the offense writes in long, flowing sentences: 290.7 passing yards a game (13th), 444.5 total yards (36th) and 37.5 points (20th). And here is the hard number I promised: we have scored on 100% of our red zone trips, first in FBS. The defense is the chapter still being revised: 390 yards allowed (108th), 236.5 passing yards allowed (104th). Opponents convert 44% of third downs (118th). But last week the defense held Missouri to 39 rushing yards on 26 carries. Defensive tackle Will Echoles said, "Stopping the run has been an issue for us at times this year, but it's gotten better".

Players to Know
QB Trinidad Chambliss: 142 of 210 for 1,676 yards, 14 TD, 4 INT. Against Missouri he threw three touchdowns and ran for another. Coach Golding: "He wasn't perfect either, but I'm glad he's on our side".
RB Kewan Lacy: 352 yards on 62 carries, 5 TD; 122 yards on 16 carries last week. Makhi Frazier added 101 yards on 15 carries.
WR Deuce Alexander: 35 catches, 523 yards, 5 TD. Caleb Odom, Horatio Fields and Caleb Cunningham each caught a touchdown against Missouri.
DT Will Echoles: five tackles, two pass breakups and a sack against Missouri. DE Blake Purchase: 3.5 sacks. LB Luke Ferrelli: team-high 39 tackles. S Nick Cull: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Ole Miss is 5-1, 3-1 in the SEC, and ranked No. 7 by both the AP and coaches. We beat Louisville 41-38 at a neutral site, Charlotte 41-9, LSU 32-24, Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3. The lone blemish: a 52-28 loss at Florida. After Austin, Auburn comes to Oxford on Oct. 31. AP notes we still face No. 1 Georgia, and four of our last five games are at home. I shall not do arithmetic upon the standings tonight. I shall only say the plot thickens beautifully. And the Florida chapter? Every great Southern novel has a tragedy in its second act. What matters is that the protagonist rises again, and since Gainesville, we have won twice by a combined 83-20.

This Week: No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1) at No. 19 Texas (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin · ABC. Kickoff forecast: 85 degrees, partly cloudy. Seersucker weather.
The history: officially, Texas leads the series 6-1; as played, 6-2 in eight meetings. The most recent: Ole Miss won 44-23 in 2013, a year after Texas won 66-31. And there was a Sugar Bowl win, 39-7, after the 1957 season.
Last week: we beat Missouri 31-3. Texas lost 27-24 to Florida.
Our offense vs. their defense: now this is the central conflict of the novel. Texas allows 272.5 yards a game (12th), 166.2 passing yards (12th) and 17.8 points (29th). Texas' Colin Simmons has 10.5 sacks. Chambliss against that pass rush is the scene I'll reread for years.
Their offense vs. our defense: Texas averages 361.3 yards (93rd) and 134.5 rushing yards (103rd). Arch Manning has 11 touchdown passes.
Availability: no official SEC availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Protecting Chambliss from Simmons. (2) Our perfect red zone record against Texas' 57th-ranked red zone defense. (3) Getting off the field on third down.
To Caroline Whitfield, Texas' insider: you price your players like assets? Madam, I prefer to read them like poetry. Let us meet in the fourth quarter.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Back in Oxford? City Grocery and Ajax Diner, both on Courthouse Square, are as much a part of the Oxford story as any novel.

report.title: "Cue the Music": Beau Cheraw Makes His Entrance as the Vols Come to Columbia
report.byline: Our Williams-Brice hype man introduces himself and previews South Carolina's home date with No. 11 Tennessee.
report.text:
Beaumont 'Beau' Cheraw · South Carolina Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
(Lights down. Music up. A single spotlight. Smoke machine, family-sized.) Cue the music. Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, Gamecock Nation: I'm Beaumont Cheraw, but you can call me Beau, and I live for the entrance. I time my podcast intro to dramatic music. I have timed my breakfast to dramatic music. I travel with this team, I live with this team, and I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines every week, with the volume where it belongs. When we win, I'll bounce like the whole of Williams-Brice when the music hits. When we lose, I'll turn the music down, just for a minute, and remind you that the band plays again next Saturday. I'm electric, I'm theatrical, and I will always be kind to the visitors, because a great show needs a great guest star. And I promise: every number I give you comes with a receipt, right there in brackets. Forever to thee.

The School in 60 Seconds
South Carolina plays in the SEC and has since 1992. Before that, the Gamecocks were in the ACC from 1953 through 1970, winning the 1969 conference title, and then a major independent from 1971 through 1991. The independent years gave us George Rogers, our 1980 Heisman Trophy winner and the No. 1 overall selection in the 1981 draft. Jadeveon Clowney went No. 1 overall in 2014. We won the SEC East in 2010. Lou Holtz and Steve Spurrier are both in the College Football Hall of Fame, and Shane Beamer was the 2024 SEC coach of the year. Home is Williams-Brice Stadium, listed at 80,250 seats. When that stadium starts bouncing, you understand. The Gamecocks finished in the final AP top 25 in 1984 and 1987 as an independent, and have posted eight final top-25 finishes in the SEC era.

The Coach and the Scheme
Beamer was hired Dec. 6, 2020, and this is his sixth season. His teams went 9-4 in 2024 and 4-8 in 2025. The 2026 Gamecocks bring the noise on offense: 474.7 yards a game (13th in FBS), 232.3 rushing yards (10th) and 37.7 points (18th). CFBD has 1,394 rushing yards on 233 carries, just about 6 yards a carry. The defense is sturdy against the run, 103.7 yards allowed a game (25th), and leakier through the air, 237.2 passing yards allowed (107th). The red zone defense, 93.8% scoring allowed, ranks 122nd. That's the one part of the show we're still rehearsing.

Players to Know
QB LaNorris Sellers: 115 of 187, 1,338 yards, 12 TD, 4 INT. Against Florida he threw for 279 yards and four touchdowns, and ran one in.
RB Matthew Fuller: 485 yards on 81 carries, 5 TD.
WR Nyck Harbor: 17 catches, 278 yards, 2 TD, including four for 83 and a score against Florida.
LB Justin Okoronkwo: a team-high 43 tackles. DE Anthony Addison: 3 sacks. DB Peyton Williams: an interception.
Freshman Julian Walker: two starts and a sack, per the school's injury rundown.

The Conference Picture
South Carolina is 3-3 and 1-3 in the SEC. The three SEC losses were by 7 to Mississippi State, by 31 at Alabama and by 1 in overtime to Kentucky, 35-34. The win at Florida, 38-19, came right before the bye. We're unranked. Next up is a trip to Oklahoma on Oct. 31. Knocking off the No. 11 team in the country at home would be one fine entrance into November.

This Week: No. 11 Tennessee (6-1) at South Carolina (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Williams-Brice Stadium · ESPN.
Last game: we beat Florida 38-19 on Oct. 10, then had the bye. Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10 last Saturday behind 159 rushing yards from DeSean Bishop.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the main event. Tennessee allows 14.7 points (9th), 280.6 yards (15th) and 159.3 passing yards (8th). It has 29 sacks. Our run game, 10th in FBS, against their run defense, 42nd, is where I'd put the spotlight.
Their offense vs. our defense: Tennessee runs for 217.1 yards a game (19th) and scores on 95.7% of red zone trips (6th). We allow 103.7 rushing yards a game (25th), so that's strength against strength. Their quarterback spot is a work in progress, per AP.
Series: UT's game notes list the all-time series at Tennessee 29, South Carolina 11, with 2 ties. From 2016 through 2025 it's even, 4-4.
Availability: Beamer, after the Florida game: "Everybody that missed the game yesterday or left the game, like Judge Collier did, we all expect to be back against Tennessee. The only one that we would be most concerned about. is QuaySheed Scott." That group included DT Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy, Walker and center Carter Miller. The first SEC availability report comes Wednesday. For Tennessee, aggregators list three players out, including LB J. Harmon (ACL).
What decides it: (1) Whether Sellers can find room against the 8th-ranked pass defense. (2) Red zone: our defense has to get stops there. (3) Whether the bye week gets our injured guys back to full speed.
And Rocky Top Haskew, Tennessee's insider, I hear you brought a banjo. Bring it on in. We'll give you a proper entrance.

report.title: "Cue the Banjo": Rocky Top Haskew Takes the Vols to Columbia
report.byline: Our banjo-picking former long snapper introduces himself and previews No. 11 Tennessee at South Carolina.
report.text:
Earl 'Rocky Top' Haskew · Tennessee Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
(banjo: plink-a-plink-plink.) Cue the banjo. Howdy, Big Orange Country, I'm Earl Haskew, but everybody on Cumberland Avenue calls me Rocky Top. I was a long snapper for the Vols, which means I spent four years looking at the world upside down and backward, and honestly it gave me a great perspective on defensive fronts. I travel with this team and live with this team, and before every stat I play a little banjo intro. Sometimes the banjo's out of tune on purpose. You'll know when. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and a few checkerboard metaphors from a fella who loves the end zones at Neyland more than his own front porch. When we win, I play "Rocky Top" until somebody stops me, and nobody ever does. When we lose, I play it slow and sad. Pull up a rocking chair.

The School in 60 Seconds
(plink.) Tennessee started playing football in 1891. The Vols claim six national titles, including two from the wire-service polls in 1951 and 1998, and 16 conference championships. We rank fifth all-time in bowl appearances, 55 of them, with four Sugar Bowls, three Cotton Bowls, two Orange Bowls, a Fiesta and a Peach among the wins. Neyland Stadium is the cathedral, and the Vols have won 485 games there, the most any program has won in its current home. Capacity is listed at 101,915 by one source and 102,455 by CFBD, so I'll just say "a whole lot of orange" and show you both. Josh Heupel's teams have gone 11-2, 9-4, 10-3 and 8-5 since 2022.

The Coach and the Scheme
Heupel was hired Jan. 27, 2021. This year's Vols win the old-fashioned way, and my banjo approves. Tennessee runs for 217.1 yards a game, 19th in FBS, and has 1,520 rushing yards on 302 carries, a little over 5 yards a pop. The passing game is more modest, 188.0 yards a game (110th). The defense is the headliner: 280.6 yards allowed (15th), 159.3 passing yards allowed (8th) and 14.7 points allowed (9th). It has 29 sacks and 13 takeaways through seven games, and it holds opponents to 30.8% on third down, 15th in FBS. The red zone offense scores on 95.7% of trips, 6th. That's checkerboard football: square by square, all the way down the field.

Players to Know
RB DeSean Bishop: 837 yards on 139 carries, 10 TD. He ran for 159 yards and two scores against Alabama, 95 of them after halftime. Heupel called him "a special back. Smart, tough, physical, great vision."
The quarterbacks: Faizon Brandon leads the team at 697 yards, 7 TD and 1 INT on 61 of 101. George MacIntyre started against Alabama and went 21 of 31 for 197 yards. AP called the position "still very much a work in progress".
WR Mike Matthews: 29 catches, 481 yards, 3 TD, including seven for 85 against Alabama.
DL Tyree Weathersby: a team-high 6.5 sacks. LB Amare Campbell: 46 tackles. DB Dejuan Lane: 3 interceptions.
(Note: ESPN's public game page showed slightly different sack and tackle leaders on Oct. 18. I'm using its season-leaders feed.)

The Conference Picture
Tennessee is 6-1 and 3-1 in the SEC, 2-0 on the road, and No. 11 in both the AP and Coaches polls this week. The only loss was 20-17 to Texas. The Vols have won three straight: Auburn 24-14, at Arkansas 24-17 and Alabama 26-10. Tennessee has now won three of its last five against Alabama, all three at home. After the field-storming, the SEC fined Tennessee $500,000, payable to Alabama under league policy. After this trip, the next game listed is a Nov. 7 home date with No. 12 Kentucky.

This Week: No. 11 Tennessee (6-1) at South Carolina (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia · ESPN.
Last week: we beat Alabama 26-10. Alabama had 201 yards, 54 on the ground, and four turnovers, and went 2 for 13 on third down. A fourth-quarter drive took 9 minutes, 32 seconds and ended with Bishop's 5-yard touchdown. South Carolina was off after beating Florida 38-19 on Oct. 10.
Our offense vs. their defense: South Carolina stops the run well, 103.7 yards allowed a game (25th), but gives up 237.2 passing yards (107th) and lets opponents score on 93.8% of red zone trips (122nd). That last number makes my banjo hum.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the heavyweight bout. South Carolina averages 474.7 yards (13th), 232.3 rushing (10th) and 37.7 points (18th). LaNorris Sellers has 12 touchdown passes and four interceptions. Our defense is 9th in scoring.
Series: UT's game notes list Tennessee 29 wins, South Carolina 11 and 2 ties. In the CFBD window from 2016 through 2025, the teams split eight meetings, 4-4.
Availability: aggregator reports list LB J. Harmon out for the season with a torn ACL, OG Wendell Moe Jr. out for the season and LS B. Brady out with an undisclosed injury, as of Oct. 17. That's not an official SEC report, and the first one comes Wednesday. For South Carolina, Beamer expected everyone who missed the Florida game back except possibly nickel Quay'Sheed Scott, pending tests.
What decides it: (1) Bishop and the run game against South Carolina's 25th-ranked run defense. (2) Who plays quarterback for us, and how cleanly. (3) Whether our defense can slow an offense that is 10th in rushing.
And Beau Cheraw, South Carolina's insider: I hear you've got an entrance planned. I've got a banjo. Let's make it a duet.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching from Knoxville? Calhoun's on the River on Neyland Drive is a fine spot to listen for the banjo.

report.title: "Darling, That's a Premium Asset": Caro Whitfield Welcomes the Rebels to Austin
report.byline: Our rodeo-queen portfolio analyst introduces herself and previews No. 19 Texas vs. No. 7 Ole Miss.
report.text:
Caroline 'Caro' Whitfield · Texas Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Darling, that's a premium asset. Well, hello, y'all, I'm Caroline Whitfield, Caro to my friends. I was a rodeo queen in a former life, I spent a few years in consulting after that, and now I bring both to the Forty Acres: big-hat polish and a very organized brain. I travel with the Longhorns and I live with the Longhorns, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. I size up every opponent's roster in imaginary Caro Bucks, and I'll tell you exactly what each player is worth to me. Darling, I don't do rebuilds. I do acquisitions. When we win, I raise a single eyebrow and say, "As forecast." When we lose, I call an emergency board meeting with myself. Hypothetically, heads roll.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Texas Longhorns began playing in 1893 and compete in the SEC. We claim four consensus national championships: 1963, 1969, 1970 and 2005, and the program has been led by three Hall of Fame coaches. Home is DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, opened in 1924 and listed at 100,119 seats. The last five seasons: 5-7, 8-5, then 12-2, 13-3 and 10-3. That, darling, is a blue-chip portfolio.

The Coach and the Scheme
Steve Sarkisian has been our head coach since CFBD's hire date of Jan. 2, 2021. CollegeFootballDigest notes he's two wins from 100 as a head coach, with 98 so far. Now, the holdings. The defense is the crown jewel: 272.5 yards allowed a game (12th in FBS), 166.2 passing yards allowed (12th), 106.3 rushing (28th) and 17.8 points (29th). We have 19 sacks. The offense, I'll admit, is underperforming its valuation: 361.3 yards a game (93rd) and 134.5 rushing yards (103rd). We've allowed 17 sacks. A smart investor knows which assets to hold and which need attention.

Players to Know
QB Arch Manning: 106 of 166 for about 1,295 yards (1,298 per AP), 11 TD, 5 INT. Against Florida he went 14 of 20 for 173 yards and a touchdown.
RB Smothers: 289 yards on 65 carries, 2 TD. ESPN lists him as Hollywood Smothers; AP says Daylan.
WR Ryan Wingo: 26 catches, 345 yards, 3 TD. Emmett Mosley V: two catches for 76 yards against Florida.
DE Colin Simmons: 10.5 sacks. In seven figures of Caro Bucks, darling, that is a premium asset.
LB Rasheem Biles: team-high 48 tackles and 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Texas is 4-2 and 1-2 in the SEC, ranked No. 19 by the AP and No. 18 by the coaches. We beat Texas State 59-7, Ohio State 24-23, UTSA 30-6 and Tennessee 20-17 on the road. Then two three-point losses: 27-24 to Oklahoma at a neutral site and 27-24 to Florida. After Ole Miss, Mississippi State visits on Oct. 31. I don't do standings math in public, darling. I'll just say two losses by three points apiece is a market correction, not a crash.
The portfolio review: the Ohio State win, 24-23, is still the holding I treasure most this year. Beating Tennessee on the road, 20-17, was a fine acquisition too. In those two big wins, the defense allowed 40 points combined. That is how this team wins, darling: suffocate people. The losses to Oklahoma and Florida were decided by a field goal each, and both opponents scored 27. A few plays here and there, and we're having a very different conversation. I've seen bigger swings in the oil patch. And unlike oil, I know this defense will keep holding up in October.

This Week: No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1) at No. 19 Texas (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 Central) · DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin · ABC. Kickoff forecast: 85 degrees, partly cloudy.

Their offense vs. our defense: this is the merger of the season. Ole Miss throws for 290.7 yards a game (13th) and scores 37.5 points (20th). Trinidad Chambliss has 14 touchdown passes. And the Rebels have scored on every one of their red zone trips, first in FBS. Our pass defense ranks 12th. Something has to give, y'all.
Our offense vs. their defense: Ole Miss allows 390 yards a game (108th), 236.5 passing yards (104th) and lets opponents convert 44% of third downs (118th). Manning should find room.
Possession: Ole Miss averages 26:59, 131st in FBS. They score fast and they leave the field fast.
Availability: no official SEC availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Simmons and our pass rush against Chambliss. (2) Manning against a 104th-ranked pass defense. (3) Red zone defense; ours ranks 57th.

report.title: "Howdy, and Let Me Yell This": Colt Wendeborn Brings the 12th Man to Tuscaloosa
report.byline: Our Corps-loving engineer introduces himself and previews Texas A&M at No. 13 Alabama.
report.text:
Colt Wendeborn · Texas A&M Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
HOWDY! Howdy, and let me yell this: welcome to The Cover Window, Aggies! I'm Colt Wendeborn, petroleum engineering graduate, and I report on football practice the way the Yell Leaders lead Midnight Yell, with my whole chest. I travel with this team and I live with this team. My one weakness is that I explain everything with an Aggie tradition, and then I explain the tradition, and then sometimes I explain the explanation. You'll learn a lot. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, delivered with the straight-arrow earnestness of a man who irons his maroon. When we win, I yell. Just yell. Joyfully. When we lose, I go practice silent yell drills in a closet until I feel better. Gig 'em, and thank you for reading.

The School in 60 Seconds
Texas A&M competes in the SEC and claims three national titles and 18 conference championships. Home is Kyle Field, an outdoor stadium on campus that seats 102,733. CFBD dates it to 1927. (A tradition explained: the student section stands the entire game because the 12th Man is ready to go in. That's why I'm standing while I write this.) The last five seasons have run 8-4, 5-7, 7-6, 8-5 and then a big 11-2 in 2025, Mike Elko's second year. Kyle Field and Bryant-Denny both hold more than 100,000 people, so Saturday is two of the biggest rooms in the sport shaking hands.

The Coach and the Scheme
Elko was hired Nov. 27, 2023. The 2026 identity is defense first, and I will yell about it. The Aggies allow 17.1 points a game (27th), 306.6 yards (29th) and just 164.1 passing yards (10th). Opponents convert only 29.8% of third downs, 11th in FBS. The team is careful, too: 41.7 penalty yards a game is 14th-best in the country. The offense is still searching. It averages 356.9 yards (97th) and 195.7 passing yards (103rd), and the pass rush has only 5 sacks in seven games. In the two SEC road losses, at LSU and at Missouri, the Aggies scored 6 points each time.

Players to Know
QB Marcel Reed: 112 of 201, 1,227 yards, 7 TD, 6 INT. At Missouri he went 19 of 39 for 189 yards and two interceptions; a week later against The Citadel he was 8 of 13 for 130 and a touchdown.
RB K.J. Edwards: 317 yards on 47 carries, 2 TD, including 116 yards on 13 carries last week.
WR Isaiah Horton: 20 catches, 280 yards, 3 TD. Aaron Gregory caught six passes for 94 yards and two touchdowns against The Citadel.
LB Ray Coney: a team-high 36 tackles. DE Marco Jones: 2 sacks. CB Julio Humphrey: an interception.

The Conference Picture
Texas A&M is 4-3 and 1-3 in the SEC, 0-2 on the road. The wins: Missouri State 50-0, Arizona State 48-20, Arkansas 34-7 and The Citadel 41-0. The losses: Kentucky 31-21, at LSU 35-6 and at Missouri 27-6. We're unranked. Next is a Nov. 7 trip to South Carolina. A win in Tuscaloosa would be the kind of thing you tell your grandchildren about at Silver Taps (that's a solemn tradition, and I won't joke about it).

This Week: Texas A&M (4-3) at No. 13 Alabama (5-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Bryant-Denny Stadium, Tuscaloosa · ABC. It's Alabama's homecoming.
Last week: we beat The Citadel 41-0. Alabama lost 26-10 at Tennessee, managed 201 yards, turned it over four times and went 2 for 13 on third down. It was the Tide's second straight loss, the first time that's happened in the regular season since 2007.
Our offense vs. their defense: Alabama allows 107 rushing yards a game (30th) but 230.9 passing (101st). Its red zone defense allows a score on 95.7% of trips, 134th. If Reed can get us inside the 20, the door is open.
Their offense vs. our defense: Alabama scores 39.3 points a game (12th). Keelon Russell has 1,746 yards, 12 TD and 4 INT. Our pass defense ranks 10th, and Russell said after Tennessee, "It was just a lack of a plan that I had. Just wasn't playing my game today." Expect him to have one this week.
Series: Alabama leads 13-3. The last meeting was a 26-20 Alabama win in College Station on Oct. 7, 2023, and the teams did not play in 2024 or 2025. Our last win in Tuscaloosa was 29-24 in 2012.
Availability: aggregator listings dated Oct. 17 have WRs Mario Craver and A.J. Bethel-Roman questionable, and OG Blake Ivy, WRs Terry Bussey and Madden Williams and RB T.J. Riden Jr. out. For Alabama, WRs Ryan Coleman-Williams (knee) and A.J. Walker are listed out and TE Jay Ford questionable. None of that is an official SEC report; the first comes Oct. 21.
What decides it: (1) Whether Reed can protect the ball on the road. (2) Our pass defense against Russell. (3) Red zone trips: Alabama has struggled to stop them.
And Mary-Kathryn Strickland, Alabama's very gracious insider: Howdy! I've brought you a tradition explained. It's long.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
In College Station? Nam Cafe on Nagle Street is a quiet bowl of pho before a long yell.

report.title: "That's a Hit Single, Y'all": Pippa Ashcroft Takes Her Guitar to Lexington
report.byline: Our Music City economics star introduces herself and previews Vanderbilt at No. 12 Kentucky.
report.text:
Penelope 'Pippa' Ashcroft · Vanderbilt Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
That's a hit single, y'all. Hey there, I'm Penelope Ashcroft, but everyone on West End calls me Pippa. I study economics at Vanderbilt by day, and by night I write country songs on a beat-up guitar, and every single one of them is about a football game. I travel with the Commodores and I live with the Commodores, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little Music City wordplay and a chorus or two. Got an interception return in my heart and a third-down stop on my mind. That's my sound. When we win, I sing a big country chorus, key change and all. When we lose, I write a sad breakup ballad to the turnover that did us in. I've got a whole album of those this month.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Commodores represent Vanderbilt University in the SEC. Home is FirstBank Stadium, right on our Nashville campus, opened in 1922 and listed at 40,351 seats. Now here's a song with a happy ending: the last five seasons went 2-10, 5-7, 2-10, then 7-6 in 2024 and a 10-3 smash hit in 2025. Ten wins at Vanderbilt. Y'all, that one went platinum. This season is the follow-up album, and follow-up albums are hard.

The Coach and the Scheme
Clark Lea is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 14, 2020. He's the producer behind that 10-3 record. This year's offense throws it, 235.1 passing yards a game (63rd), with 23.6 points a game (98th). The run game is quiet, 119.3 a game (118th). The defense has 15 sacks, but it's allowing 146.3 rushing yards (79th) and 29.7 points (115th). AP noted the defense came in highly touted but gave up 196 rushing yards to Ole Miss and 170 to Arkansas. And our turnover margin is minus-6, 126th. Coach Lea said it plainly last week: "We're actively in pursuit of a better performance".

Players to Know
QB Jared Curtis: 101 of 161 for 1,242 yards, 6 TD, 7 INT. Against Arkansas he threw for 274 yards.
WR Junior Sherrill: 41 catches, 628 yards, 4 TD. Eight catches for 99 yards and a touchdown last week. That boy is a hit single, y'all.
RB Sedrick Alexander: 270 yards on 61 carries, 5 TD; a touchdown run against Arkansas. Makhilyn Young also ran for a score.
S CJ Heard: team-high 51 tackles. LB Nick Rinaldi: 3.5 sacks. Miles Capers: 1 interception.

The Conference Picture
Vanderbilt is 3-4 and 0-4 in the SEC. We opened 3-0 with wins over Austin Peay 28-9, Delaware 35-26 and NC State 35-31. Then the SEC tour: a 21-15 loss at Auburn, 38-14 at Georgia, 52-17 to Ole Miss and 31-21 to Arkansas. After Lexington, we have a week off, then visit Mississippi State on Nov. 7. I won't do standings math, y'all. I'll write a song about turning it around.
The breakup ballad of the week: with 3:46 left against Arkansas, Curtis drove us to their 29, and an interception ended it. Verse one, chorus, heartbreak. But the Auburn game was within one score, and that tells me the band can still play.
Season so far, as an album: track one, two and three were upbeat, three straight wins at home, including a 35-31 thriller over NC State. Then came the slow songs. That's how every great record goes, y'all. You put the ballads in the middle, and you save the anthem for the end. There are still five games of this album left to write.

This Week: Vanderbilt (3-4) at No. 12 Kentucky (6-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kroger Field, Lexington · SEC Network.
The history: CFBD shows Kentucky won seven of the 10 meetings from 2016 through 2025.
Our offense vs. their defense: Kentucky's pass defense allows 249.7 yards a game, 116th in FBS. Curtis and Sherrill can write a hit against that. Kentucky's overall defense is 95th.
Their offense vs. our defense: Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey has 13 touchdown passes and only one interception. C.J. Baxter has 484 rushing yards and 8 TD. Their run game, 166.1 a game (56th), meets our run defense, which has struggled the last two weeks.
Their big weakness: Kentucky converts just 29.1% of third downs, last in FBS. Get them to third down, and we've got a shot.
Turnovers: Kentucky is plus-11, 3rd in FBS; we're minus-6. That's the whole song right there.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Protecting the football. (2) Stopping the run. (3) Winning third downs against the worst third-down offense in FBS.
To Rhett Abernathy-Coyle, Kentucky's insider: you grade bloodlines? Sugar, I grade hooks. And your team's got a catchy one this year. I'll give you that.

Why I Love This Team
I love that a school that went 2-10 twice in three years just won 10 games. I love Sherrill's hands. I love that Coach Lea talks straight. And I love writing these songs, even the sad ones. Especially the sad ones. They're the best ones on the album.

stories.title: Now Listen Here: The SEC Race at the Turn
stories.text:
Now listen here. This is a brand-new kind of SEC season. It's the first year every school plays nine conference games, in one standings table with no divisions. Here's that table heading into the week. Georgia (6-1 overall) and Kentucky (6-1 overall) are 4-1 in league play. Tennessee (6-1 overall) and Ole Miss (5-1 overall) are 3-1 in league play. Alabama (5-2 overall) and Florida (5-2 overall) are 3-2 in league play. LSU (5-2 overall), Missouri (5-2 overall), Auburn (4-2 overall), and Mississippi State (4-2 overall) are 2-2 in league play. That order is sorted by record, not by the official tiebreakers, so don't go carving it in stone. Off the field, the league fined Tennessee $500,000 after fans stormed the field following the Vols' win over Alabama. Somebody near the top is going to stumble, and somebody in the middle is going to climb. That's the sermon.

report.title: "Orange You Glad It's Saturday?": Margery Vandermolen Welcomes the Ducks to Champaign
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good afternoon, class! Oh, sorry. Old habits. Welcome to The Cover Window, Illini Nation. I'm Margery Vandermolen, your Illinois insider, and I explain football the way your best-loved teacher explained long division: patiently, cheerfully and with a lot of charts. I'm a prairie-state numbers whiz. I've crunched the numbers on just about everything, and the numbers always say the same thing: orange. You'll get corn jokes from me. You'll get chart jokes. Sometimes you'll get a corn chart, which is both. And every Saturday morning I'll ask you the same question: "Orange you glad it's Saturday?" When something wonderful happens on the field, there's only one thing to say: "Oskee-wow-wow!" Each week I'll give you the players, the coaches and the matchup, explained clearly enough that Grandma and the grandkids can both follow along.

The School in 60 Seconds
Here's your history lesson, and yes, it will be on the test. Illinois is a founding member of the Big Ten and claims five national championships: 1914, 1919, 1923, 1927 and 1951. The 1923 title team opened Memorial Stadium and introduced the world to Harold "Red" Grange, the Galloping Ghost. On Oct. 18, 1924, at the stadium's dedication game, Grange scored four touchdowns against Michigan in the first 12 minutes. He ran for a fifth and threw for a sixth in a 39-14 win. ESPN once chose the legendary No. 77 as the greatest player in college football history. The stadium honors University of Illinois students who died in World War I. Illinois also claims 15 Big Ten titles. Gold stars all around.

The Coach and the Scheme
Bret Bielema was named the 26th head coach in Illinois history on Dec. 19, 2020. He's an Illinois native, and he said at the time, "Illinois and the Big Ten is home for me". One of his early wins was a nine-overtime victory at Penn State in 2021, the longest game in college football history. The 2026 numbers show an offense that does a little of everything: 31.8 points and 405.5 yards a game, with about 48% runs at 5.06 yards a carry. Illinois takes care of the ball, with only four turnovers lost all season. Here's the part of the chart I'd circle in red: the defense allows 27.8 points and 375.2 yards a game, and opponents have 248.3 passing yards a game. The pass rush has five sacks.

Players to Know
QB Katin Houser: 122 of 184 for 1,440 yards, 12 TD and 4 INT. He broke his left hand at Michigan State and will be out.
QB Michael Clayton II (freshman): came off the bench at Michigan State, threw two touchdowns and led the overtime win. He'll likely make his first career start on Saturday.
WR Collin Dixon: 47 catches, 608 yards and 9 touchdowns, third in FBS in receiving touchdowns. I'd like everyone to take a moment to admire that number.
RB Aidan Laughery: 391 yards on 62 carries.
Defense: LB James Kreutz has 34 tackles. DB Matthew Bailey returned an interception 88 yards for a touchdown and has 41 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Illinois is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big Ten, 2-2 at home and 1-1 on the road. The Illini are not ranked. They lost to Duke 31-27 and Purdue 24-17 at home, and 42-19 at Ohio State. A win over a ranked Oregon team at home would be the kind of result that rearranges a whole spreadsheet. Pardon me, a whole chart.

This Week: Oregon (4-2) at Illinois (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 2 p.m. CT (3 p.m. ET) · Gies Memorial Stadium · Big Ten Network · Military Appreciation and Foundation Weekend.
Last week: Illinois had a bye, coming off the 38-37 overtime win at Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon beat Nebraska 17-14 on Dylan Raiola's touchdown pass with 28 seconds left.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the tough homework assignment. Oregon allows only 3.25 yards a carry and 20.7 points a game, and it has nine interceptions. LB Matayo Uiagalelei has five sacks. A freshman quarterback will need help from our run game, which averages 5.06 a carry.
Their offense vs. our defense: Oregon throws for 283.3 yards a game. Its starting quarterback, Dante Moore, has missed two games with a concussion and has no announced return date. Raiola and Brock Thomas are competing to start.
Series: Oregon leads 3-1. The Ducks won the last meeting 38-9 in Eugene in 2024, and Illinois's only win came in 1970, 20-16.
Availability: Houser is out with a broken left hand. Oregon's last official report (Oct. 17) listed Moore, WR Evan Stewart, Aaron Flowers and Jeremiah McClellan out. I found no official report for this game as of Oct. 18, 2026.

report.title: "Bless Your Yards-Per-Play": Mallory Penhallow Takes the Hoosiers to the Big House
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well hello, Hoosier Nation, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Mallory Penhallow, former Miss Monroe County runner-up, and these days I run a 40-tab efficiency model on everything this football team does. I travel with the team, I live with the numbers, and yes, the clicker is rhinestone. My pageant answer to every question is the same: "It's the explosives, darling." Each week I give one opponent my honorary Miss Congeniality sash. It goes to whoever I roast the hardest, and I always do it with love. When we win, you get the full pageant wave. When we lose, it's "grace in defeat". and then I quietly open tab 41.

The School in 60 Seconds
Before Curt Cignetti showed up, Indiana had the most losses of any program in college football, 713 of them over 130-plus years. It had won three bowl games in its whole history, and the last one came in 1991. Then 2025 happened. The Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship. The last team to win 16 games without a loss was Yale in 1894. Quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman, and he scored the deciding touchdown himself on a 12-yard run on fourth-and-4. Cignetti's quote still sounds like an acceptance speech to me: "We won the national championship at Indiana University. It can be done."

The Coach and the Scheme
Cignetti was hired on Nov. 30, 2023. Part of his rebuild came from bringing 13 transfers with him from his old school, James Madison. The 2026 numbers show what this team is. On offense, Indiana averages 36.6 points and 449.3 yards a game. It runs for 5.67 yards a carry, and Josh Hoover has 18 touchdown passes with no interceptions. On defense, the Hoosiers allow 12.9 points a game, which ranks 4th in FBS. Opponents gain only 2.28 yards a carry, and Indiana has 24 sacks against 10 allowed. The team has lost just three turnovers all season and gives up 30.7 penalty yards a game, 3rd-fewest in FBS. Clean football is my love language.

Players to Know
QB Josh Hoover: 1,660 yards, 18 TD, 0 INT, 63.9% completions. Against Ohio State he landed on his right shoulder, missed one play and came back. I found no official status for Saturday as of Oct. 18.
RB Turbo Richard: 643 yards on 87 carries, 6 TD. RB Lee Beebe: 575 yards on 107 carries, 4 TD.
WR Charlie Becker: 39 catches, 694 yards, 8 TD, including 9 for 165 against Ohio State. WR Nick Marsh: 32 catches, 585 yards, 7 TD.
Tobi Osunsanmi (sack leader): 7 sacks, 11.5 tackles for loss. Isaiah Jones: a team-high 51 tackles. Amare Ferrell: team-high 2 INT, with an interception against Ohio State.

The Conference Picture
Indiana is 6-1 overall and 3-1 in the Big Ten, and 2-0 on the road. The Hoosiers dropped from No. 5 to No. 6 in the AP poll after losing 19-15 to Ohio State, which ended a 22-game winning streak and Cignetti's 19-game unbeaten run at home. In Cignetti's words: "We can accomplish anything we want, all of our goals, except going undefeated."

This Week: No. 6 Indiana (6-1) at Michigan (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor · FOX. The game is sold out, and it's Michigan's Block Cancer Game and Parents Weekend.
Last week: Indiana lost 19-15 to Ohio State. On the last play, Marsh caught a fourth-and-4 pass but couldn't get his left foot down inbounds. The defense held the Buckeyes to 313 yards, only 78 of them on the ground. Michigan beat Penn State 21-18 after true freshman Tommy Carr replaced Bryce Underwood at halftime.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is a real test. Michigan allows 256.5 yards a game, 3rd in FBS, and 89.7 rushing yards a game, 13th. Indiana has also been held under 75 rushing yards in each of its last two games.
Their offense vs. our defense: Michigan averages 22.7 points a game (105th) and 165.7 passing yards (125th). The Wolverines have lost 11 turnovers and are minus-3 in turnover margin, while Indiana is plus-3.
Series: Michigan leads 62-11. Indiana won the last meeting, 20-15 in Bloomington in 2024, and the teams did not play in 2025.

What decides it: (1) How healthy Hoover is and how well he throws. (2) Whether Indiana's run game can do anything against Michigan's front. (3) Who plays quarterback for Michigan, which Kyle Whittingham may not announce before kickoff.
And yes, Gus Hartwell, Michigan's very charming insider, I'm holding the Miss Congeniality sash for you. With love.
