report.title: "A Good Punt Is a Love Letter to Your Defense": Orrin Kalvelage Heads North for the Pig
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hello, neighbors. I'm Orrin Kalvelage, your Iowa insider at The Cover Window. I grew up on a farm near Iowa City and haven't missed a home opener in my life. I own one black-and-gold sweater, and I wear it with pride every single week. My wife says it needs retiring. I say it's undefeated in October.

I'm gentle and I'm stubborn, and I'm wildly proud of defense and special teams. I believe a good punt is a love letter to your defense. Here's my pledge: every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you plainly. I celebrate our players as young men first, I respect every opponent, and I give thanks to God for honest work and honest football. Go Hawks.

The School in 60 Seconds

Iowa joined the conference that became the Big Ten in 1899 and played its first league season in 1900. The Hawkeyes play at Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, capacity 69,250. They've won 13 conference championships, including 11 in the Big Ten. Iowa has been ranked No. 1 in the AP and Coaches polls 15 times.

The last five seasons are steady as a fence post: 10-4, 8-5, 10-4, 8-5 and 9-4. That's Iowa football. You know what you're getting, and what you're getting is tough.

The Coach and the Scheme

Kirk Ferentz is in his 28th season as head coach, the longest current tenure in FBS. He's led Iowa since 1999. He's the Big Ten's all-time leader in wins. Before Iowa he was head coach at Maine from 1990 to 1992 and an assistant with the Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens. He played linebacker at UConn.

This year's defense is pure Iowa. It allows 293.3 yards per game (22nd in FBS) and just 14.5 points (8th). The run defense allows 84.7 yards per game, 7th in FBS. At Washington it held the Huskies to minus-3 rushing yards, with six sacks and nine tackles for loss. That's a defense built in a barn.

The offense runs for 194.0 yards per game (36th) and scores 31.0 points (61st). The passing game sits at 209.2 yards per game (93rd). Third downs convert at 39.4% (80th), and the red-zone offense ranks 36th at 89.5%.

Players to Know

QB Hank Brown: the season passing leader with 832 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. AP reported he was injured and didn't start at Washington. His status for Saturday is unknown.
QB Jeremy Hecklinski: started at Washington and went 14 of 19 for 202 yards and three touchdowns. Steady as you like.
RB Kamari Moulton: 519 yards on 76 carries and four touchdowns. At Washington he ran 26 times for a career-high 208 yards, including a 56-yard touchdown. That came a week after Ohio State held him to 27 yards. He said he had "a chip on my shoulder".
TE DJ Vonnahme: two touchdown catches at Washington, from 20 and 27 yards.
WR Tony Diaz: team-best 28 catches for 329 yards.
K Caden Buhr: field goals of 51 and 27 yards at Washington. A man after my own heart.
Cam Buffington: team-high 52 tackles.
Joseph Anderson: team-high three sacks.

The Conference Picture

Iowa is 5-1 overall and 2-1 in the Big Ten. The Hawkeyes are No. 15 in the AP poll and No. 14 in the Coaches poll. They're 3-1 at home and 2-0 on the road. The wins: 40-0 over Northern Illinois, 16-13 over Iowa State, 55-0 over Northern Iowa, 20-19 at Michigan and 41-24 at Washington. The only loss was 31-14 to Ohio State.

The win at Washington was Iowa's first in the Pacific Time Zone since the 2019 Holiday Bowl. Next come Wisconsin at home, Northwestern on the road, Purdue at home, Illinois on the road and Nebraska at home.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

No. 15 Iowa (5-1) at Minnesota (4-2) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET · Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis · FS1

Last time out. Iowa beat Washington 41-24 on Friday, Oct. 9, then had an open week. Minnesota lost 41-13 at Purdue on Oct. 10.

Iowa's offense vs. Minnesota's defense. Minnesota's defense is stout. It allows 288.8 yards per game (18th) and 159.7 passing yards (9th). Opponents convert 30.9% of third downs (17th). But the Gophers' red-zone defense ranks 102nd, allowing scores on 88.9% of trips. Run with Moulton, get inside the 20 and finish.

Minnesota's offense vs. Iowa's defense. Minnesota runs for 104.8 yards per game, 129th. Against Purdue it managed 25 rushing yards on 12 carries. Against our 7th-ranked run defense, that's a tough row to hoe. Drake Lindsey has 1,335 passing yards and nine touchdowns, and Javon Tracy has 32 catches. Our pass defense ranks 68th, so that's where Minnesota will try us. Minnesota holds the ball 32:47 per game (22nd), and Iowa 28:36 (104th).

Series. The winner takes home Floyd of Rosedale, a bronze pig trophy introduced in 1935. CFBD shows Iowa 9-1 against Minnesota from 2016 to 2025. Last year Iowa won 41-3. A TV station's summary lists Minnesota ahead 63-54-2 all-time and Iowa ahead 46-43-2 in trophy games. I'll call those figures thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. Hank Brown's status is unknown after his injury.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Who plays quarterback, and can he keep the ball safe?
2. Can Iowa's run defense keep Minnesota one-dimensional?
3. Can the Hawkeyes cash in against Minnesota's 102nd-ranked red-zone defense?

Local Flavor

It's a road trip north to Minneapolis for the pig. Late-October weather up there can turn, so bring the warm sweater. I'm bringing my one sweater. Be kind to the Gopher fans; they're good Midwestern folks like us. Not an ad. Go Hawks.

report.title: "Crack it open: Old Bay on that stat": Abigail 'Abby' Chesapeake Takes the Open Week
report.byline: Our insider (archetype: glam crab-feast queen) introduces the Maryland Terrapins during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Abigail 'Abby' Chesapeake · Maryland Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Crack it open: Old Bay on that stat! I'm Abigail 'Abby' Chesapeake, and I'm your Maryland insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a dC-suburb lobbyist type who networks with every coordinator and cracks crabs on air. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. Fair warning about my habit: old Bay is her universal answer to every problem. On the podcast, my segment is called Old Bay Index. The show card describes it like this: seasons each stat to taste. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Terrapins have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is SECU Stadium in College Park, MD, built in 1950 with a listed capacity of 51,802. The fight song is "Maryland Victory Song; Maryland Fight Song (Played after scoring a touchdown)", per Wikipedia. The band is the Mighty Sound of Maryland, per Wikipedia. The program claims national titles from 1953, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 7-6, 8-5, 8-5, 4-8 and 4-8, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Indiana (4-6 in 10 meetings), Rutgers (6-4 in 10 meetings), Penn State (1-8 in 9 meetings), Michigan State (3-6 in 9 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 43 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about Testudo; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Mike Locksley leads the Terrapins; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 4, 2018. Through 7 games, Maryland scores 28.3 points a game and allows 33.3. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 43% of its plays, gaining 133.0 rushing yards and 244.7 passing yards a game. That's a team that wants to throw it around. On third down, Maryland converts 33.7% of the time and opponents convert 42.4%. The defense has 17 sacks and 36 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 7 giveaways against 10 takeaways. Penalties cost 63.6 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 62 points against Hampton on Sept. 6, 2026, and 1 of the 7 games was decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, opponents have outscored Maryland by a combined 35 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB Malik Washington (passing leader): 155/261, 1615 yards, 9 TD, 6 INT.
RB DeJuan Williams (rushing leader): 38 carries, 281 yards, 3 TD.
WR Chris Durr Jr. (receiving leader): 52 catches, 580 yards, 4 TD.
On defense, LB Daniel Wingate leads with 44 tackles; LB Zion Elee has 3.5 sacks; DB Jamare Glasker has 2 interceptions.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Maryland is 2-5 overall, 1-3 at home and 1-2 away. In Big Ten play the Terrapins are 0-4, which sorts them No. 17 of 18 by record. Ohio State sits on top at 4-0 in league games. Right around us: Penn State (0-4) and Michigan State (0-4). The top of the table: Ohio State (4-0), UCLA (4-0), Indiana (3-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Maryland this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Terrapins lost to Rutgers at home, 37-30. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, vs. Illinois, in SECU Stadium, College Park, with a kickoff time to be announced. Illinois comes in at 3-3. After that, CFBD lists at Purdue (Nov. 7), vs. Wisconsin (Nov. 14), at USC (Nov. 21), vs. Penn State (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Terrapins come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. He spent 21 seasons as Utah's head coach, went 177-88 there, and had eight seasons with 10 or more wins. Our offense vs. their defense: this is the hard part. Indiana allows 12.9 points a game (4th in FBS) and 75.4 rushing yards a game (4th). It has 24 sacks, seven of them by Tobi Osunsanmi.
Their offense vs. our defense: Indiana scores 36.6 points a game, and Josh Hoover hasn't thrown an interception. Michigan's pass defense ranks 14th. Hoover hurt his right shoulder against Ohio State. He missed one play and finished the game. I found no official update as of Oct. 18.
Series: Michigan leads 62-11, but Indiana won the last meeting, 20-15 in 2024. The teams did not play in 2025.
What decides it: (1) Who plays quarterback, and whether Michigan can stop losing the ball. (2) Michigan's red-zone defense, which has allowed scores on 92.9% of opponent trips (118th). (3) Whether Michigan's run defense can keep Indiana's ground game quiet for a third straight week.

report.title: "Framed It. Strike Three.": Shay Kowalczyk Calls the Pitches for Michigan State at No. 9 UCLA
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hey, Spartans. I'm Shay Kowalczyk, your Michigan State insider at The Cover Window. I caught softball in the East Lansing area for years, and I still frame every defensive call like a pitch sequence. Fastball inside, change-up away, and then you get 'em. I travel and live with this team. I also maintain that Ann Arbor is just a suburb with a stadium. That's not a stat. That's a lifestyle.

Here's my deal. I'm blunt and honest, and every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll say I'm still waiting on the sign from the dugout. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I give thanks to God for every chance to compete. Green and white, all day.

The School in 60 Seconds

Michigan State claims six national championships, including two from the major wire services in 1952 and 1965. The Spartans have won eleven conference titles, nine of them in the Big Ten. Home is Spartan Stadium on the main campus, regularly among the top 25 in NCAA attendance. CFBD lists it at 75,005 seats.

The last five seasons: a great 11-2 in 2021, then 5-7, 4-8, 5-7 and 4-8. We're in a slump at the plate. Every great hitter has one. What matters is the next at-bat.

The Coach and the Scheme

Pat Fitzgerald is in his first season as head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 1, 2025. He was head coach at Northwestern from 2006 to 2023. He took that job at 31, the youngest head coach in the Big Ten and FBS at the time. As a Northwestern linebacker, he won the Bronko Nagurski Trophy and Chuck Bednarik Award twice each. He's in the College Football Hall of Fame.

The discipline numbers show his touch. Michigan State averages just 36.3 penalty yards per game, 7th in FBS. The defense allows 342.6 yards per game (56th) and 25.4 points (82nd). AP lists MSU's red-zone defense at 135th. That's where pitches are catching too much plate.

The offense is the slump. MSU gains 310.7 yards per game (128th) and scores 21.3 points (113th). It throws for 191.6 yards (107th) and runs for 119.1 (119th). It converts 40.2% of third downs (77th). MSU is -5 in turnover margin, 122nd.

Players to Know

QB Alessio Milivojevic: 1,263 yards, seven touchdowns, three interceptions, 65.4% completions. Against Northwestern he went 19 of 30 for 216 yards and two touchdowns, plus a 3-yard touchdown run on fourth-and-1.
WR Chrishon McCray: caught a 53-yard touchdown against Northwestern.
WR Bryson Williams: caught a 32-yard touchdown just before halftime against Northwestern.
WR Jayden Savoury: team-best 27 catches for 261 yards.
RB Jaziun Patterson: 327 yards on 76 carries and five touchdowns. He ran 15 times for 72 yards against Northwestern.
Eli Coenen: team-high 3.5 sacks, plus a blocked field goal against Northwestern. Framed it.
Devin Vaught: team-high 46 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Michigan State is 2-5 overall and 0-4 in the Big Ten. The Spartans beat Toledo 30-20 and Eastern Michigan 35-7. Then came five straight losses: 27-10 at Notre Dame, 31-13 to Nebraska, 31-3 at Wisconsin, 38-37 in overtime to Illinois and 24-21 to Northwestern.

Those last two hurt. Illinois won when MSU's 2-point try failed in overtime, and Northwestern won on a field goal with two seconds left. Fitzgerald said the staff has to "coach better to get over the hump". After UCLA, MSU has an open week, then plays at Michigan, hosts Washington and Oregon, and finishes at Rutgers.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Michigan State (2-5) at No. 9 UCLA (6-0) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET · Rose Bowl, Pasadena, Calif. · CBS

Last time out. Michigan State lost 24-21 to Northwestern on Oct. 17. MSU led 21-13 early in the fourth quarter before Northwestern tied it, blocked a Spartan field goal and kicked the winner. UCLA beat Wisconsin 17-7 the same night.

MSU's offense vs. UCLA's defense. This is a tough count. UCLA allows 292.3 yards per game (20th) and 16.2 points (21st). Opponents convert only 25.9% of third downs against the Bruins, 3rd in FBS. UCLA is +10 in turnover margin, 5th. So Milivojevic has to protect the ball and win early downs. UCLA's pass defense (47th) is a bit more hittable than its run defense (20th).

UCLA's offense vs. MSU's defense. UCLA runs for 231 yards per game, 12th in FBS. Wayne Knight has 571 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns, with a rushing score in all six games. Starter Nico Iamaleava hurt his leg at Oregon and missed the Wisconsin game. Backup Ty Dieffenbach went 22 of 33 for 264 yards in his first start. Our advantage here is discipline: UCLA averages 83.2 penalty yards per game, 133rd.

Series. UCLA leads the all-time series 4-3, per both schools' history pages. Three meetings came in the Rose Bowl game itself: MSU won 28-20 in 1954 and 17-14 in 1956, and UCLA won 14-12 in 1966. Treat those details as thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. Iamaleava's status is unknown.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can MSU protect the ball against UCLA's +10 turnover margin?
2. Can the Spartans move the chains against the No. 3 third-down defense?
3. Can MSU's discipline turn UCLA penalties into points?

Local Flavor

The Rose Bowl is a bucket-list stop for any Spartan, and we've won there before. Wear your green with pride and be a gracious guest. I'll share confirmed tips for traveling fans before kickoff. Not an ad. Green and white, all day.

report.title: "Ski-U-Mah!": Tor Engebretsen Wants Floyd of Rosedale Back in Minneapolis
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Well, hello there. I'm Torvald Engebretsen, Tor to my friends, and I'm your Minnesota insider at The Cover Window. I grew up in Minneapolis ice-fishing with my grandpa, and I know the history of every rivalry trophy this program plays for. Minnesota has more trophies than I have winter coats, and I have a lot of winter coats.

I'm dry, I'm earnest and I'm polite, but get me started on rivalry lore and I'm unstoppable. Here's my promise: every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you so. I celebrate our players as young people first, I respect every opponent, even the ones from south of the border, and I thank God for crisp autumn Saturdays. Cold enough for ya? Good.

The School in 60 Seconds

Minnesota started playing football in 1882 and has been in the Big Ten since the league began in 1896 as the Western Conference. The Golden Gophers claim seven national championships. Four of them, in 1936, 1940, 1941 and 1960, came from the major wire-service polls. Since 2009, home has been Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. CFBD lists 50,850 seats.

The last five seasons have been sturdy: 9-4, 9-4, 6-7, 8-5 and 8-5. Four winning seasons in five years. My grandpa would call that a good catch.

The Coach and the Scheme

P.J. Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017. CFBD lists his hire date as Jan. 6, 2017. He coached Western Michigan from 2013 to 2016. He played receiver at Northern Illinois and spent time with the San Francisco 49ers. He was a receivers coach at Northern Illinois, Rutgers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In 2019 he led the Gophers to one of their best seasons in half a century.

This year's defense is the strength. Minnesota allows 288.8 yards per game (18th in FBS) and 159.7 passing yards (9th). Opponents convert 30.9% of third downs, 17th. The red-zone defense is the soft spot, ranking 102nd at 88.9%.

The offense throws for 236.5 yards per game (61st) and scores 28.8 points (73rd). The run game is the worry, at 104.8 yards per game (129th). The Gophers control the clock well, though, at 32:47 per game (22nd).

Players to Know

QB Drake Lindsey: 1,335 yards, nine touchdowns, five interceptions, 64.8% completions. At Purdue he threw for 248 yards on 22-of-39 passing with a touchdown and an interception.
WR Javon Tracy: team-best 32 catches for 375 yards and a touchdown.
WR Jalen Smith: three catches for 89 yards at Purdue, including a 42-yard touchdown.
RB TJ Thomas Jr.: the leading rusher. AP lists 319 yards on 52 carries and ESPN 317 on 51, a tiny conflict.
RB Darius Taylor: seven catches for 51 yards at Purdue.
K Luke Drzewiecki: a 49-yard field goal at Purdue.
TJ Bush Jr.: team-high four sacks.
Maverick Baranowski: team-high 45 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Minnesota is 4-2 overall and 2-1 in the Big Ten. The Gophers are 3-1 at home and 1-1 on the road. They beat Eastern Illinois 59-7, lost 38-13 to Mississippi State and beat Akron 41-7. Then came two big Big Ten wins: 27-24 at Washington and 20-14 over Michigan. The 41-13 loss at Purdue followed.

The road ahead is steep, like a ski hill in January. After Iowa come Indiana on the road, UCLA at home, Penn State on the road, Northwestern at home and Wisconsin on the road. A home win Saturday would mean a lot.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

No. 15 Iowa (5-1) at Minnesota (4-2) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET · Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis · FS1

Last time out. Minnesota lost 41-13 at Purdue on Oct. 10. Fleck called it a game where Purdue "dominated the game in pretty much every facet". Both teams then had an open week. Iowa beat Washington 41-24 on Oct. 9.

Minnesota's offense vs. Iowa's defense. This is the hard part. Iowa allows 14.5 points per game (8th) and 84.7 rushing yards (7th). At Washington, Iowa held the Huskies to minus-3 rushing yards and had six sacks. Our run game managed 25 yards on 12 carries at Purdue. So Lindsey and the receivers will carry the load. Iowa's pass defense ranks 68th, which is the opening.

Iowa's offense vs. Minnesota's defense. Our pass defense ranks 9th. Iowa's passing game ranks 93rd, and quarterback Hank Brown missed the Washington game with an injury. Jeremy Hecklinski threw three touchdowns in his place. Kamari Moulton ran for 208 yards at Washington, so stopping the run is job one. Our red-zone defense (102nd) needs to hold up.

Series. The winner gets Floyd of Rosedale, a bronze pig trophy introduced in 1935. I could talk about that pig all afternoon. CFBD shows Iowa 9-1 against us from 2016 to 2025, and Iowa won 41-3 last year. A TV station's summary lists Minnesota ahead 63-54-2 all-time. That figure is thin, but it's history worth remembering.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Minnesota injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Minnesota run at all against Iowa's 7th-ranked run defense?
2. Can the Gophers' red-zone defense hold up?
3. Can Minnesota bounce back from the Purdue loss with an open week behind it?

Orrin, the Iowa insider, wears one sweater every week. I respect a man with commitment, and I own enough coats to lend him one.

Local Flavor

The pig is up for grabs, and this one's at home. Bundle up, bring a thermos of hot cocoa and greet the Iowa fans politely. They drove a long way. I'll share confirmed pregame spots before kickoff. Not an ad. Ski-U-Mah!

report.title: "Go Big Red": Darla Rasmussen Takes the Open Week
report.byline: Our insider (archetype: corn-country farm-girl jock) introduces the Nebraska Cornhuskers during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Darla Rasmussen · Nebraska Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Go Big Red! I'm Darla Rasmussen, and I'm your Nebraska insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm an ex-Husker volleyballer and farm girl who sells out every argument. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. Fair warning about my habit: mentions the sellout streak every segment. On the podcast, my segment is called Sellout Report. The show card describes it like this: the sellout streak bit, every segment. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Cornhuskers have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Memorial Stadium (Lincoln, NE) in Lincoln, NE, built in 1923 with a listed capacity of 85,458. The fight song is "Hail Varsity", per Wikipedia. The band is the Cornhusker Marching Band, per Wikipedia. The program claims national titles from 1970, 1971, 1994, 1995, 1997, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 3-9, 4-8, 5-7, 7-6 and 7-6, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Iowa (1-9 in 10 meetings), Northwestern (5-4 in 9 meetings), Illinois (5-4 in 9 meetings), Purdue (5-4 in 9 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 88 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about the sellout streak; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Matt Rhule leads the Cornhuskers; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Nov. 26, 2022. Through 7 games, Nebraska scores 35.6 points a game and allows 15.4. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 54% of its plays, gaining 194.4 rushing yards and 235.7 passing yards a game. That's a balanced menu. On third down, Nebraska converts 50.5% of the time and opponents convert 19.3%. The defense has 19 sacks and 47 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 4 giveaways against 10 takeaways. Penalties cost 68.7 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 56 points against Bowling Green on Sept. 12, 2026, and 2 of the 7 games were decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, Nebraska has outscored opponents by a combined 141 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB Anthony Colandrea (passing leader): 137/219, 1570 yards, 14 TD, 4 INT.
RB Jamal Rule (rushing leader): 60 carries, 391 yards, 5 TD.
WR Kwazi Gilmer (receiving leader): 38 catches, 492 yards, 7 TD.
On defense, LB Owen Chambliss leads with 46 tackles; DL Jahsear Whittington has 3.5 sacks; DB Dwayne McDougle III has 2 interceptions.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Nebraska is 5-2 overall, 4-1 at home and 1-1 away. In Big Ten play the Cornhuskers are 2-2, which sorts them No. 10 of 18 by record. Ohio State sits on top at 4-0 in league games. Right around us: Wisconsin (2-1) and Purdue (2-2). The top of the table: Ohio State (4-0), UCLA (4-0), Indiana (3-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Nebraska this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Cornhuskers lost to Oregon on the road, 17-14. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, vs. Washington, in Memorial Stadium, Lincoln, with a kickoff time to be announced. Washington comes in at 4-3. After that, CFBD lists at Illinois (Nov. 6), at Rutgers (Nov. 14), vs. Ohio State (Nov. 21), at Iowa (Nov. 27). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Cornhuskers come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Go Big Red!

report.title: "Footnote: I Was Right": Ezra Lindqvist Welcomes Rutgers to the New Ryan Field
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, Wildcats, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Ezra Lindqvist, your Northwestern insider. I'm a data journalist by training, which means I fact-check the coaches in real time. Politely. Mostly politely. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I'm fully aware that I'm doing the "smartest kid in the Big Ten" bit. I footnote my own jokes¹, and then I footnote the footnotes². When we win, I publish a formal correction to everyone who doubted us. When we lose, I file a 2,000-word investigative piece on the punter. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, sourced and double-checked. My motto: "Footnote: I was right."
¹ This one. ² Also this one.

The School in 60 Seconds
The headline this season is home. Northwestern opened 2026 with two games at Martin Stadium, right on the shore of Lake Michigan, and then opened the brand-new Ryan Field against Penn State on Oct. 2. Northwestern won that one 34-13. Correction to my earlier draft: there was no earlier draft. Northwestern has won all four of its home games this season. The coach is David Braun, who became interim coach in 2023, was named the permanent head coach on Nov. 15 of that year and was the consensus Big Ten Coach of the Year. Footnote: that's a very good first season.

The Coach and the Scheme
Braun's start date in the coaching database is July 10, 2023. The 2026 numbers say Northwestern runs the ball and protects it. It runs on about 62% of its plays for 191.5 yards a game (39th in FBS), with 14 rushing touchdowns. It averages 33.5 points a game. And here's the headline stat: Northwestern has lost only two turnovers all season. Its plus-7 turnover margin ranks eighth in FBS. In the red zone the Wildcats score 96.4% of the time, fourth in FBS. The defense allows 17.0 points a game (26th), but 230.5 passing yards a game ranks 100th. Correction requested. Two more items for the record: the pass rush has 9 sacks, and the protection has allowed 14. Opponents average 4.27 yards a carry against us. I'm filing that under "areas for improvement," with a footnote noting how good everything else has been.

Players to Know
QB Aidan Chiles: 1,398 yards, 9 TD, 0 INT and 70.5% completions. Against Michigan State he went 18 of 27 for 226 yards and ran for a touchdown.
RB Caleb Komolafe: 401 yards and 4 TD on 75 carries. Against MSU: 67 rushing yards, a touchdown and four catches for 51 yards.
WR Griffin Wilde: 30 catches, 482 yards, 3 TD.
K Jackson Kleather: three field goals against Michigan State, including the 34-yard winner with two seconds left.
Matthew Smith: blocked a Michigan State field-goal try late.

The Conference Picture
Northwestern is 5-1 overall and 2-1 in the Big Ten, 4-0 at home and 1-1 on the road. The Wildcats are No. 24 in the AP poll and No. 23 in the Coaches Poll. The only loss was 29-23 at Indiana. Next week is a trip to Oregon, so footnote this: winning this week matters. Holding serve at home before going to Eugene puts Northwestern in good shape for the second half of the season. Data journalism suggests momentum is mostly a myth. Data journalism has never been to a Northwestern pep rally.

This Week: Rutgers (2-4) at No. 24 Northwestern (5-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 11 a.m. CT (noon ET) · Ryan Field, Evanston · Peacock.
Last week: Northwestern won 24-21 at Michigan State. Rutgers came back from 23-13 down at halftime to win 37-30 at Maryland.
Our offense vs. their defense: Rutgers allows 185.2 rushing yards a game (118th) and 31.8 points (119th). Our run game should have room.
Their offense vs. our defense: Rutgers throws for 265.8 yards a game, and our pass defense ranks 100th. WR K.J. Duff has 741 yards and 9 TDs. That's the matchup I'd circle, and I'd footnote it too.
Series: a full series record wasn't in a free source I could verify. I won't guess. You knew that.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 9 sacks and has allowed 14, with 9 takeaways against 2 giveaways, and it has 14 rushing and 9 passing touchdowns.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our run game control the clock? (2) Can our secondary keep up with Duff? (3) Turnovers. We're plus-7, Rutgers is minus-5. One fact for balance: Rutgers is the least penalized team in FBS.
And to Vinny Scolari, Rutgers's insider: a warm Evanston welcome. I've prepared directions from Exit 9. They are 47 footnotes long.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Evanston? Le Peep on Church Street for a game-day breakfast. Footnote: the pancakes are excellent.

report.title: "Uniform of the Week? Ten Out of Ten": Nix Wyatt-Aldana Takes the Ducks to Champaign
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hey, Duck fans, welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Phoenix Wyatt-Aldana, but please call me Nix. I'm a sneaker-and-uniform designer from Eugene, which means I review jerseys and route trees with exactly the same ferocity. A slant with sloppy footwork? That's a wrinkled hem, darling. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and before I analyze anybody, I rate their uniform. It's the law. My catchphrase is "Uniform of the week? Ten out of ten." When we win, the review reads "10 out of 10, uniform AND execution." When we lose, I review it like a runway show where somebody tripped in the wrong shoes: honest, kind and very detailed. Each week you get the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a little sparkle.

The School in 60 Seconds
Oregon has played football since 1894. Autzen Stadium opened in 1967 and is listed at 54,000 seats, though anyone who's been inside knows it sounds much bigger. In 2014 quarterback Marcus Mariota became Oregon's first Heisman Trophy winner, after throwing for 4,454 yards and 42 touchdowns. He finished with the second-most points of any Heisman winner, behind only O.J. Simpson. The Ducks moved to the Big Ten in 2024 and won the league right away: 13-1 overall and 9-0 in conference play. Last year they went 13-2 and 8-1 in the league. Two straight seasons of runway-ready football.

The Coach and the Scheme
Dan Lanning was hired on Dec. 11, 2021. His 2024 team went 9-0 in the Big Ten and won the title, and Ducks Wire notes he has never lost a Big Ten road game. In 2026 the offense throws the ball well: 283.3 passing yards a game and 16 passing touchdowns, with an even split between runs and passes (about 48% runs). Oregon averages 37.0 points and 420.3 yards a game. The defense allows 20.7 points and only 3.25 yards a carry, and it has intercepted nine passes. One thing to tailor: Oregon has lost 11 turnovers and forced 11. That's a perfectly even hem, but I want it tucked.

Players to Know
QB Dante Moore: 69 of 99 for 926 yards, 9 TD and no interceptions in four games, with a 178.27 rating. He suffered a concussion at USC on Sept. 26. His MRI and CT scans were clean, but he was listed OUT on every Big Ten availability report for UCLA and Nebraska. Oregon has not announced a return date.
QB Dylan Raiola: 515 yards, 6 TD, 2 INT this season. Against Nebraska, his former team, he came in with Oregon down 14-6 and threw the winning 4-yard touchdown to TE Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds left. QB Brock Thomas started that game and went 9 of 20 for 54 yards. Lanning said the two will keep competing in practice.
RB Jordon Davison: 301 yards and 6 TD on 62 carries.
WR Evan Stewart: 27 catches, 352 yards, 4 TD. He was listed out on the Oct. 17 report.
Defense: LB Matayo Uiagalelei has 5 sacks, DB Jett Washington has 2 interceptions, and DB Koi Perich has 34 tackles and 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Oregon is 4-2 overall and 2-1 in the Big Ten, 3-1 at home and 1-1 on the road. The Ducks are No. 25 in this week's Coaches Poll. The losses came at Oklahoma State, 39-31, and at home to UCLA, 17-15. With a road trip this week and Northwestern next, this is a stretch where the outfit has to come together.

This Week: Oregon (4-2) at Illinois (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3 p.m. ET (noon PT) · Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign · Big Ten Network. It's only Oregon's third visit to Illinois, and the first since 1993.
Last week: Oregon beat Nebraska 17-14 with two fourth-quarter scoring drives. Illinois had a bye after winning 38-37 in overtime at Michigan State on Oct. 10.
Our offense vs. their defense: Illinois allows 27.8 points and 375.2 yards a game, and 248.3 passing yards. Whoever plays quarterback for us should have chances through the air.
Their offense vs. our defense: Illinois averages 31.8 points and runs for 5.06 yards a carry. WR Collin Dixon has 47 catches, 608 yards and 9 touchdowns, which ranks third in FBS in receiving touchdowns. Starting QB Katin Houser broke his left hand at Michigan State, and freshman Michael Clayton II will likely make his first career start.
Series: Oregon leads 3-1 and won the last meeting 38-9 at Autzen in 2024.
Availability: On Oregon's last official report (Oct. 17), Aaron Flowers, Dante Moore, Evan Stewart and Jeremiah McClellan were out and Dave Iuli was a game-time decision. The first report for this game comes out during game week. Illinois: Houser is out with the broken hand. I found no other official Illinois report as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Who plays quarterback for us: Moore, Raiola or Thomas. (2) Can our secondary stay with Dixon? (3) How a freshman QB handles his first start against a defense allowing 3.25 yards a carry.
And to Margery Vandermolen, Illinois's insider: your orange is gorgeous this time of year. I'm giving the Illini uniforms a sincere nine. The tenth point is reserved for us.

Watching in Eugene? The Big Dirty on Olive Street does a game-day burger worthy of a runway.

report.title: "Exit 9 Never Lies": Vinny Scolari Takes the Scarlet Knights to Evanston
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Yo, Rutgers! How you doin'? Welcome to The Cover Window! Vinny Scolari here, your Rutgers insider, born and raised off Exit 9 of the New Jersey Turnpike. I give directions by Turnpike exit for everything, and I mean everything. Where's the stadium? Exit 9. How am I feeling after a loss? Somewhere around Exit 7A. I grade every Big Ten trench battle like a boardwalk arm-wrestle: who leaned in, who flinched, who walked away with the stuffed animal. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I order a sub big enough for the whole studio. Six feet. Everybody eats. When we lose, I say "Fuhgeddaboudit". and then I can't. I really can't. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, Jersey-style. "Exit 9 never lies."

The School in 60 Seconds
Here's something every college football fan should know. The very first college football game was played right in New Brunswick on Nov. 6, 1869, and Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4. That's right: the birthplace of the whole sport is off Exit 9. Home now is SHI Stadium in Piscataway, listed at 52,454. The man running the show is Greg Schiano, who came back to coach Rutgers again in December 2019. The Scarlet Knights play in the Big Ten, and every week is a heavyweight fight.

The Coach and the Scheme
Schiano's second stint began with his return on Nov. 30, 2019. The 2026 numbers say this offense can sling it: 265.8 passing yards a game (35th in FBS) and 16 passing touchdowns. Rutgers averages 31.2 points and 403.3 yards a game. And here's a stat I'll yell from the top of the Driscoll Bridge: Rutgers is the least penalized team in FBS, at 28.7 penalty yards a game. Discipline, baby. The defense, though, needs some fixing. It allows 31.8 points a game (119th) and 185.2 rushing yards (118th). Turnovers are a problem too, at minus-5 (122nd).

Players to Know
WR K.J. Duff: 42 catches, 741 yards and 9 TD. At Maryland he had 9 catches for 113 yards and two touchdowns, including a catch AP called incredible. The man's a Turnpike express lane.
QB Dylan Lonergan: 1,066 yards, 10 TD, 6 INT. He went 23 of 35 for 291 yards and three touchdowns at Maryland.
RB Antwan Raymond: 498 yards and 5 TD on 105 carries.
RB Clay Thevenin: 109 rushing yards and a touchdown at Maryland, plus a receiving TD.
I couldn't verify current defensive leaders from a free source, so I'm not guessing. Jersey guys are loud, not sloppy.

The Conference Picture
Rutgers is 2-4 overall and 1-2 in the Big Ten, 1-3 at home and 1-1 on the road. We're not ranked. The losses were to UMass, at Boston College, to USC (42-35) and to Indiana. We hung with USC until the end, losing by seven, and the Maryland comeback showed what this team's made of. On the ground we're at 3.78 yards a carry, and the protection has given up 14 sacks. If the big guys win their arm-wrestles, this offense can go the whole length of the Turnpike. Michigan comes to Piscataway next week, so this is a big two-week stretch.

This Week: Rutgers (2-4) at No. 24 Northwestern (5-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET (11 a.m. CT) · Ryan Field, Evanston · Peacock. The new Ryan Field opened this season.
Last week: Rutgers trailed Maryland 23-13 at halftime and came back to win 37-30. Northwestern beat Michigan State 24-21 on a 34-yard field goal with two seconds left.
Our offense vs. their defense: Northwestern allows just 17.0 points a game (26th), but its pass defense ranks 100th at 230.5 yards a game. Lonergan to Duff is our best punch.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the arm-wrestle I'm worried about. Northwestern runs on about 62% of its plays for 191.5 yards a game. Our run defense allows 185.2 a game. QB Aidan Chiles hasn't thrown an interception all year, and Northwestern scores on 96.4% of red-zone trips (fourth).
Series: a full series record was not in a free source I could verify.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 9 sacks and has allowed 14, with 6 takeaways against 11 giveaways, and it has 9 rushing and 16 passing touchdowns.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our front stop Northwestern's run game? (2) Turnovers. They're plus-7 and we're minus-5. (3) Can Duff win his matchups against a pass defense ranked 100th?
And to Ezra Lindqvist, Northwestern's insider: I hear you footnote your own jokes. Here's one for you. Footnote: we came to win, pal. Exit 9 never lies.

report.title: "And. Scene.": Kenzie Rhee Pitches No. 9 UCLA's Next Episode Against Michigan State
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hello, darlings! I'm Kensington Rhee, Kenzie to everyone who matters, and I'm your UCLA insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Westwood film-school producer, I storyboard every drive, and I travel and live with this team. Every game is a movie pitch to me. This season's logline? "First-year coach, unbeaten team, backup quarterback steps into the spotlight." Honestly, I'd greenlight it.

Here's my promise. Glam, yes. Fiction, never. Every number in this report has a source, like a properly cleared script. If I don't know something, I'll say it's still in development. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I'm grateful to God for every sunny Saturday in Pasadena. And. scene.

The School in 60 Seconds

UCLA plays its home games at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena. CFBD lists 88,565 seats. The Bruins now play in the Big Ten. UCLA has been ranked in the AP top 10 at least once in every decade since the poll began in the 1930s. Under Red Sanders in the 1950s, UCLA won the 1954 Coaches' Poll national championship and three conference titles. Under Terry Donahue in the 1980s and 1990s, the Bruins went 151-74-8 with an NCAA-record eight straight bowl wins.

The recent box office: 8-4, 9-4, 8-5, then 5-7 and 3-9. Which makes this season's 6-0 start the comeback story of the year.

The Coach and the Scheme

Bob Chesney is the first-year head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 6, 2025. He's a Dickinson College graduate who has been head coach at Salve Regina, Assumption, Holy Cross and James Madison. At Holy Cross he won five straight Patriot League titles. Now he's the first UCLA coach to begin his tenure 6-0. That's a breakout debut.

The defense is the star of the ensemble. UCLA allows 292.3 yards per game (20th in FBS) and 16.2 points (21st). The run defense allows 97.7 yards per game (20th). Opponents convert only 25.9% of third downs, 3rd in FBS. UCLA is +10 in turnover margin, 5th.

The offense runs the show on the ground: 231 rushing yards per game, 12th in FBS. It scores 35.5 points per game (33rd) and holds the ball 34:01 per game, 4th. The blooper reel: 83.2 penalty yards per game, 133rd. We'll fix that in the edit bay.

Players to Know

QB Nico Iamaleava: 982 yards, four touchdowns, four interceptions. He injured his leg at Oregon and missed the Wisconsin game. His status for Saturday is unknown.
QB Ty Dieffenbach: went 22 of 33 for 264 yards in his first start as a Bruin. He spent two seasons at Pitt and then played at Cal Poly before coming to UCLA. He said, "It's another game, not making the moment too big". Star quality.
RB Wayne Knight: 571 yards on 84 carries and 11 touchdowns. He has a rushing touchdown in all six games. A franchise player.
RB Anthony Woods: eight carries for 39 yards and a touchdown against Wisconsin.
WR Semaj Morgan: team-best 24 catches for 313 yards and two touchdowns. He caught five passes for 84 yards against Wisconsin.
Sammy Omosigho: team-high three sacks, plus the fourth-down stop against Wisconsin that was upheld on review.
Jalen Woods: team-high 50 tackles.
K Mateen Bhaghani: a 24-yard field goal against Wisconsin.

The Conference Picture

UCLA is 6-0 overall and 4-0 in the Big Ten. The Bruins are No. 9 in the AP poll and No. 10 in the Coaches poll. That's 3-0 at home and 3-0 on the road. The wins: 45-24 at California, 28-10 over San Diego State, 52-38 over Purdue, 54-3 at Maryland, 17-15 at Oregon and 17-7 over Wisconsin. It's the program's first 6-0 start since 2022.

After Michigan State come Nevada at home, Minnesota on the road, Illinois at home, Michigan on the road and USC at home. Big finale energy.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Michigan State (2-5) at No. 9 UCLA (6-0) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 12:30 p.m. PT / 3:30 p.m. ET · Rose Bowl, Pasadena, Calif. · CBS

Last time out. UCLA beat Wisconsin 17-7 on Oct. 17 without Iamaleava. The opening drive went 16 plays and took 8:42, both season highs. Michigan State lost 24-21 to Northwestern the same day on a field goal with two seconds left.

UCLA's offense vs. MSU's defense. Michigan State allows 25.4 points per game (82nd) and 140.7 rushing yards (67th). AP ranks MSU's red-zone defense 135th. Knight's touchdown streak should get another episode. Whoever plays quarterback can lean on that ground game and our 34:01 possession average.

MSU's offense vs. UCLA's defense. MSU gains 310.7 yards per game (128th) and scores 21.3 points (113th). Alessio Milivojevic threw for 216 yards and two touchdowns against Northwestern. Our third-down defense (3rd) and +10 turnover margin are the plot twists MSU has to solve. One caution for our side: MSU is disciplined, at 36.3 penalty yards per game (7th), and we're 133rd.

Series. UCLA leads the all-time series 4-3, per both schools' history pages. Three of those meetings came in the Rose Bowl game: MSU won in 1954 and 1956, and UCLA won 14-12 in 1966. Treat those details as thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. Iamaleava's status is unknown after his leg injury.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Who starts at quarterback, Iamaleava or Dieffenbach?
2. Can Knight score a rushing touchdown for the seventh straight game?
3. Can UCLA cut down on its 83.2 penalty yards per game?

Shay, the Michigan State insider, frames every call like a softball pitch. I frame every play like a shot list. We'd make a great buddy comedy.

Local Flavor

It's a 12:30 p.m. Pacific kickoff at the Rose Bowl on CBS. Bring sunscreen, a picnic blanket and your best blue and gold. Welcome the Spartans fans warmly; they flew a long way. I'll share confirmed tips before kickoff. Not an ad. And. scene.

report.title: "In a World.": Sterling Ashworth-Vance Premieres the Trojans in Madison
report.byline: Our Hollywood film-buff historian introduces himself and previews No. 16 USC at Wisconsin.
report.text:
Sterling Ashworth-Vance · USC Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
In a world. where one team plays every Saturday like it's opening night. Good evening, I'm Sterling Ashworth-Vance, film buff, football historian and your guide to the Trojans. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, polished and presented in glorious widescreen. I treat every game like a premiere, because at USC, every game is one. The Coliseum is the grandest movie set in sports, and every fall our Trojans play the lead. Traveler gallops, the band strikes up, and Los Angeles remembers why it loves this team. When we win, the music swells and I say, "Roll credits." When we lose, I call it a second-act setback, because the best films always have one. Fight On!

The School in 60 Seconds
The Trojans were formed in 1888. The program has more than 860 wins and claims 11 national championships, seven of them from the AP and/or Coaches polls. USC has had 13 undefeated seasons, eight of them perfect. We now play in the Big Ten, at the 77,500-seat Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Exposition Park, right next to campus. CFBD dates the Coliseum to 1923. The last five seasons: 4-8, 11-3, 8-5, 7-6 in our first Big Ten year, and 9-4. A classic comeback arc.

The Coach and the Scheme
Lincoln Riley is the director's chair; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 28, 2021. His offense is a blockbuster: 310.1 passing yards a game (7th in FBS), 462.4 total yards (17th) and 36.4 points (27th). We convert 51.2% of third downs, 14th, and hold the ball 32:50 a game (21st). The defense stops the run, 111 yards allowed (32nd), with 15 sacks. The plot hole: the pass defense allows 239 yards a game, 109th, and opponents score on 84.6% of red zone trips (76th). Every great film needs some tension.

Players to Know
QB Jayden Maiava: 152 of 224 for 2,045 yards, 18 TD, 3 INT. CollegeFootballDigest says he's No. 2 in FBS in passing yards. At Penn State he went 21 of 33 for 301 yards and three scores. Leading-man material.
RB King Miller: 595 yards on 114 carries, 4 TD; 102 yards and a touchdown at Penn State.
WR Kayden Dixon-Wyatt: 27 catches, 400 yards, 4 TD. Trent Mosley: nine catches for 111 yards and a touchdown at Penn State.
S Christian Pierce: team-leading tackler. S Kennedy Urlacher: 3 sacks. CB Prophet Brown: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
USC is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big Ten, ranked No. 16 by the AP and No. 15 in the coaches poll. The wins: San José State 42-26, Fresno State 39-0, Louisiana 49-30, at Rutgers 42-35, Washington 25-21 and at Penn State 31-23. The one loss: Oregon, 41-27. We had last week off. After Madison comes a true blockbuster: No. 3 Ohio State at the Coliseum on Oct. 31. I'm not doing standings math tonight. I'll only say the sequel is lining up beautifully.
The road so far: two road games, two wins. Our heroes travel well.
The one dark scene: Oregon came to the Coliseum and won 41-27. Every great franchise has an episode like that. What matters is what came next: a 25-21 win over Washington and that statement night at Penn State. That's a hero who gets knocked down in act two and gets back up for the finale.

This Week: No. 16 USC (6-1) at Wisconsin (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Camp Randall Stadium, Madison · NBC. Forecast at kickoff: 65 degrees, mostly cloudy, south wind 10 mph.
The backstory: USC leads the series 7-1. The meetings include the Rose Bowl after the 1962 season, a 42-37 USC win, and a Holiday Bowl after 2015 that Wisconsin won 23-21. The last meeting, in 2024, went to USC 38-21. A rich film library.
Last time out: we beat Penn State 31-23 on Oct. 10. Wisconsin lost 17-7 at UCLA on Oct. 17.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the main event. Wisconsin's defense is excellent: 286.7 yards allowed (17th), 171.2 passing yards allowed (20th) and 16.7 points (24th). Maiava against that secondary is the scene everyone will remember.
Their offense vs. our defense: Wisconsin averages 351.8 yards (103rd), but quarterback Colton Joseph is also its leading rusher, 333 yards and 4 TD. And Wisconsin scores on 94.1% of red zone trips, 14th.
Availability: no availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Maiava against a top-20 pass defense. (2) Containing Joseph's legs. (3) Our red zone defense.
To Lars "Brat" Ellefson, Wisconsin's insider: a cheese wedge at every game? Magnificent costume design. I'd cast you in a heartbeat.

Why I Love This Team
I love an offense that plays like a summer blockbuster. I love a quarterback with 18 touchdowns and three interceptions. I love that the Trojans have won on the road twice already. And I love the history: 11 national championships and a Rose Bowl win over this very opponent. Roll credits.

report.title: "Bow Down to Washington": Evangeline 'Vangie' Tollefsrud Takes the Open Week
report.byline: Our insider (archetype: lake Washington sailgate captain) introduces the Washington Huskies during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Evangeline 'Vangie' Tollefsrud · Washington Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Bow Down to Washington! I'm Evangeline 'Vangie' Tollefsrud, and I'm your Washington insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a seattle native, rows crew, boats to every home game. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. On the podcast, my segment is called Sailgate Report. The show card describes it like this: the Fanatic's weekly signature column and podcast segment. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Huskies have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Husky Stadium in Seattle, WA, built in 1920 with a listed capacity of 70,138. The playing surface is Alaska Airlines Field, per Wikipedia. The fight song is "Bow Down to Washington", per Wikipedia. The band is the University of Washington Husky Marching Band, per Wikipedia. The program claims national titles from 1960, 1991, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 4-8, 11-2, 14-1, 6-7 and 9-4, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Oregon (5-5 in 10 meetings), Washington State (7-2 in 9 meetings), Stanford (5-3 in 8 meetings), Oregon State (7-1 in 8 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 13 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about sailgating on Lake Washington; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jedd Fisch leads the Huskies; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Jan. 14, 2024. Through 7 games, Washington scores 27.9 points a game and allows 22.7. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 46% of its plays, gaining 104.0 rushing yards and 282.7 passing yards a game. That's a balanced menu. On third down, Washington converts 33.3% of the time and opponents convert 31.5%. The defense has 13 sacks and 43 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 9 giveaways against 11 takeaways. Penalties cost 67.4 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 48 points against Eastern Washington on Sept. 19, 2026, and 3 of the 7 games were decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, Washington has outscored opponents by a combined 36 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB Demond Williams Jr. (passing leader): 116/174, 1396 yards, 8 TD, 3 INT.
RB Brian Bonner Jr. (rushing leader): 64 carries, 296 yards, 1 TD.
WR Dezmen Roebuck (receiving leader): 48 catches, 484 yards, 3 TD.
On defense, S Alex McLaughlin leads with 47 tackles and has 2 interceptions; LB Jacob Manu has 2.5 sacks.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Washington is 4-3 overall, 3-2 at home and 1-1 away. In Big Ten play the Huskies are 1-3, which sorts them No. 15 of 18 by record. Ohio State sits on top at 4-0 in league games. Right around us: Rutgers (1-2) and Penn State (0-4). The top of the table: Ohio State (4-0), UCLA (4-0), Indiana (3-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Washington this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Huskies beat Purdue on the road, 38-26. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, at Nebraska, in Lincoln, Neb., with a kickoff time to be determined. Nebraska comes in at 5-2. After that, CFBD lists vs. Penn State (Nov. 7), at Michigan State (Nov. 14), vs. Indiana (Nov. 21), at Oregon (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Huskies come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Bow Down to Washington!

report.title: "Pass the Curds": Brat Ellefson Welcomes the Trojans to Camp Randall
report.byline: Our cheese-wedge-carrying former fullback introduces himself and previews Wisconsin vs. No. 16 USC.
report.text:
Lars 'Brat' Ellefson · Wisconsin Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Pass the curds. (Polka accordion: oom-pah, oom-pah.) Hiya, folks, I'm Lars Ellefson, but everybody calls me Brat. I was a fullback for the Badgers back in my day, and I still carry a cheese wedge to every game. Every single one. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, wholesome as a glass of cold milk. You'll notice I play a little polka before I share a stat. My doctor says it's good for my heart. When we win, I jump around, literally, and pass out cheese curds. When we lose, I eat a brat in thoughtful silence. Then I eat another one.

The School in 60 Seconds
(Oom-pah.) The Badgers have played in the Big Ten since it formed in 1896. Wisconsin is one of 26 programs to win 700 or more games. Home is Camp Randall Stadium, the fourth-oldest stadium in college football, opened in 1917 and listed at 80,321 seats. The last five seasons were 9-4, 7-6, 7-6, 5-7 and 4-8. So this 4-2 start? That's a fresh batch of squeaky curds, folks. Squeaky fresh.

The Coach and the Scheme
Luke Fickell is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 27, 2022. (Oom-pah.) This team is built on defense, the way a good barn is built on a stone foundation. We allow 286.7 yards a game (17th in FBS), 171.2 passing yards (20th), 115.5 rushing yards (37th) and 16.7 points (24th). Now, the offense. I love it like family, and family is honest: 351.8 yards a game (103rd) and 199.7 passing yards (100th). But in the red zone, we score on 94.1% of trips, 14th in the country. Get us close, and we'll punch it in. Spoken like a fullback.

Players to Know
QB Colton Joseph: 87 of 159 for 1,198 yards, 10 TD, 5 INT, and he's also our leading rusher, 333 yards and 4 TD on 69 carries. At UCLA he ran 18 times for 71 yards and a touchdown. That's my kind of quarterback. Fullback heart.
WR Tyrell Henry: 27 catches, 343 yards, 1 TD.
RB Abu Sama III: six carries for 34 yards at UCLA. WR Jaylon Domingeaux: two catches for 26 yards.
LB Cooper Catalano: team-high 50 tackles. LB Sebastian Cheeks: 2.5 sacks. S Marvin Burks Jr.: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
(Oom-pah.) Wisconsin is 4-2 and 2-1 in the Big Ten, 3-0 at home. We opened with a 41-13 loss to Notre Dame at a neutral site, then beat Western Illinois 36-9, Eastern Michigan 54-10, Penn State 24-20 on the road and Michigan State 31-3. Last week, UCLA beat us 17-7. After USC, we head to No. 15 Iowa on Oct. 31. I'm not doing standings math. I'm just saying a win over a ranked team at Camp Randall would make the whole state jump.
The Penn State win is the one I'll keep telling my grandkids about: on the road, 24-20. That's a cheese wedge held high.
Season so far, by the polka: the Notre Dame game was a slow waltz we didn't want to dance. Then came three home wins and that road win at Penn State, a real toe-tapper. Michigan State managed just 3 points against our defense. UCLA held us to 7, and Joseph completed 6 of 16 passes. That's a sour note, folks. But we had a week off before UCLA, and the band's been practicing ever since. (Oom-pah.) I've seen this defense all year. It's the real deal, and it'll keep us in this one.
A fullback's note on Joseph: 69 carries through six games. That young man runs like he's carrying the cheese wedge himself.

This Week: No. 16 USC (6-1) at Wisconsin (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 Central) · Camp Randall Stadium, Madison · NBC. Forecast at kickoff: 65 degrees, mostly cloudy, south wind 10 mph. Perfect brat weather.
The history: USC leads the series 7-1. Our one win came in the Holiday Bowl after the 2015 season, 23-21. The last meeting, in 2024, went to USC 38-21. Time to even things up a little, eh?
Their offense vs. our defense: here's the big one. USC throws for 310.1 yards a game (7th), and Jayden Maiava has 18 touchdown passes. Our pass defense is 20th. That's a heavyweight bout at the county fair.
Our offense vs. their defense: USC's pass defense ranks 109th, so Joseph should have chances. And USC allows opponents to score on 84.6% of red zone trips. Get us inside the 20, folks.
Availability: no availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our pass defense against Maiava. (2) Joseph's legs and our red zone finishing. (3) Third downs; USC converts 51.2% (14th).
To Sterling Ashworth-Vance, USC's insider: I'd be honored to be in your movie, as long as I get to play the fullback.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
In Madison for the game? State Street Brats on State Street. A brat before the game is tradition in my house.

stories.title: Three Things About the Big Ten Race
stories.text:
Thing one: the standings, sorted by league record. Ohio State (6-1 overall) and UCLA (6-0 overall) are 4-0 in league play. Indiana (6-1 overall) and USC (6-1 overall) are 3-1 in league play. Iowa (5-1 overall), Northwestern (5-1 overall), Minnesota (4-2 overall), Oregon (4-2 overall), and Wisconsin (4-2 overall) are 2-1 in league play. Nebraska (5-2 overall) and Purdue (3-4 overall) are 2-2 in league play. Show me the denominator: that's a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Thing two: the destination. The Big Ten Championship Game is Saturday, Dec. 5, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, on FOX. Thing three: the bottom of the table is crowded too. Penn State, Maryland and Michigan State are each 0-4 in league play. Eighteen teams, one trip to Indianapolis. The math gets interesting from here.

report.title: "Bear Down, Friends": Inez Paloverde Welcomes the Cyclones Home for Homecoming
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hi, hi, hi, Wildcat family, welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Inez Paloverde, your Arizona insider, and I am a desert-sunrise optimist. I talk fast, I love hard, and I will defend this team to the last saguaro. I love the desert and I want you to love it too, so be warned: there will be cactus metaphors. A good defense is a lot like a cactus. It's beautiful from a distance, and you do not want to touch it. And when people complain about the Tucson heat, I just smile and say, "It's a dry hype." Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus all the sunshine I can carry. And I always end the same way: "Bear Down, friends."

The School in 60 Seconds
Let's start with those two words. "Bear Down" goes back to October 1926 and John "Button" Salmon, the student-body president and the Wildcats' quarterback. He was badly hurt in a car accident, and before he died he asked coach J.F. "Pop" McKale to tell the team to "bear down". It's been our rallying cry ever since. Home is Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson, listed at 50,782 seats. The program had a big 2025, going 9-4 and reaching the Holiday Bowl, where it lost to SMU 24-19. This season is Arizona's best start since 2014. Pretty as a sunrise over the Catalinas.

The Coach and the Scheme
Brent Brennan was hired on Jan. 16, 2024. He went 4-8 his first season, then turned it around with nine wins in 2025. The 2026 numbers say this offense starts with Noah Fifita's arm. Arizona throws for 303.8 yards a game with 16 passing touchdowns, and splits runs and passes evenly. It averages 35.7 points and 456.5 yards a game. The defense is the cactus: it allows 19.0 points a game and just 3.34 yards a carry, and it has 15 sacks. Two prickly spots: 16 sacks allowed, and eight turnovers lost against five forced. Also, West Virginia put up 522 yards against us, which dropped Arizona to ninth in the Big 12 in total defense.

Players to Know
QB Noah Fifita: 140 of 191 for 1,756 yards, 16 TD and 4 INT. At West Virginia he went 16 of 23 for 341 yards and 3 TD.
WR Isaiah Mizell: 19 catches, 359 yards, 4 TD, including 6 catches for 183 yards and 2 TD at West Virginia. WR Tre Spivey: 4 touchdown catches.
RB Kedrick Reescano: 262 yards and 4 TD on 72 carries.
LB Chase Kennedy: 4 sacks. LB Taye Brown: the leading tackler. Sources differ on the total, 39 in one preview and 27 in another snapshot (conflicting).

The Conference Picture
Arizona is 5-1 overall and 2-1 in the Big 12, 3-0 at home and 2-1 on the road. The Wildcats are No. 25 in this week's AP poll. The only loss came at BYU, 28-17, and since then they've won four straight: Northern Illinois, Washington State, Cincinnati and West Virginia. Our 456.5 yards a game ranks seventh in the Big 12 in total offense, and our run defense started last week third in the league before sliding to seventh. Translation: room to grow, plenty of sunshine to grow it in. Win on homecoming and Arizona stays right in the middle of the Big 12 race.

This Week: Iowa State (3-3) at No. 25 Arizona (5-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4:30 p.m. MST (7:30 p.m. ET) · Casino Del Sol Stadium · ESPN2 · Homecoming. It's the third straight year our homecoming has kicked off before 5 p.m.
Last time out: both teams are coming off bye weeks. Arizona won 52-31 at West Virginia. Iowa State lost 24-10 at No. 8 BYU and managed just 200 total yards.
Our offense vs. their defense: Iowa State allows 21.7 points a game and 198.5 passing yards a game. Fifita against that secondary is where I'd look first.
Their offense vs. our defense: the Cyclones love to run, at 181.5 yards a game. RB Aiden Flora has 680 yards and 6 TDs. Our run defense allows 3.34 a carry. Pretty from a distance, remember?
Series: Arizona leads 4-2-1, but Iowa State won last season's meeting 39-14 in Ames. It's Iowa State's first trip to Tucson since 1966.
Availability: Iowa State WR Dominic Overby is reported out for the season with a knee injury. I found no official availability report for Arizona as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our front slow Flora? (2) Can Fifita keep finding Mizell and Spivey? (3) Turnovers. We've lost eight; Iowa State has forced eight.
And to Twyla Hemmingsen, Iowa State's insider: honey, your forecast can say whatever it wants. Down here it's sunny and 100% Bear Down.

report.title: "Hydrate and Dominate": Skylar Vanterpool Welcomes the Wildcats to Tempe
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hi, Sun Devil Nation, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Skylar Vanterpool. Yes, I'm the girl by the pool in the giant maroon sunhat, and yes, I also have a master's degree in sports science, so I will talk your ear off about recovery windows and sweat rates. I travel with this team and live with this team. Fair warning: about every 90 seconds I'm going to remind you to drink some water. It's not a bit. Okay, it's a little bit a bit. My motto is simple: "Hydrate and dominate." When we win, I cannonball into a kiddie pool on set. When we lose, it's "Hydrate, reflect, recover," and then a well-earned nap. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, with plenty of sunshine and zero sunburn.

The School in 60 Seconds
Sun Devil football has a Rose Bowl ring to it. On Jan. 1, 1987, quarterback Jeff Van Raaphorst led a comeback as Arizona State beat Michigan 22-15 in Pasadena. More recently, the Sun Devils won the 2024 Big 12 championship, beating Iowa State 45-19 in the title game. Home is Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, listed at a capacity of 65,870. This team also gets around: in Week 3 it beat Kansas 24-17 at Wembley Stadium in London, England, in the Union Jack Classic. Sip of water. Okay, moving on.

The Coach and the Scheme
Kenny Dillingham became Arizona State's 26th head coach on Nov. 27, 2022, and took the Sun Devils to the Big 12 title in his second season. The 2026 numbers say this offense lives through the air. ASU throws for 276.7 yards a game and has 15 passing touchdowns, against 7 on the ground. It averages 31.3 points and 420.3 yards a game, and runs on about 48% of its plays at 4.42 yards a carry. The defense is where we need some shade and electrolytes: ASU allows 32.0 points and 373.2 yards a game, and 4.80 yards a carry. Two more things to fix are 15 sacks allowed and 10 turnovers lost against 6 forced. After last week, Dillingham said, "We almost gotta double down on that, because we're doing a lot well."

Players to Know
QB Cutter Boley (junior, Kentucky transfer): the season starter. One preview lists him at 1,229 yards, 12 TD and 3 INT, though that snapshot may not include the most recent game. At Texas Tech he went 5 of 10 for 124 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions before he was benched at halftime.
QB Mikey Keene (sixth-year): 25 of 34 for 256 yards and two touchdowns in the second half at Texas Tech. He's on the Pat Tillman Leadership Council and has played at UCF, Fresno State and Michigan.
WR Reed Harris (senior): 34 catches, 590 yards and 7 TD in the same preview snapshot.
WR Raiden Vines-Bright: caught a 74-yard touchdown at Texas Tech. WR Derek Eusebio: led the team with seven catches for 89 yards last week after an injury-slowed start.
RB Cardae Mack (freshman): seven carries for 27 yards and a touchdown catch at Texas Tech.
I could not find current, dated season defensive leaders, so I'm leaving them out rather than guessing.

The Conference Picture
Arizona State is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 2-1 at home and 0-2 on the road, plus the Wembley win at a neutral site. The Sun Devils are not ranked this week. The league losses were 55-19 at home to Baylor and 53-25 at Texas Tech. The top two Big 12 teams meet in the championship game, and both teams in this one are 1-2, so this is a big afternoon in the desert.

This Week: Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 12:45 p.m. MST (3:45 p.m. ET) · Mountain America Stadium · ESPN2. It's K-State's first visit to Tempe since 1989.
Last week: ASU trailed Texas Tech 43-10 at halftime and lost 53-25. Kansas State came from behind to beat Kansas 35-24, with 568 yards of offense and 359 on the ground.
Our offense vs. their defense: K-State allows only 136.3 passing yards a game and has 13 sacks. Our pass protection gave up a season-high six sacks last week, even with center Tana Alo-Tupuola and guard Wade Helton back from missed time.
Their offense vs. our defense: the Wildcats run the ball well, at 6.23 yards a carry. Quarterback Avery Johnson has 462 rushing yards to go with 1,301 passing, and running back Joe Jackson ran for 159 yards against Kansas. Our run defense allows 4.80 a carry, so tackling is the whole story. Arizona Sports pointed to tackling as a problem at Texas Tech.
Series: Arizona State leads 6-1 and won the last meeting, 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026. Dillingham said he would "assess all personnel" after watching the tape and has not named a starting quarterback. Johnson was shaken up against Kansas but said he only had the wind knocked out of him.
What decides it: (1) Boley or Keene, and how quickly that quarterback gets settled. (2) Whether our front can win at the point of attack against K-State's run game. (3) Protection. Six sacks can't happen again.
And to Hattie Brandvold, K-State's insider: welcome to Tempe, sweetie! I left a cold water bottle at your seat. It's a dry heat, but your crops will still wilt.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Tempe? Grab a seafood lunch at Casey Moore's Oyster House on South Ash Avenue before kickoff.

report.title: "Let's Renovate That Offense": Maggie Whitlock Brings Her Toolbox to Lawrence
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hey, y'all! I'm Magnolia Whitlock, Maggie to my friends, and I'm your Baylor insider at The Cover Window. I run an interior-design business in Waco, and I renovate roster weaknesses live on air. Shiplap for the secondary, new fixtures for the passing game, open concept for the run fits. I travel and live with this team, and I always pack a tape measure.

Here's my promise. I'm bubbly, but I don't fake the finishes. Every number here has a source, and when I do the math myself, I'll tell you. If I don't know something, I'll say the permits haven't come through yet. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I give God thanks for this team and this town. Sic 'em.

The School in 60 Seconds

Baylor plays in the Big 12. After 64 seasons at off-campus Floyd Casey Stadium, the Bears moved into on-campus McLane Stadium in 2014. CFBD lists 45,140 seats. Talk about a glow-up.

The last five seasons have been a whole renovation show: a beautiful 12-2 in 2021, then 6-7, 3-9, 8-5 and 5-7. This year's 4-2 start has good bones.

The Coach and the Scheme

Dave Aranda has been head coach since 2020. CFBD lists his hire date as Jan. 22, 2020. Before Waco he was defensive coordinator at LSU, Wisconsin, Utah State, Hawai'i, Delta State and Cal Lutheran. He's a defense-first designer, and it shows.

This year's defense is the showpiece room. Baylor hasn't allowed more than 19 points in any game. AP says six straight games under 20 to start a season is the program's longest such run since 1966. By my math from CFBD totals, the Bears allow 14.7 points and about 327 yards per game. Opponents run for about 87 yards per game. The pass rush has 22 sacks in six games.

The offense is the room under construction. Baylor scores 30.0 points per game by my math, but it put up only six against TCU. It runs for just 3.9 yards per carry. Third downs convert at 40.2%. Against TCU, three straight first-half drives of 12 or more plays ended in field-goal tries. That's a project I can fix.

Players to Know

QB DJ Lagway: 1,116 yards, eight touchdowns, three interceptions. He went 22 of 53 for 256 yards against TCU. Two weeks earlier, he threw four touchdowns in a 55-19 win at Arizona State. Let's get him back to that.
WR Gavin Freeman: team-best 49 catches for 555 yards and two touchdowns. That's a load-bearing wall.
RB Dawson Pendergrass: team-leading 327 rushing yards on 90 carries.
S Micah Gifford: forced a fumble and intercepted a pass in the final minutes of the first half against TCU.
K Rhett Armstrong: field goals of 39 and 32 yards against TCU.
Daniel Cobbs: team-high three sacks.
Travion Barnes: team-high 36 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Baylor is 4-2 overall and 2-1 in the Big 12. The Bears are 3-1 at home and 1-0 on the road, with a neutral-site game too. They opened with a 17-16 loss to Auburn at a neutral site. Then came four straight wins: 44-3 over Prairie View A&M, 36-19 over Louisiana Tech, 23-13 over Colorado and 55-19 at Arizona State. TCU ended the streak 17-6.

After Kansas, Baylor visits UCF on Oct. 30, hosts Iowa State, visits BYU, hosts Texas Tech and finishes at Houston. That's a demanding finish.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Baylor (4-2) at Kansas (2-4) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 1:00 p.m. ET · David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence, Kan. · TNT

Last time out. TCU beat Baylor 17-6 in Waco on Oct. 17. Aranda called it "frustrating," "disappointing" and "embarrassing". Kansas lost 35-24 at Kansas State the same day.

Baylor's offense vs. Kansas' defense. By my CFBD math, Kansas allows 24.0 points and about 174 rushing yards per game. That's a window for Pendergrass and the run game. Opponents convert only 32.9% of third downs against KU, so we need efficient early downs. Lagway to Freeman is the main beam.

Kansas' offense vs. Baylor's defense. Kansas runs well, at about 207 yards per game and 5.2 yards per carry by my math. Isaiah Marshall ran for 116 yards and threw for 151 at Kansas State. Nik McMillan has 400 receiving yards. Our run defense and pass rush are built for this. Kansas also has a dangerous returner: Bryson Hayes took a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown at K-State. Kick coverage matters.

Series. CFBD shows Baylor 8-0 against Kansas from 2016 to 2025. Respect the Jayhawks anyway; streaks end.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Baylor injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Baylor finish drives with touchdowns, not field goals?
2. Can the defense keep its sub-20 streak alive against Kansas' run game?
3. Can Lagway bounce back from 22-of-53?

Fitz, the Kansas insider, converts football stats into basketball points. I'll convert his points into paint colors.

Local Flavor

It's an early kickoff in Lawrence, 1 p.m. Eastern on TNT. Memorial Stadium opened in 1921 and is one of the oldest in college football. I love a classic build. Wear your green and gold, be a gracious guest and say a prayer for safe travels. Not an ad. Sic 'em.
