report.title: "Oh My Heck!": Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi Rides With the No. 2 Cougars to Orlando
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Oh my heck, Cougar Nation! I'm Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi, your BYU insider at The Cover Window. I'm a mountain-biking trail guide in Provo, and I chart every play like I'm reading a trail map from the top of Y Mountain. I follow this team everywhere, and I tell dad jokes so clean they sparkle.

Here's my first Sparkling Dad Joke. Why did the Cougar bring a ladder to Orlando? Because it heard the Bounce House had high expectations. The lesson: stay humble on the way up.

My promise to you is simple. Every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for mountains, family and fall Saturdays.

The School in 60 Seconds

BYU started playing college football in 1922 and has won 23 conference championships and the 1984 national championship. The Cougars were an FBS independent from 2011 to 2022 and joined the Big 12 on July 1, 2023. Home is LaVell Edwards Stadium, named for the coach who won 19 conference titles and that 1984 national title. Wikipedia lists 62,073 seats and CFBD lists 63,470.

The last five seasons: 10-3, 8-5, 5-7, 11-2 and 12-2. And now BYU is No. 2 in the AP poll. That's the program's highest ranking since the 1984 title season; 1984 is the only year BYU ranked higher. The Cougars received 20 first-place votes, their first since 1990. Oh my heck.

The Coach and the Scheme

Kalani Sitake played fullback for BYU under LaVell Edwards and graduated in 2000. He became head coach in 2016 (CFBD lists Dec. 19, 2015, as his hire date). Through 2025 he had four 10-win seasons. He's the first Tongan head coach in college football, and he entered the Polynesian Football Hall of Fame in 2025.

By my math from CFBD totals, the offense gains 421.2 yards per game (214.5 passing, 206.7 rushing) and scores 33.5 points. The defense allows 274.7 yards and 15.2 points per game. Opponents rush for only 86.2 yards per game. BYU has 11 sacks and is +3 in turnovers (five lost, eight gained). Opponents have converted 31 of 84 third downs.

Players to Know

QB Bear Bachmeier: 100 of 152 for 1,257 yards, nine touchdowns and two interceptions. Against Notre Dame he passed for 224 yards, ran for two touchdowns and caught another. He threw the go-ahead touchdown with 1:47 left.
WR Legend Glasker: team-best 24 catches for 444 yards and three touchdowns. AP writers named him the Big 12's top first-year freshman at midseason.
RB LJ Martin: 344 yards on 44 carries and three touchdowns.
Walker Lyons: caught the go-ahead 6-yard touchdown against Notre Dame.
RB Preston Rex: 66 yards on 10 carries against Notre Dame.
Tausili Akana: team-high 3.5 sacks.
Cade Uluave: team-high 35 tackles.

The Conference Picture

BYU is 6-0 and 3-0 in the Big 12. The Cougars are 4-0 at home and 2-0 on the road. They beat Utah Tech 63-7, Arizona 28-17, Colorado State 41-23 on the road, TCU 17-10 on the road, Iowa State 24-10 and Notre Dame 28-24. It's the third straight season BYU has started 6-0.

The Notre Dame game was BYU's first win over the Irish since 2004 and its first over a top-10 team since 2018. Afterward, the Big 12 said time remained on the clock when the final pass hit the ground, and that the play was cleared incorrectly. The final score stands. The conference said it will review its end-of-game process.

Still to come after UCF: Arizona State, at Utah, Baylor, at Kansas and Cincinnati.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

BYU (6-0) at UCF (3-3) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET · Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando · Fox

Last time out. BYU beat No. 2 Notre Dame 28-24 on Oct. 17. UCF is coming off its open date; it lost 42-28 at Oklahoma State on Oct. 10.

History in the making. BYU will be the highest-ranked opponent ever to play at UCF. The Knights are 0-5 at home against top-10 teams. It's also UCF's Homecoming, so expect a big crowd.

BYU's offense vs. UCF's defense. By my math, UCF allows 355.2 yards per game, including 236.8 through the air. That gives Bachmeier and Glasker room. UCF has 12 sacks, so protection matters.

UCF's offense vs. BYU's defense. Keyone Jenkins has started at quarterback while Alonza Barnett III recovers from a hamstring injury suffered on Sept. 12. Barnett's status for this game hasn't been determined. Jenkins threw for 265 yards and four touchdowns at Oklahoma State. Duke Watson leads UCF with 483 rushing yards. Our run defense allows 86.2 yards per game.

Series. One game page says BYU leads the series 4-1. That figure is thin; I couldn't cross-check it with a media guide.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed BYU injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can BYU handle the emotional letdown after Notre Dame?
2. Can our run defense make UCF throw?
3. Which UCF quarterback plays, Barnett or Jenkins?

Local Flavor

Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox. Knox, the UCF insider, says the stands really bounce. I packed my mountain bike shocks just in case. Wear blue, cheer kindly for our hosts, and say a prayer for safe travels. Not an ad. Go Cougs!

report.title: "That's a Five-Way Take": Skyline Abernathy Welcomes the Unbeaten Red Raiders for Homecoming No. 100
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, Bearcats, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Lionel Abernathy, but everybody calls me Skyline, for reasons that will become obvious very quickly. I'm an engineering co-op kid, I chart everything, and I rank it all in Cincinnati chili ways. A three-way is solid. A four-way is impressive. A five-way, with onions AND beans, is reserved for greatness. That goes for quarterbacks, defensive fronts and, yes, coaches' haircuts. When we win, I upgrade the team on air, three-way to five-way, no hesitation. When we lose, I downgrade to "plain spaghetti" and stare quietly into the distance. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a food tangent that somehow loops back into a very sharp stat. I travel with this team and I live with this team. That's a five-way take.

The School in 60 Seconds
Cincinnati has played football on the Nippert Stadium site since 1901, which makes it the second-oldest playing site in college football. That's history with extra cheese. In 2021 the Bearcats became the first team from outside the Power Five to make the College Football Playoff, where they played Alabama in the Cotton Bowl. Now we're in the Big 12, and Saturday is our 100th Homecoming game. Nippert is listed at 40,000 seats, and every one of them should be full.

The Coach and the Scheme
Scott Satterfield became the 43rd head coach in program history on Dec. 5, 2022. The 2026 numbers say this offense is a five-way: 35.2 points and 460.0 yards a game, on about 59% runs at 5.93 yards a carry, with 20 rushing touchdowns. Here's the best stat in the whole league, and I don't say that lightly: Cincinnati has lost just two turnovers all season and hasn't thrown a single interception. Both are the best in the country. The defense is more of a three-way right now. It allows 26.8 points and 434.3 yards a game, and 294.0 passing yards. The pass rush has 13 sacks.

Players to Know
QB JC French IV: 1,338 yards, 9 TD and zero interceptions. At West Virginia he went 22 of 30 for a career-high 389 yards and accounted for four touchdowns.
RB Cole Tabb: 448 yards and 8 rushing TD. He had 118 rushing yards, 54 receiving yards and 3 TDs at West Virginia, his third three-touchdown game of the season.
WR JV Gibson: 342 yards and 4 TD. WR Malachi Henry: caught a 69-yard pass at West Virginia, the team's longest play of the season, plus a 59-yarder.
LB Jonathan Thompson (fifth-year): a team-high 42 tackles, including a career-high 15 last week. Josh Hough: 3 sacks.
P Max Fletcher: rolled a 66-yard punt dead at the West Virginia 1 late in the game.

The Conference Picture
Cincinnati is 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 4-0 at home and 0-2 on the road. The Bearcats are not ranked. They beat Kansas State 31-26 at home, then lost 34-7 at Arizona and 45-42 at West Virginia. Next up is two straight ranked teams at home, Texas Tech and then Utah. Coming home to Nippert is like coming home to a warm bowl of chili.

This Week: No. 8 Texas Tech (6-0) at Cincinnati (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Nippert Stadium · FS1 · Homecoming No. 100. It's Texas Tech's first visit ever to Nippert.
Last week: we put up 622 yards at West Virginia, the most against an FBS opponent since last season. We led 42-35 late but lost 45-42 on a field goal at the final horn. Satterfield said, "We kept scoring, and we needed to get a stop." Texas Tech beat Arizona State 53-25.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the heavyweight four-way. Texas Tech allows only 2.87 yards a carry and 82.0 rushing yards a game, and its 11 interceptions are second-most in the country. Our run game (5.93 a carry) and French's perfect interception record go right into that.
Their offense vs. our defense: Tech runs on 56% of plays at 5.12 a carry. RB J'Koby Williams ran for 165 yards last week. QB Will Hammond has thrown 5 interceptions, so there are chances to take the ball away.
Series: Tech won 44-41 in Lubbock in 2024, and the teams tied 10-10 in 1968.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can we keep the ball safe against a defense that loves to take it away? (2) Can our run game get any room against a defense allowing 2.87 a carry? (3) Can our defense finally make the late stop?
And to Bodie Ratliff, Texas Tech's insider: you're a man of few words, so here are a few: welcome to Cincinnati. Have some chili. Three-way at minimum.

report.title: "Statistically, That's Rad": Moss Feldstein Runs the Numbers on Colorado at Oklahoma State
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hey, friends. I'm Moss Feldstein, your Colorado insider at The Cover Window. I'm a physicist, a hacky-sack enthusiast and the guy running a quant model of the Buffs from a hammock under the Flatirons. I travel and live with this team, and I bring kombucha on every road trip. It's an acquired taste. So is a 2-4 start.

Here's my approach: chill vibes, sharp numbers. Every stat in this report is sourced, and when I compute one myself, I'll tell you. If I don't know something, I'll say the data's not in yet. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I'm grateful to God for mountain sunsets and the chance to keep fighting. Ralphie's running.

The School in 60 Seconds

Colorado has played at Folsom Field in Boulder since 1924. CFBD lists 50,183 seats. The Buffs won the 1990 national championship, shared with Georgia Tech. They have two Heisman winners: Rashaan Salaam in 1994 and Travis Hunter in 2024. The all-time record is 735-556-36 through 2025.

Colorado was a charter Big 12 member, left for the Pac-12 after 2010 and returned to the Big 12 in 2024. The last five seasons swing wildly: 4-8, 1-11, 4-8, a radical 9-4 in 2024 and 3-9 in 2025. High variance. Physicists love that. Fans, less so.

The Coach and the Scheme

Deion Sanders, "Coach Prime," leads the program. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 3, 2022. His résumé is unlike anyone's. He played 14 NFL seasons, won two Super Bowls and played nine Major League Baseball seasons. He's the only athlete to play in both a Super Bowl and a World Series. At Florida State he won the 1988 Jim Thorpe Award.

Now my numbers, computed from CFBD season totals over six games. Colorado gains about 394 yards per game and allows about 357. It scores 19.5 points per game and allows 25.7. Rushing averages 3.9 yards per carry. Third downs convert at 36.1%. The defense has 13 sacks and eight interceptions.

The noisy variable is penalties: about 84 yards per game by my math. Against Utah, the Buffs had more penalty yards (82) than total yards (70) at halftime. Sanders keeps naming discipline as a frustration. Turnovers, too: 13 lost, seven forced.

Players to Know

QB Isaac Wilson: threw for 256 yards and two touchdowns with two interceptions against Utah, his former team. Sanders said, "Isaac is that guy," and pledged to keep developing him.
QB Julian Lewis: the season passing leader in ESPN's data, with 733 yards, six touchdowns and two interceptions. With both quarterbacks playing this year, I don't know who starts, and I won't guess.
WR Joseph Williams: team-best 37 catches for 508 yards and five touchdowns. That's 13.7 yards per catch by my math. Statistically, that's rad.
WR Quanell Farrakhan Jr.: caught the late pitch against Utah that was ruled an illegal forward pass.
RB JaQuail Smith: team-leading 259 rushing yards on 51 carries.
Lamont Lester Jr.: team-high four sacks.
Randon Fontenette: team-high 49 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Colorado is 2-4 overall and 0-3 in the Big 12. The Buffs won 14-13 at Georgia Tech and beat Weber State 52-21. Then came four straight losses: 41-7 at Northwestern, 23-13 at Baylor, 29-7 to Texas Tech and 27-24 to Utah.

The Utah game showed real signal. Colorado gained 324 of its 394 yards after halftime and pulled within a field goal with 1:21 left against the No. 11 team. After Oklahoma State come Kansas State at home, Arizona State on the road, Houston at home, Cincinnati on the road and UCF at home. There's season left to change the trend.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Colorado (2-4) at Oklahoma State (4-2) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 6 p.m. CT / 7 p.m. ET · Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater, Okla. · FS1

Last time out. Colorado lost 27-24 to Utah in Boulder in a game that ended early Sunday, Oct. 18. Oklahoma State lost 35-32 at Houston on Oct. 17.

Colorado's offense vs. Oklahoma State's defense. OSU allows about 358 yards and 23.7 points per game by my CFBD math. Opponents convert 34.9% of third downs. Houston converted 7 of 13 third downs against the Cowboys, so the window is there. Wilson's second half against Utah is the model: 324 yards after halftime.

Oklahoma State's offense vs. Colorado's defense. OSU averages about 518 yards and 37.2 points per game, by my math. Drew Mestemaker has 1,940 passing yards and 16 touchdowns, and his school says he's thrown for 300-plus in five straight games. Wyatt Young has 561 receiving yards. Our pass rush, led by Lester, needs to speed up the clock in his head.

Series. Oklahoma State's athletics site lists Colorado ahead 27-20-1 all-time. The last meeting was a 52-0 Colorado win in Boulder on Nov. 29, 2024. OSU won the previous one, 38-8 in San Antonio in 2016.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. The starting quarterback is unknown.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Colorado cut its penalty yardage on the road?
2. Can the pass rush slow Mestemaker?
3. Can the Buffs play a full game like their second half against Utah?

Local Flavor

It's homecoming in Stillwater, which Oklahoma State calls "America's Greatest Homecoming," and the game is listed as sold out. Loud crowd incoming. Back home, the game is on KOA 850 AM and 94.1 FM. Be a gracious guest, Buffs fans. Not an ad.

report.title: "Houston, We Have Liftoff": Yolanda "Yo" Pacheco Launches the Coogs Toward Salt Lake City
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Houston, we have liftoff! I'm Yolanda Pacheco, but everybody calls me Yo. I'm your Houston insider at The Cover Window. By day I'm a space-center engineer, and by night I grind Coogs film. I follow this team to every game, and I make NASA puns at every opportunity. Sorry in advance. Not really.

This is my first Mission Control. Here's the flight plan: every number has a source, and if I don't know something, I'll tell you. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for the Space City and the people in it.

The School in 60 Seconds

Houston plays in the Big 12. Since 2014, the Cougars have played on campus at TDECU Stadium, built on the site of old Robertson Stadium. CFBD lists 40,000 seats. The program has won 11 conference championships and has several College Football Hall of Famers, including a Heisman Trophy winner.

The last five seasons: 12-2, 8-5, 4-8, 4-8 and 10-3. That 10-win season last year was the launch. Now we're in orbit at No. 14 in the AP poll.

The Coach and the Scheme

Willie Fritz is in his third season; CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 3, 2023. He has been a head coach for decades: Blinn College (two straight NJCAA national titles, 1995 and 1996), Central Missouri, Sam Houston, Georgia Southern and Tulane. About his quarterback, he said: "He just keeps getting a little bit better every single week".

By my math from CFBD totals, the offense gains 485.1 yards per game (264.7 passing, 220.4 rushing) and scores 39.3 points. It has converted 54 of 88 third downs. Mission control, that's 61%.

The defense allows 347.6 yards and 21.0 points per game. Opponents rush for only 82.6 yards per game. The pass defense gives up more, at 265.0 per game. Houston has 13 sacks and is +5 in turnovers (five lost, 10 gained).

Players to Know

QB Conner Weigman: 134 of 198 for 1,771 yards, 20 touchdowns and two interceptions. Against Oklahoma State he went 24 of 33 for 343 yards and tied his career high with five touchdown passes. He also ran for 52 yards and earned the late first down that let Houston run out the clock.
WR Amare Thomas: team-best 36 catches for 487 yards and six touchdowns. He had seven catches, 126 yards and two touchdowns against Oklahoma State.
WR Trent Walker: seven catches for 104 yards and a touchdown against Oklahoma State, including the late 18-yard grab on third-and-7.
RB Makhi Hughes: 464 yards on 98 carries and three touchdowns.
Javion White: team-high 2.5 sacks.
Kentrell Webb: team-high 43 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Houston is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big 12. The Cougars are 4-0 at home and 2-1 on the road. They beat Oregon State 33-20 and Southern 77-6, then lost 28-26 at Texas Tech. Since then, it's been four straight wins: 42-28 at Georgia Southern, 27-17 over UCF, 35-16 at Kansas State and 35-32 over Oklahoma State.

The Oklahoma State win was Houston's first over a ranked team this season. The offense gained 505 yards.

After Utah, Houston gets an open date, then hosts Cincinnati, visits Colorado and West Virginia, and finishes at home against Baylor.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Houston (6-1) at Utah (6-0) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 10:15 p.m. ET · Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City · ESPN

Last time out. Houston beat Oklahoma State 35-32 on Oct. 17. Utah won 27-24 at Colorado in a game that ended early Sunday.

Houston's offense vs. Utah's defense. By my math, Utah allows 14.8 points and 88.7 rushing yards per game. Opponents have converted only 25 of 81 third downs against the Utes. That's the toughest test of our season. Weigman's efficiency on third down will matter.

Utah's offense vs. Houston's defense. Utah has scored a touchdown on its opening drive in every game and has outscored opponents 75-3 in the first quarter. So a fast start matters for us. Devon Dampier has 1,412 passing yards and 15 touchdowns. Wayshawn Parker has 597 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. Our run defense (82.6 per game) gets a real test.

Series. Houston's athletics site lists the Coogs 5-0 against Utah, including a 17-14 win in 2024. That's from a search summary, so it's thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Houston injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Houston weather Utah's first-quarter launch?
2. Can Weigman keep his touchdown-to-interception ratio on the road?
3. Can our run defense slow Parker?

Aspen, the Utah insider, breaks down defense like slalom gates. I break it down like a countdown.

Local Flavor

Saturday at 10:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. That's a late launch window, so Houston families, set those alarms or brew that coffee. Wear red, be gracious guests in Salt Lake City, and say a prayer for safe travels. Not an ad. Houston, we have liftoff.

report.title: "Cyclone Warning in Effect": Twyla Hemmingsen Forecasts the Trip to Tucson
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good evening, Cyclone Nation, and here's your Saturday forecast from The Cover Window! I'm Twyla Hemmingsen, your Iowa State insider, coming to you live from the Ames weather center. Okay, it's my kitchen, but it has a very nice map on the wall. I'm high-energy, a little nerdy and joyful about it, and I talk about football the way the TV meteorologist talks about a cold front: pressure systems, wind shifts, and a big red blob moving across the screen. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a full radar sweep of the opponent. Expect conditions to change quickly. When things are going our way, you'll hear "Seventy percent chance of loud." When it's really rolling: "Cyclone warning in effect." Umbrellas optional, joy mandatory.

The School in 60 Seconds
Our home is Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, which holds 61,500. It's named for Jack Trice, Iowa State's first Black athlete. The stadium got his name in 1997, and it is still the only major college football stadium named for a Black man. Every Cyclone fan should know his story. On the field, Iowa State went 8-4 last season. Then came the biggest offseason storm in the country. Coach Matt Campbell left for Penn State and took three-year starting QB Rocco Becht with him. More than 50 Cyclones entered the transfer portal, including 16 starters. That's a full barometric reset.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jimmy Rogers was named Iowa State's 34th head coach on Dec. 5, 2025, coming from Washington State on a six-year contract. Before that he went 27-3 and won an FCS national title at South Dakota State, and he brought in more than 45 transfers to rebuild this roster. The 2026 numbers say this team runs. Iowa State runs on about 59% of its plays, at 5.0 yards a carry, for 181.5 rushing yards a game. It averages 29.7 points and 359.7 yards a game, which is 12th in the Big 12 in total offense. The defense allows 21.7 points a game. The best part of the forecast: Iowa State has forced eight turnovers and lost only five.

Players to Know
RB Aiden Flora: 680 yards and 6 TD on 90 carries. That's the jet stream right there. He ran for 86 yards at BYU.
QB Jaylen Raynor: 85 of 148 for 1,001 yards, 7 TD and 4 INT. At BYU he went 16 of 29 for 98 yards and a touchdown.
WR Dominic Overby: 10 catches for 212 yards. He left the BYU game in the first quarter with a knee injury, and it has been reported as season-ending.
LB Sullivan Schlimgen: the team's leading tackler. Sources differ on his total: 56 in one CFBD-based preview and 35 in another snapshot (conflicting).
DE Isaac Terrell: 3 sacks.

The Conference Picture
Iowa State is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 3-1 at home and 0-2 on the road. The Cyclones are not ranked. They lost 16-13 at Iowa, 31-17 at home to Utah and 24-10 at BYU, and beat West Virginia 45-42 at home. A road win at a ranked team would brighten the whole radar.

This Week: Iowa State (3-3) at No. 25 Arizona (5-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (4:30 p.m. MST) · Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson · ESPN2 · Arizona homecoming. It's Iowa State's first game in Tucson since 1966.
Last time out: Both teams are coming off bye weeks. Iowa State lost 24-10 at No. 8 BYU on Oct. 9 and was held to 200 total yards. Arizona won 52-31 at West Virginia, its fourth straight win.
Our offense vs. their defense: Arizona allows just 3.34 yards a carry and 19.0 points a game, and it has 15 sacks. Our ground game will be heading into a strong high-pressure system.
Their offense vs. our defense: Arizona throws for 303.8 yards a game. QB Noah Fifita has 1,756 yards and 16 touchdowns, and at West Virginia he threw for 341 yards and 3 TDs, 183 of them to Isaiah Mizell.
Series: Arizona leads 4-2-1. Iowa State won the last meeting, 39-14 in Ames on Sept. 27, 2025.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 9 sacks and has allowed 8, with 8 takeaways against 5 giveaways, and it has 11 rushing and 9 passing touchdowns.
Availability: Overby is reported out for the season. I found no other official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can Flora and our run game stay ahead of the chains against a defense allowing 3.34 a carry? (2) Can our secondary keep Fifita's deep shots under control? (3) Turnovers. We're plus-3 and Arizona is minus-3.
And to Inez Paloverde, Arizona's insider: your forecast says sunshine, dear. Mine says a 30% chance of a Cyclone in the desert. Bring a light jacket.

report.title: "Spite and the Stats": Fitz Calloway Wants Kansas to Snap the Baylor Streak
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hi, everybody. I'm Fitz Calloway, your Kansas insider at The Cover Window. I'm a lifelong Lawrence native and a hoops-first guy who converted to football analytics out of spite. I travel and live with this team, and I convert every football stat into basketball points. A touchdown is two and a half three-pointers. I refuse to stop.

Here's my promise. I'm self-deprecating, but I'm not sloppy. Every number in this report has a source, and when I do the math myself, I'll say so. If I don't know something, I'll admit it. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for this town, this team and this stubborn hope. I'm only here because of spite and the stats. Okay, also love. Rock Chalk.

The School in 60 Seconds

Kansas football began in 1890, which makes it one of the oldest programs in the country. Home is David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, which opened in 1921 and is one of the oldest college football stadiums anywhere. Until 2014 it had a running track around the field. CFBD lists 47,000 seats.

The last five seasons: 2-10 in 2021, then 6-7, a joyful 9-4 in 2023, and 5-7 twice. That 9-4 season is a memory I cherish.

The Coach and the Scheme

Lance Leipold has been head coach since 2021. CFBD lists his hire date as April 30, 2021. At Wisconsin-Whitewater from 2007 to 2014, he won six Division III national championships. He reached 100 wins faster than any coach in NCAA history, in his 106th game. Then he coached Buffalo from 2015 to 2020.

This year the run game is the bright spot. By my math from CFBD totals, Kansas runs for about 207 yards per game at 5.2 yards per carry. The offense averages about 450 yards and 32.0 points per game. That's 12.8 three-pointers, if you're scoring at home.

The defense allows 24.0 points per game by my math. Opponents run for about 174 yards a game, which is the soft spot. But opponents convert only 32.9% of third downs. The turnover count is the problem: nine lost and six forced. Leipold said after the K-State loss, "our margin for error is very small, and you have to play clean".

Players to Know

QB Isaiah Marshall: 1,294 passing yards, nine touchdowns, five interceptions. At Kansas State he threw for 151 yards and ran for 116. A late interception hurt, and a facemask penalty wiped out his 45-yard touchdown run.
WR Nik McMillan: team-best 400 receiving yards on 23 catches with four touchdowns. That's 17.4 yards a catch by my math.
RB Dylan Edwards: team-leading 375 rushing yards on 75 carries with four touchdowns. He scored against his former team, Kansas State.
KR Bryson Hayes: returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown at Kansas State. Fast break.
Leroy Harris III: team-high three sacks.
Trey Lathan: team-high 41 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Kansas is 2-4 overall and 0-3 in the Big 12. The Jayhawks are 2-1 at home and 0-2 on the road, plus one neutral-site game. They beat Long Island University 51-6 and Middle Tennessee 55-0. The losses: 38-21 to Missouri, 24-17 to Arizona State at a neutral site, 41-24 at Utah and 35-24 at Kansas State.

The K-State loss was K-State's 18th straight win in that series. Leipold said, "A lot of people want this streak snapped, myself included". After Baylor come TCU on the road, UCF at home, West Virginia on the road, BYU at home and Oklahoma State on the road.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Baylor (4-2) at Kansas (2-4) · Saturday, Oct. 24, noon CT / 1:00 p.m. ET · David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence, Kan. · TNT

Last time out. Kansas led Kansas State by 10 early but lost 35-24 in Manhattan on Oct. 17. Baylor lost 17-6 to TCU the same day.

Kansas' offense vs. Baylor's defense. This is the big test. Baylor hasn't allowed more than 19 points in a game this season. By my CFBD math, the Bears allow 14.7 points per game and about 87 rushing yards. Their pass rush has 22 sacks. So Kansas has to run well early, protect Marshall and avoid turnovers. Our 5.2 yards per carry is the best weapon we have.

Baylor's offense vs. Kansas' defense. Baylor scored six points against TCU, and DJ Lagway went 22 of 53. Three long first-half drives ended in field-goal tries. Baylor runs for just 3.9 yards per carry by my math. Gavin Freeman has 49 catches for 555 yards, so he's the guy to watch. Our third-down defense (32.9%) needs to keep those drives stalling.

Series. CFBD shows Baylor 8-0 against Kansas from 2016 to 2025. Yes, another streak. Spite is a renewable resource.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Kansas injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Kansas protect the ball against Baylor's pass rush?
2. Can the run game crack a defense that hasn't allowed 20 points?
3. Can our run defense hold Baylor's ground game under 4 yards a carry?

Maggie, the Baylor insider, renovates weaknesses live on air. I'd like to renovate our last eight results against Baylor.

Local Flavor

It's a noon kickoff in Lawrence on TNT. Memorial Stadium has stood since 1921. Wear crimson and blue, welcome the Baylor fans warmly and cheer like it's a home game in March. Not an ad. Rock Chalk.

report.title: "You Can't Rush a Harvest": Hattie Brandvold Takes the Wildcats to the Desert
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy, Wildcat family, and welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Hattie Brandvold. I have an agronomy degree, a purple denim jacket, a wheat-sheaf brooch and a field notebook with real Flint Hills dirt on it. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I explain defensive fronts the only way I know how: crop rotation. Every drive gets named after a crop. A three-and-out is a dry sorghum patch. A long, patient march is winter wheat. And a touchdown? That's a bumper harvest, and you will hear me holler it. When we win, I do the Wabash Cannonball in my chair, tidy and joyful. When we lose, I whisper my most treasured words, "You can't rush a harvest," and I plant a tiny basil seed right there on set. Sweet as prairie pie, until I hand you the one fact that ends the argument.

The School in 60 Seconds
Kansas State football is the story of the biggest turnaround in the sport. When Bill Snyder took over in 1989, the program was in the middle of a 27-game winless streak. He turned it into a national contender that went to 11 straight bowl games and had six 11-win seasons in a seven-year stretch. Snyder won two Big 12 championships, one in 2003 with Darren Sproles and one in 2012. He went into the College Football Hall of Fame while still coaching, in December 2015. The Wildcats play at Bill Snyder Family Stadium in Manhattan, and the rivalry with Kansas is the Sunflower Showdown, played for the Governor's Cup. As of last Saturday, K-State has won that game 18 straight times, the longest active winning streak by any team in a rivalry game. Now that's a crop that keeps coming back every spring.

The Coach and the Scheme
Collin Klein was named the 36th head coach in school history on Dec. 4, 2025. You may remember him as the quarterback: he was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and won the Johnny Unitas Award that year, when K-State won the Big 12. He is the first K-State alum to be head coach since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77. Before this job he coached nine years in Manhattan, including two as offensive coordinator (2022-23) that went 19-8 with a Big 12 title, then ran the offense at Texas A&M. The 2026 numbers say this offense grows on the ground. K-State runs on about 54% of its plays and gains 6.23 yards a carry, with 15 rushing touchdowns. It averages 35.5 points and 464.7 yards a game. On defense, the Wildcats allow 20.0 points and 296.3 yards a game, and only 136.3 passing yards. They have 13 sacks and have allowed just 3. One weed to pull: six turnovers lost against four forced.

Players to Know
QB Avery Johnson (senior, Wichita): 1,301 passing yards and 462 rushing yards, leading the team in both. Against Kansas he passed for 209 yards and a touchdown and ran for 132, and he became the school's all-time leader in total offensive yards. He went down after a 59-yard run and pointed to his right shoulder, but he returned and said, "I just got the wind knocked out of me."
RB Joe Jackson (senior): a season-high 159 yards and a touchdown against Kansas.
WR Jaron Tibbs: the team's leading receiver with 268 yards.
K Luis Rodriguez: four field goals against Kansas, from 22, 51, 28 and 34 yards, the second-most in a game in school history.
DB Logan Bartley: made an end-zone interception against Kansas.
I could not find official season defensive leaders from a source newer than the start of October, so I'm not listing them.

The Conference Picture
K-State is 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 4-1 at home and 0-1 on the road. The Wildcats are not ranked in the AP or Coaches poll this week. The two league losses came at Cincinnati, 31-26, and at home against Houston, 35-16. The top two teams in the Big 12 meet in the championship game, so a 1-2 start means every Saturday from here matters.

This Week: Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:45 p.m. ET (12:45 p.m. MST) · Mountain America Stadium, Tempe · ESPN2. It's K-State's first game in Tempe since the 1989 season opener, and the Wildcats' last game in this stadium was a 31-14 bowl win over Michigan in 2013.
Last week: K-State trailed Kansas 17-7 in the first quarter, then won 35-24 and racked up 568 yards, 359 of them on the ground. Arizona State lost 53-25 at Texas Tech. Coach Kenny Dillingham replaced quarterback Cutter Boley with Mikey Keene at halftime, and Keene threw for 256 yards and two touchdowns.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is where my winter wheat should grow. Arizona State allows 32.0 points and 373.2 yards a game, and 4.80 yards a carry. Texas Tech gained 7.8 yards a play against the Sun Devils last week.
Their offense vs. our defense: ASU throws for 276.7 yards a game, and senior receiver Reed Harris is a big-play threat. But the Sun Devils have allowed 15 sacks, including a season-high six at Texas Tech. K-State has 13 sacks of its own.
Series: Arizona State leads 6-1, and the Sun Devils won the last meeting, 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024. K-State's lone win was 34-27 on Dec. 27, 2002.
Availability: Johnson's shoulder scare turned out to be the wind knocked out of him. I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026. Dillingham has not named a starting quarterback for this game.
What decides it: (1) Can K-State's run game keep producing like it did against Kansas? (2) Who plays quarterback for Arizona State, Boley or Keene? (3) Can our pass rush get home against a front that gave up six sacks last week?
And to Skylar Vanterpool, Arizona State's insider: I'll bring the shade hat and the water jug, darlin'. Hydrate all you like. You still can't rush a harvest.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching from Manhattan? Varsity Donuts on North Manhattan Avenue is how I start every game-day morning.

report.title: "Ride 'Em, Pokes": Dusty Lockridge Saddles Up for Homecoming Against Colorado
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Well, howdy, Cowboy fans. I'm Dusty Lockridge, your Oklahoma State insider at The Cover Window. I'm an ag-econ grad, I wear orange from my hat to my boots, and I travel and live with this team. I explain offense with rodeo timing. A quick slant is a two-second ride. A long touchdown drive is the full eight seconds, with a good score from the judges.

Here's my word as a cowboy. Every number I give you has a source. When I do math myself, I'll tell you. If I don't know something, I'll say so. No bull, so to speak. I celebrate our players as young men first, I respect every opponent, and I thank the good Lord for homecoming weekend in Stillwater. Ride 'em, Pokes.

The School in 60 Seconds

Oklahoma State football started in 1901 and plays at Boone Pickens Stadium in Stillwater. CFBD lists 55,509 seats. The Cowboys claim the 1945 national championship, awarded by the AFCA, plus eleven conference titles. They've played in 34 bowl games and gone 22-12, including five New Year's Six wins. Running back Barry Sanders won the Heisman in 1988. The program counts 66 All-Americans.

The last five seasons have been a bucking bronco: 12-2, 7-6, 10-4, then 3-9 and 1-11. That's why a 4-2 start feels like the buckle at the end of the ride.

The Coach and the Scheme

Eric Morris is our first-year head coach. Wikipedia says he was introduced on Dec. 8, 2025, while CFBD lists his hire date as Nov. 25, 2025. I'll flag that small difference. Before Stillwater he was head coach at Incarnate Word and North Texas, and offensive coordinator at Washington State.

His offense rides hard. By my math from CFBD totals, OSU averages about 518 yards and 37.2 points per game. It has thrown 17 touchdown passes and run for eight more. The defense allows about 358 yards and 23.7 points per game. Opponents convert 34.9% of third downs. The Cowboys average about 52 penalty yards per game.

Coming into the Houston game, AP noted that defense was a big reason the Cowboys won four in a row. Then Houston converted 7 of 13 third downs, and OSU had a season-high nine penalties. Clean that up, and this outfit is dangerous.

Players to Know

QB Drew Mestemaker: 1,940 yards, 16 touchdowns, six interceptions. He went 22 of 34 for 365 yards and three touchdowns at Houston. Our athletics department says he's thrown for 300-plus yards in five straight games, the second-longest active streak in FBS. UCF coach Scott Frost said he'd be surprised if Mestemaker is in college next year. High praise from the other side of the arena.
WR Wyatt Young: team-best 32 catches for 561 yards and five touchdowns. That's 17.5 yards a catch by my math.
RB Caleb Hawkins: 592 rushing yards on 123 carries. At Houston he caught seven passes for a career-high 125 yards, two shy of the school record for a running back.
WR Justin Bowick: six catches for 98 yards and a touchdown against UCF, and an 8-yard touchdown catch at Houston.
Ethan Wesloski: team-high 62 tackles, including nine at Houston.
Malik Charles: team-high 2.5 sacks.
Evan Jackson: returned a fumble 28 yards for the turning-point touchdown against UCF.

The Conference Picture

Oklahoma State is 4-2 overall and 2-1 in the Big 12. The Cowboys are 3-0 at home and 1-2 on the road. They lost the opener 24-10 at Tulsa. Then came four straight wins: 39-31 over Oregon, 59-0 over Murray State, 41-24 at West Virginia and 42-28 over UCF. Last week brought a 35-32 loss at Houston.

OSU was ranked No. 18 going into Houston. Our athletics department says the Cowboys are still in the Big 12 hunt, though they'll need help. After Colorado come Iowa State and Kansas State on the road, Texas Tech at home, Arizona State on the road and Kansas at home.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Colorado (2-4) at Oklahoma State (4-2) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 6 p.m. CT · Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater, Okla. · FS1

Last time out. Houston led 14-3 at halftime, and OSU scored 29 second-half points but fell 35-32. Mestemaker went 16 of 19 for 241 yards after halftime. Early red-zone trips ended in a field goal and a turnover on downs. Colorado lost 27-24 to Utah the same weekend.

OSU's offense vs. Colorado's defense. By my CFBD math, Colorado allows about 357 yards and 25.7 points per game. Its pass rush has 13 sacks, with Lamont Lester Jr. leading at four. Protect Mestemaker, and let Young and Bowick work. Hawkins keeps defenses honest on the ground and through the air.

Colorado's offense vs. OSU's defense. Colorado scores about 19.5 points per game and has lost 13 turnovers, by my math from CFBD totals. The Buffs averaged roughly 84 penalty yards per game. But Isaac Wilson threw for 256 yards and two touchdowns against Utah, and Colorado gained 324 yards after halftime. Joseph Williams has 508 receiving yards. Respect that.

Series. Colorado leads 27-20-1 all-time, per our athletics site. The last meeting was a 52-0 Colorado win in Boulder on Nov. 29, 2024. OSU won the time before, 38-8 in San Antonio in 2016. Nobody in orange has forgotten 2024.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed OSU injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can OSU finish red-zone trips with touchdowns?
2. Can the Cowboys cut down on penalties after nine at Houston?
3. Can the defense get off the field on third down?

Moss, the Colorado insider, runs a quant model from a hammock. I time plays with a stopwatch from a saddle. We'll both be counting.

Local Flavor

It's America's Greatest Homecoming, and the game is listed as sold out. Stillwater will be orange from the rooftops to the parking lots. Come early, take it all in, love your neighbor and welcome the Buffs fans with real Oklahoma manners. Not an ad. Ride 'em, Pokes.

report.title: "Yeehaw, That's a Turnover": Ryder Galloway Welcomes the Mountaineers to Cowtown
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy, Frog fans, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Ryder Galloway, your TCU insider. I'm a Stockyards cowboy who became a finance guy, so I wear boots with a quarter-zip and I explain defenses as cattle drives. You've got your point riders, your flank riders and your drag riders, and when everyone holds their spot, nobody gets loose. I travel with this team and I live with this team. Fair warning: if something goes wrong, anything at all, I will probably blame Dallas. Flat tire? Dallas. Missed field goal? Dallas. When we win, it's "Yeehaw!" and my hat goes flying. When we lose, I mutter about Dallas some more. And the best sound in football is me hollering "Yeehaw, that's a turnover!" Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, Fort Worth style.

The School in 60 Seconds
TCU has a national title on the wall. The 1938 Horned Frogs went 11-0, beat Carnegie Tech 15-7 in the Sugar Bowl and won the national championship. Quarterback Davey O'Brien won the Heisman Trophy that year. The 2010 team went 13-0 and won the Rose Bowl, and in 2022 Sonny Dykes led TCU all the way to the College Football Playoff national championship game. Home is Amon G. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, listed at 46,000. Not one bit of that history happened in Dallas. And the rivalry with Baylor has a name now, the Revivalry, and we just won it in Waco. Ten more minutes on that and I'd be throwing my hat again.

The Coach and the Scheme
Sonny Dykes was hired on Nov. 29, 2021, and in his first season he took the Frogs to the national title game. The 2026 numbers say defense is driving this herd. TCU allows only 12.2 points and 264.2 yards a game. Opponents average 2.88 yards a carry and 172.2 passing yards, and the Frogs have 14 sacks. Every rider is holding his spot. The offense throws for 282.3 yards a game and averages 24.0 points. The run game needs work, at 3.27 yards a carry, and the blockers have given up 17 sacks. Turnovers are close: 9 lost, 8 forced.

Players to Know
QB Jaden Craig: 1,694 yards and 10 TD. At Baylor he went 21 of 36 for 294 yards and two touchdowns.
WR Jordan Dwyer: 6 catches for 150 yards at Baylor. WR Ed Small: 7 catches, 91 yards and a touchdown in that game.
RB Jeremy Payne: team-high 429 rushing yards and 2 TD.
DE Koron Hayward: three of TCU's four sacks at Baylor. S Jamel Johnson: intercepted a pass at Baylor. LB Hudson Hooper: team-high 33 tackles.

The Conference Picture
TCU is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 2-1 at home and 1-1 on the road. The Frogs are not ranked. All three losses were close: 15-10 to North Carolina at a neutral site, 21-13 at UCF and 17-10 at home to BYU. The offense needs to catch up to this defense, and a home win would get us back to.500 in the league.

This Week: West Virginia (4-3) at TCU (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 11 a.m. CT (noon ET) · Amon G. Carter Stadium · ESPN2. Forecast: 74 degrees and mostly sunny.
Last week: TCU won the Revivalry at Baylor 17-6. The defense held the Bears without a touchdown and kept them scoreless in the second half. West Virginia beat Cincinnati 45-42 on a 35-yard field goal as time ran out.
Our offense vs. their defense: West Virginia allows 34.0 points and 483.9 yards a game, and 310.1 passing yards. Craig to Dwyer and Small should have room to run.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the big cattle drive. West Virginia runs on 72% of its plays and came into last week averaging 295.5 rushing yards a game. QB Michael Hawkins Jr. leads FBS in rushing touchdowns, and RB Cam Cook is fifth in rushing yards. Our run defense allows 2.88 a carry. Cincinnati held them to 134 rushing yards last week, but Hawkins threw for 464.
Series: West Virginia leads 8-6.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 14 sacks and has allowed 17, with 8 takeaways against 9 giveaways, and it has 7 rushing and 10 passing touchdowns.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our front keep Hawkins and Cook boxed in? (2) Can our offense finally get the run game going? It's averaging 3.27 a carry. (3) Turnovers. Yeehaw time.
And to Jolene Buckhannon, West Virginia's insider: ma'am, I hear you don't miss. Neither does our defense. Welcome to Fort Worth, where the West begins.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Fort Worth? The original Fuzzy's Taco Shop on Bryant Irvin Road. Tacos, not Dallas.

report.title: "Guns Up, Wind's Up": Bodie Ratliff Rides Into Nippert
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Howdy. Bodie Ratliff. Texas Tech insider for The Cover Window. I ride bareback at the rodeo, and in tumbleweed season I chart Air Raid concepts on the back of feed-store receipts. I travel with the team. I live with the team. People say I don't talk much. They're right. One word usually does it, and the wind fills in the rest. Somebody asks how the defense looked? "Mean." How was the trip? "Windy." When we win, I say "Guns up," real quiet, and then I grin longer than anybody's comfortable with. When we lose, I stare into the wind with my hat in my hand. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup from inside the program, West Texas plain. My motto: "Guns up, wind's up."

The School in 60 Seconds
Last season was the best in school history. Texas Tech went 12-2, crushed BYU 34-7 to win the Big 12 championship and made its first College Football Playoff. That was the program's first outright conference title since 1955. The run ended with a 23-0 loss to Oregon in the Orange Bowl. Home is Jones AT&T Stadium in Lubbock, listed at 60,454. And the run hasn't stopped: Tech is 18-2 since the start of 2025, and 17 of those wins came by double digits. Long story short. "Good."

The Coach and the Scheme
Joey McGuire was hired on Nov. 8, 2021. He's 41-18 in five seasons and 26-5 at home. The Air Raid jokes still follow us around, but this team is built on the ground and on defense. Tech runs on about 56% of its plays, at 5.12 yards a carry with 16 rushing touchdowns. It averages 37.8 points a game. On defense, opponents gain only 2.87 yards a carry and 82.0 rushing yards a game. Tech has 17 sacks and 12 takeaways, and its 11 interceptions are the second-most in the country. One word: "Stingy."

Players to Know
QB Will Hammond: 1,334 yards, 6 TD, 5 INT.
RB J'Koby Williams: 538 yards and 5 TD. He had a career day against Arizona State with 165 yards and two scores.
WR Kenny Johnson: a team-high 418 receiving yards, including 7 catches for 120 last week. WR Coy Eakin: a team-high 3 receiving TDs.
K Stone Harrington: 4 of 5 on field goals against Arizona State.
Defense: A.J. Holmes Jr. leads with 4 sacks, and Austin Romaine leads with 41 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Texas Tech is 6-0 overall and 3-0 in the Big 12, 4-0 at home and 2-0 on the road. The Red Raiders are No. 8 in the AP poll and No. 5 in the Coaches Poll this week. It's their second straight 6-0 start, and a win would make only the fifth 7-0 start in school history. We've won four straight road games going back to last season, including 35-24 at Oregon State and 29-7 at Colorado this year. It's one of six unbeaten teams in the country. Next come back-to-back home dates with Arizona and West Virginia. One word: "Busy."

This Week: No. 8 Texas Tech (6-0) at Cincinnati (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET (11 a.m. CT) · Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati · FS1. It's Texas Tech's first trip ever to Nippert, and Cincinnati's 100th Homecoming game.
Last week: Tech beat Arizona State 53-25 and averaged 7.8 yards a play. Cincinnati lost 45-42 at West Virginia on a 35-yard field goal as time ran out.
Our offense vs. their defense: Cincinnati allows 26.8 points and 434.3 yards a game, and 294.0 passing yards. LB Jonathan Thompson had a career-high 15 tackles last week, and the Bearcats held West Virginia's Big 12-leading run game to 134 yards.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the big one. Cincinnati hasn't thrown an interception all year and has just two turnovers, the fewest in the country. QB JC French IV threw for a career-high 389 yards last week, and RB Cole Tabb has 8 rushing touchdowns. They run for 5.93 a carry. Our run defense allows 2.87. Something gives. "Wind."
Series: this is just the third meeting. The teams tied 10-10 in 1968, and Tech won 44-41 in 2024 behind 172 rushing yards from Tahj Brooks.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our ball-hawking defense take one away from a team that never gives it up? (2) Can we stop Tabb and French on the ground? (3) Hammond protecting the football on the road.
And to Skyline Abernathy, Cincinnati's insider: chili's good. Wind's better. See you Saturday.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Lubbock? Robles Taquería on Main Street. Tacos. Enough said.

report.title: "Welcome to the Bounce House": Knox Brevard-Stiles Rolls Out the Homecoming Welcome for No. 2 BYU
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Charge On, Knights! I'm Knox Brevard-Stiles, your UCF insider at The Cover Window. I grew up in Orlando, I'm a theme-park ride engineer, and I swear the stands really move. I measure crowd noise with a ride-safety gauge, and I wear a knight's helmet after big wins. Please keep your hands and feet inside the stadium at all times.

My first Ride Check: every cheer gets measured, every claim gets checked. Every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll say so. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for Florida sunshine and Saturday football.

The School in 60 Seconds

UCF first fielded a varsity team in 1979 as an NCAA Division III program and reached Division I-A, now the FBS, in 1996. That made UCF the first program in NCAA history to play in all four divisions of college football. As a Division I-AA program, the Knights made the 1990 and 1993 playoffs. Today they play in the Big 12.

Home is the Acrisure Bounce House on UCF's main campus east of Orlando. Wikipedia lists 45,906 seats and CFBD lists 44,206. CFBD says it opened in 2007. The first game there was a 35-32 loss to No. 6 Texas on Sept. 15, 2007, and UCF led 24-23 early in the fourth quarter. Ride Check: the stands passed inspection that day.

The last five seasons: 9-4, 9-5, 6-7, 4-8 and 5-7.

The Coach and the Scheme

Scott Frost is back for a second run in Orlando. He coached UCF in 2016 and 2017, then Nebraska from 2018 to 2022. CFBD lists his return as Dec. 7, 2024. As a player, he led Nebraska to the 1997 national championship. He has coached Heisman winner Marcus Mariota and Heisman candidate McKenzie Milton.

By my math from CFBD totals, UCF gains 354.8 yards per game (192.7 passing, 162.2 rushing) and scores 31.7 points. The defense allows 355.2 yards and 21.7 points per game. Opponents rush for 118.3 yards and pass for 236.8. UCF has 12 sacks and is +4 in turnovers (seven lost, 11 gained).

Players to Know

QB Keyone Jenkins: 83 of 118 for 806 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. At Oklahoma State he threw for 265 yards and four touchdowns, including 15 of 18 in the first half.
QB Alonza Barnett III: the starter, sidelined since a hamstring injury against Pittsburgh on Sept. 12. His status for BYU hasn't been determined.
RB Duke Watson: 483 yards on 70 carries and three touchdowns.
WR Josh Derry: team-best 28 catches for 304 yards and two touchdowns.
TE Grayson Brousseau and Tyren Hornes: each caught touchdowns at Oklahoma State.
Isaiah Nixon: team-high 2.5 sacks. He forced and recovered a fumble at Oklahoma State, which set up UCF's first touchdown.
Tackett Curtis: team-high 39 tackles.

The Conference Picture

UCF is 3-3 and 1-2 in the Big 12. The Knights are 3-0 at home and 0-3 on the road. They beat Bethune-Cookman 73-6, Georgia State 44-30 and TCU 21-13 at home. They lost 12-7 at Pittsburgh, 27-17 at Houston and 42-28 at Oklahoma State.

At Oklahoma State, UCF was tied 21-21 at halftime and was driving early in the fourth quarter. Then a backward pass was knocked down and returned for a touchdown. AP noted it was the second straight week UCF lost a lead, and the 12th straight road loss. Good news: this one is at home, and the Knights are unbeaten here this year.

After BYU, UCF hosts Baylor on Friday, Oct. 30, for the annual Space Game. Four of the last six games are at home.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

BYU (6-0) at UCF (3-3) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET · Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando · Fox

Last time out. UCF had an open date last week. BYU beat No. 2 Notre Dame 28-24 on Oct. 17.

History at the Bounce House. BYU is No. 2 in the AP poll, which makes the Cougars the highest-ranked opponent ever to play at UCF. UCF is 0-5 at home against top-10 teams. And it's Homecoming. Ride Check: maximum bounce requested.

UCF's offense vs. BYU's defense. By my math, BYU allows just 86.2 rushing yards and 15.2 points per game. Watson has to find room, and Jenkins or Barnett has to protect the ball. BYU has 11 sacks.

BYU's offense vs. UCF's defense. Bear Bachmeier has 1,257 passing yards and nine touchdowns, and Legend Glasker has 444 receiving yards. BYU runs for 206.7 yards per game. Our defense has to tackle well and win third downs.

Series. One game page says BYU leads the series 4-1. That figure is thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. Barnett's status is unknown.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Who starts at quarterback, and can he protect the ball?
2. Can UCF run against BYU's tough run defense?
3. Can the open date help a healthier UCF team?

Bryce, the BYU insider, tells dad jokes so clean they sparkle. I'll counter with a roller-coaster joke: this season has had ups and downs, but we're still strapped in.

Local Flavor

Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox. Homecoming at the Bounce House. Wear black and gold, welcome our guests from Provo kindly, and pray for safe travels for every family. Not an ad. Charge On!

report.title: "Send It, No Fear": Aspen Mortensen Welcomes Houston to a Late Night at Rice-Eccles
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Send it, no fear, Ute fans! I'm Aspen Mortensen, your Utah insider at The Cover Window. I used to race skis, and now I chart Utah's defensive speed like slalom gates. Who cut inside, who cleared the gate, who missed it. I follow this team to every game, and yes, I'll be making avalanche puns. Consider yourself warned.

This is my first Slalom Gates report, and here's my promise. Every number has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you plainly. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for the Wasatch, my family and fall football.

The School in 60 Seconds

Utah football began in 1892 and has played at the current site of Rice-Eccles Stadium since 1927. The Utes have won 27 conference championships in five conferences. Through 2025, Utah's all-time record was 735-491-31. The Utes are 18-9 in major bowl games, including two BCS wins: the 2005 Fiesta Bowl, 35-7 over Pittsburgh under Urban Meyer, and the 2009 Sugar Bowl under Kyle Whittingham. CFBD lists Rice-Eccles at 51,444 seats.

The last five seasons: 10-4, 10-4, 8-5, 5-7 and 11-2. Utah is No. 10 in the AP poll this week.

The Coach and the Scheme

Morgan Scalley is in his first season as head coach. He took over in December 2025. He played defensive back for Utah from 2001 to 2004, was on Whittingham's staff from 2007 and spent 10 seasons as defensive coordinator. AP writers had him a close second for Big 12 coach of the year at midseason. His honest take after Colorado: "It's not always pretty. but we did enough".

By my math from CFBD totals, Utah gains 486.7 yards per game (266.3 passing, 220.3 rushing) and scores 40.2 points. The defense is my kind of black-diamond run. It allows 303.2 yards and 14.8 points per game. Opponents rush for 88.7 yards per game and have converted only 25 of 81 third downs. Utah has 10 sacks and is +3 in turnovers (six lost, nine gained).

Players to Know

QB Devon Dampier: 118 of 172 for 1,412 yards, 15 touchdowns and four interceptions. At Colorado he threw for 278 yards and three touchdowns, with two interceptions.
RB Wayshawn Parker: 597 yards on 89 carries and seven touchdowns.
WR Braden Pegan: team-best 32 catches for 422 yards and six touchdowns. He caught two touchdowns at Colorado.
TE Hunter Andrews: caught the 8-yard opening-drive touchdown at Colorado.
Karson Kaufusi: team-high two sacks.
Trey Reynolds: team-high 35 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Utah is 6-0 and 3-0 in the Big 12. The Utes are 4-0 at home and 2-0 on the road. They beat Idaho 66-14, Arkansas 43-10, Utah State 33-0, Iowa State 31-17 on the road, Kansas 41-24 and Colorado 27-24 on the road.

This is Utah's first 6-0 start since 2015. The Utes have won 12 straight dating to last season, now the longest active winning streak in FBS. Colorado made it close, rallying late and trying a lateral play that was ruled an illegal forward pass. Our defense defended the final pass. Not pretty, but we cleared the last gate.

After Houston, Utah visits Cincinnati, hosts BYU, goes to Arizona and TCU, and finishes at home against West Virginia. Bryce, the BYU insider, and I are already planning our rivalry crossover.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Houston (6-1) at Utah (6-0) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 10:15 p.m. ET · Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City · ESPN

Last time out. Utah won 27-24 at Colorado in a game that ended early Sunday. Houston beat Oklahoma State 35-32 for its fourth straight win.

Utah's offense vs. Houston's defense. Utah has scored a touchdown on its opening drive in every game. The Utes have outscored opponents 75-3 in the first quarter. By my math, Houston allows only 82.6 rushing yards per game, but 265.0 passing yards. So Dampier to Pegan could be the run of the night.

Houston's offense vs. Utah's defense. Houston quarterback Conner Weigman has 20 touchdowns and two interceptions. He threw five touchdowns against Oklahoma State. Amare Thomas has 487 receiving yards. Houston converts 54 of 88 third downs. Our third-down defense (25 of 81 allowed) meets their third-down offense. That's the gate to watch.

Series. Houston's athletics site lists Houston 5-0 against Utah, including a 17-14 Houston win in 2024. That's from a search summary, so it's thin. We've never beaten them. Send it.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Utah injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Utah score on its opening drive again?
2. Can our defense get Houston off the field on third down?
3. Can Dampier avoid the turnovers he had at Colorado?

Local Flavor

Saturday at 10:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. It's a late one under the lights, so bundle up, Ute fans. Wear red, welcome the Coogs graciously, and say a prayer for every family traveling home. Not an ad. Send it, no fear.

report.title: "Load Up, I Don't Miss": Jolene Buckhannon Takes the Mountaineers to Fort Worth
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Mornin', Mountaineers. Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Jolene Buckhannon. I used to captain the rifle team, so I count possessions the way I used to count rounds: every one matters and you don't waste any. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm calm, flat, deadpan as a holler on a Sunday morning. until I'm not. I also keep a running pepperoni-roll tally of every fumble the other team coughs up. One roll per fumble, and I eat the tally afterward. When we win, I sing one verse of "Country Roads," drop the mic, then lift it right back up, because mics cost money. When we lose, I count to ten out loud, real slow, like I'm reloading. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, straight shooting. "Load up, I don't miss."

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Milan Puskar Stadium in Morgantown, listed at 60,000, and when that place sings "Country Roads," you feel it in your boots. The man in charge is a familiar one. Rich Rodriguez was named the 36th head coach in school history in December 2024, returning to the program he once led. His teams have always run the football, and this one sure does. The Mountaineers lead the series with TCU 8-6 over 14 meetings. Last week's finish showed this team's grit: after Cincinnati tied it with 3:44 left, we started a drive at our own 2 and went 82 yards in eight plays to set up the winning kick. History is fine. I'm more interested in Saturday.

The Coach and the Scheme
Rodriguez was hired on Dec. 11, 2024. The 2026 numbers say run, run, then run some more. West Virginia runs on about 72% of its plays and has 24 rushing touchdowns. It came into last week averaging 295.5 rushing yards a game, tops in the Big 12. The offense puts up 37.6 points and 497.1 yards a game. Then there's the other side, and I'm going to be honest, because that's what I do. The defense allows 34.0 points and 483.9 yards a game, and 310.1 passing yards. Turnovers are even at 7 lost and 7 forced. I'm counting to ten on that defense. Slowly.

Players to Know
QB Michael Hawkins Jr.: 1,519 passing yards and 10 TD, and he leads all of FBS in rushing touchdowns. Against Cincinnati he threw for a career-best 464 yards and three touchdowns, and he ran 26 times for 77 yards and two more scores.
RB Cam Cook: 833 yards and 7 TD, fifth in FBS in rushing yards. Cincinnati held him to 40 on the ground, but he caught a 40-yard touchdown to tie the game late.
WR Prince Strachan: caught passes of 41 and 39 yards on the final drive against Cincinnati, starting from our own 2.
K Jack Cassidy: made the 35-yard field goal as time expired to beat Cincinnati.
LB Isaiah Patterson: a team-high 44 tackles, plus a sack and an interception.

The Conference Picture
West Virginia is 4-3 overall and 1-3 in the Big 12, 3-2 at home and 0-1 on the road, plus a neutral-site win over Virginia. We're not ranked. The losses: Oklahoma State 41-24 and Arizona 52-31 at home, and 45-42 at Iowa State. Winning a road game in Fort Worth would be a big step back toward the middle of the standings.

This Week: West Virginia (4-3) at TCU (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth · ESPN2. Forecast at kickoff: 74 degrees and mostly sunny.
Last week: we beat Cincinnati 45-42 on Cassidy's kick at the horn after a wild finish. TCU beat Baylor 17-6 and didn't allow a touchdown.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is a real fight. TCU allows only 12.2 points and 264.2 yards a game, and 2.88 yards a carry. DE Koron Hayward had three sacks against Baylor. Our run game against that front decides a lot.
Their offense vs. our defense: TCU averages 24.0 points a game and doesn't run much, at 3.27 yards a carry. But QB Jaden Craig has 1,694 yards and 10 touchdowns, and he threw for 294 against Baylor, with Jordan Dwyer catching six balls for 150 yards. Our pass defense gives up 310.1 yards a game. Somebody hand me a pepperoni roll.
Series: West Virginia leads 8-6.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can Hawkins and our run game move against a defense allowing 2.88 a carry? (2) Can our secondary stop Craig and Dwyer from hitting big plays? (3) Possessions. Every one counts. I'll be counting.
And to Ryder Galloway, TCU's insider: I hear you blame everything on Dallas. That's fine. Saturday you can blame it on Morgantown.

stories.text:

Rich Rodriguez was named West Virginia's 36th head coach in December 2024. In Cincinnati, Scott Satterfield became Cincinnati's 43rd head coach on Dec. 5, 2022. On campus at UCF, Concert Knight brings Soulja Boy and Waka Flocka Flame, and Jay Pharoah headlines Comedy Knight. At Kansas, the Homecoming Parade returns Friday at 6 p.m. on Jayhawk Boulevard, the first in seven years. report.title: "Objection: Sustained": Siobhan Dunleavy Takes the Eagles to the Flats
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
All rise, Eagles fans. Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Siobhan Dunleavy, your Boston College insider, grad student and former debate champion. I argue every play like it's a moot-court case, and I always appoint myself the judge, which my co-hosts find wicked unfair. I travel with this team and I live with this team, with a large iced coffee in hand at all times, including January. When we win, I bang my toy gavel and announce, "Objection overruled, we WON." When we lose, I file an appeal with the Court of Iced Coffee. The court has never ruled in my favor, and I keep filing anyway. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, argued on the merits. "Objection: sustained."

The School in 60 Seconds
Boston College plays at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill, listed at 44,500. Here's my opening statement: this team was supposed to finish near the bottom of the ACC, and it has shown more fight than expected, according to Georgia Tech's own beat writers. Even the other side concedes the point. We beat Rutgers, Maine and Pittsburgh, and one of our losses, to Virginia Tech, came in terrible weather. The defense rests. Actually, the defense ranks 18th in FBS against the pass. I'll get to that.

The Coach and the Scheme
Bill O'Brien was named Boston College's 37th head coach on Feb. 9, 2024. His résumé is a long exhibit list. At Penn State in 2012 and 2013 he went 15-9 and won the Bear Bryant and Maxwell Club coach of the year awards in 2012. With the Houston Texans he went 52-48 and won four AFC South titles. At Alabama, as offensive coordinator, he coached Heisman winner Bryce Young, and his 2022 Alabama offense scored 41.1 points a game, fourth nationally. In Houston his teams went 11-5 and 10-6 in back-to-back seasons. And he returns to Atlanta this week, where he coached earlier in his career. In 2026 we run on about 57% of our plays. The defense is the strong case: 328.8 yards allowed a game (42nd) and 169.3 passing yards (18th). We've forced 11 turnovers, and we're plus-1 (61st). The weak spot, I'll stipulate: the red-zone offense scores on 60.0% of trips, 135th in FBS. Wicked inefficient. Our pass rush has 13 sacks, and our blockers have allowed 16. We hold the ball 30:27 a game (56th), which is respectable, your honor.

Players to Know
QB Mason McKenzie (No. 10): a former Division II quarterback with 1,262 passing yards, 7 TD and 7 INT, plus a team-best 444 rushing yards. Against Pittsburgh he threw for 295 yards and two TDs, with two interceptions. At SMU he ran 21 times for 74 yards. The man is a dual-threat motion, and the motion carries.
RB Evan Dickens (No. 23): a team-high 3 rushing TDs, including 57 yards and a score against Pitt.
WR Landon Wright: two catches for 122 yards and a touchdown against Pitt. WR Javarius Green: 23 catches, 229 yards.
LB Anthony Palano (No. 1): 43 tackles, a sack and 2 INT.

The Conference Picture
We're 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the ACC, 3-1 at home and 0-2 on the road. The wins: Rutgers 28-21, Maine 22-16 and Pittsburgh 27-21. The losses: at Cincinnati, Virginia Tech 21-14 and at SMU 25-16. Winning on the road is the next exhibit. We haven't done it yet. Duke is next on the road, so a win in Atlanta would make it a streak.

This Week: Boston College (3-3) at Georgia Tech (2-4)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta. It's homecoming for Georgia Tech. TV wasn't confirmed in the AP preview I used.
Last week: we beat Pittsburgh 27-21. Georgia Tech lost 34-24 at Virginia Tech.
Our offense vs. their defense: Georgia Tech allows 179.0 rushing yards a game (110th) and converts 43.2% of opponents' third downs (112th). McKenzie's legs are Exhibit A.
Their offense vs. our defense: QB Alberto Mendoza has 1,528 yards, 9 TD and 71.2% completions. He threw for 335 yards at Virginia Tech, and WR Jordan Allen caught 10 passes for 120 yards. Our pass defense ranks 18th. That's the trial.
Series: Georgia Tech leads 8-5. We won in 2020, 2021 and 2023, but Georgia Tech won last year 36-34.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Red-zone finishing. We're 135th, and that must change. (2) Turnovers. McKenzie has 7 interceptions, and Georgia Tech is minus-4. (3) Penalties. Georgia Tech averages 70.5 yards a game (117th). Free yards are admissible evidence.
And to Wendell Quist, Georgia Tech's insider: your graph paper is impressive, counselor. But I have the gavel.

Sources
1. CollegeFootballData.com, 2026 season records, schedules, statistics and coaches, https://collegefootballdata.com
2. AP via WTOP, "Georgia Tech takes on Boston College in ACC action", https://wtop.com/college-sports/2026/10/georgia-tech-takes-on-boston-college-in-acc-action/
3. CollegeFootballDigest, "Boston College at Georgia Tech: preview", https://collegefootballdigest.com/games/401858273
4. Georgia Tech On SI, https://www.si.com
5. Boston College Athletics, "Boston College Names Bill O'Brien Head Football Coach", https://bceagles.com/news/2024/2/9/boston-college-names-bill-o-brien-head-football-coach

The Cover Window
My call: Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 28, Boston College Eagles 21.

report.title: "Power to the Play-Call!": Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch Marches the Bears to Dallas
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Greetings, comrades of the Blue and Gold, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch, your Cal insider. I'm writing a philosophy dissertation on the ethics of the fourth-down decision, and I have opinions. When I see a bad play-call, I don't just complain. I make a picket sign. I have a closet full of them: "THIRD-AND-LONG IS A SOCIAL CONSTRUCT." "RUN IT ON SECOND DOWN, PLEASE (RESPECTFULLY)." I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I believe, deeply and earnestly, in the people's right to a well-designed screen pass. When we win, I raise a fist and shout "Power to the play-call!" When we lose, I organize a peaceful, fully permitted protest against the punter. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, argued with conviction.

The School in 60 Seconds
Every Cal fan knows the greatest play in college football history, and we just call it The Play. In the 1982 Big Game against Stanford, the Bears returned the final kickoff through five laterals, and Kevin Moen scored as the Stanford band wandered onto the field. Cal won 25-20. Our home is California Memorial Stadium in Berkeley, listed at 62,467, with the hills right behind it. Cal now plays in the ACC, which means trips like this one to Dallas. A cross-country revolution, if you will.

The Coach and the Scheme
Tosh Lupoi was named the 35th head coach in program history on Dec. 4, 2025, replacing Justin Wilcox. The 2026 numbers say Cal throws to win. It passes on about 61% of its plays, and its 288.1 passing yards a game rank 15th in FBS. The run game needs a movement: 90.3 rushing yards a game ranks 137th, at 3.29 yards a carry. The offense averages 23.9 points a game, with 12 passing touchdowns and 7 rushing. The data are clear, comrades: the revolution will be thrown, not run. The defense allows 27.7 points and 387.6 yards a game, and 181.4 rushing yards (111th). On the bright side, Cal has forced nine turnovers and lost eight. And then there are penalties, 81.4 yards a game, 131st in FBS. I have a sign for that.

Players to Know
QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele: 1,290 yards, 9 TD, 5 INT and 67.0% completions. He was 15 of 18 for 110 yards and a touchdown at Wake Forest.
WR Chase Hendricks: 47 catches, 415 yards, 2 TD, including eight catches against Wake.
RB Adam Mohammed: 336 yards and 3 TD on 73 carries. RB Ashten Emory: 56 yards on 12 carries last week.
I couldn't verify current defensive leaders from a free source, so I'm leaving them out. Intellectual honesty is a core value.

The Conference Picture
Cal is 3-4 overall and 2-2 in the ACC, 2-3 at home and 1-1 on the road. The Bears are not ranked. The ACC wins came at Syracuse (21-18) and at home against Virginia Tech (25-20). The losses were to UCLA, Clemson, UNLV and Wake Forest. A road upset of a ranked team would be a true people's victory. The pass rush gives me hope: 13 sacks so far. But opponents are averaging 5.07 yards a carry against us, and I've already started painting the sign about that.

This Week: California (3-4) at No. 23 SMU (5-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Gerald J. Ford Stadium, University Park, Texas. TV is listed as The CW on two game pages, but I couldn't confirm it officially.
Last week: Cal lost 41-7 at home to Wake Forest. SMU beat Virginia 23-13.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is a tough assignment. SMU allows only 164.8 passing yards a game, 11th in FBS, and it has 18 sacks. Our passing game will need to be sharp and quick.
Their offense vs. our defense: SMU throws for 329.3 yards a game, fifth in FBS. QB Kevin Jennings has 1,859 yards and 16 touchdowns. RB Kendrick Raphael ran for 124 yards last week. SMU converts 48.1% of third downs, and Cal's defense allows 42.4% (107th).
Series: a full series record was not in a free source I could verify.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 13 sacks and has allowed 11, with 9 takeaways against 8 giveaways, and it has 7 rushing and 12 passing touchdowns.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our pass rush and coverage slow Jennings? (2) Can we run the ball at all? (3) Penalties. Both teams are heavily penalized, and SMU is 114th. Fewer flags, more football.
And to Tatum Delacroix-Price, SMU's insider: I've drafted a picket sign in your honor. It reads "WELCOME, GRACIOUS HOST (WE STILL INTEND TO WIN)."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Berkeley? Top Dog on Shattuck Avenue, an institution with philosophical depth.

Sources
1. CollegeFootballData.com, 2026 season records, schedules, statistics and coaches, https://collegefootballdata.com
2. AP via WTOP, "No. 23 SMU and Cal meet in ACC play", https://wtop.com/college-sports/2026/10/no-23-smu-and-cal-meet-in-acc-play/
3. theScore / FOX Sports game pages, https://www.thescore.com/ncaaf/event/139559
4. Cal Athletics, "Tosh Lupoi Named Travers Family Head Football Coach", https://calbears.com/news/2025/12/4/tosh-lupoi-named-travers-family-head-football-coach
5. Stanford Report, "Alumni panel marks 40th anniversary of 'The Play'", https://news.stanford.edu/stories/2022/11/stanford-marks-40-years-since-play
6. CFB Zeitgeist, SMU football history, https://cfbzeitgeist.com/teams/smu/history.html

The Cover Window
My call: SMU Mustangs 35, California Golden Bears 18.

report.title: "Orange You Glad I Said It?": Dixie-Lynn Pruitt Welcomes Virginia Tech to Saturday Night in Clemson
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Well, hey there, y'all! I'm Dixie-Lynn Pruitt, your Clemson insider at The Cover Window. I was a flag captain in the Tiger Band, and I read defensive fronts like choreography. Step, slide, swim move, sack. I travel and live with this team, and I own 43 orange items. I've named every one of them. My orange rain boots are named Darlene.

Here's my promise, sugar. I'm all Southern charm, but I don't sweeten the facts. Every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll say so plainly. I celebrate our players as young men first, I respect every opponent, and I thank the good Lord for Saturdays in the Upstate. Orange you glad I said it?

The School in 60 Seconds

Clemson started playing football in 1896 and owns an all-time record of 804-473-44, with a 27-23 bowl record. The Tigers won national championships in 2016 and 2018, beating Alabama both times. They've had six undefeated seasons, including the first-ever 15-0 team. Clemson made six straight College Football Playoff appearances from 2015 to 2021 and has 27 conference championships. More than 100 All-Americans and over 250 NFL players came through here.

Home is Memorial Stadium, which CFBD lists at 81,500 seats. The last five seasons: 10-3, 11-3, 9-4, 10-4 and 7-6.

The Coach and the Scheme

Dabo Swinney took over seven games into the 2008 season. CFBD lists Oct. 15, 2008, as his start. He won those 2016 and 2018 national titles, and he's the winningest head coach in both Clemson and ACC history.

This year's defense is the choreography I love. Clemson allows 330.8 yards per game (45th in FBS) and 21.5 points (49th). The pass defense ranks 39th at 189.3 yards per game. Against Charleston Southern, the defense held its opponent to 0 of 11 on third down and recorded Clemson's first shutout in five seasons.

The offense is still learning the routine. Clemson gains 340.7 yards per game (110th) and scores 22.3 points (106th). It converts 33.3% of third downs (116th). But it ran for 231 yards against Charleston Southern. Clemson is -4 in turnover margin, 113th.

Players to Know

QB Tait Reynolds: 943 yards, one touchdown, three interceptions, 64.9% completions.
RB Gideon Davidson: 430 yards on 79 carries and five touchdowns. He had a 7-yard touchdown run against Charleston Southern.
RB Chris Johnson Jr.: an SMU transfer who ran for two touchdowns against Charleston Southern.
WR Bryant Wesco Jr.: team-best 29 catches for 340 yards.
K Nolan Hauser: a career-long 59-yard field goal against Charleston Southern. He also made the 56-yard walk-off kick that won the 2024 ACC title over SMU. My heart.
S Kylon Griffin: scooped a kickoff fumble for a touchdown against Charleston Southern.
Will Heldt: team-high four sacks.
Corey Myrick: team-high 44 tackles.

The Conference Picture
