report.title: "I Also Passed That Exam": Harrison Wexley-Moore IV Takes the Blue Devils to Charlottesville
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Good evening. I'm Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, your Duke insider at The Cover Window. I'm pre-law, pre-med and, frankly, pre-everything. I know the playbook and the LSAT, and I travel and live with this team. Did I mention I also passed that exam? I did. Whichever one you're thinking of.

Here's my academic honor code for this column. Every fact has a citation, like any good thesis. If I don't know something, I'll mark it "incomplete" rather than invent an answer. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I give thanks to God for the gift of a Friday night game. Durham, class is in session.

The School in 60 Seconds

Duke plays in the ACC and has won 18 conference championships: eight in the ACC and ten in the Southern Conference. The program counts 53 All-Americans, ten ACC Players of the Year and three Pro Football Hall of Famers. Home is Wallace Wade Stadium in Durham, which CFBD lists as built in 1929 with 40,004 seats.

For decades the university de-emphasized football, starting around the mid-1960s. Then came a renaissance under David Cutcliffe from 2008 to 2021, including Duke's first Coastal Division title in 2013, clinched with a win over North Carolina. The last five seasons show the progress: 3-9 in 2021, then 9-4, 8-5, 9-4 and 9-5. Four straight winning seasons. I've written longer papers on less.

The Coach and the Scheme

Manny Diaz is our head coach. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 7, 2023. He was head coach at Miami from 2019 to 2021 and defensive coordinator and linebackers coach at Penn State in 2022 and 2023. He's also coached at Mississippi State, Louisiana Tech, Texas, Middle Tennessee, NC State and Florida State. That's a doctoral program in defense.

The 2026 defense earns honors. Duke allows 292.7 yards per game (21st in FBS) and 16.0 points (19th). The run defense ranks 18th at 92.5 yards per game. Opponents convert only 29.2% of third downs, 9th in FBS.

The offense controls the clock. Duke gains 442.7 yards per game (37th) and runs for 209.5 (22nd). It averages 33:17 of possession per game, 13th in FBS. Scoring sits at 31.7 points per game (52nd). The one failing grade: 73.8 penalty yards per game, 123rd. Even honor students get detention sometimes.

Players to Know

QB Walker Eget: 1,229 yards, 8 TD, 2 INT, 62.8% completions. Against North Carolina he went 24 of 38 for 249 yards with a touchdown and an interception.
RB Nate Sheppard: 820 rushing yards on 138 carries, eight touchdowns. He also leads the team in receiving with 28 catches for 259 yards and four scores. Against UNC he ran 20 times for 77 yards and caught 11 passes for 98 yards and a touchdown. He's a double major.
WR Jared Richardson: three catches for 55 yards against North Carolina.
Kevin O'Connor: team-high three sacks.
Nick Morris Jr.: team-high 33 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Duke is 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the ACC. The Blue Devils started 4-0: 17-3 over Tulane, 31-27 at Illinois, 35-7 over Stanford and 62-7 over William & Mary. Then came two close losses: 28-25 at Georgia Tech and 24-20 to North Carolina. Both were decided by four points or fewer.

The rest of the ACC syllabus is demanding. After Virginia come Boston College at home, NC State and Miami on the road, Clemson at home and Wake Forest on the road. A win Friday gets Duke back to.500 in league play.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Duke (4-2) at Virginia (4-3) · Friday, Oct. 23, 7:00 p.m. ET · Scott Stadium, Charlottesville, Va. · ESPN

Last time out. Duke lost 24-20 to North Carolina on Oct. 17. Virginia lost 23-13 at SMU the same day.

Duke's offense vs. Virginia's defense. Virginia's pass defense is strong, allowing 173.9 yards per game (25th). Its run defense is softer, at 152.7 yards per game (88th). My thesis: hand it to Sheppard, keep the clock moving, and let our 33:17 possession average do the rest. Virginia is +5 in turnover margin (15th), so Eget must protect the ball.

Virginia's offense vs. Duke's defense. Beau Pribula has thrown 13 touchdowns with one interception. AP lists 1,217 passing yards and ESPN 1,211, so that's conflicting. Da'Shawn Martin has five touchdown catches. Virginia converts just 33.0% of third downs (120th) and scores on 74.1% of red-zone trips (124th). Our third-down defense ranks 9th. Peer review says that's a favorable matchup for our side.

Series. CFBD shows Virginia 8-2 against Duke from 2016 to 2025. Humbling. I've cited it anyway, because honesty is the whole point.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Duke injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Sheppard and the run game exploit Virginia's 88th-ranked run defense?
2. Can our 9th-ranked third-down defense keep Virginia off schedule?
3. Can Duke trim those 73.8 penalty yards per game?

Prescott, the Virginia insider, refuses to say "campus." I'll refrain from charging him tuition for the word "Grounds."

Local Flavor

Charlottesville on a Friday night in late October should be a lovely setting, and Scott Stadium seats 61,500. Virginia's intro notes its stadium sits right next to the World Heritage Site portion of the university. Bring a coat, bring your manners, and bring your loudest Duke cheer. Not an ad.

report.title: "Graph Paper Doesn't Lie": Wendell Quist Plots a Homecoming Win
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Greetings, Jackets fans, and welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Wendell Quist, your Georgia Tech insider. I'm an aerospace-engineering grad, and I model the trajectory of every punt, every pass and every kickoff. Everything is physics. I mean everything, including my relationship with the coaching staff, which I describe as a stable orbit. I travel with this team and I live with this team, with graph paper in my pocket. When we win, I calculate the exact trajectory of the winning kick and cheer in decimals. When we lose, I re-run the simulation 10,000 times looking for the bug. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, plotted to scale. "Graph paper doesn't lie."

The School in 60 Seconds
Georgia Tech claims national championships in 1917, 1928 and 1990. Home is Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field, listed at 55,000, in the middle of Midtown Atlanta. Last season was an excellent trajectory: Georgia Tech went 9-4 and 6-2 in the ACC. This season the curve has dipped. We're 2-4. But Saturday is homecoming, and I've done the math on homecoming energy. Dimensionless, but large.

The Coach and the Scheme
Brent Key was hired on Nov. 29, 2022. In 2026 the offense is pass-friendly: 254.7 passing yards a game (44th) and only 127.2 rushing yards (112th), with runs on about 48% of plays. Nine passing touchdowns and nine rushing. The defense is the variable to fix. It allows 392.2 yards a game (110th) and 179.0 rushing yards (110th). Turnovers, too: we've lost 7 and forced only 3, a minus-4 margin (113th). Penalties average 70.5 yards a game (117th). And the clock: we hold the ball only 27:47 a game, 120th in FBS. Three variables. Solve for all three, and the output improves.

Players to Know
QB Alberto Mendoza: 1,528 yards, 9 TD, 4 INT, 71.2% completions. At Virginia Tech he went 29 of 38 for 335 yards and two TDs. A very accurate launch angle. Against Duke he completed 23 of 30 for 218 yards and a TD.
WR Jordan Allen: 38 catches, 432 yards, 1 TD, including 10 catches for 120 yards last week.
RB Justice Haynes (No. 22): 462 yards and 3 TD on 87 carries. RB Trelain Maddox: 96 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries at Virginia Tech.
DT Tawfiq Thomas (No. 95): 32 tackles and 2 sacks.

The Conference Picture
We're 2-4 overall and 1-2 in the ACC, 2-2 at home and 0-2 on the road. The losses: Colorado 14-13 at home (one point! I've re-run that simulation more than 10,000 times), Tennessee, at Stanford 34-27 and at Virginia Tech 34-24. The wins: Mercer 44-11 and Duke 28-25. At Virginia Tech we fell behind 24-3, then cut it to seven early in the second half before falling short. The comeback curve was there. The finishing slope wasn't. Georgia Tech On SI listed the recurring bugs: turnovers, missed field goals and explosive plays allowed on defense. Three bugs. Every one is fixable in the code.

This Week: Boston College (3-3) at Georgia Tech (2-4)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Bobby Dodd Stadium · Homecoming. TV wasn't listed in the AP preview I used.
Last week: we lost 34-24 at Virginia Tech. Boston College beat Pittsburgh 27-21.
Our offense vs. their defense: Boston College's pass defense ranks 18th, allowing 169.3 yards a game. But its run defense allows 159.5 (95th). The geometry says run the ball, then throw off it once the safeties step up.
Their offense vs. our defense: BC QB Mason McKenzie is a former Division II quarterback and a running threat, with 444 rushing yards. He's also thrown 7 interceptions. Boston College scores on only 60% of red-zone trips (135th), and our red-zone defense ranks 44th.
Series: Georgia Tech leads 8-5. Last year we won 36-34 at Boston College, snapping a three-game losing streak in the series. Before that, BC won 48-27 in 2020, 41-30 in 2021 and 38-23 in 2023. The data has variance. Let's keep the most recent data point.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Run defense against McKenzie. (2) Turnovers. We're minus-4, and BC is plus-1. (3) Penalties. Seventy yards a game is a lot of drag. (4) Possession. BC holds the ball 30:27 a game, and we hold it 27:47. Shorter possessions for us means fewer chances, so third downs on both sides matter.
And to Siobhan Dunleavy, Boston College's insider: I respect the gavel. But the gavel obeys gravity too, counselor.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Near campus? Tin Lizzy's Taco Americana on 12th Street Northeast in Midtown. Or Dua Vietnamese, same building.

The Conference Picture
Miami is 6-0 overall and 4-0 in the ACC, 3-0 at home and 3-0 on the road. The Canes are No. 1 in the AP and Coaches polls. They're one of six unbeaten teams in FBS. Road wins at Stanford, Wake Forest and Clemson (41-13) show this team travels well. Next up is a trip to North Carolina.

This Week: Pittsburgh (5-2) at No. 1 Miami (6-0)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Hard Rock Stadium · ESPN. Forecast: 80 degrees, a 44% chance of storms and an 18 mph northeast wind. Typical South Florida, mi gente.
Last week: Miami beat Florida State 43-35. Pitt lost 27-21 at Boston College.
Our offense vs. their defense: Pitt has the best run defense in FBS, allowing 57.3 yards a game. But its pass defense ranks 115th at 249.0 yards a game. Mensah to Toney, baby. "The ball's in the air, Toney's there!"
Their offense vs. our defense: Pitt lost starting QB Mason Heintschel for the season to a torn ACL. Corey Dailey started at BC and went 11 of 25 with two interceptions, and Narduzzi hasn't named a starter for this game. WR Cataurus Hicks is a big-play threat, with 135 yards last week.

And to Yinz Bertolucci, Pitt's insider: much respect, hermano. Enjoy the sunshine. And grab some cafecito, it's on me.

report.title: "Wolfpack, Howl!": Ruff Pegram Fires Up the Grill for a Late Night in Palo Alto
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hey there, Pack! I'm Rutherford Pegram, but everybody calls me Ruff, and I'm your NC State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Wake County native and an engineer, and I grill at the same Carter-Finley lot every home game. I explain schemes with grill thermometers. A defense running at 225 degrees? That's low and slow. An offense at 450? That's a sear.

Here's my promise. I'm loud, I'm warm and I'm gloriously dramatic, but I don't cook the numbers. Every stat here has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you the thermometer's still reading. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for good friends, good food and good football. I howl once per segment, no more, no less. Wolfpack, howl!

The School in 60 Seconds

NC State plays in the ACC and was a founding member in 1953, after years in the Southern Conference. The Wolfpack has won seven conference championships and played in 34 bowl games, winning 17. Since 1966, home has been Carter-Finley Stadium, the largest college football stadium in North Carolina. CFBD lists it at 58,000 seats. In 2010 the school brought back a live mascot, a Tamaskan dog named Tuffy. Good boy.

The last five seasons have been steady heat: 9-3, 8-5, 9-4, 6-7 and 8-5. Four winning seasons in five years. The grill stays lit in Raleigh.

The Coach and the Scheme

Dave Doeren is in his 14th season. He's coached NC State since 2013, and CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 1, 2012. Before Raleigh he was head coach at Northern Illinois in 2011 and 2012. He was an assistant at Wisconsin, Kansas, Montana and USC, and he played at Drake.

The offense is cooking at the right temperature. NC State gains 426.3 yards per game (43rd in FBS) and scores 33.0 points (44th). It throws for 257.8 yards (41st) and runs for 168.5 (54th). It converts 51.1% of third downs, 15th in FBS, and holds the ball 32:52 per game (20th).

The defense needs adjusting. It allows 363.8 yards per game (78th), 230.3 passing yards (99th) and 27.7 points (104th). After the Wake Forest loss, Doeren said the defense wasn't playing with discipline in the second half. He also said the team needed to get some injured players back. He didn't name them in that AP report, so I won't either.

Players to Know

QB CJ Bailey: 1,507 yards, nine touchdowns, four interceptions, 66.7% completions. Against Wake Forest he completed his first 16 passes. AP's recap lists him 28 for 40 for 241 yards, and the preview lists 28 of 39, so that's conflicting.
WR Keenan Jackson: team-best 27 catches for 400 yards and five touchdowns. Nearly 15 yards a grab. That's a sizzle.
RB Jayden Scott: 358 yards on 62 carries and four touchdowns.
RB Davion Gause: seven carries and five catches against Wake Forest.
LB Popo Aguirre: team-high 54 tackles. After the Wake loss he said, "We got to be a little bit more disciplined". A leader's answer.
Elijah Satchell: team-high three sacks.

The Conference Picture

NC State is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the ACC. The Wolfpack are 3-1 at home and 0-2 on the road. They lost the opener 34-8 at Virginia, then beat Richmond 73-0. They lost 35-31 at Vanderbilt. Then came wins over App State (41-31) and Louisville (31-28) before the 38-14 loss to Wake Forest.

This is NC State's first road game since Sept. 19. After Stanford, the Pack gets three straight at home: California, Duke and Syracuse. Then come trips to Florida State and North Carolina. Three wins in the final six would reach six.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

NC State (3-3) at Stanford (3-4) · Friday, Oct. 23, 10:30 p.m. ET · Stanford Stadium, Stanford, Calif. · ESPN

Last time out. NC State led Wake Forest 14-10 at halftime on Oct. 10, then gave up the game's final 31 points in a 38-14 loss. The Wolfpack ran for only 15 yards. Then came a week off to regroup. Stanford beat FCS Elon 34-7 on Oct. 17.

NC State's offense vs. Stanford's defense. The grill is hot here. Stanford allows 452.0 yards per game (134th) and 36.6 points (133rd). Its run defense allows 196.6 yards per game (125th). Opponents convert 47.8% of third downs (131st), and Stanford's red-zone defense allows scores on 96.4% of trips, 136th. Bailey to Jackson, Scott on the ground, and keep that 32:52 possession average going.

Stanford's offense vs. NC State's defense. Stanford gains 342.9 yards per game (106th) and scores 18.3 points (127th). Its run game ranks 131st at 103.4 yards per game. But Micah Ford just ran for 179 yards and four touchdowns against Elon, and Davis Warren has 1,630 passing yards. Our pass defense ranks 99th, so we have to tighten the coverage.

Series. NC State Athletics lists one meeting: a 59-28 Wolfpack win in Raleigh on Nov. 2, 2024. This is the first trip to Stanford.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. Doeren mentioned injured players after the Wake game but named no one in that report. Status unknown.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can the Pack bounce back from allowing 31 straight points to Wake Forest?
2. Can our run game get going against Stanford's 125th-ranked run defense?
3. Can our pass defense slow Warren?

Local Flavor

It's a 10:30 p.m. Eastern kickoff, so set the coffee maker, Raleigh. Out in Palo Alto it's an early-evening game. If you're traveling, wear your red with pride and be a gracious guest. If you're home, I'd fire up a late-night grill, but safely and quietly. The neighbors will understand. Not an ad. Wolfpack, howl! (That's my one.)

report.title: "Carolina Blue, Through and Through": Ainsley Pemberton Welcomes the Orange to Kenan
report.byline: Our Chapel Hill debutante with a kinesiology PhD introduces herself and previews North Carolina vs. Syracuse.
report.text:
Ainsley Pemberton · North Carolina Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Carolina blue, through and through. Hello, darlings, I'm Ainsley Pemberton. I grew up in Chapel Hill, I came out at a debutante ball, and then I went and earned a PhD in kinesiology, because a lady should understand exactly how a linebacker generates force. I travel with the Tar Heels and I live with the Tar Heels, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with Southern charm and, I'll confess, a gentle little roast of a certain school eight miles down the road. I don't even need Duke to be on the schedule. When we win, I graciously thank our guests, then whisper "Carolina blue, through and through." When we lose, I say "Carolina blue skies will return," and I absolutely refuse to cry on camera. Mostly.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Tar Heels, often just "Carolina," represent the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in the ACC. North Carolina has played in 37 bowl games and won three Southern Conference titles and five ACC titles. Home is Kenan Stadium, opened in 1927 and listed at 50,500 seats, and darling, there is no prettier place in college football on an autumn evening. The last five seasons: 6-7, a lovely 9-5 in 2022, 8-5, 6-7 and 4-8 last year.

The Coach and the Scheme
Bill Belichick is our head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2024. This team wins with defense and discipline. We allow 19.2 points a game, 34th in FBS, our red zone defense ranks 22nd, and we average just 33.7 penalty yards a game, 5th in the country. Darling, that's manners. Xavier Lewis has 7 sacks. The offense is a work in progress: 329.7 yards a game (117th) and 116.2 rushing yards (120th). And opponents convert 43.3% of third downs against us (113th). Elegant, mostly. Not always. But a team that wins close games on the road, two weeks in a row, has learned how to finish, and finishing is the most elegant skill of all.

Players to Know
QB Billy Edwards Jr.: 94 of 157 for about 1,260 yards (1,259 per AP), 9 TD, 5 INT. A first-year Tar Heel, he said he felt "the weight of this game" against Duke.
WR Jordan Shipp: 33 catches, 441 yards. He caught the first touchdown at Duke and said, "That's why you come to Carolina, for a rivalry game like that".
RB Jaylen McGill: 12 carries for 75 yards and the game-winning 24-yard touchdown with 1:53 left at Duke. RB Benjamin Hall: the season leader with 283 yards.
TE Jelani Thurman: caught the 12-yard fourth-and-4 conversion on the winning drive.
DL Xavier Lewis: 7 sacks. LB Derek McDonald: team-high 55 tackles. DB Greg Smith III: 3 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
North Carolina is 4-2 and 2-1 in the ACC. We beat TCU 15-10 at a neutral site, East Tennessee State 35-3, Pittsburgh 21-17 on the road and Duke 24-20 on the road. We lost at Clemson 28-20 and to Notre Dame 37-26. After Syracuse, No. 1 Miami comes to Kenan on Oct. 31. I won't do standings math, darling. I'll only say it's a lovely time to be wearing blue.
And the Victory Bell is home. After the Duke game, our players rushed across the field to reclaim it. AP says the bell kept ringing so loudly outside the locker room it nearly interrupted Coach Belichick's press conference. I'd call that the sweetest music in the Triangle. And two years ago in that same stadium, Duke rallied from 20 points down to beat us. This time, darling, the bell came home with us, where it belongs. Duke had won eight straight against in-state opponents before we arrived. Bless their hearts.

This Week: Syracuse (2-4) at North Carolina (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill · ACC Network.
Last week: we beat Duke 24-20. We led 17-0, went more than 41 minutes without scoring, then marched 78 yards for the winner. On fourth-and-4 from our own 28, Coach said, "I wasn't punting again. I wanted to take our best shot". Syracuse lost to Louisville 34-26.
Their offense vs. our defense: Syracuse throws for 291 yards a game (12th), and Umari Hatcher has 784 receiving yards, including 224 last week. Darling, we must know where he is at all times. Their quarterback situation is unsettled; no Week 8 ACC report yet.
Our offense vs. their defense: Syracuse's pass defense ranks 43rd and its run defense 64th. Syracuse is also 138th in penalty yards. Free yards are always welcome at Kenan.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
Availability: no North Carolina availability report found as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Containing Hatcher. (2) Getting off the field on third down. (3) Staying the most disciplined team on the field.
To Nico Calabrese, Syracuse's insider: a snowbank shaped like a block S? How charming. We have dogwoods. Come in April, darling.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
In Chapel Hill for the game? La Residence on West Rosemary Street is a lovely sit-down supper.

report.title: "Dat's a Yinz Problem, Not a Yikes Problem": Yinz Bertolucci Takes the Panthers to No. 1 Miami
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hey, Pitt fans! How's it goin', n'at? Welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Dominic Bertolucci, but around here they call me Yinz. I played linebacker back in a little steel-mill town, and these days I grade every tackle this team makes on my personal scale. It goes from "yinz," meaning a beautiful, textbook form tackle, all the way down to "yikes," meaning somebody whiffed. I blow a homemade whistle for every grade. The producers love it. Okay, they tolerate it. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I holler "Yinz SEE that?!" so loud the board op flinches. When we lose, I eat a sandwich with the fries right inside it, in total silence. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, loud and lovable.

The School in 60 Seconds
Pitt has a national championship in its trophy case: the 1976 Panthers went 12-0, and running back Tony Dorsett won the Heisman Trophy that season. Then in 2021 under Pat Narduzzi, Pitt won its first ACC championship, beating Wake Forest 45-21 in the title game. Home is Acrisure Stadium, listed at 68,400, right there on the North Shore. The series with Miami is a long one, 43 meetings, though the Hurricanes lead 30-12-1. Dat's history, n'at.

The Coach and the Scheme
Pat Narduzzi was hired on Dec. 16, 2014. Defense is his thing, and this year's group is a "yinz" all the way. Pitt allows only 57.3 rushing yards a game, the best in FBS, and 16.4 points a game, 23rd. Opponents average 2.02 yards a carry. The Panthers have 15 sacks and 11 takeaways. The offense puts up 32.9 points and 450.1 yards a game, and its 284.6 passing yards rank 17th. Now for the "yikes" section: 81.7 penalty yards a game, which ranks 132nd. And the pass defense allows 249.0 yards a game, 115th.

Players to Know
QB Mason Heintschel: 1,304 yards, 14 TD and only 1 INT. But he tore the ACL in his right knee at Virginia Tech and is out for the season. Prayers for a full recovery, kid.
QB Corey Dailey: made his first start at Boston College and went 11 of 25 for 193 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Narduzzi said he hasn't decided who will start at Miami.
RB Damon Ferguson Jr.: 438 yards and 3 TD on 83 carries, including 119 yards at BC.
WR Cataurus Hicks: 26 catches, 500 yards, 4 TD. He had five catches for 135 yards and a touchdown at BC.
DB Cruce Brookins: a team-high 46 tackles. That's a whole lotta "yinz."

The Conference Picture
Pitt is 5-2 overall and 2-2 in the ACC, 4-1 at home and 1-1 on the road. We're not ranked. We started 5-0, including a 35-33 win at Virginia Tech, but then lost 21-17 at home to North Carolina and 27-21 at Boston College. Beating No. 1 on the road would flip this whole season around.

This Week: Pittsburgh (5-2) at No. 1 Miami (6-0)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens · ESPN. Forecast: 80 degrees, a 44% chance of storms and an 18 mph wind.
Last week: Pitt lost 27-21 at Boston College. Miami beat Florida State 43-35.
Our offense vs. their defense: this is a big ask. Miami allows only 58.5 rushing yards a game, second in FBS, and 14.0 points a game. Opponents average 2.34 yards a carry. We'll need Hicks to make plays down the field.
Their offense vs. our defense: Miami scores 48.5 points a game, the most in FBS, and it's the only team that has scored 30 or more in every game. QB Darian Mensah has 18 touchdowns, one interception and an 80.8% completion rate. WR Malachi Toney has 758 yards. Our run defense is the best in the country, but Miami's passing game is the real test for a pass defense ranked 115th.
Series: Miami leads 30-12-1.
Availability: Heintschel is out for the season. Pitt hasn't named a starting quarterback. One unofficial site reports Miami LB Max Buchanan out after knee surgery, but I could not confirm it officially. I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Who plays quarterback for Pitt, and can he protect the ball? (2) Can our secondary slow down Mensah and Toney? (3) Penalties. We can't give a team this good free yards.
And to Javi Castillo, Miami's insider: nice sunglasses, buddy. Bring 'em to Pittsburgh sometime and we'll find out if they work in the snow.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Oakland? Hello Bistro on Forbes Avenue for a quick game-day bite.

report.title: "Pony Up or Sit Down, Sugar": Tatum Delacroix-Price Welcomes Cal to the Hilltop
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, hello, Mustangs, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Tatum Delacroix-Price, your SMU insider. I run a little boutique in Highland Park. I know every handshake in this town, and I know every nickel blitz in our playbook. I travel with this team and I live with this team. Now, fair warning: I grade the other team's sideline outfits on air, and darling, I am never wrong. Polished, sweet as can be, and then savage. That's the Dallas way. When we win, I pop imaginary confetti and declare the Boulevard officially iconic. When we lose, I put on bigger sunglasses. Much bigger. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with just a little sparkle. My motto: "Pony up or sit down, sugar."

The School in 60 Seconds
SMU has a Heisman Trophy winner: Doak Walker in 1948. Then came the Pony Express era, with Eric Dickerson and Craig James in the backfield. More recently, the Mustangs played in the 2024 ACC championship game and lost to Clemson 34-31 on a field goal at the end. Home is Gerald J. Ford Stadium in University Park, listed at 32,000, an intimate little jewel box of a stadium. And it's spotless. This season that little jewel box has been perfect: four home games, four wins. Bring your sunglasses, Cal. The regular ones, I mean.

The Coach and the Scheme
Rhett Lashlee was hired on Nov. 30, 2021. The 2026 numbers say SMU lives through the air: 329.3 passing yards a game, fifth in FBS, and 470.8 total yards, 14th. It averages 32.7 points a game and converts 48.1% of third downs (23rd). The defense is a showstopper against the pass, allowing just 164.8 yards a game, 11th in FBS. SMU has 18 sacks and has allowed only 7. Overall the defense allows 303.0 yards a game, 26th in FBS. It's a bit softer against the run (138.2 yards a game, 61st) than the pass. Two things that need a tailor: 69.0 penalty yards a game (114th), and a red-zone offense that scores on 81.5% of trips (95th).

Players to Know
QB Kevin Jennings: 1,859 yards, 16 TD, 5 INT and 72.9% completions. He was 23 of 36 for 246 yards and two touchdowns against Virginia, with no interceptions.
RB Kendrick Raphael: 542 yards and 6 TD on 99 carries, including 124 yards against the Cavaliers.
WR Yamir Knight: 35 catches, 418 yards, 2 TD. WR Yannick Smith: 5 catches for 87 yards last week.
I couldn't verify defensive leaders from a free source as of Oct. 18, so I'm not naming names. A lady doesn't guess.

The Conference Picture
SMU is 5-1 overall and 3-1 in the ACC, 4-0 at home and 1-1 on the road. The Mustangs are No. 23 in the AP poll and No. 20 in the Coaches Poll. The only loss came at Louisville, 41-31, and the wins include a 27-24 road win at Florida State. Next comes a trip to Syracuse. Keep winning and SMU stays in the ACC title conversation. At home the Mustangs have outscored visitors 138-63. Fair warning, though: the turnover column needs work, with 9 lost and only 6 forced. Darling, we do not hand out free gifts at this boutique.

This Week: California (3-4) at No. 23 SMU (5-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET (11 a.m. CT) · Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Two game pages list the TV as The CW, but I couldn't confirm that officially.

Our offense vs. their defense: Cal allows 27.7 points a game and 181.4 rushing yards (111th). Raphael should have room to run. Cal's defense also allows 42.4% on third down (107th).
Their offense vs. our defense: Cal throws on about 61% of its plays for 288.1 yards a game (15th). QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele has 1,290 yards. Our pass defense ranks 11th. That's the matchup. And Cal's offense has been held to 10 points or fewer in two of its last four games. Our pass rush, with 18 sacks, will want to make it three. Cal's sideline outfits? I'll review those live, sugar.
Series: a full series record wasn't in a free source I could verify.

report.title: "Let's Pivot to the Run Game": Iggy Yamamoto-Ross Ships the Cardinal's NC State Preview
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hey, team! I'm Ignatius Yamamoto-Ross, Iggy for short, your Stanford insider at The Cover Window. I've founded three apps that failed and built one Cardinal model that works. I travel and live with this team, and I describe football in startup jargon. A two-minute drill is a sprint. A punt is a pivot. A blowout loss is a learning opportunity, and we've had a few.

Here's my mission statement. I disrupt hype, not facts. Every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll mark it "pending data." I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I'm grateful to God for a Friday night under the lights at home. Let's ship it.

The School in 60 Seconds

Stanford has fielded teams nearly every year since 1892. The school dropped football in favor of rugby from 1906 to 1917. Fun branding history: the teams were the "Cardinal," then mostly the "Cardinals," then the "Indians" from 1930 to 1972, then "Cardinals" again, and finally "Cardinal" since the 1982 season. A student vote in 1975 to become the "Robber Barons" wasn't approved. Best rejected rebrand ever.

Stanford now plays in the ACC after many years in the Pac-12. Home is Stanford Stadium, which CFBD lists as built in 2006 with 50,424 seats. The last five seasons were rough: four straight 3-9 years from 2021 to 2024, then 4-8 in 2025. This is a rebuild, and we're in the early funding rounds.

The Coach and the Scheme

Tavita Pritchard is the new head coach, hired for the 2026 season. CFBD records his hire date as Nov. 28, 2025. He's a Stanford alum and former quarterback. He played on the 2007 team that upset USC, widely considered one of the biggest upsets in college football history. He started coaching as a Stanford graduate assistant in 2010 and became offensive coordinator in 2018. From 2023 to 2025 he coached quarterbacks for the Washington Commanders. Founder returns to the company. Love that story.

The 2026 product is still in beta. Stanford gains 342.9 yards per game (106th) and scores 18.3 points (127th). The passing game is solid at 239.4 yards per game (59th). The run game sits at 103.4 yards (131st).

The defense needs a full refactor. It allows 452.0 yards per game (134th), 36.6 points (133rd) and 196.6 rushing yards (125th). Opponents convert 47.8% of third downs (131st) and score on 96.4% of red-zone trips (136th). On the bright side, Stanford's 2026 recruiting class ranks 37th, per CFBD. Pipeline matters.

Players to Know

QB Davis Warren: 1,630 yards, seven touchdowns, two interceptions, 60.3% completions. Against Elon he went 27 of 39 for 279 yards and a touchdown.
RB Micah Ford: 529 yards on 114 carries and eight touchdowns. Against Elon he ran 19 times for 179 yards and four touchdowns, including an 81-yard score. His four touchdowns tied Stanford's single-game record. He also scored three times against Hawai'i in the opener. That's product-market fit.
WR Caden High: team-best 21 catches for 337 yards and three touchdowns.
WR JonAnthony Hall: five catches for 70 yards against Elon.
WR Sedrick Irvin: a 27-yard touchdown catch against Elon.
Jay Green: team-high 43 tackles.
Gabe Kaminski: team-high two sacks.

The Conference Picture

Stanford is 3-4 overall and 1-3 in the ACC. The Cardinal are 3-1 at home and 0-3 on the road. The wins: 37-27 over Hawai'i, 34-27 over Georgia Tech and 34-7 over Elon. The losses: 45-6 to Miami, 35-7 at Duke, 57-3 at Wake Forest and 58-7 at Notre Dame.

The home splits are the key metric. All three wins came at Stanford Stadium, and Friday is home again. After that come Louisville, Virginia Tech and California on the road, then SMU at home.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

NC State (3-3) at Stanford (3-4) · Friday, Oct. 23, 7:30 p.m. PT / 10:30 p.m. ET · Stanford Stadium, Stanford, Calif. · ESPN

Last time out. Stanford beat FCS Elon 34-7 on Oct. 17. Pritchard said he challenged the team at halftime after a flat first half. The Cardinal outscored Elon 34-7 from the second quarter on. NC State lost 38-14 to Wake Forest on Oct. 10 and then had a bye.

Stanford's offense vs. NC State's defense. Here's our growth opportunity. NC State's pass defense allows 230.3 yards per game (99th), and it allows 27.7 points (104th). Warren to High through the air, Ford on the ground. Wake Forest scored the game's final 31 points against NC State. Their coach said the defense lacked discipline in the second half.

NC State's offense vs. Stanford's defense. This is our biggest risk. NC State converts 51.1% of third downs (15th) and holds the ball 32:52 per game (20th). CJ Bailey has 1,507 passing yards, and Keenan Jackson has 400 receiving yards. Our third-down defense (131st) and red-zone defense (136th) need a big upgrade. One opening: NC State ran for only 15 yards against Wake Forest.

Series. NC State Athletics lists one meeting, a 59-28 NC State win in Raleigh on Nov. 2, 2024. First time in Palo Alto.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Stanford injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Ford keep running like he did against Elon?
2. Can our defense get off the field on third down?
3. Can Stanford stay perfect at home?

Ruff, the NC State insider, explains football with grill thermometers. I explain it with pitch decks. Let's call it a partnership.

Local Flavor

It's a Friday night in Palo Alto, with the game starting at 7:30 p.m. Pacific. Bring a jacket, bring a friend and welcome the Wolfpack fans who flew across the country. I'll share confirmed pregame spots before kickoff. Not an ad. Let's pivot to the run game, and let's go Card.

report.title: "A Foot of Snow of a Take": Nico Calabrese Heads South to Chapel Hill
report.byline: Our lake-effect survivor introduces himself and previews Syracuse at North Carolina.
report.text:
Nico Calabrese · Syracuse Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
That's a foot of snow of a take. Hey, how ya doin', I'm Nico Calabrese, born and raised in the Salt City, survivor of more lake-effect winters than I can count. I travel with the Orange and I live with the Orange, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with full upstate bluster. My scale for every play is feet of snow. A two-yard run? A dusting. A long touchdown? Twenty inches overnight, school's canceled. A turnover by us? That's the plow truck sliding into the ditch. When we win, I'll yell "That's a foot of snow of a WIN!" so loud they'll hear me in Utica. When we lose, I shrug: "Just a lake-effect squall." Then I grab a salt potato and get back to work.

The School in 60 Seconds
Syracuse plays in the ACC, and here's a fact I love: it's the only FBS school in New York in a Power Four conference. Home is the JMA Wireless Dome on campus, also known as "The Loud House", opened in 1980 and listed at 49,057 seats. The last five seasons: 5-7, 7-6, 6-7, a big 10-3 in 2024 and 3-9 last year. That 10-3 year? That was the Blizzard of '93, the one we still talk about.

The Coach and the Scheme
Fran Brown is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 28, 2023. This offense throws it: 291 passing yards a game, 12th in FBS, and 449.7 total yards (29th). We hold the ball 33:59 a game, 5th in FBS. The defense is solid against the pass, 191.8 yards allowed (43rd), with 15 sacks. The problem? Penalties. We average 98 penalty yards a game, 138th in the country. That's driving the Thruway in a whiteout with the brakes on. And in the red zone we score on 78.1% of trips, 111th. Clean those two up and this is a different team.

Players to Know
WR Umari Hatcher: 50 catches, 784 yards, 7 TD. Against Louisville he caught 13 passes for 224 yards and a touchdown. That's three feet overnight, folks. Lake Ontario is jealous.
QB Malachi Nelson: threw for 315 yards and two touchdowns, with two interceptions, against Louisville. The local paper's headline says he left that game with another injury.
QB Steve Angeli: the season passing leader, 57 of 104, 731 yards, 4 TD, 5 INT. He was out for the Louisville game.
RB Tylik Hill: 431 yards on 80 carries. RB Ahmad Miller: 123 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries against Louisville.
LB Chris D'Appolonia: team-high 42 tackles. LB Keyshawn Johnson: 4 sacks. DB Davien Kerr: 3 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Syracuse is 2-4 and 0-4 in the ACC. We beat New Hampshire 66-3 and won a 42-41 thriller at UConn. The four league losses: California 21-18, at Pittsburgh 27-13, at Virginia 28-25 and Louisville 34-26. Three of those were one-score games. After Chapel Hill, No. 23 SMU comes to the Dome on Oct. 31. I'm not doing standings math today. I'm just saying this team has been close, real close.
The close ones: a field goal against Cal, a field goal at Virginia, one score against Louisville. That's a whole winter of near-misses on the plow route.
Why I love this team anyway: because it keeps moving the ball no matter who's under center. Hatcher is on pace for a monster year. Miller ran hard last week. And the team that went 10-3 two years ago had a coach named Fran Brown too. Upstate folks don't quit when it snows. We shovel out, and we go to work.

This Week: Syracuse (2-4) at North Carolina (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill · ACC Network.
The quarterback question: I can't tell you who starts. The ACC hasn't posted a Week 8 availability report yet. Angeli was out last week, Nelson played and then, per the local paper's headline, left with another injury. I'll update you when the report comes out. I won't guess.
Our offense vs. their defense: North Carolina allows opponents to convert 43.3% of third downs (113th), and its pass defense is 69th. Hatcher should get his chances. But the Tar Heels' red zone defense ranks 22nd, and that's where we've struggled.
Their offense vs. our defense: North Carolina averages 329.7 yards a game (117th) and 116.2 rushing yards (120th). Jordan Shipp leads them with 441 receiving yards. Our defense can win this matchup.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
What decides it: (1) Who's healthy at quarterback. (2) Penalties; they average 33.7 penalty yards a game (5th), we average 98. (3) Red zone finishing.
To Ainsley Pemberton, North Carolina's insider: Carolina blue is nice, but have you ever seen a snowbank shaped like a block S? Come visit in February.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Back home? Varsity Pizza on South Crouse Avenue has been feeding Orange fans on the hill for a long time. Get a slice.

report.title: "As Mr. Jefferson Would've Charted It": Prescott Ashby-Lowell Welcomes Duke to the Grounds
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Good evening, and welcome. I am Prescott Ashby-Lowell, your Virginia insider at The Cover Window. I'm a fourth-generation Wahoo, I wear a bow tie on game days, and I travel and live with this team. I refer to our university's home only as "the Grounds." Anyone who uses the other word owes me a nickel, payable in bagels.

A word on method. As Mr. Jefferson would've charted it, every claim deserves evidence, so every number here carries a source. If I don't know a thing, I'll say so plainly. I celebrate our players as fine young people first, I respect every opponent, and I'm grateful to God for autumn in Charlottesville. Hoos fans, the architecture is coming along nicely.

The School in 60 Seconds

Virginia football was established in 1887. Home is Scott Stadium, capacity 61,500, which sits next to the World Heritage Site portion of the university, including the historic Academical Village. CFBD lists the stadium as built in 1931.

History, you say? UVA helped shape the modern game's ethics, eligibility and safety rules. The program put together 28 straight winning seasons after its first in 1887 and won 12 Southern championships in 20 seasons. In 1915 Virginia became the first Southern program to beat Yale, 10-0, at the Yale Bowl.

The recent record is a renovation in progress: 6-6, 3-7, 3-9, 5-7, then a splendid 11-3 in 2025. Eleven wins. I had it framed.

The Coach and the Scheme

Tony Elliott is head coach. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 10, 2021. Before Virginia he coached at Clemson from 2011 to 2021, finishing as associate head coach, offensive coordinator and tight ends coach. He won the 2017 Broyles Award as the top assistant in college football. He also played wide receiver at Clemson from 2000 to 2003.

This season the defense is the cornerstone. Virginia allows 326.6 yards per game (39th) and 19.7 points (38th). The pass defense is excellent at 173.9 yards per game (25th). The run defense is a wing under repair, at 152.7 yards per game (88th). UVA is +5 in turnover margin, 15th in FBS, and we're disciplined, at 49.3 penalty yards per game (38th).

The offense gains 362.9 yards per game (90th) and scores 30.0 points (65th). Two numbers need attention: a 33.0% third-down rate (120th) and a 74.1% red-zone scoring rate (124th). Even Monticello had a few rooms under construction.

Players to Know

QB Beau Pribula: 13 touchdown passes, one interception, 65.4% completions. AP lists 1,217 passing yards and ESPN lists 1,211, so that's conflicting. At SMU he went 13 of 22 for 137 yards and ran for a touchdown.
RB Jekail Middlebrook: 396 yards on 81 carries, three touchdowns. He ran 14 times for 59 yards at SMU.
WR Da'Shawn Martin: five touchdown catches on 15 receptions. AP lists 231 yards and ESPN 225, another small conflict. AP also spells his first name "Dashawn".
DL Matthew Fobbs-White: team-high four sacks.
Jacobie Henderson: team-high 38 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Virginia is 4-3 overall and 2-2 in the ACC. On the Grounds, the Cavaliers are a perfect 4-0. They beat NC State 34-8, Norfolk State 59-3, Delaware 42-3 and Syracuse 28-25. The losses came 38-27 to West Virginia at a neutral site, 38-7 at Florida State and 23-13 at SMU. Not one loss on the Grounds, and I intend to keep it that way.

Next come Wake Forest on the road, then California and North Carolina at home, and the finale at Virginia Tech.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Duke (4-2) at Virginia (4-3) · Friday, Oct. 23, 7:00 p.m. ET · Scott Stadium, Charlottesville, Va. · ESPN

Last time out. Virginia fell 23-13 at SMU on Oct. 17. Duke lost 24-20 to North Carolina the same day.

Virginia's offense vs. Duke's defense. Duke's defense is formidable. It allows 292.7 yards per game (21st) and 92.5 rushing yards (18th). Opponents convert only 29.2% of third downs, 9th in FBS. So Pribula must win early downs, and our red-zone trips must end in touchdowns. Duke's red-zone defense ranks 42nd, a bit more forgiving.

Duke's offense vs. Virginia's defense. Nate Sheppard has 820 rushing yards and also leads Duke in receiving. Duke runs for 209.5 yards per game (22nd) and holds the ball 33:17 per game (13th). That tests our 88th-ranked run defense. Walker Eget has 1,229 passing yards, but our pass defense ranks 25th. Our +5 turnover margin against Duke's 123rd-ranked penalty yardage could tilt a close game.

Series. CFBD shows Virginia 8-2 against Duke from 2016 to 2025. We respect Duke's recent rise all the same.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Virginia injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can our run defense slow Sheppard?
2. Can Virginia convert third downs against Duke's 9th-ranked defense?
3. Can the Hoos turn red-zone trips into touchdowns?

Harrison, the Duke insider, will mention his degrees. I'll mention our 1915 win at Yale.

Local Flavor

Friday night on the Grounds is a fine thing. Wear your orange and blue, stroll past the Academical Village if you have time, and greet our Duke guests kindly. I'll share confirmed pregame stops before kickoff. Not an ad. Wahoowa.

report.title: "Exit Light, Enter Stats": Ruthanne Dellinger Marches the Hokies Into Clemson
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hey, Hokie Nation! I'm Ruthanne Dellinger, your Virginia Tech insider at The Cover Window. I grew up on a farm outside Blacksburg, and I was a drum major in the Corps of Cadets. I analyze defense like it's a lunch-pail job, because it is. I travel and live with this team, and I jump, audibly, every time our defense makes a stop. My producer has stopped apologizing for it.

Here's my promise. I've got mountain-girl spunk, but I don't stretch the truth. Every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you straight. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for country roads, crisp fall air and Hokie football. Exit light, enter stats.

The School in 60 Seconds

Virginia Tech has played football since 1892 and has won more than 700 games. The Hokies have appeared in 33 bowl games, including the 2000 BCS National Championship Game. They play in the ACC after previously competing in the Big East. Home is Lane Stadium in Blacksburg, with seating for more than 65,000. ESPN voted it No. 2 on its 2007 list of the "Top 20 Scariest Places to Play". CFBD lists 65,632 seats.

The last five seasons were a climb: 6-7, 3-8, 7-6, 6-7 and 3-9. That's why this 5-2 start has me jumping already.

The Coach and the Scheme

James Franklin is in his first season as head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Nov. 17, 2025. He coached Vanderbilt from 2011 to 2013 and Penn State from 2014 until 2025. That's a lot of big Saturdays on his résumé.

His offense has come out swinging. Virginia Tech gains 451.3 yards per game (25th in FBS) and scores 37.1 points (23rd). The passing game ranks 11th at 301.6 yards per game. The Hokies hold the ball 32:12 per game (28th).

The defense is a lunch-pail crew against the run. It allows just 87.4 rushing yards per game, 10th in FBS. Opponents convert 32.6% of third downs (29th). The pass defense needs work, at 227.3 yards per game (95th). The Hokies allow 21.1 points per game (46th). One worry: Virginia Tech is -4 in turnover margin, 113th.

Players to Know

QB Ethan Grunkemeyer: 1,984 yards, 15 touchdowns, two interceptions, 72.6% completions. Against Georgia Tech he went 15 of 22 for 250 yards and three touchdowns, plus a rushing touchdown.
WR Que'Sean Brown: team-best 46 catches for 616 yards and three touchdowns. Against Georgia Tech he caught six passes for a career-high 182 yards, the sixth-most in a game in school history. He also had a 63-yard punt return. AP's preview prints his name as "Sean Brown".
RB Jeffrey Overton Jr.: 613 yards on 103 carries and four touchdowns. He caught a 26-yard touchdown against Georgia Tech.
K John Love: a 24-yard field goal against Georgia Tech.
Aycen Stevens: team-high seven sacks. I jump for every one of those.
Keon Wylie: team-high 37 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Virginia Tech is 5-2 overall and 2-2 in the ACC. The Hokies are 3-1 at home and 2-1 on the road. They started 4-0: 73-3 over VMI, 44-21 over Old Dominion, 35-26 at Maryland and 21-14 at Boston College. Then came two losses that came down to the final play, 35-33 to Pittsburgh and 25-20 at California. Last week they beat Georgia Tech 34-24.

AP calls the next stretch the hardest part of the season: three of the next four games are on the road, at Clemson, SMU and Miami. Stanford and Virginia visit Lane Stadium to close it out.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Virginia Tech (5-2) at Clemson (4-2) · Saturday, Oct. 24, 7:00 p.m. ET · Memorial Stadium, Clemson, S.C. · ESPN

Last time out. Virginia Tech beat Georgia Tech 34-24 on Oct. 17 after leading 24-3 at halftime. Clemson shut out FCS Charleston Southern 37-0 the same day.

Virginia Tech's offense vs. Clemson's defense. Clemson's pass defense is good, allowing 189.3 yards per game (39th). Its run defense allows 141.5 yards (70th). So Overton on the ground can open things up for Grunkemeyer and Brown. Clemson's defense held Charleston Southern to 0 of 11 on third down, but that was an FCS opponent. Ball security is a must: we're -4 in turnovers.

Clemson's offense vs. Virginia Tech's defense. Clemson gains 340.7 yards per game (110th) and scores 22.3 points (106th). Its third-down rate is 33.3% (116th). Tait Reynolds has 943 passing yards and one touchdown. Gideon Davidson has 430 rushing yards. Our 10th-ranked run defense should be ready. Our pass defense (95th) has to tighten up against Bryant Wesco Jr.

Series. Clemson leads the series 24-12-1 and has won seven straight since 2011, per TigerNet and Clemson's game notes. Clemson won 24-14 in Blacksburg in 2024. Those figures are thin, but the streak is real enough to sting.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Virginia Tech injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Grunkemeyer keep his efficiency on the road?
2. Can the Hokies win the turnover battle after a -4 start?
3. Can our run defense make Clemson one-dimensional?

Dixie-Lynn, the Clemson insider, owns 43 orange items. I own one maroon drum major's baton, and it's plenty.

Local Flavor

It's a Saturday night in Clemson, 7 p.m. on ESPN. Clemson's team runs down the hill in its traditional game-day entrance, so expect noise. Wear maroon and orange, cheer with class, and say a prayer for safe travels. Not an ad. Exit light, enter stats.

report.title: "Roll the Quad": Eloise Brightman-Rowe Takes the Open Week
report.byline: Our insider (archetype: glam preppy Winston-Salem academic) introduces the Wake Forest Demon Deacons during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Eloise Brightman-Rowe · Wake Forest Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Roll the Quad! I'm Eloise Brightman-Rowe, and I'm your Wake Forest insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a debate-team darling and Wake grad who rolls the Quad and roasts bad tackling. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. Fair warning about my habit: debate-club roasts of bad tackling. On the podcast, my segment is called Debate Club. The show card describes it like this: a polite debate-team roast of bad tackling. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Demon Deacons have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium in Winston-Salem, NC, built in 1968 with a listed capacity of 31,500. The fight song is "O' Here's to Wake Forest", per Wikipedia. The band is the The Spirit of the Old Gold & Black, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 11-3, 8-5, 4-8, 4-8 and 9-4, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: NC State (5-5 in 10 meetings), Duke (4-5 in 9 meetings), Clemson (0-9 in 9 meetings), Syracuse (5-3 in 8 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 39 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about rolling the Quad; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jake Dickert leads the Demon Deacons; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 18, 2024. Through 7 games, Wake Forest scores 37.4 points a game and allows 19.4. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 53% of its plays, gaining 155.6 rushing yards and 290.3 passing yards a game. That's a balanced menu. On third down, Wake Forest converts 48.9% of the time and opponents convert 42.6%. The defense has 18 sacks and 49 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 3 giveaways against 4 takeaways. Penalties cost 84.1 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 57 points against Stanford on Oct. 3, 2026, and 2 of the 7 games were decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, Wake Forest has outscored opponents by a combined 126 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB Gio Lopez (passing leader): 140/207, 1947 yards, 17 TD, 1 INT.
RB Ty Clark III (rushing leader): 70 carries, 328 yards, 4 TD.
WR Carlos Hernandez (receiving leader): 49 catches, 720 yards, 4 TD.
On defense, LB Vincent Firenze leads with 49 tackles; DL Langston Hardy has 5.5 sacks; DL Dallas Afalava has 1 interception.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Wake Forest is 6-1 overall, 2-1 at home and 4-0 away. In ACC play the Demon Deacons are 4-1, which sorts them No. 2 of 17 by record. Miami sits on top at 4-0 in league games. Right around us: Miami (4-0) and SMU (3-1). The top of the table: Miami (4-0), Wake Forest (4-1), SMU (3-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. The Demon Deacons are No. 17 in the latest AP poll in our data. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Wake Forest this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Demon Deacons beat California on the road, 41-7. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, vs. Virginia, in Allegacy Financial Stadium, Winston-Salem, with a kickoff time to be announced. Virginia comes in at 4-3. After that, CFBD lists vs. Merrimack (Nov. 7), at SMU (Nov. 14), at Georgia Tech (Nov. 21), vs. Duke (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Demon Deacons come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Roll the Quad!

stories.title: Coaches Worth a Second Look
stories.text:
Start at the top. Mario Cristobal was hired at Miami in December 2021. His Canes are 3-0 on the road this season, with wins at Stanford, Wake Forest and Clemson. Pat Narduzzi has led Pitt since December 2014. At Clemson, Dabo Swinney took over seven games into the 2008 season. He won national titles in 2016 and 2018 and is the winningest coach in Clemson and ACC history. In Chapel Hill, Bill Belichick leads North Carolina; CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2024. Fran Brown leads Syracuse; CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Nov. 28, 2023. Out West, Dave Doeren is in his 14th season at NC State, after coaching Northern Illinois in 2011 and 2012. Tavita Pritchard is in his first season as Stanford's head coach. Tosh Lupoi was named Cal's 35th head coach on Dec. 4, 2025, replacing Justin Wilcox. In Atlanta, Brent Key was hired at Georgia Tech on Nov. 29, 2022. Bill O'Brien became Boston College's 37th head coach on Feb. 9, 2024. Rewind it and watch the sidelines. That's where the stories are.

report.title: "Copy That, and Beat Navy": Capt. Thaddeus Rourke Deploys the Black Knights to Tulsa
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Attention on deck. I'm Captain Thaddeus Rourke, retired, your Army insider at The Cover Window. I spent my career as a logistics officer, so I read every option play like a supply-chain plan: right item, right place, right time. I travel and live with this team, and my boots are always shined.

Standing orders for this column. Every fact is sourced, like a properly filed report. If I don't know something, I'll log it as "status unknown" and move on. I celebrate these cadets as young leaders first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God daily for the men and women who serve. Discipline is a love letter to your teammates. Copy that, and beat Navy.

The School in 60 Seconds

Army football represents the United States Military Academy and plays at Michie Stadium in West Point, New York. Wikipedia lists capacity at 36,000 and CFBD at 38,000, so I'm flagging that as conflicting. The Black Knights play in the American Conference.

The honors roll is long. Army claims five national championships, including AP titles in 1944 and 1945. The academy has three Heisman winners: Doc Blanchard (1945), Glenn Davis (1946) and Pete Dawkins (1958). It counts 24 players and four coaches in the College Football Hall of Fame and 37 consensus All-Americans.

The last five seasons: 9-4, 6-6, 6-6, a magnificent 12-2 in 2024 and 7-6 in 2025. Mission accomplished more often than not.

The Coach and the Scheme

Jeff Monken has commanded since 2014, and CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 24, 2013. He was head coach at Georgia Southern from 2010 to 2013. Before that he worked under Paul Johnson as running backs coach and special teams coordinator at Georgia Southern, Navy and Georgia Tech. Yes, Navy. We've forgiven him.

The scheme is the option ground game, and the numbers prove it. Army runs for 357.5 yards per game, first in FBS. It throws for 69.2 yards per game, 137th, which is entirely by design. The Black Knights score 34.8 points per game (39th) and convert 95.2% of red-zone trips (11th). They hold the ball 34:42 per game, 3rd in FBS. And they're disciplined, at 35.8 penalty yards per game (6th).

The defense is our soft spot. Army allows 368.0 yards per game (84th) and 20.0 points (40th). Opponents convert 52.1% of third downs, 124th in FBS. That needs fixing on the double.

Players to Know

QB Cale Hellums: 719 rushing yards on 129 carries and 13 touchdowns, plus 358 passing yards with three touchdowns and one interception. Against FAU he ran 25 times for 195 yards and five touchdowns, including a 58-yard score. Outstanding execution.
RB Jake Rendina: seven carries for 86 yards against FAU, including a 61-yard touchdown.
RB Samari Howard: a 30-yard touchdown run on the game's second snap against FAU.
RB Bryson Luter: a 69-yard touchdown run on Army's final possession against FAU.
WR Brady Anderson: team-best seven catches for 102 yards. In this offense, every catch is a special operation.
Elijah Walton: team-high 42 tackles, and an interception on the first snap against FAU.
Victor Afolabi: team-high three sacks.

The Conference Picture

Army is 4-2 overall and 3-1 in the American. The Black Knights are 3-1 at home and 1-1 on the road. They beat Bryant 59-3, lost 28-24 to South Florida, won 21-17 at Temple and lost 31-29 at Louisiana Tech. Then came a 20-17 win over Tulane and the 56-24 win over Florida Atlantic. Both losses were by four points or fewer.

After Tulsa, Army goes to Memphis on Oct. 31. Then come Air Force and East Carolina at home, a trip to Rice, and Navy at a neutral site on Dec. 12. Beat Navy.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Army (4-2) at Tulsa (4-3) · Friday, Oct. 23, 8:30 p.m. ET · Skelly Field at H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa, Okla. · ESPN2

Last time out. Army beat Florida Atlantic 56-24 at West Point on Oct. 17. The Black Knights scored on their first seven possessions, ran for 479 yards on 60 carries and threw only two passes. Tulsa beat Rice 38-17 in Houston the same day.

Army's offense vs. Tulsa's defense. The supply chain looks open. Tulsa allows 191.6 rushing yards per game, 121st in FBS. Our ground game ranks first. One caution: Tulsa is +11 in turnover margin, 3rd in FBS. Ball security is the mission. Every pitch must arrive like a supply drop, on time and on target.

Tulsa's offense vs. Army's defense. Baylor Hayes threw for 249 yards and three touchdowns at Rice, and Oran Singleton Jr. leads Tulsa with 474 receiving yards. Tulsa converts 31.3% of third downs (125th), while our defense allows 52.1% (124th). Something has to give. Kyran Duhon has six sacks for Tulsa, so protection matters on our rare passes.

Series. Army's athletics site lists Tulsa ahead 2-1 all-time. Tulsa's own site lists only the last two games, 1-1, so that's conflicting. Army won 49-7 at Tulsa in 2024. Last November, Tulsa rallied from 11 points down to win 26-25 at West Point on a 27-yard field goal with 12 seconds left. We remember.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Army injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Army's top-ranked run game hold the ball against Tulsa's +11 turnover margin?
2. Can our defense improve on its 52.1% third-down rate?
3. Can Army win the possession battle, 34:42 against 27:31?

Local Flavor

Friday night in Tulsa, far from the Hudson. If you're traveling, wear your black and gold with pride and thank any service member you see. The Corps travels in spirit even when cadets can't. I'll share confirmed gathering spots for Army families before kickoff. Not an ad. Copy that, and beat Navy.

report.title: "Hoist the Colors": Bart Quidley Sails the Pirates West to Memphis
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Ahoy, shipmates! I'm Bartholomew Quidley, Bart to my friends, and I'm your East Carolina insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Pitt County native, and my family has tailgated the same spot in Greenville since before I could walk. I wear a purple tricorn hat for big games only, and I grade every opposing mascot's costume. Memphis, your tiger had better be brushed.

Here's my promise. Every number I give you has a source behind it. If I don't know something, I'll say so plainly rather than make up a tale. I respect every opponent, and I celebrate our players as people first. Arrr-guably the best fans anywhere are reading this right now. Hoist the colors.

The School in 60 Seconds

East Carolina played its first season in 1932. The Pirates have won seven conference championships and eleven bowl games, and they've produced 20 All-Americans. Four players have their jerseys retired. Except for the 1999 Miami game, the Pirates have played every home game at Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium since 1963. CFBD lists the stadium's capacity at 50,000 on natural grass. Today ECU plays in the American Conference at the FBS level.

The last five seasons have had real swells and troughs: 7-5 in 2021, 8-5 in 2022, a rough 2-10 in 2023, then 8-5 in 2024 and 9-4 in 2025. That 9-4 finish last year is the best of the stretch.

The Coach and the Scheme

Blake Harrell is the captain on this deck. Wikipedia lists him as head coach since the 2024 season, and CFBD records his hire date as Nov. 27, 2024. Fun timing: Wikipedia lists his birthday as Oct. 20, 1979, so the man turns a year older two days before kickoff. My public sources don't detail his earlier coaching stops, so I won't guess at them.

What does the 2026 ship look like? The defense is the sturdier hull. ECU allows 326.5 yards per game (38th in FBS) and 187.5 passing yards per game (34th). It gives up 139.0 rushing yards (63rd) and 23.8 points per game (72nd). The defense has also returned two interceptions for touchdowns this season.

The offense is still finding its wind. The Pirates gain 339.5 yards per game (112th) and score 23.5 points per game (99th). They run for 155.8 yards a game (69th) and throw for 183.7 (114th). report.title: "Surf's Up on Tempo, Babe": Kaia Brightwater Welcomes Rice to Boca
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hey, Owls, welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Kaia Brightwater, your Florida Atlantic insider. I used to play beach volleyball here in Boca Raton, and now I analyze offenses like swell reports. Choppy means three-and-outs. Clean means long, smooth drives. And a closeout? That's when the whole wave crashes at once, which is how a defense feels when we go tempo. I travel with this team and I live with this team. The beachy talk is real, but so is the analysis underneath it, I promise. When we win, it's "a perfect swell day" and a slow-motion hair flip. When we lose, I sigh "flat water" and post a sunset anyway, because it's still Boca. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, sun and stats. "Surf's up on tempo, babe."

The School in 60 Seconds
Florida Atlantic football is young, and it was built by a legend. Howard Schnellenberger founded the program from scratch and served as its first head coach. Home is Flagler Credit Union Stadium (Howard Schnellenberger Field) in Boca Raton, listed at 29,419, close enough to the Atlantic to smell the salt on a breezy Saturday. The Owls play in the American Athletic Conference, and the series with Rice is as even as a glassy morning: 3-3. The recent history is a lot of close finishes: FAU won in 2025 (24-17 per the school) and 17-14 in 2022, and Rice won 24-21 in 2023. Back in 2016, FAU won 42-25. I love a program that's still writing its story.

The Coach and the Scheme
Zach Kittley was named the Hagerty Family Head Football Coach on Dec. 2, 2024. The 2026 numbers say this offense is all about the air. FAU throws for 307.3 yards a game with 15 passing touchdowns. It averages 35.0 points and 422.3 yards a game. The run game is choppier, at 3.29 yards a carry. On defense, the waves are bigger than I'd like. FAU allows 31.5 points a game and 5.43 yards a carry. On the bright side, the Owls have forced eight turnovers and lost six.

Players to Know
QB Caden Veltkamp: 1,743 yards and 15 TD. At Army he went 33 of 48 for 318 yards and three touchdowns. That's a clean swell, and the kind of day I want every Saturday.
WR Kelby Valsin: 47 catches, 601 yards and 6 TD, including 7 catches, 89 yards and a touchdown at Army.

I couldn't verify other season leaders from a free source, so I'm keeping the list short and accurate.

The Conference Picture

The wins came against Navy (38-30), FIU (16-10), UL Monroe and Texas Southern, and the losses were at Florida and at Army. Staying perfect at home keeps FAU in the conference mix. At home the Owls are outscoring opponents 120-50, which is my kind of clean, glassy water. On the road it's been choppier, with 66 points allowed at Florida and 56 at Army. Good news, babe: this one's at home.

This Week: Rice (1-6) at Florida Atlantic (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Flagler Credit Union Stadium · ESPNU. Surf report: 81 degrees, a 52% chance of showers and storms, and a 20 mph northeast wind. Choppy, babe.

Our offense vs. their defense: Rice allows 29.0 points a game and 188.7 passing yards. Veltkamp and Valsin should find room, as long as the wind cooperates.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the wave to watch. Rice runs on 79% of its plays, and QB Jacurri Brown has 668 rushing yards, including 154 against Tulsa. Our run defense allows 5.43 a carry, and Army just ran all over us. Everyone has to stay in their lane. One positive: Rice has lost 10 turnovers and forced just 4, and its passing game averages only 78.7 yards a game. So if our front gets Rice behind schedule, that's when the closeout wave comes.
Series: tied 3-3. FAU won the last meeting in 2025, though the score is in conflict: 27-21 per, 24-17 in Houston per FAU Athletics, and we trust the school.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 8 sacks and has allowed 11, with 8 takeaways against 6 giveaways, and it has 8 rushing and 15 passing touchdowns.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our defense stop a run-heavy offense one week after Army scored 56? (2) Can Veltkamp handle the wind? (3) Tempo. If we go fast and stay clean, it's a perfect swell day.

report.title: "That Drive Had a Backbeat": Otis Delaney-Crum Tunes Up the Tigers for Thursday Night
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Well, hello there, friends. I'm Otis Delaney-Crum, your Memphis insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Memphis native. I play blues guitar on weeknights and sing bass in the gospel choir on Sunday mornings, and to me football and music are the same thing. A good drive has a groove. A great one has a backbeat.

Here's how I work. I hum a riff whenever the Tigers score, and I rank opposing fight songs on my personal soul scale. I'm smooth and I laugh loud, but I don't play loose with facts. Every number I give you has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you I'm still tuning that string. I celebrate our players as young men first, and I respect every opponent who walks into our house. Go Tigers Go.

The School in 60 Seconds

Memphis started playing football in 1912. Since then the Tigers have won more than 500 games and appeared in 17 bowl games. For a long stretch, football lived in the shadow of the university's basketball program. Things changed starting with coach Justin Fuente's tenure. As of the end of the 2025 season, Memphis has been bowl-eligible every year since 2014. That's more than a decade of steady rhythm.

The Tigers play in the American Conference at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium. CFBD lists it at 58,325 seats, built in 1965, with an artificial surface. The last five seasons went 6-6, 7-6, 10-3, 11-2 and 8-5. That 11-2 in 2024 is a record I play on repeat.

The Coach and the Scheme

Charles Huff is new on the bandstand. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 8, 2025. Wikipedia says he coached Southern Miss in 2025 and Marshall from 2021 to 2024. Before that he was associate head coach and running backs coach at Alabama, with stints at Mississippi State and Penn State. He's known as one of the top recruiters in college football. He was born in 1983, so he's a young bandleader.

Huff's first Memphis offense really swings. The Tigers gain 512.6 yards per game, 6th in FBS. They run for 237.7 yards per game (8th) and throw for 274.9 (25th). They score 35.4 points per game (35th). They're disciplined too, with 44.3 penalty yards per game (22nd).

The defense is a mixed song. It allows 372.4 yards per game (89th) and 172.9 rushing yards (104th). But it shines when it matters. Opponents convert just 31.5% of third downs (20th), and the red-zone defense ranks 6th at 66.7%. Points allowed sit at 22.3 per game (58th).

Players to Know

QB Marcus Stokes: 1,841 yards, 18 TD, 6 INT, 66.9%. At Tulane he threw for 306 yards and two touchdowns on 20-of-37 passing. AP's preview counts three interceptions in that game and the AP recap counts four, so that count is conflicting. He also lost two fumbles there.
RB Jaylin Carter: 780 yards on 112 carries, eight touchdowns. He ran 23 times for 135 yards at Tulane. That's the bass guitar of this offense.
WR Hunter Tipton: 22 catches, 380 yards, five touchdowns.
WR Stonka Burnside: seven catches for 151 yards at Tulane, including a 76-yard touchdown. AP's preview prints a different name for this receiver; the roster and the AP recap say Stonka Burnside, so I'm going with that.
DL Elijah Kinsler: team-high 4.5 sacks.
LB Mike Montgomery: team-high 47 tackles.
K Philippe Laforge: opened the Tulane game with a 44-yard field goal.

The Conference Picture

Memphis is 5-2 overall and 2-1 in the American. The Tigers are 3-0 at home and 2-2 on the road. The wins: 27-21 at UNLV, 42-24 over Arkansas State, 45-21 over UT Martin, 59-8 at Charlotte and 38-13 over UAB. The losses came at Boise State (38-20) and at Tulane (31-17).

Both losses were on the road. Thursday brings the Tigers home, where they're unbeaten. Next comes Army at home on Oct. 31, then South Florida, Navy and Temple to finish.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

East Carolina (3-3) at Memphis (5-2) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:30 p.m. ET · Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis, Tenn. · ESPN2

Last time out. That one hit a sour note. Tulane forced six turnovers and won 31-17. Memphis led 10-3 after Burnside's long touchdown. Tulane answered with three field goals, a touchdown pass and a 76-yard interception return at halftime. ECU fell 30-17 in overtime at UAB on Oct. 15 after leading 14-0.

Memphis' offense vs. ECU's defense. ECU's defense is solid. It allows 326.5 yards per game (38th) and 187.5 passing yards (34th). Its run defense is more ordinary, at 139.0 yards per game (63rd). I want Carter and the ground game setting the tempo, then Stokes finding Tipton deep. Most of all, I want the ball held tight. ECU's defense has two interception-return touchdowns this year.

ECU's offense vs. Memphis' defense. ECU gains 339.5 yards per game (112th) and scores 23.5 points (99th). TJ Engleman Jr. has 490 rushing yards and ran for 104 at UAB. Our run defense ranks 104th, so he's the man to watch. But ECU converts only 31.3% on third down (125th), and its red-zone rate ranks 125th. Our third-down and red-zone defenses rank 20th and 6th. That's harmony.

Series. ECU's athletics site lists the Pirates ahead 18-8 all-time. ECU won last year's meeting 31-27 in Greenville on Nov. 15, 2025. That's from a search summary, so I'll call it thin. Either way, the Pirates hold the bragging rights until we earn them back.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Memphis injury news, so I won't speculate.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Memphis protect the ball after six turnovers at Tulane?
2. Can the run defense (104th) slow Engleman?
3. Can the red-zone defense (6th) keep forcing field goals?

Local Flavor

Thursday night football in Memphis is a show. On ESPN2, the whole country gets to hear the Bluff City sing. I'll post confirmed spots for game-night barbecue before kickoff. Not an ad. Come early, come loud, love your neighbor, and if you hear a man humming a riff after a touchdown, come say hello.

report.title: "Steady as She Goes": Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather Welcomes the Mean Green to Annapolis
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good afternoon, and welcome aboard The Cover Window. I'm Commander Annabel Merriweather, retired, your Navy insider. I spent my career as a surface warfare officer, and I read an option play the way I read a nautical chart: depth, current and where the rocks are hiding. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I speak in nautical terms, and I cannot be stopped. When we win, I say, "Anchors aweigh!" and ring a ship's bell. When we lose, I say, "Steady as she goes," and plot a new course. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with crisp navigation.

The School in 60 Seconds
Navy plays at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis, listed at 34,000. Last season was a fine voyage. Navy went 11-2 and 7-1 in the American, won the Liberty Bowl 35-13 and finished No. 23 in the final AP poll. The Midshipmen also won the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy for the second straight season, beating Air Force 34-31 and Army 17-16. The win over Army came on a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass. Anchors aweigh. Navy has now beaten Army in back-to-back seasons, and in Annapolis that's the voyage everyone remembers.

The Coach and the Scheme
Brian Newberry was hired on Dec. 19, 2022. The scheme is the option, and it's the fleet's pride. Navy runs on 81% of its plays, for 297.8 yards a game, 4th in FBS, at 5.74 yards a carry. That's 17 rushing touchdowns. The passing game is used sparingly, at 115.5 yards a game, but it hits big: Jordan Collins has 189 yards on just five catches. On defense, Navy allows only 98.8 rushing yards a game (21st) and 2.73 yards a carry. The pass defense allows 247.7 yards (113th). The ship has a leak, too: Navy is minus-6 in turnovers (126th), with 9 lost and 3 forced. That needs patching. The pass rush has 14 sacks, and the blockers have allowed only 9, which is fine seamanship for an option team that rarely drops back. We are disciplined, at 45 penalty yards a game (24th).

Players to Know
QB Jackson Gutierrez (No. 8): our captain. He has 640 rushing yards and 9 TD on 123 carries, plus 559 passing yards, 6 TD and 1 INT. At UTSA he ran 21 times for 139 yards and two TDs and threw two TD passes. Against Tulsa, he ran for 232 yards and three scores.

The Conference Picture
Navy is 2-4 overall and 1-3 in the American, 2-0 at home and 0-4 on the road. The losses were all on the road and close: 38-30 at Florida Atlantic, 24-20 at UAB, 14-9 at Air Force and 38-34 at UTSA. That's four losses by a combined 21 points. The wins were at home, over Towson 42-15 and Tulsa 34-26. Good news, then: we're home this week. Steady as she goes. Notre Dame is next, so this one matters before the schedule gets heavier.

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium · CBS Sports Network.
Last week: Navy lost 38-34 at UTSA. North Texas had a week off after beating Charlotte 50-10 on Oct. 10.
Our offense vs. their defense: North Texas allows 142.7 rushing yards a game (73rd) and 29.2 points (113th). That's open water for the option.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the storm. North Texas averages 42.2 points (5th in FBS) and 347 passing yards (2nd). QB Tayven Jackson has 1,868 yards and 15 TDs. Our pass defense ranks 113th. The best defense may be our offense, keeping the ball and keeping their quarterback on the sideline.
Series: North Texas won last year 31-17, but Navy leads 2-1. Navy won the 2007 meeting 74-62, which I consider a historical anomaly. In 2023, a closer contest: Navy 27, North Texas 24. That's the course I'd like to chart again, a tight game decided late, at home, in front of the Brigade.
