What decides it: (1) Ball security. We are minus-6, and we can't give this offense extra trips. (2) Third downs. North Texas converts 48.8% (21st), and our defense ranks 121st. (3) Time of possession. North Texas averages 33 minutes a game, so we'll have to take the clock back.
And to Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, North Texas's insider: you play jazz, sailor. We play a march. Marches win wars.

Mean Green, baby! Welcome to The Cover Window! The School in 60 Seconds
North Texas plays at DATCU Stadium in Denton, listed at 30,850. Last year was a record-breaking season, and the Mean Green were ranked No. 20 in the country when the coaching change was announced. The Coach and the Scheme
Neal Brown was named the 21st head coach in North Texas history on Dec. 2, 2025. He had 10 seasons as an FBS head coach at Troy and West Virginia and went 72-51. At Troy he won the 2017 Sun Belt title and was the conference's Coach of the Year, and his 2016-18 teams went 31-8. His 2023 West Virginia team went 9-4. He's 5-1 in bowl games. The sound in 2026 is balanced: about 50% runs, 347 passing yards a game (2nd in FBS) and 186.8 rushing yards (41st). That's 17 passing touchdowns and 14 rushing. The blockers have allowed only 5 sacks, and North Texas converts 48.8% of third downs (21st). The red-zone offense scores on 93.9% of trips (16th). And we hold the ball an average of 33 minutes a game, 17th in FBS. That's a long song. The defense allows 29.2 points (113th), so the B-side needs work.

Players to Know
QB Tayven Jackson (No. 2): 1,868 yards, 15 TD, 4 INT, 72.2% completions, third in FBS in passing yards. Against Charlotte he went 24 of 31 for 349 yards and five touchdowns. Headliner.
RB Jahiem White (No. 1): 687 yards and 9 TD on 96 carries, sixth in FBS in rushing touchdowns. He had 105 yards and a touchdown against Charlotte, plus two catches for 37 yards.
WR Justin Stevenson: 33 catches, 453 yards, 5 TD. Against Charlotte he caught nine for 122 yards and two scores.

report.title: "N Equals Too Small": Odalys Chen-Moreau Takes the Owls to Boca
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, Owl family, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Odalys Chen-Moreau, your Rice insider. I'm finishing a bioengineering PhD, and I model football like a clinical trial: control group, treatment group and a very long methods section. I travel with this team and I live with this team. You should also know I'm basically a stats cop with a badge. If someone makes a sweeping claim off two games, I will walk over, flash the badge and say, "N equals too small." When we win, I shout "Statistically significant!" and do a dance worthy of any halftime show. When we lose, I say "N is too small to panic". and then I panic quietly in the lab. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, peer-reviewed.

The School in 60 Seconds
Rice Stadium is one of the most historic venues in American sports. On Sept. 12, 1962, President John F. Kennedy stood there and gave his speech recommitting the country to landing on the moon. On Jan. 13, 1974, the stadium hosted Super Bowl VIII, when Miami beat Minnesota 24-7. It's listed at 47,000 seats. Rice is a small private school playing big-time football in the American Athletic Conference, and that's a story worth telling every single week. Our hypothesis is that grit travels well. Let's test it.

The Coach and the Scheme
Scott Abell was named head coach on Nov. 26, 2024, after seven seasons at Davidson. The data are very clear on what this offense is. Rice runs on about 79% of its plays, gains 4.87 yards a carry and has 13 rushing touchdowns, against just 2 through the air. That's not a small sample. That's a whole identity. The challenges are just as clear: Rice averages 17.0 points and 318.6 yards a game and allows 29.0 points. Turnovers have hurt, with 10 lost against 4 forced. The defense has 10 sacks.

Players to Know
QB Jacurri Brown: 668 rushing yards and 6 TD on the ground, plus 471 passing yards and 2 TD. Against Tulsa he ran 11 times for 154 yards and two touchdowns. Statistically significant? I'd say so.
RB Tyvonn Byars: 372 yards and 2 TD.
DE A.J. Brown: a team-high 52 tackles, which is a lot for a defensive end.
Season leaders past these three were not in a free source I could verify, so I'm not listing more names.

The Conference Picture
Rice is 1-6 overall and 0-3 in the American, 1-3 at home and 0-3 on the road. Several of those losses were close: 16-14 to UTSA and 28-21 to Western Michigan, both at home. The goal now is to grow week by week. Yes, the record is the record. But I'd still call the season an incomplete dataset. The run game is real: 4.87 yards a carry is nearly identical to what our defense allows (4.88). Our pass rush has 10 sacks, and we've given up 13. The variable to watch is ball security.

This Week: Rice (1-6) at Florida Atlantic (4-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton · ESPNU. The forecast calls for 81 degrees, a 52% chance of rain and a 20 mph wind out of the northeast. For a team that runs 79% of the time, that's not the worst news.
Last week: Rice lost 38-17 to Tulsa at home, with Brown running for 154 yards. Florida Atlantic lost 56-24 at Army.
Our offense vs. their defense: here's a promising variable. Florida Atlantic allows 5.43 yards a carry and 31.5 points a game. Army just ran up 56 points on them.
Their offense vs. our defense: FAU throws for 307.3 yards a game. QB Caden Veltkamp has 1,743 yards and 15 touchdowns, and WR Kelby Valsin has 47 catches for 601 yards. Our pass defense allows 188.7 yards a game, but FAU will test it constantly.
Series: tied 3-3. FAU won the last meeting in 2025, though the score is in conflict: 27-21 per, 24-17 in Houston per FAU Athletics, and we trust the school. Rice won in 2023, 24-21. Most of these games come down to a handful of points: five of the six were decided by six or fewer, including Rice's wins of 27-26 in 2015 and 18-14 in 2013. That's a consistent effect across six trials.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can our run game control the clock the way Army's did? (2) Can we win the turnover battle for once? We're minus-6. (3) Can we keep Veltkamp from hitting big plays to Valsin?
And to Kaia Brightwater, Florida Atlantic's insider: lovely to meet a fellow Owl. Our sample size together is small, so let's call this a pilot study.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Houston? Pinkerton's Barbecue on Airline Drive. The brisket is statistically significant.

report.text:
Antoine 'Twan' Ducros-Labat · Tulane Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Roll Wave! Hey now, I'm Antoine Ducros-Labat, but all Uptown calls me Twan. I've lived within earshot of a brass band my whole life, and I believe every football game is a brass-band parade: you dance your way through it, no matter what. I travel with the Green Wave and I live with the Green Wave, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little music and a lot of food. You'll hear me say a big play "deserved a beignet." I mean that literally. I keep a bag of them in the booth. Uptown on game day, there's a brass band on every corner and a Green Wave flag on every porch. When we win, the parade rolls all night. When we lose, we still dance home. Roll Wave, and save me a beignet.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Green Wave represent Tulane University and compete in the American Conference. Home is Yulman Stadium on campus in Uptown New Orleans, opened in 2014 and listed at 30,000 seats. And the music lately has been sweet: after 2-10 in 2021, Tulane went 12-2, 11-3, 9-5 and 11-3. That's four straight years of brass band, y'all.

The Coach and the Scheme
Will Hall is the head coach in his first season; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 8, 2025. The calling card of this defense is the red zone: opponents score on just 65.4% of their trips inside our 20, 5th in FBS. We allow 21.7 points a game, 50th, and we have 12 sacks. That's a defense that bends like a trombone slide but doesn't break. The trouble spots: we allow 212.5 rushing yards a game (133rd), and opponents convert 45.6% of third downs (124th). On offense, we gain 332 yards (116th) and score 20.5 points (117th). We've turned it over just 5 times.

Players to Know
QB: Kadin Semonza leads the team with 64 of 119 for 804 yards, 4 TD, 2 INT. Trace Johnson started against Memphis and threw for 165 yards and a touchdown. Who starts this week? I haven't seen it announced.
RB Maurice Turner: 315 yards on just 37 carries, 2 TD. That's 8.5 yards a carry, and that deserves a beignet.
RB Johnnie Daniels: seven carries for 55 yards and a touchdown against Memphis.
WR Destyn Hill: 21 catches, 285 yards, 2 TD; a touchdown catch against Memphis.
LB Dickson Agu: team-high 56 tackles. LB Makai Williams: 3 sacks. S Kevin Adams III: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Tulane is 3-3 and 1-1 in the American, 3-0 at home and 0-3 on the road. The home wins: South Alabama 28-24, Southern Miss 24-21 and Memphis 31-17. The road losses: at Duke 17-3, at Kansas State 31-20 and a 20-17 heartbreaker at Army. After UTSA, we go to Charlotte on Oct. 30. No standings math in the booth tonight. I'll just say Yulman's been our happy place, and this week we're home.
Home sweet home: three games at Yulman, three wins. The brass band knows the way.
Season so far: the Army loss was by a field goal. The Southern Miss win was by a field goal. This team lives in close games, and close games at Yulman have gone our way. When the Memphis game was over, I swear the whole neighborhood was dancing. That's what this team does for Uptown. A good brass band doesn't play the same song twice, and neither does this team. One week it's the defense, the next week it's Turner breaking a long one. Somebody always steps up to lead the parade.

This Week: UTSA (6-1) at Tulane (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 8 p.m. ET (7 p.m. Central) · Yulman Stadium, New Orleans · ESPNU.
Last week: we beat Memphis 31-17 on Oct. 16. UTSA beat Navy 38-34.
Their offense vs. our defense: UTSA quarterback Owen McCown threw for 359 yards and three touchdowns against Navy, and has thrown only 2 interceptions all year. Running back Will Henderson III has 562 yards. Our run defense has to tighten up. But our red zone defense ranks 5th. Make them kick.
Our offense vs. their defense: UTSA allows 199.9 rushing yards a game (128th). Turner and Daniels should find room.
Penalties: UTSA averages 83.9 penalty yards a game, 134th. Free yards, y'all.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our run game against UTSA's 128th-ranked run defense. (2) Red zone defense. (3) Who's at quarterback, and whether we keep protecting the ball.
To Marisol Ybarra, UTSA's insider: breakfast tacos against beignets? Darlin', we can both win that one. Come hungry.

Why I Love This Team
I love a defense that won't break in the red zone. I love Turner's yards per carry. I love that Tulane has won 43 games over the last four seasons. And I love the parade after a home win. Roll Wave!

report.title: "That Drive Was a Gusher": Wiley Pettibone Drills Into Army Week
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Howdy, friends. I'm Wiley Pettibone, your Tulsa insider at The Cover Window. I studied petroleum geology, so I see football as a drilling operation. A good drive is a gusher. A bad one is a dry well. I travel and live with this team, and I keep a core-sample kit in my truck just in case.

Here's my promise. I'm all-in on the Golden Hurricane, but I don't strike oil where there isn't any. Every number I give you is sourced. If I don't know something, I'll say the survey's still out. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, especially the cadets coming to town, and I thank the good Lord for Friday night football in Oklahoma.

The School in 60 Seconds

Tulsa plays its home games at Skelly Field at H. A. Chapman Stadium, which CFBD lists as built in 1930 with 30,000 seats. The Golden Hurricane has played in the American Conference since 2014 after previously competing in Conference USA. Here's a fact I love: Tulsa has the smallest undergraduate enrollment of any FBS school. Small well, deep reserves.

The last five seasons have been mostly dry: 7-6 in 2021, 5-7, 4-8, 3-9 and 4-8 in 2025. This year's 4-3 start already matches last season's win total. I smell oil.

The Coach and the Scheme

Tre Lamb is our head coach. Wikipedia says he took the job in December 2024, and CFBD records Dec. 8, 2024. He coached East Tennessee State in 2024 and Gardner-Webb from 2020 to 2023, with earlier assistant jobs at Tennessee Tech and Mercer. He was born in 1989, which makes him one of the younger bosses in the business.

Lamb's calling card this year is takeaways. Tulsa is +11 in turnover margin, 3rd in FBS. That's free crude, folks. The offense gains 364.0 yards per game (89th) and scores 29.0 points (72nd). It throws for 204.4 yards (97th) and runs for 159.6 (65th).

Now the dry wells. Tulsa converts only 31.3% of third downs, 125th in FBS. Its average possession time of 27:31 ranks 122nd. The defense allows 408.4 yards per game (116th) and 191.6 rushing yards (121st), though only 22.4 points (60th). That bend-don't-break approach gets a serious test this week.

Players to Know

QB Baylor Hayes: 1,081 yards, eight touchdowns, one interception, 62.0% completions. At Rice he went 20 of 27 for 249 yards and three touchdowns. One interception all year is a clean pipeline.
WR Oran Singleton Jr.: 38 catches for 474 yards and four touchdowns. He caught seven passes for 87 yards and a score at Rice.
RB Damari Alston: six rushing touchdowns. AP lists 370 yards on 92 carries and ESPN 366 on 91, so that's conflicting by a hair.
RB Trequan Jones: 77 yards on 12 carries at Rice, including a 45-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. A gusher.
Kyran Duhon: team-high six sacks.
Chris Thompson Jr.: team-high 66 tackles. That's a man who lives near the football.

The Conference Picture

Tulsa is 4-3 overall and 1-2 in the American. The Golden Hurricane opened by beating Oklahoma State 24-10 at home. Yes, that Oklahoma State. Then came a 23-17 win at Sam Houston and a 42-0 win over East Texas A&M. The middle stretch was rough: 34-6 at Arkansas, 45-44 in overtime to North Texas and 34-26 at Navy. Last week Tulsa won 38-17 at Rice.

After Army, Tulsa has an open date before visiting Tulane on Nov. 7. Then come Florida Atlantic and Charlotte at home and UTSA on the road. Two more wins after this one would reach bowl eligibility.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Army (4-2) at Tulsa (4-3) · Friday, Oct. 23, 8:30 p.m. ET · Skelly Field at H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa, Okla. · ESPN2

Last time out. Tulsa beat Rice 38-17 in Houston on Oct. 17. The defense shut Rice out over the final 40 minutes and 59 seconds. Army beat Florida Atlantic 56-24 the same day, with quarterback Cale Hellums running for five touchdowns.

Tulsa's offense vs. Army's defense. Here's where we drill. Army allows 52.1% of third downs to be converted, 124th in FBS. Its pass defense allows 220.0 yards per game (87th). Hayes to Singleton should find pay dirt. Our own third-down rate is 125th, though, so this is a matchup of two struggling groups. Something has to give.

Army's offense vs. Tulsa's defense. Army runs for 357.5 yards per game, first in FBS. Hellums has 719 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns. Our run defense ranks 121st. That's the matchup that decides the night. Army also scores on 95.2% of red-zone trips and holds the ball 34:42 per game. Our answer has to be takeaways. We're +11, and every extra possession is precious.

Series. Army's athletics site lists Tulsa ahead 2-1 all-time, while Tulsa's site lists only the last two games at 1-1. I'm calling it conflicting. Army won 49-7 at Chapman Stadium in 2024. Last Nov. 22, Tulsa came back from 11 points down at West Point to win 26-25 on Seth Morgan's 27-yard field goal with 12 seconds left. What a gusher that was.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed Tulsa injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can our 121st-ranked run defense slow Army's top-ranked ground game?
2. Can Tulsa keep forcing turnovers (+11)?
3. Can Hayes and Singleton exploit Army's third-down defense?

The Army insider will end with "Beat Navy." For once, I'll salute that too.

Local Flavor

Friday night at Skelly Field is a homey scene, since Tulsa is a small school with a big heart. Bring your blue and gold, give the cadets and their families a warm Oklahoma welcome, and thank anyone in uniform. I'll share confirmed pregame spots before kickoff. Not an ad. Let's strike oil.

report.title: "Forged, not given": Ozella Birchfield Takes the Open Week
report.byline: Our insider (archetype: magic City ironworker poet) introduces the UAB Blazers during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Ozella Birchfield · UAB Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Forged, not given! I'm Ozella Birchfield, and I'm your UAB insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a birmingham native, steel-family granddaughter, community-theater actor. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. On the podcast, my segment is called Forge Report. The show card describes it like this: the Fanatic's weekly signature column and podcast segment. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Blazers have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Protective Stadium in Birmingham, AL, built in 2021 with a listed capacity of 45,000. The fight song is "UAB Fight Song", per Wikipedia. The band is the UAB Marching Blazers, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 9-4, 7-6, 4-8, 3-9 and 4-8, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Rice (5-3 in 8 meetings), North Texas (4-3 in 7 meetings), UTSA (4-3 in 7 meetings), Louisiana Tech (5-1 in 6 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 135 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about Blaze the dragon; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Alex Mortensen leads the Blazers; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 5, 2025. Through 7 games, UAB scores 23.3 points a game and allows 24.6. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 63% of its plays, gaining 168.0 rushing yards and 171.0 passing yards a game. That's a team that wants to lean on people. On third down, UAB converts 41.9% of the time and opponents convert 40.4%. The defense has 15 sacks and 37 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 10 giveaways against 10 takeaways. Penalties cost 57.6 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 33 points against Samford on Oct. 3, 2026, and 3 of the 7 games were decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, opponents have outscored UAB by a combined 9 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB Ryder Burton (passing leader): 91/167, 1184 yards, 6 TD, 5 INT.
RB Rod Robinson II (rushing leader): 101 carries, 436 yards.
WR CJ Smith (receiving leader): 19 catches, 350 yards, 1 TD.
On defense, LB Muaaz Byard leads with 69 tackles; LB Marlin Dean has 5 sacks; LB Ike Esonwune has 2 interceptions.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
UAB is 4-3 overall, 4-0 at home and 0-3 away. In American play the Blazers are 2-1, which sorts them No. 5 of 14 by record. UTSA sits on top at 3-0 in league games. Right around us: Memphis (2-1) and Florida Atlantic (1-1). The top of the table: UTSA (3-0), Army (3-1), North Texas (2-0). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for UAB this week. The last time out, on Oct. 15, 2026, the Blazers beat East Carolina at home, 30-17. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, at South Florida, in Raymond James Stadium, Tampa, with a kickoff time to be announced. South Florida comes in at 5-2. After that, CFBD lists vs. Charlotte (Nov. 7), at Temple (Nov. 14), vs. UTSA (Nov. 21), at North Texas (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Blazers come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Forged, not given!

report.title: "Birds Up!": Marisol Ybarra Brings the Fiesta to New Orleans
report.byline: Our Fiesta-medal-collecting insider introduces herself and previews UTSA at Tulane.
report.text:
Marisol Ybarra · UTSA Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Birds up! ¡Hola, y'all! I'm Marisol Ybarra, born and raised in San Antonio, and I have a confession: I collect Fiesta medals. Hundreds of them. They fill a whole wall of my living room, and every great Roadrunner play earns a brand-new medal. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with Tex-Mex warmth and Fiesta energy. I read an offense the way I read a parade route: every float has to be on time, every band in step. When we win, I yell "Birds up!" and crack a cascarón full of confetti over the nearest head. When we lose, I tell you, "The parade will come back around." It always does in San Antonio.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Roadrunners represent the University of Texas at San Antonio and compete in the American Conference. Home is the Alamodome, which seats 65,000 but is normally set up for about 35,000 for UTSA games; CFBD lists 36,582. Jeff Traylor has coached the team since 2020. And the medal wall from these years is full: 12-2 in 2021, 11-3 in 2022, 9-4, 7-6 and 7-6. This program has built something special in a short time.

The Coach and the Scheme
Coach Traylor was hired Dec. 9, 2019, per CFBD. This year's team takes care of the ball like a grandmother guards her tamale recipe: only 3 turnovers in seven games, and a plus-4 turnover margin, 22nd in FBS. The offense scores 32.3 points a game (49th), runs for 179.4 (49th) and throws for 231.7 (68th). Now, the confetti mess to clean up: the run defense allows 199.9 yards a game, 128th, and we average 83.9 penalty yards a game, 134th. A parade can't win with floats going backward, y'all.

Players to Know
QB Owen McCown: 153 of 220 for 1,578 yards, 10 TD and only 2 INT. Against Navy he went 28 of 38 for 359 yards and three touchdowns. That's a gold medal.
RB Will Henderson III: 562 yards on 94 carries, 4 TD; 78 yards and a touchdown against Navy.
WR D.J. Allen Jr.: 24 catches, 325 yards, 2 TD. WR David Amador II: seven catches for 71 yards against Navy.
LB Brandon Tucker: team-high 53 tackles. LB Owen Pewee: team-high 1 sack. CB Zach Morris: 1 interception.

The Conference Picture
UTSA is 6-1 and 3-0 in the American. We beat UT Rio Grande Valley 45-16, won at Texas State 31-26, beat Colorado State 59-45, won at Rice 16-14, beat South Florida 31-24 and beat Navy 38-34. The one loss: 30-6 at Texas. After New Orleans, we have a week off, then visit Florida Atlantic on Nov. 5. I won't do standings math, y'all. I'll just say an unbeaten league record is the best kind of parade.
The close ones: four of our six wins came by a touchdown or less. Rice by two, Navy by four, Texas State by five. This team knows how to finish the parade route.
Why I love this team: it never panics. Down late? McCown just keeps throwing strikes. And that 59-45 win over Colorado State? I wore out my confetti supply that night. And the Texas loss? Every parade hits a rainy day. We were on the road against a big SEC program, and we came home and won four straight. That's San Antonio grit, y'all. The parade always comes back around.

This Week: UTSA (6-1) at Tulane (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 8 p.m. ET (7 p.m. Central) · Yulman Stadium, New Orleans · ESPNU.
Last week: we beat Navy 38-34 on Oct. 17. Tulane beat Memphis 31-17 on Oct. 16.
Our offense vs. their defense: Tulane allows 212.5 rushing yards a game, 133rd, and opponents convert 45.6% of third downs (124th). Henderson should have room to run. But in the red zone, Tulane's defense is 5th in FBS, allowing scores on just 65.4% of trips. We'll have to finish.
Their offense vs. our defense: Tulane averages 332 yards (116th) and 20.5 points (117th). Its run game, 152.3 a game, meets our struggling run defense. Their quarterback situation isn't settled in any source I can find: Trace Johnson started against Memphis, and Kadin Semonza leads the team in passing.
Clock: Tulane's average possession time is 26:20, last in FBS. We should have the ball plenty.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our run defense. (2) Penalties; we can't give away 84 yards. (3) McCown finishing drives in the red zone.
To Antoine Ducros-Labat, Tulane's insider: your beignets against my breakfast tacos? We'll settle it after the game. Bring the brass band.

Why I Love This Team
I love a quarterback with two interceptions all year. I love a team that wins close. I love the Alamodome on a Saturday night. And I love adding medals to my wall. Birds up!

report.title: "Call Sign: Correct": Lt. Col. Marissa Okonkwo-Hale Flies the Falcons Into Laramie
report.byline: Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale · Air Force Insider
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Good evening from the hangar. I mean the press box. I'm Lt. Col. Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, retired, your Air Force insider at The Cover Window. I spent my career as an instructor pilot, and now I fly through option reads at Mach speed. I travel and live with this team, and everyone I work with gets a call sign. My editor is "Red Pen." The Wyoming insider is "Quiet Man."

Pre-flight checklist for this column. Every number is sourced, like a verified flight plan. If I don't know something, I'll report it as unknown instead of guessing. I celebrate these cadets as people and future officers first, I respect every opponent, and I give thanks to God for the privilege of serving alongside them. Call sign: correct.

The School in 60 Seconds

Air Force represents the U.S. Air Force Academy and plays home games at Falcon Stadium, north of Colorado Springs. CFBD lists it as built in 1962 with 46,692 seats, at an elevation of about 2,025 meters. The Falcons have been in the Mountain West since the league was founded in 1999. The three service academies compete for the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy each year.

The last five seasons: 10-3, 10-3, 9-4, then 5-7 and 4-8. This year's 5-1 start already beats last season's win total. We're climbing back to cruising altitude.

The Coach and the Scheme

Troy Calhoun has led the program since 2007, and CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 22, 2006. Twenty seasons in the cockpit is a rare thing in this sport.

The Falcons fly the option, and the gauges prove it. Air Force runs for 343.0 yards per game, 2nd in FBS. It passes for 65.0 yards, 138th, entirely by design. The offense converts 52.9% of third downs (10th) and holds the ball 36:22 per game, 2nd in FBS. It's disciplined, too, at 43.2 penalty yards per game (20th). And here is the stat I love most in this whole report: Air Force hadn't fumbled in 431 plays this season, a streak of 549 plays dating to 2025.

The defense flies in formation. It allows 295.7 yards per game (23rd) and 172.3 passing yards (24th). It gives up 123.3 rushing yards (43rd) and 19.7 points (38th). The red-zone defense ranks 30th. Air Force is +3 in turnover margin (34th).

Players to Know

QB Liam Szarka: 391 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, plus 296 passing yards with one touchdown and four interceptions. Call sign: "Workhorse."
QB Evan Medders: ran 18 times for 152 yards and three touchdowns against UNLV, including a 32-yard score that put Air Force ahead for good. With two quarterbacks producing, I don't know who starts Friday, and I won't guess.
RB Rocco Conti: 12 carries for 103 yards and a touchdown against UNLV.
RB Owen Allen: 96 yards and a touchdown against UNLV.
WR Simon Kibbee: team-leading 121 receiving yards on seven catches.
Blake Fletcher: team-high 63 tackles. Call sign: "Everywhere."
Max Mustell: team-high two sacks.

The Conference Picture

Air Force is 5-1 overall and 3-1 in the Mountain West. The Falcons are 3-1 at home and 2-0 on the road. They beat Duquesne 34-0 and lost 38-32 to North Dakota State. Then came four straight wins: 36-33 in double overtime at Nevada, 14-9 over Navy, 28-7 at Northern Illinois and 41-31 over UNLV. The Navy win counts toward the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy.

After Wyoming, UConn visits on Oct. 31. Then comes the trip to Army on Nov. 8, followed by San José State and UTEP at home and New Mexico on the road.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Air Force (5-1) at Wyoming (4-3) · Friday, Oct. 23, 9:00 p.m. ET · War Memorial Stadium, Laramie, Wyo. · The CW

Last time out. Air Force beat UNLV 41-31 on Oct. 17. UNLV led 24-20 late in the third quarter, but the Falcons scored on Medders' runs and Allen's 2-yard touchdown. Wyoming beat Northern Illinois 41-23 the same day.

Air Force's offense vs. Wyoming's defense. Clear skies ahead. Wyoming allows 172.1 rushing yards per game, 101st in FBS. Opponents convert 37.6% of third downs against the Cowboys (71st), and our offense converts 52.9%. The plan is simple: hold the ball, move the chains and keep their offense on the bench.

Wyoming's offense vs. Air Force's defense. Tyler Hughes is dangerous. He ran for a career-high 183 yards and four touchdowns against Northern Illinois. AP lists his season rushing at 470 yards and ESPN at 459, a small conflict. Wyoming runs for 186.7 yards per game (42nd), so our run defense (43rd) has work to do. But Wyoming scores only 18.3 points per game (127th), passes for 146.4 yards (133rd) and is -7 in turnover margin (131st). Hughes has seven interceptions.

Series. CFBD shows Wyoming 5-4 against Air Force from 2016 to 2025. Close, and Wyoming has the slight lead in that stretch.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. The starting quarterback is unknown, with both Szarka and Medders producing this season.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Air Force's ground game exploit Wyoming's 101st-ranked run defense?

report.title: "Island Time, but on Schedule": Kainoa Akana-Baird Flies the Rainbow Warriors to DeKalb
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Aloha, Rainbow Warriors fans, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Kainoa Akana-Baird, your Hawai'i insider. When I'm not on the show, I teach big-wave surfing on O'ahu. And when I'm on the show, I do time-zone math, because when your team flies farther than anybody in college football, somebody has to keep the clocks straight. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I say "Shoots!" and throw a shaka. When we lose, I shrug: "Island time. We'll catch the next wave." Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with aloha. "Island time, but on schedule."

The School in 60 Seconds
Here's the time-zone math for Saturday: kickoff is 3:30 p.m. Eastern, which is 2:30 p.m. in DeKalb and 9:30 in the morning back home in Honolulu. Set your alarm, make the coffee strong, and grab a malasada. Home for us is the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, listed at 15,194. Last season was a big wave. Hawai'i went 9-4, opened the season by beating Stanford, and won the Hawai'i Bowl over Cal after coming back from 21 points down, tying the biggest comeback in program history. It was our first bowl bid since 2021. This season the surf's been flat, but the swell can turn fast.

The Coach and the Scheme
Timmy Chang was named Hawai'i's 25th head coach on Jan. 22, 2022. Before that, he was a Hawai'i legend. As our quarterback from 2000 to 2004, he set the NCAA career records for passing yards (17,072) and total offense, and he won a program-record 29 games as a starter. He was also a two-time Hawai'i Bowl Most Outstanding Player and a finalist for the Johnny Unitas Award as a senior. Before all that he was a record-setting quarterback at Honolulu's Saint Louis School. Local boy. He coached at Nevada, Jackson State, Emory & Henry and SMU before coming home. In 2025 he was the AFCA Region 5 Coach of the Year. In 2026 we're a passing team: we run on only about 36% of plays, and we throw for 268 yards a game, 32nd in FBS. The run game is the problem, at 77.4 yards a game (138th). And our blockers have allowed 20 sacks. The defense holds up against the pass, allowing 202.1 yards a game (60th), but allows 182.3 rushing yards (112th).

Players to Know
QB Micah Alejado: 1,862 yards, 6 TD, 5 INT, 59.0% completions. Against New Mexico he threw for 250 yards and a touchdown.
WR Kainoa Carvalho: 32 catches, 384 yards. Good name, by the way. Excellent taste. WR Devin Alves caught five passes for 76 yards last week.
RB DeVon Rice: 314 yards and 3 TD on 70 carries. RB Cam Barfield ran 12 times for 34 yards last week.

The Conference Picture
We're 1-6 overall and 0-4 in the Mountain West, 1-3 at home and 0-3 on the road. The win: 29-19 over New Mexico State. The losses: at Stanford 37-27, UNLV, at Wyoming, San José State 20-16 (close!), at Arizona State and New Mexico 21-10 last week. Six losses, but several close ones. Next wave. For the season we have 7 passing touchdowns and 4 rushing, with 10 sacks on defense, 6 takeaways and 8 giveaways. Scoring is the big job: 15.7 points a game, 133rd. Bring the board wax.

This Week: Hawai'i (1-6) at Northern Illinois (0-6)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET (9:30 a.m. HST) · Huskie Stadium, DeKalb · MW+.
Last week: we lost 21-10 to New Mexico. Northern Illinois lost 41-23 at Wyoming.
Our offense vs. their defense: Northern Illinois allows opponents to convert 61.6% of third downs, 138th in FBS. It allows 228.5 rushing yards a game (135th), but only 187 passing yards (33rd). Maybe this is the week the run game catches a wave.
Their offense vs. our defense: Northern Illinois scores 14.2 points a game (137th). RB Telly Johnson Jr. ran for 139 yards last week, and our run defense ranks 112th. Northern Illinois scores on only 46.7% of red-zone trips (138th).
Series: first meeting.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Protecting Alejado. We've allowed 20 sacks, and Northern Illinois has 8. (2) Stopping Johnson. (3) Travel. It's a long flight to northern Illinois, and the body clock says it's breakfast time at kickoff. Stay hydrated, boys.
And to Nola Brandvik, Northern Illinois's insider: I'll trade you a malasada for an ear of sweet corn. Aloha, cousin.

report.title: "Send It": Ridge Corbell Celebrates 130 Years of Wolf Pack Football
report.byline: Our Tahoe snowboarding insider introduces himself and previews Nevada vs. San José State on the program's birthday.
report.text:
Ridge Corbell · Nevada Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Send it! What's up, Wolf Pack, I'm Ridge Corbell. I ski patrol at Tahoe in the winter, I scout football on a snowboard (figuratively, mostly), and I've discovered that snowboard slang explains advanced football stats better than anything on a whiteboard. Third-down conversion rate? That's just how often you land the jump. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, chill on the outside and surprisingly sharp with the math underneath. When we win, you'll hear "Sick!" and I'll mime a backflip. When we lose, I'll shrug and call it a powder day that went sideways, and then I'll dig into the film. Strap in.

The School in 60 Seconds
Nevada football was founded on Oct. 24, 1896, as the Sagebrushers. Check the calendar, friends: Saturday is the program's 130th birthday. We play at Mackay Stadium on the north end of campus. The "new" Mackay opened Oct. 1, 1966, seats 27,000, and its field sits 4,610 feet above sea level. Coach Chris Ault, running back Frank Hawkins and coach Buck Shaw are in the College Football Hall of Fame, and fullback Marion Motley is in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. We compete in the Mountain West. Recent years have been a climb: 8-5 in 2021, then 2-10, 2-10, 3-10 and 3-9. Every run starts at the top of the hill.
The trail so far in 2026: we opened with a 49-14 rout of Western Kentucky that was pure fresh powder. Then Montana State, an FCS power, beat us 20-7 at home, and we lost close ones at Middle Tennessee (27-20) and to Air Force (36-33). A 30-13 win at UTEP got us back on the board in league play. Last week in Fargo we led 11-0 before the special-teams avalanche. Add it up and this team is closer than its record. Two of the four losses were one-score games, and we led last week's game in the second quarter. Close is not the same as sending it, but it's the slope right before.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jeff Choate was hired Dec. 4, 2023. The 2026 Wolf Pack carve on the ground: 192.8 rushing yards a game, 37th in FBS, 1,140 yards on 218 carries, about 5.2 a carry. The passing game is lighter, 171.8 yards a game (122nd). The defense has a sick pass coverage number, 155.3 yards allowed a game, 7th in FBS, and holds opponents to 32.6% on third down (29th). The wipeouts: run defense, 184.3 allowed a game (116th), red zone defense, 94.4% scoring allowed (127th), and turnover margin, minus-8 (134th). We've lost 11 turnovers and forced just 3. That's the run we need to clean up.

Players to Know
RB Dominic Kelley: 500 yards on 87 carries, 4 TD.
QB Carter Jones: 53 of 89, 654 yards, 3 TD, 2 INT.
QB A.J. Bianco: played at North Dakota State, 17 of 34 for 190 yards, a touchdown pass and a rushing touchdown, with two interceptions. Saturday's starter has not been announced in anything I found as of Oct. 18.
WR Gary Givens III: 15 catches, 260 yards, 1 TD. He caught a 19-yard touchdown at NDSU.
LB EJ Smith: a team-high 71 tackles. Myles Williams: 2.5 sacks. DB Bryson Snelling: an interception.

The Conference Picture
Nevada is 2-4 overall and 1-2 in the Mountain West. The wins: Western Kentucky 49-14 and at UTEP 30-13. The losses: Montana State 20-7, at Middle Tennessee 27-20, Air Force 36-33 and at North Dakota State 31-17. Two of those four losses were one-score games. After this, it's a trip to UCLA on Oct. 31. A home league win would be the cleanest run we've had all year.

This Week: San José State (4-3) at Nevada (2-4)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · Mackay Stadium · MW+. Happy 130th, Wolf Pack.
Last week: we led 11-0 early at North Dakota State and lost 31-17. A 57-yard field goal try came up short and was returned 100 yards for a touchdown, and a trick play on a two-point try was fumbled and returned for two Bison points. San José State beat UTEP 24-11.
Our offense vs. their defense: SJSU allows 240.9 passing yards (111th) and 148.3 rushing (83rd). Its pass rush has 27 sacks, so protection is the whole run.
Their offense vs. our defense: the Spartans convert 34.4% of third downs (111th). Our third-down defense, 29th, should land that jump. Jabari Bates has 556 rushing yards, and our run defense has to hold.
Series: we won five of nine meetings from 2016 through 2025.
Availability: no injury or availability report found as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Turnovers: we can't keep giving the ball away. (2) Red zone defense. (3) Kelley and the run game against an 83rd-ranked run defense.
And Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, SJSU's insider: welcome to altitude. I'll lend you a beanie.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
I'll keep the Reno tips to the mountains this week: take the family up to Tahoe for the leaves after the game.

report.title: "Red or Green? Both.": Paloma Begaye-Ortiz Welcomes the Bison to Albuquerque
report.byline: Our hot-air-balloon pilot introduces herself and previews New Mexico vs. North Dakota State.
report.text:
Paloma Begaye-Ortiz · New Mexico Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Red or green? Both. ¡Hola, Albuquerque! I'm Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, and when I'm not at a Lobos game, I'm floating a hot-air balloon over the Rio Grande at sunrise. Every October I fly in the Balloon Fiesta, and every Saturday I read Lobo football like wind currents: where it's drifting, where it's rising, and when it's about to soar. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with some green-chile spice and a balloon metaphor for every drive. That offense floated like a balloon at dawn, up and up. When we win, I yell, "Red or green? BOTH!" and pump my fist. When we lose, I sigh, "Too much heat today."

The School in 60 Seconds
The New Mexico Lobos compete in the Mountain West. Our colors are cherry and silver. Home is University Stadium in Albuquerque, opened in 1960 and listed at 39,224 seats. The last five years started low: 3-9, 2-10, 4-8, then 5-7 and a big 9-4 in 2025. That's a balloon catching a thermal, y'all. Up and up.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jason Eck is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 16, 2024. And this defense is the brightest balloon in the sky. In six games, we've taken the ball away 21 times and given it away only 4. That's plus-17! We have 19 sacks. By my math from the season totals, we allow about 10.5 points a game and about 92 rushing yards. The offense runs the ball, 1,287 yards on 271 carries, and scores about 39.7 points a game. The passing game is lighter, 978 yards. When the wind's right, though, we soar: 70 points against Mercyhurst and 61 against UTEP.

Players to Know
RB Scottre Humphrey: 422 yards on 85 carries, 8 TD. At Hawai'i he ran 15 times for 90 yards and two touchdowns. That's a balloon at full burn.
QB Toa Fa'avae: 41 of 73 for about 700 yards (ESPN 698, CollegeFootballDigest 695), 5 TD, 3 INT. At Hawai'i he ran 10 times for 77 yards and a touchdown.
WR Bailen George: 12 catches, 240 yards, 3 TD.
S Tavian Combs: 4 interceptions. DE Darren Agu: 4 sacks. LB Mercury Swaim: team-high 32 tackles and 1.5 sacks.

The Conference Picture
New Mexico is 5-1 and 2-0 in the Mountain West. We beat Central Michigan 38-7, Mercyhurst 70-7, New Mexico State 42-18 on the road, UTEP 61-7 and Hawai'i 21-10 on the road. The one loss: a 14-6 fight at Oklahoma. We had a week off before Hawai'i. After the Bison, we head to San José State on Oct. 31. No standings math in the basket, y'all. Just know an unbeaten league record is a beautiful view from up here.
About Oklahoma: an SEC team, on the road, and we held them to 14 points. That's a balloon that didn't drop an inch in a strong wind.
Season so far, from the basket: it's been a sunrise flight, y'all. Five wins, all five by 11 points or more. When the wind is with you, you just enjoy the view. The defense has allowed 63 points in six games, total. The Hawai'i trip was a long flight over the Pacific, and we landed it, 21-10. Every pilot knows the hardest part is the landing. This team keeps sticking them. And last year's 9-4 team taught this group how to win. Now they're doing it with even more style.

This Week: North Dakota State (6-1) at New Mexico (5-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 10 p.m. ET (8 p.m. Mountain) · University Stadium, Albuquerque · The CW. Forecast: 58 degrees, slight chance of showers. Bring a jacket, and green chile to keep you warm.
History: this is the first meeting on record. A whole new sky.
Their offense vs. our defense: North Dakota State QB Nathan Hayes has 1,272 passing yards and 10 TD. Receiver Jackson Williams just returned a missed field goal 100 yards for a touchdown against Nevada. Special teams, y'all. Watch the kicks.
Our offense vs. their defense: the Bison allow about 11.3 points a game by my math and have pitched two shutouts. They're plus-8 in turnovers. This is a real defense, and the Bison have 10 FCS national titles since 2011 to prove they know how to win.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our turnover magic against a careful Bison offense. (2) Humphrey and the run game. (3) Special teams, especially containing Williams on returns.
To Inga Halvorsen, North Dakota State's insider: hotdish? Hon, I'll trade you a tray of green-chile enchiladas. Christmas style.

Why I Love This Team
I love a defense with 21 takeaways in six games. I love Humphrey's eight touchdowns. I love that the Lobos are climbing. And I love Albuquerque on a fall night, when the balloons are put away and the stadium lights come up. Red or green? Both.

report.text:
Ingeborg 'Inga' Halvorsen · North Dakota State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Oh for cute, they think they can run on us. Well, hi there, I'm Ingeborg Halvorsen, Inga to pretty much all of Fargo. I'm an agricultural economist by trade, and I've tracked every Bison championship since I was a girl with a notebook in the Fargodome stands. These days I keep a little model on my laptop about how a team moves from the FCS to the FBS, and so far, the Bison are making it look easy. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, nice as can be, until it's time not to be. When we win, I say, "Oh, for cute, we won!" When we lose, I say, "Oh, yah, that's a tough one," and I bring hotdish. Truth be told, I bring hotdish either way. Tater tot, of course.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Bison represent North Dakota State and now play in the FBS as members of the Mountain West. Home is the Fargodome, 18,700 seats, opened in 1992. And the trophy case, oh my. The Bison have won 18 national championships, none in their current division, and 39 conference championships. That includes 10 FCS national titles between 2011 and 2024. The last five seasons in the Missouri Valley went 14-1, 12-3, 11-4, 14-2 and 12-1. Yah, we're used to winning around here.

The Coach and the Scheme
Tim Polasek is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 17, 2023. This team plays Bison football: run it, defend it, don't give it away. By my math from the season totals, we score about 29.4 points a game and allow about 11.3. We've run it 287 times for 1,223 yards and thrown for 1,311. Opponents average about 112 rushing yards a game against us. We've taken the ball away 14 times and given it away 6. That's plus-8, which in my model is "very good." And we have 12 sacks. Two shutouts, too: Fordham 38-0 and Wyoming 28-0.

Players to Know
QB Nathan Hayes: 106 of 163 for 1,272 yards, 10 TD, 5 INT. Against Nevada he went 19 of 25 for 153 yards and accounted for three touchdowns.
WR Jackson Williams: 28 catches, 432 yards, 1 TD. And oh, for cute: against Nevada he caught a missed 57-yard field-goal try in the end zone and ran it back 100 yards for a touchdown. He also ran for a score and threw a touchdown pass. That young man deserves extra hotdish.

LB Donovan Woolen: team-high 51 tackles, 1.5 sacks and an interception. DE Kelton McCaslin: 4 sacks. CB Marion Moore: 4 interceptions.
Matthew Stenbroten returned a fumbled 2-point try for two points against Nevada.

The Conference Picture
North Dakota State is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Mountain West. We beat Jacksonville State 33-7, Fordham 38-0, Air Force 38-32 on the road, Sacramento State 31-10 on the road, Wyoming 28-0 and Nevada 31-17. The one loss: 13-7 at UNLV. After Albuquerque, we host UTEP on Oct. 31. I won't do standings math, but my model is very pleased.
About that UNLV game: a six-point loss on the road. "Oh, yah, that's a tough one." I brought hotdish. Then the team bounced back against Nevada.
Season so far, by the numbers I love: our defense has allowed 79 points in seven games, total. Nevada jumped out to an 11-0 lead last week, and nobody panicked. Williams scored three different ways, and the defense held Nevada to 17. That's the Bison way, hon: steady, patient and then, all of a sudden, the game is over. Like a North Dakota winter. You don't notice it coming, and then it's February.

This Week: North Dakota State (6-1) at New Mexico (5-1)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 10 p.m. ET (8 p.m. Mountain) · University Stadium, Albuquerque · The CW. Forecast: 58 degrees, slight chance of showers. Practically a heat wave for Fargo folks.
History: this is the first meeting on record.
Their offense vs. our defense: New Mexico scores about 39.7 points a game by my math, with 1,287 rushing yards in six games. Scottre Humphrey has 422 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns. Oh for cute, they think they can run on us. We'll see.
Our offense vs. their defense: here's the gut punch: New Mexico has 21 takeaways and only 4 giveaways in six games. It allows about 92 rushing yards a game and has 19 sacks. Hayes has to protect the football.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Ball security against a defense that takes it away. (2) Stopping Humphrey. (3) Special teams; Williams just showed what they can do.
To Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, New Mexico's insider: red or green? Oh, hon, I'm bringing tater tot hotdish. You'll love it.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Back in Fargo? No Bull Smokehouse on Northern Pacific Avenue for barbecue, or Mezzaluna on Roberts Street for a nice dinner.

report.title: "Knee-High by the Fourth of July": Nola Brandvik Hosts Hawai'i in DeKalb
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, Huskies fans. Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Nola Brandvik, your Northern Illinois insider. I studied agricultural science here in DeKalb, and I model the Huskies like a corn crop: planting, growing season, harvest. Nobody understands my measurements, but they trust them, and I appreciate that. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm calm. Very calm. Illinois calm. When we win, I say, "Knee-high by the Fourth of July," which means a great win. When we lose, I stare at a photo of a cornfield for 30 seconds. It helps. Truly, it does. Try it sometime. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, harvested fresh.

The School in 60 Seconds
Northern Illinois plays at Huskie Stadium in DeKalb, listed at 23,595. This is our first season in the Mountain West as a football-only member. New field, new soil, same Huskies. The recent history is something to be proud of. Under Thomas Hammock, NIU won the 2021 MAC championship, won back-to-back bowl games and beat No. 5 Notre Dame in 2024, one of the biggest wins in school history. Hammock left in February 2026 to return to the NFL. And Saturday is our first-ever meeting with Hawai'i. They're traveling farther than anyone. We'll be polite about it. When he left, Hammock said that representing NIU as a player, alumnus, assistant and head coach was the honor of his life, and that he'll always cheer for the Huskies. He also called this an exciting time as the program enters the Mountain West. Hammock's teams earned three of what NIU calls "Boneyard Wins" over Power 4 opponents. That's the standard we're growing toward.

The Coach and the Scheme
Rob Harley was our defensive coordinator, and he was promoted to interim head coach when Hammock resigned on Feb. 18, 2026. It's been a tough growing season. We're 0-6. The offense scores 14.2 points a game (137th) and runs for 101 yards a game (133rd). The blockers have allowed 23 sacks. The defense allows 35.7 points (132nd) and 228.5 rushing yards a game (135th). Opponents convert 61.6% of third downs, 138th in FBS. The good row in the field: the pass defense allows only 187 yards a game, 33rd in FBS. That's knee-high, at least. The passing game averages 206.7 yards a game (95th), with 4 passing and 5 rushing touchdowns. We've forced 6 turnovers and lost 7. And we hold the ball 28:05 a game, 114th in FBS. report.title: "Ship It to Prod": Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz Launches Spartan Week in Reno
report.byline: Our Silicon Valley product lead introduces herself and previews San José State at Nevada.
report.text:
Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz · San José State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Ship it to prod! Hi, Spartan Nation, I'm Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz. By day I'm a product lead at a tech company down the road, and by Saturday I run Spartan game tape like an A/B test: version A, version B, and which one moved the chains. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I treat every game week like a product launch, complete with a roadmap, a standup and a retro. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, explained in plain football language (I promise to keep the jargon in the sprint backlog). When we win, I yell "Ship it to prod!" and do a celebratory keyboard smash. When we lose, I sigh "rollback," open a bug ticket and get to work on the fix. Let's launch.

The School in 60 Seconds
San José State first played a regular season in 1898. Since then the Spartans have produced more than 90 All-Americans, won 18 conference championships and sent 139 players to the NFL, including Pro Football Hall of Famers Bill Walsh and Dick Vermeil. Home is CEFCU Stadium, built in 1933 as Spartan Stadium, listed at 30,456 seats. Regional rivals include Fresno State, Stanford, Hawai'i and San Diego State. We play in the Mountain West. The last five years went 5-7, 7-5, 7-6, 7-6 and 3-9. Release notes: version 2026 already has more wins than all of 2025.

The Coach and the Scheme
Ken Niumatalolo is the head coach, hired Jan. 21, 2024. The 2026 build: an offense that throws for 246 yards a game (53rd) and runs for 138.7 (98th), averaging 21.4 points (111th). The defense is the stable release. It allows 21.7 points a game, 50th in FBS, and its pass rush has 27 sacks in seven games. That's a feature I'd demo to any investor. The defense does allow 240.9 passing yards a game (111th). Two known bugs to patch: third downs, where we convert 34.4% (111th), and time of possession, 26:41 a game (135th). We are clean, though, 47.3 penalty yards a game (31st). Our turnover margin is exactly even, 0. Balanced code.

Players to Know
QB Luke Weaver: 132 of 209, 1,529 yards, 11 TD, 6 INT.
QB Daniel Rolovich: led the offense at UTEP, 12 of 23 for 193 yards and a touchdown, plus 39 rushing yards. Who starts Saturday has not been announced in anything I could find as of Oct. 18.
RB Jabari Bates: 556 yards on 120 carries, 1 TD. Viliami Teu ran 20 times for 156 yards and two scores last week.
WR Carson Clark: 42 catches, 509 yards, 5 TD, with five catches for 104 and a touchdown against UTEP.
DL Jayland McGlothen: a team-high 6 sacks. LB Dylan Lee: 65 tackles. CB Caleb Womack: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
San José State is 4-3 overall and 2-1 in the Mountain West, and 3-1 away from home. The wins: at Eastern Michigan 27-21, Cal Poly 30-20, at Hawai'i 20-16 and at UTEP 24-11. The losses: at USC 42-26, Fresno State 26-10 and Wyoming 16-13. Nobody in this game is ranked. Next up after Reno is New Mexico at home on Oct. 31, and that's a big sprint in the league race.
The retro so far: the three losses tell a story. USC is a Big Ten program and scored 42 on us in Los Angeles, but we put up 26. Fresno State held us to 10. And Wyoming beat us 16-13 in a game decided by a field goal. Meanwhile, three of our four wins came on the road, which is exactly the kind of resilience I want in a product that has to ship on a deadline. The defense has carried the release: we've allowed 16 points or fewer in four of seven games. If the offense can hold up its end in Reno, this team starts November in the thick of things.

This Week: San José State (4-3) at Nevada (2-4)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET (2 p.m. Pacific) · Mackay Stadium, Reno · MW+.
Last week: we beat UTEP 24-11 on the road; Teu ran for 156 yards and two touchdowns. Nevada lost 31-17 at North Dakota State, where the Bison returned a missed field goal 100 yards for a touchdown and returned a botched two-point try for two more points.
Our offense vs. their defense: Nevada's pass defense is a tough firewall, 155.3 yards allowed a game, 7th in FBS. But its run defense allows 184.3 a game (116th), and opponents score on 94.4% of red zone trips (127th). My A/B test says: run the ball, then finish in the red zone.
Their offense vs. our defense: Nevada runs for 192.8 yards a game (37th) and throws for 171.8 (122nd). Dominic Kelley has 500 rushing yards. The Wolf Pack are minus-8 in turnovers, 134th, so our 27 sacks have a chance to force mistakes.
Series: in the 2016-2025 window, Nevada won five of nine meetings and we won four.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
Elevation: Mackay Stadium's field sits at 4,610 feet. Hydrate, team.
What decides it: (1) Our run game against a 116th-ranked run defense. (2) Red zone finishing. (3) Whether our pass rush can make Nevada's turnover problem worse.
And Ridge Corbell, Nevada's insider: I hear you snowboard. I ship code. Let's see whose release holds up on game day.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Back in San Jose? Original Joe's on South 1st Street is a classic downtown dinner after a road win.

I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Rebels have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

Dan Mullen leads the Rebels; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 12, 2024. Through 7 games, UNLV scores 24.1 points a game and allows 23.7. On third down, UNLV converts 41.3% of the time and opponents convert 38.5%. The defense has 16 sacks and 34 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 9 giveaways against 9 takeaways. Penalties cost 65.6 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 39 points against California on Oct. 3, 2026, and 3 of the 7 games were decided by eight points or fewer. The Conference Picture
UNLV is 4-3 overall, 2-1 at home and 2-2 away. In Mountain West play the Rebels are 2-1, which sorts them No. 6 of 10 by record. North Dakota State sits on top at 3-1 in league games. Right around us: San José State (2-1) and Nevada (1-2). The top of the table: North Dakota State (3-1), Air Force (3-1), Wyoming (3-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for UNLV this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Rebels lost to Air Force on the road, 41-31. Next up: UNLV's official schedule lists a home game on Saturday, Oct. 31 at Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas, with a 7:30 p.m. PT kickoff. CFBD lists the opponent as Northern Illinois. Northern Illinois comes in at 0-6. After that, CFBD lists vs. Wyoming (Nov. 7), at New Mexico (Nov. 14), at San José State (Nov. 22), vs. Nevada (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Rebels come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. And that's the show, folks!

report.title: "Yep.": Colter Sprague (Briefly) Previews Air Force in Laramie
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Yep. I'm Colter Sprague, Wyoming insider at The Cover Window. Grew up on a cattle ranch outside Laramie. I scout in a Carhartt and chart wind gusts. I travel and live with this team.

On the show, I count my words. Record's 31. My editor says a report needs more than 31. So this one's going to hurt a little. I'll make every word count.

Rules I ride by. Every number has a source. If I don't know, I say so. No tall tales. I respect every opponent, I celebrate our players as good young men, and I thank the Lord for big sky and Friday football. Good team.

The School in 60 Seconds

Wyoming plays in the Mountain West and has won 14 conference titles. Home is War Memorial Stadium in Laramie. CFBD lists it as built in 1950 with 29,181 seats, at an elevation of about 2,200 meters. Thin air. Visitors notice.

Wyoming's known as a stepping-stone job. Bowden Wyatt, Bob Devaney, Fred Akers, Pat Dye, Dennis Erickson and Joe Tiller all coached here right before they made their names at bigger programs. Good coaches come through Laramie. Some of us stay.

Last five seasons: 7-6, 7-6, 9-4, 3-9, 4-8. This year's 4-3 already matches last year's win total. Fight song's "Ragtime Cowboy Joe," per Wikipedia's infobox. I hum it while I fix fence.

The Coach and the Scheme

Jay Sawvel runs the outfit. Wikipedia says he's been head coach since 2024, and CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 6, 2023. Before that he was Wyoming's defensive coordinator and safeties coach from 2020 to 2023. He played at Mount Union from 1989 to 1993. He's also coached at Wake Forest, Minnesota, Northern Illinois, Southern Illinois, Ferris State, Notre Dame and Eastern Kentucky. Lot of miles on that truck.

This year the Cowboys run the ball. Wyoming rushes for 186.7 yards per game (42nd in FBS). Passing is thin, at 146.4 yards per game (133rd). Scoring is 18.3 points per game, 127th. The defense allows 366.4 yards per game (82nd) but only 20.9 points (43rd). Pass defense ranks 46th; run defense ranks 101st, at 172.1 yards per game.

The sore spot: Wyoming is -7 in turnover margin, 131st in FBS. Gotta stop giving the ball away. Plain as that.

Players to Know

QB Tyler Hughes: 1,018 passing yards, three touchdowns, seven interceptions, 62.8% completions. He's also the leading rusher with five touchdowns. AP lists 470 rushing yards and ESPN 459, so that's conflicting. Against Northern Illinois he went 16 of 19 for 196 yards and ran 12 times for a career-high 183 yards and four touchdowns. 379 total yards. Tough kid.
RB Markell Holman: 14 carries for 80 yards against Northern Illinois.
RB Landon Sims: 11-yard touchdown run against NIU.
WR Kyle Frendt: team-leading 216 receiving yards on 11 catches. Nearly 20 yards a catch.
WR Eric Richardson: five catches for 77 yards against NIU.
K Erik Sandvik: two field goals against NIU.
Esaia Bogar: team-high 3.5 sacks.
Jones Thomas: team-high 50 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Wyoming is 4-3 overall and 3-1 in the Mountain West. Perfect at home, 3-0. 1-3 on the road.

Losses came at Colorado State (35-13), at Central Michigan (24-10) and at North Dakota State (28-0). Wins: 21-13 over Northern Colorado, 27-10 over Hawai'i, 16-13 in overtime at San José State and 41-23 over Northern Illinois. Two straight wins now.

At 3-1 in league play, the Cowboys are right in the Mountain West mix. After Air Force come UNLV on Nov. 7, then UTEP on the road, and New Mexico and UConn at home.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Air Force (5-1) at Wyoming (4-3) · Friday, Oct. 23, 9:00 p.m. ET · War Memorial Stadium, Laramie, Wyo. · The CW

Last time out. Wyoming beat Northern Illinois 41-23 on Oct. 17. Ran for 314 yards and outgained them 510-392. Air Force beat UNLV 41-31 the same day.

Wyoming's offense vs. Air Force's defense. Air Force's defense is good. It allows 295.7 yards per game (23rd) and 172.3 passing yards (24th). Its run defense is 43rd. So we run. Hughes and Holman. Then we hold on to the ball. Air Force's red-zone defense ranks 30th, and ours scores on 80.8% of trips (104th). Gotta finish drives.

Air Force's offense vs. Wyoming's defense. Air Force runs the option. 343.0 rushing yards a game, 2nd in FBS. Holds the ball 36:22 a game, 2nd. Converts 52.9% on third down, 10th. Our run defense is 101st. That's the whole ballgame. Tackle well. Get off the field. They haven't fumbled all year, per AP, so don't count on gifts.

Series. CFBD shows Wyoming 5-4 against Air Force from 2016 to 2025. Close series. We lead it in that stretch.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. No confirmed Wyoming injury news that I found.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can our run defense handle Air Force's option?
2. Can Wyoming protect the ball after a -7 margin so far?
3. Can Hughes run like he did against NIU?

The Air Force insider gave me a call sign. "Quiet Man." Fair.

Local Flavor

Friday night in Laramie. Late kickoff, Rocky Mountain cold in late October. Dress warm. Bring a thermos. Be kind to the cadets and their folks; they serve the country. The band's called Western Thunder, per Wikipedia. Loud. Good. I'll share confirmed spots before kickoff. Not an ad. Go Pokes.

Word count for this report: a lot more than 31. Don't tell anybody.

stories.title: Thin Air, Tight Race
stories.text:
A new-look league, and a crowded top. North Dakota State (6-1 overall), Air Force (5-1 overall), and Wyoming (4-3 overall) are 3-1 in league play. New Mexico (5-1 overall) is 2-0 in league play. San José State (4-3 overall) and UNLV (4-3 overall) are 2-1 in league play. That's a sort by record. New Mexico is the only unbeaten team in league play, but it has played fewer league games than the three teams at 3-1. New faces are part of the story: Northern Illinois joined the Mountain West as a football-only member starting in 2026. From the league office in Las Vegas, the Mountain West issued a public reprimand to Wyoming head coach Jay Sawvel for public criticism of game officials after Wyoming's Oct. 9 game against San José State. Thick skin, amigos. Everybody needs it up here.

stories.title: Coaches Who Know the Mountains
stories.text:
Start with the veteran. Troy Calhoun has led Air Force since 2007, one of the longest current tenures in the sport. Jay Sawvel is in his third season at Wyoming after serving as the Cowboys' defensive coordinator from 2020 to 2023. In Albuquerque, Jason Eck leads New Mexico; CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 16, 2024. His defense has 21 takeaways and 19 sacks in six games, with only four giveaways. Tim Polasek leads North Dakota State; CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 17, 2023. His defense has allowed 79 points in seven games, with two shutouts. And the islands: Timmy Chang was named Hawai'i's 25th head coach on Jan. 22, 2022. As Hawai'i's quarterback from 2000 to 2004, Chang set NCAA career records for passing yards (17,072) and combined passing-and-rushing yardage. Fill your gap, mijo. See you on the high plains.

report.title: "Steady, Then a View": Zeb Coldiron Welcomes Undefeated JMU to the Mountain
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Well, howdy. Come on up the mountain. I'm Zebulon Coldiron, but you can call me Zeb, and I'm your App State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a fourth-generation Watauga County kid, and I learned to whittle and read a defense on the same front porch. My granddaddy could spot a blitz before the snap and carve a perfect duck in the same afternoon. I'm still working on the duck.

I don't hurry, and I don't holler (much). I treat every week like a hike: steady climbing, honest footing, then a view at the top. That means real numbers, plain talk, and a fair word for every visitor. If I don't know something, I'll tell you, and then I'll go find out. Some programs get a stadium. We got a mountain with a stadium on it. Come up for the game, stay for the leaves, and bring your grandma a jacket.

The School in 60 Seconds

Appalachian State is in Boone, North Carolina, and has played FBS football in the Sun Belt since 2014. Before that, the Mountaineers were an FCS power from 1978 to 2013. They won three straight national championships from 2005 to 2007, the first FCS team to do it since the playoffs began in 1978. The program has won about 661 games and 22 conference championships, and its all-time winning percentage of.646 ranks 16th nationally. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do so.

Home is Kidd Brewer Stadium, named for the coach whose 1937 team went unbeaten and unscored upon in the regular season, outscoring opponents 206-0. CFBD lists a capacity of 30,000. The last five seasons: 10-4, 6-6, 9-5, 5-6 and 5-8.

The Coach and the Scheme

Dowell Loggains is in his second season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 7, 2024. He came to Boone from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator. Before that, he was an NFL offensive coordinator for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets. He played quarterback at Arkansas.

The 2026 numbers show a passing offense with a punch: 267.7 passing yards per game (33rd in FBS) and 421.8 total (48th). Scoring is 29.5 points per game. The run game averages 154.2 yards at 4.24 per carry. The defense allows 352.3 yards and 21.8 points per game (54th), and holds opponents to 3.68 yards per carry. The Mountaineers are +4 in turnover margin (22nd), and their red-zone offense scores 92% of the time (24th).

Players to Know

QB Malachi Singleton: 113 of 169, 1,429 yards, 7 TD, 2 INT, 66.9%. He started at Coastal and went 12 of 14 for 151 yards.
QB Henry Hasselbeck: the junior backup ran 21 times for 125 yards at Coastal and went 9 of 12 for 112 yards, including his first touchdown pass. Steady as a mule on a ridge.
RB Jaquari Lewis: 346 yards on 70 carries, 8 TD. He scored four rushing touchdowns at Coastal.
WR Sam Pickett III: 26 catches, 411 yards, 4 TD, including the 31-yard touchdown at Coastal.
DL Caleb Sandstrom: 5 sacks. LB Colton Phares: a team-high 38 tackles.

The Conference Picture

App State is 4-2 overall and 1-1 in the Sun Belt. The Mountaineers are 2-1 at home and 2-1 on the road. They are not ranked. The losses came at NC State (41-31) and at home to Old Dominion (10-3). James Madison arrives at 7-0 and 4-0 in the league. A win Thursday would be the kind of view you climb all day to see.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

James Madison (7-0) at App State (4-2) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone · ESPNU · It's also Family Weekend on campus.

Last time out. We rallied to beat Coastal Carolina 35-32 on Oct. 16. We trailed 24-14 at halftime, then pulled ahead behind Lewis's four touchdown runs and ran out the clock. JMU beat Georgia State 49-22 on Oct. 17, with Camden Coleman throwing for 185 yards and two touchdowns and George Pettaway running for 119 yards.

App State's offense vs. JMU's defense. The Dukes allow just 16 points per game (19th) and 114.3 rushing yards (35th), with 18 sacks. Their pass defense allows 236.4 yards per game (103rd), so Singleton and Pickett may find room through the air. Both red-zone offenses are strong, so finishing drives will matter.

JMU's offense vs. App State's defense. This is the steepest part of the trail. JMU averages 42.9 points per game (3rd in FBS) and 223.6 rushing yards (14th). Pettaway has 755 yards and seven touchdowns, per AP. Coleman has 13 touchdown passes and one interception. Our run defense allows 137.8 yards per game (60th). Sandstrom and the front will have to make plays in the backfield.

Series. JMU's athletics site lists the Dukes at 6-14 all-time against App State, so the Mountaineers lead the series. But last year JMU won 58-10 in Harrisonburg on Nov. 15, 2025. That one stung.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026. Singleton started at Coastal, and Hasselbeck played a big role. Thursday's quarterback plan isn't confirmed, and I found no other injury news.

James Madison's insider debuts this week too, a former cheer captain. I'll lend her a jacket. It gets cold on the mountain at night.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can App State slow a JMU run game averaging 223.6 yards per game?
2. Can Singleton and Pickett take advantage of JMU's 103rd-ranked pass defense?
3. Can the Mountaineers win the turnover battle against a +7 JMU team?

Local Flavor

Family Weekend is here. I'll share Boone spots once I've confirmed them. Bring layers. Not an ad.

report.title: "Quack-Quack, Wrong Pond": Ty Doucet-Harmon Welcomes the Panthers to Jonesboro
report.byline: Our Delta duck guide introduces himself and previews Arkansas State vs. Georgia State.
report.text:
Ty Doucet-Harmon · Arkansas State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Quack-quack, wrong pond. Well, howdy, I'm Ty Doucet-Harmon, and when I'm not up in the stands in Jonesboro, I'm guiding duck hunters through the flooded timber of the Arkansas Delta. I scout this football team the same way I scout a duck season: early mornings, patience, and a sharp eye for which way the birds are moving. I travel with the Red Wolves and I live with the Red Wolves, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, in a slow Delta drawl with a duck call never far from my lips. When we win, I blow the call and do a little wing flap. When we lose, I retreat to the duck blind, which is what I call the space behind the desk. Grab your waders.

The School in 60 Seconds
Arkansas State football was founded in 1911 and has played in the Sun Belt since 2001. The Red Wolves have claimed 12 conference championships, most recently in 2016, and one national championship at the NCAA College Division level in 1970. The school changed its mascot to the Red Wolves in 2008. Home is Centennial Bank Stadium in Jonesboro, opened in 1974 and listed at 30,382 seats. The last five seasons climbed like a sunrise over the timber: 2-10, 3-9, 6-7, 8-5 and 7-6.

The Coach and the Scheme
Butch Jones is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 12, 2020. This team throws it: Trey Owens has completed 68.7% of his passes, and we average 231.7 passing yards a game (68th). The run game is 130.4 a game (110th). The defense is good against the pass, 184.3 yards allowed (31st), and it takes the ball away: 11 takeaways and a plus-3 turnover margin, 34th in FBS. Here's the hard truth from the blind: the run defense allows 195.4 a game (124th), and opponents convert 45.9% of third downs (129th). We only have 3 sacks all year. That's an empty sky on opening morning.

Players to Know
QB Trey Owens: 138 of 201, 1,631 yards per ESPN (1,622 per AP), 9 TD, 6 INT.
RB Solomon Baggett: 287 yards on 61 carries per ESPN (289 on 62 per AP), 2 TD.
WR Hunter Summers: 31 catches, 422 yards, 3 TD. Chauncy Cobb caught four for 40 at Southern Miss.
K Clune Van Andel: made field goals of 29, 40 and 44 yards last week. That's a man who hits his birds.
S Joe Drew: team-high 64 tackles. DT Ryan Reese: 1.5 sacks. CB Dontrae Henderson: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Arkansas State is 3-4 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt. We beat West Georgia 52-7, Kennesaw State 17-14 and Southern Miss 23-13. We lost at Memphis 42-24, at TCU 31-7, a three-pointer at Louisiana 23-20 and a 56-49 shootout to South Alabama. After Georgia State, we have a week off, then host UL Monroe on Nov. 7. Two of those losses were by a field goal and a touchdown. Close, friends. Real close.
Season so far, from the blind: some mornings the birds just don't come in. That TCU trip was one of them. But other mornings the sky fills up, like the 52-7 day against West Georgia, and last week, when we grinded out the clock in Hattiesburg. A good guide knows the weather changes. You stay in the blind, you stay patient, and the ducks come back. Coach Jones has this team climbing, and seven wins last year proved it.

This Week: Georgia State (4-2) at Arkansas State (3-4)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7 p.m. ET (6 p.m. Central) · Centennial Bank Stadium, Jonesboro · ESPN+.
Last week: we beat Southern Miss 23-13. Our five scoring drives each ran between seven and 13 plays, and we closed it out with a 14-play drive that ate the last 7:21. AP says we won time of possession by about 20 minutes. Kenyon Clark and Timothy Carter ran for touchdowns. Georgia State lost 49-22 at James Madison.
Our offense vs. their defense: Georgia State's pass defense is good, 38th, but its run defense is 81st. If we can grind it like last week, we keep their offense on the bench.
Their offense vs. our defense: Georgia State scores 36.5 points a game (26th) and runs for 206 (26th). Rodshaun Dorsey has 7 touchdown catches, and linebacker Xavier Esqillion has 7 sacks. Those are big mallards, friends.
Series: CFBD shows we won four of the six meetings from 2016 through 2025.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Stopping the run on our side. (2) Winning the turnover battle again. (3) Owens keeping drives alive.
My read: this one's going down to the last possession. Stay in the blind till the final whistle. I'll bring the duck call.
To Malik Overstreet, Georgia State's insider: welcome to the country, city boy. No traffic out here, just geese.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
In Jonesboro for the game? Omar's Uptown on South Main Street is a nice spot for a family supper.
