report.title: "Gray Turf, Bright Future": Imogen Tremblay Brings Her Spreadsheet to Athens
report.byline: Our gray-turf data nerd introduces herself and previews Eastern Michigan at Ohio.
report.text:
Imogen Tremblay · Eastern Michigan Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Gray turf, bright future! Hi, I'm Imogen Tremblay. I studied education in Ypsilanti, I build spreadsheets for fun, and I have one tab, color-coded, devoted entirely to the "gray turf advantage." My model says it's worth 1.3 points. My heart says 13. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll walk you through the players, the matchups and the history, plus at least one gentle reminder that Ypsilanti is not Ann Arbor's little brother. We are Ann Arbor's cooler cousin with better parking. When we win, I'll show you a spreadsheet with one enormous green cell, and I will squeal. When we lose, I'll update the model, grimly, and come back next week with more columns. Thanks for being here.

The School in 60 Seconds
Eastern Michigan has played football since 1891, missing only 1944. Before we were the Eagles, we were the Normalites (1899-1928) and the Hurons (1929-1990). We've had five undefeated seasons: 1906, 1925, 1927, 1943 and 1945, and the 1943 team didn't allow a point. Our golden age ran from 1925 through 1939 under Elton Rynearson, and our stadium carries his name. The field inside is Crosby Field at "The Factory," and yes, it's gray. CFBD lists Rynearson at 30,200 seats. We compete in the Mid-American Conference. Spreadsheet note: the all-time record is 490-622-47. Honesty is a column too.

The Coach and the Scheme
Chris Creighton was hired Dec. 11, 2013, which makes him a fixture in Ypsilanti. His teams went 7-6 and 9-4 in 2021 and 2022. The 2026 offense leans on the arm: 215 passing yards a game (86th) and 105 rushing yards (128th), for 21.5 points a game (110th). It converts 41.9% of third downs, 56th in FBS, which is a nice green cell. The defense allows 379.3 yards a game (97th) and 25.9 points (92nd). The stat I love most is quieter: EMU averages just 41.8 penalty yards a game, 15th-fewest in the country. Clean football is my love language, and also my spreadsheet's.

Players to Know
QB Noah Kim: 169 of 285, 1,678 yards, 11 TD, 4 INT. Against Toledo he threw for 214 yards and two touchdowns.
RB Amareon Blue: 338 yards on 68 carries, 3 TD.
TE Joshua Long: a team-high 38 catches for 366 yards and 2 TD, including seven for 84 and a score last week.
LB Zach Mowchan: a team-high 58 tackles. DL Quincy Byas: 4 sacks. DB Caleb Dobbs: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Eastern Michigan is 4-4 overall and 3-1 in the MAC. The league wins came at Massachusetts 38-14, at Akron 25-23 and against Sacramento State 28-17 to open the year. The MAC loss was last week, 34-14 to Toledo. Non-league games at Michigan State and Wisconsin were losses. After this, Central Michigan is next, on Nov. 4. A road win in Athens would keep the Eagles near the top of the MAC standings. My spreadsheet would need a new color.
The season, cell by cell: we opened by beating Sacramento State 28-17 and lost 27-21 to San José State, then dropped road games at Michigan State (35-7) and Wisconsin (54-10). Since then: Lindenwood 29-3, at UMass 38-14, at Akron 25-23 and the Toledo loss. That's three road wins already, and two of them were MAC games. On defense, we've forced nine turnovers and committed ten. The pass rush has 12 sacks and has allowed 14. None of those cells are glowing green yet, but none of them are red either. They're gray. Like the turf. Which, as I've explained, is a good sign.

This Week: Eastern Michigan (4-4) at Ohio (5-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Peden Stadium, Athens, Ohio · ESPNU. It's Ohio's Senior Day and Heroes Day, and the Bobcats' last Saturday home game of 2026.
Last week: we lost 34-14 to Toledo on homecoming; Kim was 16 of 36 for 214 yards. Ohio beat Sacramento State 48-7.
Our offense vs. their defense: Ohio allows 198.4 passing yards (52nd) and 138.7 rushing (62nd). But the Bobcats let opponents convert 42.1% of third downs, 106th, and we're 56th at converting them. That is a column I'm watching.
Their offense vs. our defense: Ohio runs for 207 yards a game, 24th in FBS. We allow 142.3 on the ground (71st). Our run defense is the whole story.
Series: Ohio leads 22-12-1 and has won four straight, including 28-21 in Ypsilanti last year. Our last win was 27-20 in Athens in 2016. Ten years! My model would like a word. Last year's game was a shootout of sorts on our gray turf: Ohio quarterback Parker Navarro threw for a career-high 315 yards, and two Bobcat receivers went over 100 yards. Keeping their passing game in check this time starts with knowing that Ohio's 2026 offense is built differently, on the ground.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Whether we can slow Ohio's run game. (2) Third downs on both sides. (3) Kim's accuracy; 44.4% last week won't do.
And Penny Trautman, Ohio's lovely insider: I hear you build things brick by brick. I build them cell by cell. Let's compare blueprints.

report.title: "I Expected This. I Always Expect This.": Ozzie Brannigan Guards the Wagon Wheel
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, Golden Flashes fans. Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Ozzie Brannigan, your Kent State insider. I graduated from a campus with a famous fashion school, so I rate two things every week: uniforms and fourth-down decisions. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm a pessimist, and the annoying part is how often I'm right. When we lose, I say, "I expected this," and I mean it. When we win, there's a stunned silence, and then I say, "I expected this," which is not true at all. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with realistic expectations. Very realistic. "I expected this. I always expect this."

The School in 60 Seconds
Kent State plays at Dix Stadium, listed at 25,319. This week is the Wagon Wheel game against Akron, a trophy that dates to 1946. Here is a rare happy fact: Kent State won the first nine Wagon Wheel games. And another one, which makes me nervous: we hold the Wheel right now after beating Akron 42-35 last season. We also won in 2020, 2021 and 2022, including a 69-35 game in 2020. Akron won in 2023 and 2024. Akron leads the all-time series, 26-19-1 per CollegeFootballDigest, or 37-29-2 per other references. Either way, I expected that.

The Coach and the Scheme
Mark Carney is Kent State's 24th head coach. He was interim coach starting in April 2025, and the school removed the interim tag on Oct. 30, 2025. This season has been a struggle. We score 12 points a game, 138th in FBS, and gain 273.1 yards a game (137th). The running game averages 2.93 yards a carry, with 5 rushing touchdowns and 4 passing. The defense allows 32 points (120th). The bright spot: the pass rush has 15 sacks. The other spot, less bright: 72.6 penalty yards a game, 120th in FBS, and a minus-4 turnover margin. I'm rating the uniforms higher than the turnover margin. The uniforms are lovely. On defense, the totals are mid-pack: 363.6 yards allowed a game (77th) and 141.4 rushing yards (69th). The pass defense allows 222.1 (89th). Not terrible. I'm not saying good. I'm saying not terrible.

Players to Know
QB Dru DeShields: 1,145 yards, 4 TD, 6 INT, 57.3% completions. At South Florida he went 17 of 30 for 165 yards with no interceptions. Progress. I'm suspicious of progress.
WR Wayne Harris: 30 catches, 384 yards, 1 TD. WR Brendyn Smith had four catches for 56 yards last week.
RB Mason King: 202 yards and 1 TD on 52 carries. RB Brandon White ran 10 times for 37 yards at South Florida and caught two passes.
LB Hayden Dawahare: 33 tackles and 2 sacks, including 9 tackles and a sack at South Florida.

The Conference Picture
We're 2-5 overall and 1-2 in the MAC, 2-1 at home and 0-4 on the road. The wins: Wofford 36-15 and Ball State 26-13, both at Dix. The losses included trips to South Carolina and Ohio State, plus a 13-10 loss to Ohio at home. Then came 38-7 at Western Michigan and 29-2 at South Florida. Two points last week. I expected this. But we're home again, and home is where the wins have been.

This Week: Akron (1-6) at Kent State (2-5)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 1 p.m. ET · Dix Stadium · ESPN+. Forecast: 59 degrees and sunny. I'll bring an umbrella anyway.
Last week: we lost 29-2 at South Florida. Akron lost 34-14 at Miami (OH), with QB Brayden Roggow throwing four interceptions.
Our offense vs. their defense: Akron allows 200.4 rushing yards a game, 130th in FBS, and 6.05 yards a carry. If our run game is ever going to work, it's this week. I'm saying that out loud, which means it probably won't.
Their offense vs. our defense: RB Jordan Gant has 452 yards. Roggow has thrown 8 interceptions, and Akron has given up 19 sacks. Our 15 sacks could matter a lot. Akron's red-zone defense ranks 114th, so if we ever get inside the 20, we have to finish. Historically, I would not assume that.
Series: Akron leads (26-19-1 per CollegeFootballDigest), but we won last year 42-35.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Turnovers. Akron is minus-7, and we're minus-4. (2) Can our run game exploit Akron's run defense? (3) Penalties. Ours are a problem.
And to Zip Grubbs, Akron's insider: your tread is impressive. I fully expect it to be a close game. That's the scary part.

report.title: "Shot Heard 'Round the Film Room": Abner Kettleworth Marches the Minutemen to East Hartford
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Greetings from the Pioneer Valley, friends. I'm Abner Kettleworth, your Massachusetts insider at The Cover Window. I was an organic farmer in the Five College area until I started grinding game tape, and now I travel and live with this team. I still bring kale chips on the bus. Nobody eats them.

Fair warning: I make a Revolutionary War pun for every scheme. One if by run, two if by pass. I'm also a stickler for the truth, which seems fitting for a Minuteman. Every number I give you carries a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you I'm still waiting on Paul Revere's report. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for every chilly autumn Friday. Shot heard 'round the film room.

The School in 60 Seconds

UMass began playing football in 1879. The Minutemen reached three FCS national championship games and won the title in 1998. They've played home games at Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium since 1965, and CFBD lists its capacity at 17,000. UMass began moving up to FBS in 2011 and was an associate MAC member until leaving after the 2015 season. After years as an independent, the school announced in February 2024 that it would rejoin the MAC. CFBD lists UMass as a MAC member this season.

The last five seasons were a long winter at Valley Forge: 1-11, 1-11, 3-9, 2-10 and 0-12 in 2025. That's why this year's 4-3 start feels like spring planting.

The Coach and the Scheme

Joe Harasymiak leads the regiment. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 4, 2024. In December 2015 he became the youngest head coach in Division I football when Maine hired him. He went 20-15 there in three seasons, and his 2018 team won the CAA and reached the FCS semifinals. He later was co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach at Minnesota, then defensive coordinator at Rutgers from 2022 to 2024.

You can see that defensive résumé in the numbers. UMass allows 307.9 yards per game (30th in FBS) and 19.1 points (33rd). The pass defense ranks 30th at 183.1 yards per game, and the run defense ranks 45th at 124.7. The Minutemen are +7 in turnover margin, 8th in FBS, and they've returned two interceptions for touchdowns. That's a militia that shows up on time.

The offense is a work in progress. UMass gains 339.1 yards per game (113th) and scores 28.0 points (77th). It runs for 160.1 yards per game (64th) and throws for 179.0 (117th).

Players to Know

QB William Watson III: 820 yards, 7 TD, 2 INT, 74.0% completions. CollegeFootballDigest lists him going 20 of 27 for 210 yards against Eastern Michigan.
QB Logan Inagawa: played quarterback at Buffalo, going 14 of 25 for 168 yards with an interception. He also ran 19 times for 66 yards and a touchdown. I don't know which quarterback starts Friday, and I won't guess.
RB Elijah Faulkner: 361 yards on 83 carries, one touchdown. He ran 23 times for 84 yards and scored at Buffalo.
RB Curtis Kimmons IV: 297 rushing yards and four touchdowns, per ESPN.
WR T.Y. Harding: team-best 28 catches for 327 yards and two touchdowns. CollegeFootballDigest lists nine catches for 91 yards against Miami (Ohio).
WR Kezion Dia-Johnson: five catches for 79 yards at Buffalo.
LB Timmy Hinspeter: the tackle leader. ESPN's API lists 59 tackles and its web page lists 51, so his total is conflicting.
DL William DePaepe: team-high two sacks.

The Conference Picture

UMass is 4-3 overall and 1-3 in the MAC. The Minutemen won their first four games: 37-21 at Rutgers, 37-10 over Sacred Heart, 36-14 over Stonehill and 35-6 at Sacramento State. Then came three losses: 38-14 to Eastern Michigan, 20-19 to Miami (Ohio) and 25-18 in overtime at Buffalo. Two of those three were decided by a point or in overtime.

This is a nonconference game, since UConn is an FBS independent. After it, UMass hosts Ball State on Nov. 4. Then come Toledo on the road, Akron at home and Bowling Green on the road.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

UMass (4-3) at UConn (3-3) · Friday, Oct. 23, 7:00 p.m. ET · Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field, East Hartford, Conn. · CBS Sports Network

Last time out. UMass lost 25-18 in overtime at Buffalo on Oct. 17. UConn had a bye after beating Temple 34-20 on Oct. 10.

UMass' offense vs. UConn's defense. Here's the opening for our redcoats-and-raccoon-caps attack. UConn's pass defense allows 290.5 yards per game, 135th in FBS. Opponents convert 43.3% of third downs against the Huskies (113th). Watson completes 74% of his passes, so short throws to Harding can move the chains. UConn's run defense is stronger, at 117.0 yards per game (39th).

UConn's offense vs. UMass' defense. UConn can fire cannons. The Huskies gain 451.8 yards per game (24th) and score 35.7 points (29th). Kalieb Osborne has 1,421 passing yards and Cyncir Bowers has 433 rushing yards. At Temple, Trey Cornist ran seven times for 114 yards. Our defense has the numbers to answer, and the turnover margin matters most. UMass is +7, and UConn is even. UConn also averages 79.0 penalty yards a game, 130th in FBS.

Series. CFBD shows UConn 4-2 against UMass from 2016 to 2025. CollegeFootballDigest lists UConn ahead 6-4 all-time, with a 47-42 UConn win in 2024 and a 27-13 UMass win in 2021. Those last figures are thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. The quarterback plan is unknown after Inagawa played at Buffalo.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Watson or Inagawa exploit UConn's 135th-ranked pass defense?
2. Can the +7 turnover margin travel?
3. Can UMass finally win a close one after two one-score league losses?

Local Flavor

It's Friday night under the lights at the Rent. UConn calls it "The Rent at Night," and it's also the Huskies' Cancer Awareness game. That's a cause worth cheering for, whatever colors you wear. I'll bring a thermos of cider and a heart full of thanks. Not an ad.

report.title: "Another Coach from the Cradle, Darling": Cordelia Van Doren Takes the RedHawks to Mount Pleasant
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good afternoon, RedHawks, and welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Cordelia Van Doren, your Miami (OH) insider. I'm a brick-campus girl through and through, and I know every coach who has ever walked through Oxford. I travel with this team and I live with this team, usually in a cardigan. I do have one small habit. I ambush my co-hosts with coaching-tree trivia when they least expect it. When we win, I add a gold star to my Cradle of Coaches chart. When we lose, I remind everyone that even legends lost once, and then I tell you exactly which legends and when. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with a little history pinned to the lapel. "Another coach from the Cradle, darling."

The School in 60 Seconds
Miami is the Cradle of Coaches, and that's not my phrase. The term was coined in 1959 by Bob Kurz. The honor roll includes Paul Brown, Weeb Ewbank, Ara Parseghian and Bo Schembechler. Pop quiz: name another campus that produced all four. I'll wait. In the modern era the RedHawks keep adding chapters. Under Chuck Martin, Miami won the 2019 MAC championship, beating Central Michigan 26-21 in the title game, and the 2023 title, beating No. 23 Toledo 23-14. Home is Yager Stadium in Oxford, listed at 24,286.

The Coach and the Scheme
Chuck Martin was hired on Dec. 3, 2013, which makes him one of the longest-serving coaches in the conference. Here's how the 2026 team plays, by the numbers. Miami runs on about 56% of its plays, at 4.44 yards a carry, with 10 rushing touchdowns. It throws for 216.3 yards a game, with 9 passing touchdowns. The offense averages 26.9 points, and the defense allows 25.6. The defense holds opponents to 3.6 yards a carry, but the pass defense allows 276.9 yards a game. Miami has forced 8 turnovers and lost only 5. The pass rush has 14 sacks, though the protection has given up 16. My mild worry, said with love.

Players to Know
QB David McComb (No. 16): 1,120 passing yards and 7 TD. Against UConn he went 19 of 29 for 312 yards and two touchdowns, then ran one in himself.
RB Rodney Nelson (No. 5): 348 yards and 2 TD. Last week against Akron he ran 13 times for 142 yards and two scores. A gold star, darling, and a second one for style.
LB Malcolm McCain (No. 3): 57 tackles, including 10 against Akron.

The Conference Picture
Miami is 4-3 overall and 2-1 in the MAC, 3-1 at home and 1-2 on the road. The early schedule was demanding: a 59-14 loss at Pittsburgh, a 35-31 loss at Cincinnati, and a 24-21 win over UConn. The conference loss was 24-20 to Bowling Green. Since then we've won at Massachusetts 20-19 and beaten Akron 34-14. Two straight wins, and a chance to make it three. The margins have been tight: four of our seven games were decided by four points or fewer: Cincinnati, UConn, Bowling Green and Massachusetts. Darling, that is game management, and Coach Martin has run this sideline since he was hired in December 2013. Close games are where experience earns its gold stars.

This Week: Miami (OH) (4-3) at Central Michigan (3-4)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 1 p.m. ET · Kelly/Shorts Stadium, Mount Pleasant · ESPN+. The forecast calls for 60 degrees and mostly sunny. Cardigan weather, naturally, with pearls optional.
Last week: Miami beat Akron 34-14. Central Michigan lost 21-14 to Western Michigan.
Our offense vs. their defense: Central Michigan allows 4.82 yards a carry, so Nelson and our run game have a real opportunity. The Chippewas allow 174.3 passing yards a game.
Their offense vs. our defense: Central Michigan runs on 66% of its plays. QB Angel Flores has 618 rushing yards and 4 TD on the ground, plus 475 passing yards. We hold teams to 3.6 yards a carry. Contain Flores, and the Chippewas' passing game, at 108.1 yards a game, has to carry the load.
Series: Miami leads 17-13-1 and has won five straight, most recently 46-7 in 2024. Central Michigan's last win came in 2014.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 14 sacks and has allowed 16, with 8 takeaways against 5 giveaways, and it has 10 rushing and 9 passing touchdowns.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Containing Flores on the ground. (2) Protecting McComb from a defense with 12 sacks. (3) Turnovers. Central Michigan has lost 11.
And to Brynn Haverkamp, Central Michigan's insider: trivia ambush, darling. Who coached both at Miami and Michigan? You have until kickoff.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Visiting Oxford? Bagel & Deli on East High Street is an institution. Mac & Joe's is on the same street.

report.title: "Brick by Brick": Penny Trautman Lays Out Senior Day at Peden
report.byline: Our brick-street archivist introduces herself and previews Ohio vs. Eastern Michigan.
report.text:
Penny Trautman · Ohio Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Brick by brick, friends. I'm Penny Trautman, and I live in Athens, Ohio, where the streets are brick, the hills are green, and the Bobcats run the football like they're laying Court Street, one solid block at a time. I'm a brick-street archivist by hobby (it's a real hobby; I have a binder), and I chart this run game the same way. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with some hill-country wit and an unreasonable number of brick puns. When we win, I tap a brick for luck and grin. When we lose, I say "brick by brick" and start rebuilding by Monday. Welcome to the porch. One more thing: I'll always be honest with you, even when the mortar's cracked.

The School in 60 Seconds
Ohio is the senior member of the Mid-American Conference. The Bobcats have played home games at Peden Stadium since 1929, and CFBD lists it at 24,000 seats. The recent run has been one of the steadiest in the league: 10-4 in 2022, 10-3 in 2023, 11-3 in 2024 and 9-4 in 2025. That's four straight winning seasons stacked like good masonry. Saturday is the last Saturday home game at Peden this year, with a Senior Day celebration before kickoff and Heroes Day honoring military members and first responders. Bring a flag and a thank-you.

The Coach and the Scheme
John Hauser is in his first season as head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 26, 2025. His Bobcats run it with purpose: 207 rushing yards a game, 24th in FBS, 1,449 yards on 289 carries. The passing game is a supporting wall, 164.3 yards a game (126th). The defense allows 22.1 points (57th) and 337.1 yards (51st). One crack to fill: opponents convert 42.1% of third downs, 106th. And we play clean, 42.6 penalty yards a game, 18th-fewest. A tidy wall stands longer.
The season, brick by brick: we opened at Nebraska and lost 49-21, then beat Jacksonville State 29-27. A 41-36 loss at South Alabama followed, and since then it's been four straight wins: Stonehill 35-7, at Kent State 13-10, Central Michigan 31-14 and at Sacramento State 48-7. The Kent State game was a grinder, the kind you win with defense and patience. The Central Michigan game was the template: run the ball, avoid mistakes, and let the fourth quarter come to you. Turnovers have been even-ish, eight lost and five gained, and the pass rush has 13 sacks while allowing 12.

Players to Know
QB Nick Poulos: 38 of 68, 503 yards, 5 TD, no interceptions. Last week he went 11 of 14 for 165 and a touchdown, and ran five times for 48 yards.
RB Duncan Brune: 330 yards on 73 carries, 3 TD. Irving Brown ran eight times for 87 yards and a score at Sacramento State.
WR Riley Neer: 32 catches, 441 yards, 5 TD. Preston Bowman caught three for 94 and a touchdown last week.
LB Michael Molnar: a team-high 52 tackles and an interception. DE Ike Ackerman: 4.5 sacks.

The Conference Picture
Ohio is 5-2 and 3-0 in the MAC, and 3-0 at home. The losses were at Nebraska and at South Alabama, both outside the league. In the MAC we've beaten Kent State 13-10, Central Michigan 31-14 and Sacramento State 48-7. Eastern Michigan comes in 3-1 in the league, so this is a real conference test. Next is a trip to Akron on Nov. 3.

This Week: Eastern Michigan (4-4) at Ohio (5-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Peden Stadium · ESPNU. Senior Day and Heroes Day.
Last week: we beat Sacramento State 48-7 out west. Eastern Michigan lost 34-14 to Toledo.
Our offense vs. their defense: EMU allows 142.3 rushing yards a game (71st) and 237 passing (106th). That is a street I'd like to pave.
Their offense vs. our defense: Noah Kim has 1,678 passing yards and 11 TD, and EMU converts 41.9% on third down. Our third-down defense, 106th, is the brick that has to hold. EMU's run game, 128th, gives our front a chance to make them one-dimensional.
Series: Ohio leads 22-12-1 in 35 meetings since 1976. We've won four straight, including 28-21 in Ypsilanti last year and 35-10 here in 2024. EMU's last win in the series was 27-20 in Athens in 2016. Last year in Ypsilanti, Parker Navarro threw for a career-high 315 yards, and receivers Rodney Harris and Chase Hendricks each went over 100. Different Bobcats this year, same goal.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our run game against a 71st-ranked run defense. (2) Third-down defense. (3) Poulos staying turnover-free.
And Imogen Tremblay, EMU's insider: I like your spreadsheet. I'll trade you a brick for a cell.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
In Athens on Saturday? Casa Nueva on West State Street is a long-loved local spot for a family meal.

report.title: "Plate It Up": Mateo Villaseñor Brings the Hornets to Muncie
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
¡Hola, Hornets! Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Mateo Villaseñor, your Sacramento State insider. I'm a farm-to-fork chef in the capital city, and before that I played linebacker for the Hornets, so I explain defenses the only way I know: like recipes. A good defense is a good sauce. Balance, heat and nobody leaving early. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I narrate every play like a cooking competition. When we win, it's "Plate it up, chef!" and a chef's kiss. When we lose, I say, "Back to the kitchen," and sharpen a knife. On paper. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, served fresh.

The School in 60 Seconds
This is a brand-new menu. Sacramento State joined the MAC as a football-only member on July 1, 2026, for a five-year term, moving up from FCS to FBS. The Hornets took the spot left by Northern Illinois, which moved to the Mountain West. The rest of our sports play in the Big West. Last year, in our final Big Sky season, we went 7-5 and 5-3 in the league. Home is Hornet Stadium in Sacramento, listed at 21,195. And this is our first-ever meeting with Ball State. New dish, new kitchen, same hungry Hornets.

The Coach and the Scheme
Alonzo Carter was hired on Dec. 15, 2025, after Brennan Marion left for Colorado. Carter is a first-time head coach who spent eight seasons on Brent Brennan's staffs at San Jose State and Arizona, and he's a Northern California native who started out as a high school coach in the state. In 2026 the ingredients are still coming together. We score 15.0 points a game (135th) and gain 302.7 yards (132nd). The pass defense is our best dish, allowing just 188.9 yards a game, 37th in FBS. But the run defense allows 176.1 yards a game (107th). And the turnover margin is minus-10, 137th in FBS, with 13 lost and 3 forced. Third downs (33.0%, 120th) and penalties (77.1 yards a game, 128th) need seasoning, too. Back to the kitchen.

Players to Know
WR Matthew Coleman (No. 2): 36 catches, 473 yards, 4 TD. At Bowling Green he caught six for 85 yards and a touchdown. Plate it up.
QB Jackson Sharman (No. 8): 1,070 yards, 6 TD, 6 INT, 55.5% completions. QB Brian Salazar went 4 of 5 for 71 yards and a TD against Ohio.
RB Isaiah Ene: 246 yards and 1 TD on 48 carries, including 59 yards on seven carries last week.
S Boogsie Silvera (No. 1): 42 tackles and an interception. At Bowling Green he had nine tackles and an interception. The man is a five-star ingredient.

The Conference Picture
We're 1-6 overall and 0-4 in the MAC. The win: 52-0 over Mississippi Valley State. The losses include Eastern Michigan 28-17, Fresno State, North Dakota State, UMass, Bowling Green and Ohio, 48-7 last week. Year one at a new level is a long tasting menu. Kent State visits next. Here's the honest chef's note: the jump from FCS is the hardest recipe in college football, and the MAC paid attention to Sacramento State for a reason. When the league added us, the commissioner talked about the school's demonstrated success in football and its commitment to investing in the program. Year one is the prep work. The plating comes later.

This Week: Sacramento State (1-6) at Ball State (2-5)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Scheumann Stadium, Muncie · ESPN+. It's Ball State's homecoming, and the school is celebrating 100 years of homecoming. A big party. We're the guests.
Last week: we lost 48-7 to Ohio. Ball State beat Bowling Green 32-31.
Our offense vs. their defense: Ball State allows 37.9 points (135th), 445.3 yards (131st) and 201.6 rushing yards a game (131st). Its third-down defense ranks 126th. This is the best chance we've had in weeks to cook. Ene ran for 59 yards on seven carries last week, so give him more touches against a defense allowing over 200 yards a game on the ground.
Their offense vs. our defense: Ball State QB Keldric Luster ran 17 times for 125 yards and a touchdown last week. RB T.J. Horton has 7 rushing TD. Our run defense ranks 107th, so stopping the run is job one.
Series: first meeting.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Turnovers. We're minus-10. That has to stop. (2) The red zone. We score on 70.6% of trips (130th). (3) Penalties. Both teams are near the bottom.
And to Gus Ponder, Ball State's insider: happy 100th homecoming, my friend. I'll bring dessert, fresh from the Sacramento farms.

report.title: "That's 400 Horsepower of Run Game": Rocco Szczepanski Welcomes the Champs to the Glass Bowl
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
How ya doin', Rocket fans! Welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Rocco Szczepanski, your Toledo insider. That's Szczepanski. It's silent. nah, it's all pronounced, just fast. I come from a Jeep-plant family here in the Glass City, so I grade offenses the only way I know how: in horsepower. A sputtering three-and-out is a lawnmower engine. A long, physical drive is a big V8 rumbling down Front Street. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I rev an imaginary engine and do a burnout gesture right there on set. When we lose, I say "engine trouble" and pop the hood on the depth chart. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, Northwest Ohio style. "That's 400 horsepower of run game."

The School in 60 Seconds
Toledo plays at the Glass Bowl, listed at 26,038, a great old stadium in a city built on hard work. The Rockets won the MAC championship in 2022. This season there's a new man in charge: Mike Jacobs came from Mercer to replace Jason Candle as head coach. The rivalry with Western Michigan goes back a long way, and Toledo leads the all-time series 39-24. But the Broncos won last year's meeting 14-13, and you better believe that's been in the garage all year.

The Coach and the Scheme
Mike Jacobs was named head coach on Dec. 10, 2025. The 2026 numbers say this engine is running. Toledo averages 36.3 points (28th in FBS) and 459.0 yards a game (20th). It passes for 273.4 yards a game and runs for 185.6, at 5.09 yards a carry, with 16 rushing touchdowns. Here's the best part, horsepower-wise: the blockers have allowed only 3 sacks all season. The Conference Picture
Toledo is 5-2 overall and 2-1 in the MAC, 3-1 at home and 2-1 on the road. The Rockets aren't ranked. The losses were at Michigan State, 30-20, and at home to Buffalo, 23-8. The wins: Central Connecticut 63-10, San Diego State 41-16, Ball State 39-24 on the road and Eastern Michigan 34-14. There was also a wild 49-48 win over Temple. Beat the defending MAC champs and we're right back in the race.

This Week: Western Michigan (5-2) at Toledo (5-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Glass Bowl · CBS Sports Network.

Our offense vs. their defense: this is the dyno test. Western Michigan allows only 16.9 points a game (25th), and its red-zone defense ranks 17th. The Broncos have 16 sacks, but we've only allowed 3.
Their offense vs. our defense: Western Michigan runs on 63% of plays, and RB Jalen Buckley ran for 150 yards last week. Its passing game ranks 129th. If we stop Buckley, they'll have a hard time catching up.
Series: Toledo leads 39-24, but Western Michigan won last year 14-13.
One more set of numbers for the notebook: this team has 20 sacks and has allowed 3, with 8 takeaways against 8 giveaways, and it has 16 rushing and 15 passing touchdowns.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can Richter keep the ball safe against a team that's plus-4 in turnovers? (2) Can our run defense stop Buckley? (3) Penalties. Ours have to come down. Seventy-six yards a game is like driving with the parking brake on. Fix that and this engine purrs. (4) Ball security. We've lost 8 turnovers and forced 8, so it's even, but the Broncos only give it away about once every other game.
And to Corwin Dahlquist, Western Michigan's insider: love the pancakes, buddy. Bring syrup. We'll bring the horsepower.

report.title: "That's a Full Stack": Corwin Dahlquist Takes the Broncos to the Glass Bowl
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hi there, Bronco fans, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Corwin Dahlquist, your Western Michigan insider. I studied paper engineering here in Kalamazoo, a town with deep paper-mill roots, so yes, I can tell you the tensile strength of a playbook page. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm an earnest Michigan nerd, and I rate every opponent the way you'd rate a Kalamazoo diner breakfast. A short stack is light work. A full stack means you'll need a nap afterward. When we win, I declare a full stack and do a big syrup-pour gesture. When we lose, I mourn "short stack today" and eat dry toast on air, because I believe in accountability. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, served hot.

The School in 60 Seconds
Last season was a full stack with whipped cream on top. Western Michigan won the 2025 MAC championship, only the fourth conference title in school history. Lance Taylor was named MAC Coach of the Year. Quarterback Broc Lowry was MAC Offensive Player of the Year, and defensive end Nadame Tucker was Defensive Player of the Year and won the Vern Smith Leadership Award as the league's top player. The 2025 team won seven conference games, tied for the second-most in school history behind the 8-0 run in 2016. The Broncos also won the Cannon Trophy in 2023 and 2025, and Michigan MAC Trophies in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and they finished the season in the Myrtle Beach Bowl against Kennesaw State. Last year they averaged 20,000 fans a game at home for the first time since 2016. Home is Waldo Stadium in Kalamazoo, listed at 30,200.

The Coach and the Scheme
Lance Taylor was hired on Dec. 8, 2022, and in December 2025 he signed an extension through the 2030 season. The 2026 numbers say Western Michigan runs the ball and plays defense. It runs on about 63% of its plays for 164.7 yards a game, with 13 rushing touchdowns. The defense allows just 16.9 points a game, 25th in FBS. It has 16 sacks and has allowed only 9. The Broncos have lost only three turnovers and are plus-4 in turnover margin (22nd). They're also disciplined, at 45.0 penalty yards a game (24th). The passing game is the short stack right now: 157.6 yards a game ranks 129th.

Players to Know
RB Jalen Buckley: 542 yards and 7 TD on 102 carries. At Central Michigan he ran 24 times for 150 yards and two touchdowns. He was the 2023 MAC Freshman of the Year. Full stack.
QB Broc Lowry: 1,044 yards, 8 TD, just 1 INT, 68.0% completions. He's the reigning MAC Offensive Player of the Year.
WR Aveion Chenault: 22 catches, 326 yards, 1 TD.
I couldn't verify 2026 defensive leaders from a free source, so I'm not listing any. Accuracy is a full stack, too.

The Conference Picture
Western Michigan is 5-2 overall and 3-0 in the MAC, 2-1 at home and 3-1 on the road. The wins: Monmouth 49-14, Rice 28-21, Buffalo 20-17, Kent State 38-7 and Central Michigan 21-14. The Broncos have won three straight and four of their last five. The losses were 13-12 at Michigan and at home to Boise State. Staying unbeaten in the MAC is the goal, and Bowling Green comes to Waldo next.

This Week: Western Michigan (5-2) at Toledo (5-2)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Glass Bowl, Toledo · CBS Sports Network.
Last week: we beat Central Michigan 21-14 on the road, with Buckley running for 150 yards. Toledo beat Eastern Michigan 34-14.
Our offense vs. their defense: Toledo allows 125.4 rushing yards a game (46th) and 23.6 points (69th). Buckley and our run game need to win up front.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is a big one. Toledo scores 36.3 points a game (28th) and averages 459.0 yards (20th). QB John Alan Richter has 1,853 yards, 14 TDs and one interception. Our defense allows 16.9 points a game, and our red-zone defense is 17th. Toledo has allowed only 3 sacks all year, so getting pressure will be hard.
Series: Toledo leads the all-time series 39-24, but we won last year's meeting 14-13.
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026.
What decides it: (1) Can Buckley keep the chains moving and the Toledo offense off the field? (2) Can our defense slow Richter? (3) Penalties. We're 24th in FBS, Toledo is 126th. Free yards matter in a close game.
And to Rocco Szczepanski, Toledo's insider: I rate your offense a full stack, my friend. Ours is a full stack with blueberries.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Watching in Kalamazoo? Studio Grill on West Michigan Avenue. Pancakes, obviously.

report.title: "I Brought a Pen": Hen Lofland Opens a New Chapter in the First State
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Good evening, and please lower your voices; this is a library. Kidding. Shout all you like. I'm Henrietta Lofland, but my friends and the circulation desk call me Hen, and I'm your Delaware insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Newark native, a librarian by day and a wing-T devotee by night. I have opinions about the buck sweep that I've been asked not to share at dinner parties.

Delaware is the First State, and our Blue Hens are writing a brand-new chapter at the FBS level. I'm here to annotate it carefully. You'll get footnotes, because every fact I give you will have a source. You'll get honesty, because if we stumble I'll say so, kindly. You'll also get a librarian's promise: if I don't know something, I'll go look it up before I say it. I brought a pen. A blue one, naturally.

The School in 60 Seconds

Delaware plays in Conference USA at the FBS level. The school announced its move to Conference USA and FBS in 2023, ahead of the 2025 season. Before that, the Blue Hens were an FCS power. They claim six national titles, in 1946, 1963, 1971, 1972, 1979 and 2003, and they reached the FCS title game again in 2007 and 2010. Delaware has produced quarterbacks Rich Gannon and Joe Flacco, among others. From 1999 to 2010, it was the only FCS program to average more than 20,000 fans at every regular-season home game.

Home is Tubby Raymond Field at Delaware Stadium in Newark. The stadium dates to 1952 per CFBD. Capacity is conflicting: CFBD lists 22,000, while Wikipedia says 18,500 seats. The last five seasons: 5-6, 8-5, 9-4, 9-2 and 7-6.

The Coach and the Scheme

Ryan Carty has led the program since the 2022 season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 10, 2021. This is his fifth season.

In 2026 the Blue Hens lean on the pass. They average 271.0 passing yards per game (29th in FBS) but just 94.0 rushing yards (135th), and 3.12 yards per carry. My wing-T heart aches a little. Total offense is 365.0 yards per game, and scoring is 22.8 points per game. The bright spot is the pass rush: 18 sacks in six games. The defense allows 390.7 yards per game, with 259.2 through the air (125th). Turnovers are even, eight lost and eight forced.

Players to Know

QB Nick Minicucci: the season passing leader, at 838 yards, 5 TD, 3 INT, 57.3%. AP reported he missed the Middle Tennessee game, his second straight game out. I haven't found an update on his status for Tuesday, so it's unknown.
QB Tyler Bell: started in Minicucci's place at Middle Tennessee and threw for 306 yards and two touchdowns on 22 of 36. He also caught a 15-yard touchdown pass from Bryson Graves. Versatile young man.
RB Jo'Nathan Silver: 230 yards on 58 carries, 1 TD.
WR Sean Wilson: 25 catches, 339 yards, 3 TD. Donovan Lewis caught six passes for 83 yards against MTSU.
LB Blake Matthews: 4.5 sacks. LB Colin Gallagher: a team-high 42 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Delaware is 2-4 overall and 0-2 in Conference USA. The Blue Hens are 2-1 at home and 0-3 on the road. They are not ranked. The losses: at Vanderbilt (35-26), at Virginia (42-3), Liberty at home (30-14), and at Middle Tennessee (33-30). Tuesday is a chance at the first league win of the season, at home, on national television.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Missouri State (2-4) at Delaware (2-4) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:00 p.m. ET · Delaware Stadium, Newark · ESPNU

Last time out. Delaware led 30-26 with 9:57 left at Middle Tennessee after Bell's 23-yard touchdown pass to Kaderris Roberts. Then the Blue Raiders went 93 yards to win 33-30. Missouri State beat Kennesaw State 24-21 the next night on Yousef Obeid's 20-yard field goal as time expired. It was the Bears' first FBS win under Casey Woods.

Delaware's offense vs. Missouri State's defense. This one looks promising on paper. The Bears allow 430.8 yards per game (127th), including 254.3 passing (120th) and 176.5 rushing (108th). They give up 30.5 points per game, and opponents convert 44.4% of third downs (120th). If our run game, at 94.0 yards per game, can find even modest room, Bell or Minicucci gets to throw on schedule.

Missouri State's offense vs. Delaware's defense. Here is my worry. The Bears average 224.7 passing yards per game, and Isaiah Myers has 554 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Henry Belin IV threw for a career-high 300 yards in the last game, with two touchdowns to Myers. Our pass defense ranks 125th. Our 18 sacks are the best counterargument I have.

Series. I found no Delaware-Missouri State meeting in CFBD's 2016-2025 list of most frequent opponents, and I haven't confirmed the all-time series. Not found, so not stated.

Availability. No official conference availability report for this game as of Oct. 18, 2026. The one confirmed item is that Minicucci missed the Oct. 13 game, his second straight. His status for Tuesday is unknown.

Missouri State also debuts an insider this week. I'm told she guides float trips. I'll lend her a library card. Fair trade.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Who plays quarterback for Delaware, and does it matter as much as protection does?
2. Can the Blue Hens' pass defense slow Myers?
3. Can Delaware's pass rush, with 18 sacks, finish drives the way MTSU's offense finished ours?

Local Flavor

I'm keeping my best-loved Newark spots in my card catalog until I can confirm them. Not an ad.

report.title: "Right Down the Street": Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate Brings the 305 Heart to Tuesday Night
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

¡Hola, Panther people! Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, and I grew up in Sweetwater, five minutes from campus, at a kitchen table where my abuela taught me football with cafecito and dominoes. The dominoes were the players. The sugar packets were the defense. To this day I can't watch a fourth-down stop without craving a colada.

Here's what I am: the loudest, warmest, most bilingual hype machine FIU has ever had, and I will never, ever let anybody sleep on this program. Here's what I'm not: a person who makes things up. Every week I'll bring you the real numbers, the real schedule, and an honest, kind look at whoever we're playing. If I don't know something, I'll say "no sé" and go find out. Miami has a lot of teams, but only one is right down the street from my abuela's house. ¡Vamos, Panthers!

The School in 60 Seconds

FIU plays in Conference USA at the FBS level, and home is Pitbull Stadium in Miami. The stadium opened in 1995, and CFBD lists its capacity at 20,000, which matches Wikipedia's figure. The program's trophy case includes a share of the 2010 Sun Belt championship and three bowl appearances. Last season was a big one: under first-year coach Willie Simmons, the Panthers went 7-6 and made their first bowl trip since 2019.

Look at the last five seasons and you'll see why that mattered so much to my family: 1-11 in 2021, then three straight 4-8 years, then 7-6 in 2025. The Panthers also play Florida Atlantic every year in the Shula Bowl.

The Coach and the Scheme

Willie Simmons is in Year Two. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 7, 2024. Before FIU, he was head coach at Florida A&M from 2018 to 2023, winning a black college national championship and a SWAC title in 2023, and at Prairie View A&M from 2015 to 2017. He played quarterback at Clemson and The Citadel.

What do the 2026 numbers say? This team wins with defense. FIU allows 14.7 points per game, and opponents average just 3.21 yards per carry. The Panthers have 14 sacks in six games. The offense is perfectly balanced in volume, with 214 rushing attempts and 214 pass attempts, but it averages only 19.7 points per game and 3.36 yards per carry. Ball security needs work: nine giveaways against eight takeaways.

Players to Know

QB JJ Kohl: 116 of 199 for 1,458 yards, 7 TD, 7 INT. He threw for 278 yards and two touchdowns in the loss at Jax State.
RB Devonte Lyons: 268 yards on 65 carries, 1 TD. He ran for 78 yards on 14 carries against New Mexico State.
WR Maguire Anderson: 33 catches, 534 yards, 4 TD, the team's top receiver.
DL DeeJay Holmes Jr.: 5 sacks, plus 6 tackles for loss.
DB DeAndre Boykins: a team-high 37 tackles.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Middle Tennessee (3-3) at FIU (3-3) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:00 p.m. ET · Pitbull Stadium, Miami · CBS Sports Network

Last time out. FIU lost 27-24 at Jax State on Oct. 13, when Garrison Rippa kicked a 26-yard field goal with 44 seconds left. Middle Tennessee rallied past Delaware 33-30 the same night. FIU's offense vs. MTSU's defense. The Blue Raiders allow 28.3 points per game and 5.21 yards per carry. They gave up 55 points at Kansas. If Lyons and the run game can get going, Kohl gets manageable third downs. MTSU's defense does have a playmaker in linebacker Korey Smith, who leads his team with 56 tackles.

Availability. No official conference availability report for this game as of Oct. 18, 2026. I found no confirmed FIU or MTSU injury news in the sources above, so every status is unknown to me until game notes come out.

Middle Tennessee debuts its own insider this week too. Welcome, neighbor.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can FIU's pass rush rattle Gagliano, who has thrown just two interceptions all year?
2. Can the Panthers finish drives with touchdowns instead of leaning on Czeremcha?
3. Does the 3-0 home magic hold one more Tuesday?

report.title: "Low and slow wins the fourth quarter": Burl Ashcraft-Neeley Takes the Open Week
report.byline: Our insider (archetype: northeast Alabama hometown hero) introduces the Jacksonville State Gamecocks during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Burl Ashcraft-Neeley · Jacksonville State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Low and slow wins the fourth quarter! I'm Burl Ashcraft-Neeley, and I'm your Jacksonville State insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a calhoun County barbecue pitmaster who has never lived more than ten miles from campus. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. On the podcast, my segment is called Smokehouse Talk. The show card describes it like this: the Fanatic's weekly signature column and podcast segment. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Gamecocks have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is AmFirst Stadium in Jacksonville, AL, built in 1947 with a listed capacity of 24,000. The band is the Marching Southerners, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 5-6, 9-2, 9-4, 9-5 and 9-5, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Kennesaw State (3-4 in 7 meetings), Eastern Kentucky (4-2 in 6 meetings), Murray State (6-0 in 6 meetings), North Alabama (5-0 in 5 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 86 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about Cocky the Gamecock; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Charles Kelly leads the Gamecocks; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 21, 2024. Through 7 games, Jacksonville State scores 27.3 points a game and allows 22.7. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 54% of its plays, gaining 150.1 rushing yards and 240.4 passing yards a game. That's a balanced menu. On third down, Jacksonville State converts 46.2% of the time and opponents convert 45.8%. The defense has 11 sacks and 36 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 10 giveaways against 6 takeaways. Penalties cost 61.1 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 49 points against Eastern Kentucky on Sept. 5, 2026, and 4 of the 7 games were decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, Jacksonville State has outscored opponents by a combined 32 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB Caden Creel (passing leader): 129/192, 1637 yards, 12 TD, 6 INT.
QB Caden Creel (rushing leader): 105 carries, 500 yards, 4 TD.
WR Deondre Johnson (receiving leader): 22 catches, 431 yards, 3 TD.
On defense, S Caleb Nix leads with 43 tackles and has 2 interceptions; DL Tae Floyd has 2 sacks.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Jacksonville State is 5-2 overall, 4-0 at home and 1-2 away. In Conference USA play the Gamecocks are 3-0, which sorts them No. 1 of 10 by record. That's the top spot in the table, at least for now. Right around us: Liberty (2-0). The top of the table: Jacksonville State (3-0), Liberty (2-0), Western Kentucky (2-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Jacksonville State this week. The last time out, on Oct. 14, 2026, the Gamecocks beat Florida International at home, 27-24. Next up: Wednesday, Oct. 28, at NM State, in Las Cruces, N.M., with a 7 p.m. kickoff. New Mexico State comes in at 2-4. After that, CFBD lists vs. Sam Houston (Nov. 8), at Western Kentucky (Nov. 14), vs. Missouri State (Nov. 21), at Delaware (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Gamecocks come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Low and slow wins the fourth quarter!

report.title: "Writing It Live": Ximena Holcombe-Reyes Opens a New Chapter Against Liberty
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Hey, Owl Nation! I'm Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, your Kennesaw State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Marietta native with a computer science degree, and I've cheered this program since its very first season. I was there for version 1.0. I still have the T-shirt. It no longer fits. That's growth.

Here's my operating system. I'm a builder. I love that some programs have a hundred years of history while Kennesaw State gets to write ours right now, live, in front of us. I'm keeping the notes. Every number I share is sourced and debugged. Every opponent gets respect. When I don't know something, I'll log it as "unknown" instead of guessing. Bugs happen. We patch them, and we ship again. Let's go, Owls.

The School in 60 Seconds

Kennesaw State football began play in 2015 as an FCS member of the Big South Conference. In 2022 the Owls moved to the ASUN's new FCS football league, and after that season they began the transition to FBS ahead of joining Conference USA in 2024. That's an entire program history in about a decade. Speedrun.

Home is Fifth Third Stadium, just outside the Kennesaw city limits. The game feed lists it as Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, and CFBD lists it as built in 2010 with a capacity of 11,040. The last five seasons: 11-2, 5-6, 3-6, 2-10, and then a big jump to 10-4 in 2025. Last year the Owls finished the regular season 9-3 and 7-1 in Conference USA.

The Coach and the Scheme

Jerry Mack is the head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 1, 2024, so this is his second season. He was head coach at North Carolina Central from 2014 to 2017, going 31-15, and was later offensive coordinator and associate head coach at Rice. He played wide receiver at Jackson State and Arkansas State.

The 2026 numbers show a balanced offense, with 193 rushes and 198 passes. It averages 223.7 passing and 143.7 rushing yards per game, and scores 22.3 points. Yards per carry is 4.47. The defense allows 376.3 yards (94th) and 23.5 points (66th) per game. Two things to patch: penalties, at 77.8 yards per game (129th), and red-zone defense, where opponents score on 95.5% of trips (132nd).

Players to Know

QB Rickie Collins: completing 70.1% of his passes. Season yardage is conflicting: AP lists 1,287 and ESPN lists 1,302, both with 4 TD and 3 INT. He also leads the team in rushing, with 271 yards and 5 TD on 64 carries. Against Missouri State he threw for 260 yards and ran for a touchdown.
WR Javon Rogers: 18 catches, 308 yards, 1 TD.
WR Dylan Gary: 10 catches for 135 yards and a touchdown at Missouri State.
RB Alan Woods III: 47 rushing yards and a touchdown on 13 carries at Missouri State, plus six catches.
DL Ugonna Nwoha: 3 sacks. LB Tywon Christopher: a team-high 48 tackles.

The Conference Picture

Kennesaw State is 1-5 overall and 0-2 in Conference USA. The Owls are 1-2 at home and 0-3 on the road. They are not ranked. They've lost five straight since a 47-0 win over West Georgia in the opener. But look closer at the commit history: the losses to Arkansas State (17-14), Jacksonville State (27-26) and Missouri State (24-21) were all by three points or fewer. The code is close to compiling. A home win Thursday would be the first league win of 2026.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Liberty (5-1) at Kennesaw State (1-5) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw, Ga. · CBS Sports Network

Last time out. The Owls took a halftime lead at Missouri State on a 10-yard Collins-to-Gary touchdown pass, but lost 24-21 on a field goal as time expired. Liberty beat Sam Houston 35-3 on Oct. 8, its fifth straight win.

KSU's offense vs. Liberty's defense. I'll be straight with you: this is a tough draw. Liberty allows 15.3 points per game (15th), 167.5 passing yards (15th), and just 28.4% on third down (8th). Our path is Collins's efficiency and his legs. Staying on schedule, and converting the 40.3% of third downs we've managed so far (74th), decides whether drives keep running.

Liberty's offense vs. KSU's defense. The Flames run for 223.0 yards per game (15th). Kam Davis has 524 yards, and quarterback Deshawn Purdie hasn't thrown an interception all season. Our run defense allows 143.0 yards per game (74th). Makai Jackson averages more than 23 yards a catch, so the deep ball is a threat too. Liberty is heavily penalized, at 85.8 yards per game (137th), so our defense can't give back the yards it gets for free.

Series. This one has some code history. Kennesaw State has won the last three meetings, including 48-42 in double overtime in Lynchburg on Nov. 29, 2025. A search summary of the schools' records puts the Owls ahead 3-2 all-time, and CFBD shows KSU 3-1 against Liberty from 2016 to 2025.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026. I found no confirmed injury news for either team, so every status is logged as unknown.

Liberty's debut insider is a youth pastor with a big laugh. I respect anybody who coaches middle schoolers. He'll be kind; so will I.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can the Owls finish one of these close games? Three losses by three points or fewer.
2. Can our defense hold up in the red zone (132nd) against Liberty's run game?
3. Can Collins make plays on third down against the nation's No. 8 third-down defense?

Local Flavor

I'll publish my Kennesaw food list after verifying it. Release notes pending. Not an ad.

report.title: "Somebody's Son": Gideon Fairweather Brings Joy (and a Five-Game Streak) to Kennesaw
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Well, praise the Lord and pass the program! I'm Gideon Fairweather, your Liberty insider at The Cover Window. I grew up in Lynchburg, and I'm a youth pastor who coaches middle-school football on the side. That means I've given a halftime speech about perseverance to eleven 12-year-olds who were mostly worried about Gatorade flavors. I'm ready for anything.

You'll hear a big laugh from me, and a lot of encouragement. When I look at a roster, I see a hundred-some young men who are each somebody's son, and I'll write about them that way. I'll also tell you the truth. Every number here is sourced. If we play poorly, I'll say so gently. If I don't know something, I'll admit it. Lynchburg on game day feels like a family reunion with a marching band. Our guys play hard, play fair, and you can see the joy on their faces.

The School in 60 Seconds

Liberty University is a private Christian university in Lynchburg, Virginia. Its football program announced the move from FCS to FBS in July 2017, became a provisional FBS member in 2018, and became a full member with bowl eligibility in 2019. In 2020 the Flames entered the AP poll for the first time, at No. 25. They joined Conference USA for the 2023 season.

Home is Williams Stadium, which CFBD lists as built in 1989 with a capacity of 25,000. The last five seasons: 8-5, 8-5, a magnificent 13-1 in 2023, 8-4, and then a humbling 4-8 in 2025. That makes a 5-1 start this year a joyful sight.

The Coach and the Scheme

Jamey Chadwell has led Liberty since the 2023 season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 4, 2022. Before Lynchburg, he was head coach at North Greenville (2009-11), Delta State (2012), Charleston Southern (2013-16) and Coastal Carolina, first as interim in 2017 and then from 2019 to 2022. He played quarterback at East Tennessee State. (One AP recap credited Liberty's record to a different coach. CFBD and Wikipedia both list Chadwell, so I treat that as an error.)

The 2026 Flames run the ball and play defense. They average 223.0 rushing yards per game (15th in FBS) at 5.27 yards per carry, and they have 254 rushing attempts to 129 passes. The defense allows 291.7 yards (19th) and 15.3 points (15th) per game, and opponents convert just 28.4% of third downs (8th). The area for growth is penalties, at 85.8 yards per game, 137th in FBS.

Players to Know

The Conference Picture

Liberty has won five straight, including road wins at Coastal Carolina and Delaware. A win Thursday would make the Flames 3-0 in league play.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Liberty (5-1) at Kennesaw State (1-5) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw, Ga. · CBS Sports Network

Last time out. Liberty beat Sam Houston 35-3 on Oct. 8, piling up 297 rushing yards. Kennesaw State lost 24-21 at Missouri State on Oct. 14 on a field goal as time expired. That's the Owls' fifth straight loss since a 47-0 opening win over West Georgia.

Liberty's offense vs. KSU's defense. The Owls allow 143.0 rushing yards per game (74th) and 376.3 total yards (94th). Our ground game is the plan, with Davis, Coleman and Purdie's legs. Kennesaw State ranks 132nd in red-zone defense, allowing scores on 95.5% of trips, and our red-zone offense scores 88.5% of the time (45th). Jackson against a pass defense allowing 233.3 yards per game (102nd) could produce a big play or two.

KSU's offense vs. Liberty's defense. Rickie Collins is a dual threat. He's completed 70.1% of his passes and leads the Owls in rushing, with 271 yards and five touchdowns. Against Missouri State, Dylan Gary caught 10 passes for 135 yards. Our defense allows 167.5 passing yards per game (15th), and slowing Collins on third down, where KSU converts 40.3% (74th), is the job.

Series. I won't sugarcoat it. Kennesaw State has won the last three meetings, including 48-42 in double overtime in Lynchburg on Nov. 29, 2025. A search summary of the schools' records puts KSU ahead 3-2 all-time, and CFBD shows the Owls 3-1 against us from 2016 to 2025. My youth group calls this a "growth opportunity."

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026. I found no confirmed injury news for either team, so all statuses are unknown.

Kennesaw State is debuting its own insider, and I hear she's keeping notes on a young program's story. I'll pray for her keyboard, and for our tackling.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Liberty clean up the penalties (85.8 yards a game) on the road?
2. Can the Flames contain Collins as a passer and runner?
3. Can the run game control the clock the way it has all year, with a 33:26 average possession time (12th)?

report.title: "Sit With Us": Opal Stonebriar Packs a Cooler for Miami
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Well, hey there, sugar. Come in, sit down, and have a biscuit. I'm Opal Stonebriar, your Middle Tennessee insider here at The Cover Window. I'm a Rutherford County girl and a church choir director, raised on Friday-night lights and Saturday Blue Raiders. Folks call me the front-row grandma of Murfreesboro. I'm 34. It's a spiritual title.

Here's how this works. I will feed you, I will love on these boys like they're my own, and if you say something about my team that isn't true, I will correct you sweetly and with a citation. I don't make up numbers, I don't make up injuries, and when I don't know something I'll say, "Honey, I don't know yet." Murfreesboro is a city that grew up fast, and so did our program. Come sit with us, and you'll leave a Blue Raider. I promise.

The School in 60 Seconds

Middle Tennessee plays FBS football in Conference USA, out of Murfreesboro, Tennessee. The Blue Raiders have played in 14 bowl games and seven I-AA playoffs. Home is Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, which opened in 1933. The sources disagree on its size. CFBD lists a capacity of 30,788, and Wikipedia lists 27,303. I'm noting both until I check the media guide.

The last five seasons have been a climb and then a dip: 7-6 in 2021, 8-5 in 2022, 4-8 in 2023, and 3-9 in both 2024 and 2025. So a 3-3 start in 2026 already beats last year's win total by midseason, and in my kitchen that calls for a pound cake.

The Coach and the Scheme

Derek Mason was hired on Dec. 6, 2023, as the 15th head coach in program history. Before Murfreesboro, he was head coach at Vanderbilt from 2014 to 2020. This is his third season.

Here's what the 2026 numbers show. The offense averages 22.8 points per game, with 200.7 passing yards and 120.8 rushing yards per game. It runs efficiently, at 4.74 yards per carry, and it takes care of the football: only four giveaways all season, against eight takeaways. Defense is the worry. Opponents average 28.3 points per game and 5.21 yards per carry. FOX Sports lists the Blue Raiders' 11 tackles for loss as the second-fewest in FBS. That's not a scheme label, just the numbers.

Players to Know

QB Roman Gagliano: 110 of 188, 1,204 yards, 11 TD, just 2 INT. Against Delaware he threw for 291 yards and three touchdowns, ran for another, and led the game-winning 93-yard drive. Sweet as tea and twice as cool.
RB Antonio Martin Jr.: 433 yards on 83 carries, 1 TD.
WR Cam'ron Lacy: 35 catches, 369 yards, 4 TD.
WR Neo Clifton and WR Koraun Perdue: against Delaware, Clifton caught four passes for 64 yards and two touchdowns, including the winner. Perdue caught four for 103 yards and an 80-yard score.
LB Korey Smith: leads the team in tackles. ESPN lists 56 and FOX lists 55, so the count is conflicting by one.
Sacks: the sources disagree on the team leader. ESPN lists Kaven Call (1), while FOX and Sports-Reference list Ashton Taylor (2 per FOX, 1 per Sports-Reference). Conflicting, so I'm showing all of it.

The Conference Picture

report.title: "Pack a Snack": Clementine Bilyeu Floats the Bears to Newark
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Howdy from the Ozarks! I'm Clementine Bilyeu, your Missouri State insider here at The Cover Window. I'm a Springfield native and a float-trip guide, and I've been maroon since the day I was born. Mama swears my first word was "Bears." It was probably "boat," but I've chosen my story and I'm sticking with it.

I take a practical view of football, the same way I take a river. Read the current, respect the rocks, and keep everybody in the canoe. Missouri State is on a brand-new ride as an FBS program, and I'm thrilled to be your guide. I'll give you real numbers, honest takes, and kind words for every opponent. If I don't know something, I'll tell you, and then I'll paddle off and find out. Springfield is the heart of the Ozarks, and our Bears are taking the whole region along. Pack a snack. It's going to be a fun float.

The School in 60 Seconds

Missouri State University is in Springfield, Missouri, and its first football team took the field in 1909. Until 2005, the school was known as Southwest Missouri State. The Bears were a founding member of the Gateway Football Conference in 1985, which later became the Missouri Valley Football Conference. They joined Conference USA in 2025 and became a full FBS member in 2026. Wikipedia lists an all-time record of 492-532-39 and 10 conference championships.

Home is Plaster Sports Complex, which CFBD lists with a capacity of 17,337 and a 1941 construction year. The last five seasons: 8-4, 5-6, 4-7, 8-4 and 7-6.

The Coach and the Scheme

Casey Woods is in his first season as head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 19, 2025. He was previously offensive coordinator at SMU and played wide receiver at Tennessee.

The 2026 offense is fairly balanced, with 202 rushing attempts and 183 pass attempts. It averages 359.5 yards per game, 224.7 passing and 134.8 rushing, and scores 22.2 points per game. Yards per carry sits at 4.00. The defense is the stretch of river with rocks in it. It allows 430.8 yards (127th in FBS) and 30.5 points per game (116th). The Bears have seven sacks, seven giveaways and six takeaways. Penalties have been a drag, at 394 yards in six games.

Players to Know

QB Henry Belin IV: threw for a career-high 300 yards on 28 of 39 against Kennesaw State, with two touchdowns. He also ran nine times for 24 yards.
QB Skyler Locklear: the season passing leader, at 788 yards, 4 TD, 2 INT, 65.7%. AP's preview doesn't say who will start Tuesday, so I'm calling the starter unconfirmed.
WR Isaiah Myers: 27 catches, 554 yards, 5 TD. He had seven catches for 135 yards and both touchdowns against KSU, tying the game twice in the second half. That boy can run a rapid.
Rushing leader: conflicting. AP lists Jambres Dubar (233 yards on 42 carries, 2 TD), and ESPN lists Ramone Green Jr. (227 yards on 51 carries, 2 TD). Connor Lair carried 14 times for 65 yards against KSU.
LB Jared Lloyd: a team-high 71 tackles.
K Yousef Obeid: made the 20-yard game-winner as time expired, plus two earlier field goals.

The Conference Picture

Missouri State is 2-4 overall and 1-1 in Conference USA. The Bears are 2-1 at home and 0-3 on the road. They are not ranked. The Kennesaw State win was their first FBS victory under Woods. Their earlier win came over FCS member Lindenwood. Their losses were at Texas A&M, to Marshall at home (30-24), at SMU (34-24) and at Western Kentucky (34-13). A road win in Newark would make them 2-1 in league play, and I'd like that very much.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Missouri State (2-4) at Delaware (2-4) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:00 p.m. ET · Delaware Stadium, Newark · ESPNU

Last time out. The Bears beat Kennesaw State 24-21 on Oct. 14. After taking over with 6:06 left, they marched to set up Obeid's field goal as time expired. Delaware lost 33-30 at Middle Tennessee on Oct. 13, giving up a 93-yard drive in the final minutes.

Missouri State's offense vs. Delaware's defense. I like this current. Delaware allows 259.2 passing yards per game (125th), and our passing game just put up 300 yards. Myers against that secondary is my top storyline. The Blue Hens do have 18 sacks, with Blake Matthews at 4.5, so protection comes first. We'd also like to finish better in the red zone, where we rank 106th, scoring on 80.0% of trips.

Delaware's offense vs. Missouri State's defense. The Blue Hens throw for 271.0 yards per game (29th) but run for just 94.0 (135th). Our pass defense allows 254.3 yards per game (120th), so slowing Sean Wilson (339 yards, 3 TD) is the job. Delaware's quarterback situation is uncertain. Nick Minicucci missed his second straight game on Oct. 13, and Tyler Bell threw for 306 yards in his place. Stopping third downs would help too, since opponents convert 44.4% against us.

Series. I found no meeting between these two programs in CFBD's 2016-2025 list of most frequent opponents, and I haven't confirmed the all-time series. Not found, so not stated.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026. I found no confirmed Missouri State injury news. Delaware's Minicucci missed the Oct. 13 game, and his Tuesday status is unknown.

Delaware is debuting a librarian insider this week. I promise to return my books on time if she promises to be gentle with us.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Myers keep rolling against a pass defense ranked 125th?
2. Can the Bears' defense get off the field on third down?
3. Can Missouri State win its first road game of the season?

Local Flavor

I'm not recommending Newark spots I haven't checked. Bring a thermos and a smile. Not an ad.

report.title: "Turn Up the Heat": Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya Roasts Up a Wednesday in Huntsville
report.byline: Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya · New Mexico State Insider
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

¡Buenas noches, Aggies! I'm Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, your New Mexico State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Las Cruces native, a chile farmer's daughter and an ag-science grad. That means I can tell you the soil pH of the practice field and how much Scoville heat a fourth-down stop packs. (A lot. A fourth-down stop is Christmas-style, red and green.)

Everything gets a chile rating from me. A routine first down? Mild. A 40-yard run? Hatch hot. But I don't heat up the facts. Every number I give you is real and sourced. Every opponent gets respect. If I don't know something, I'll say so, and then I'll go find out. In the Mesilla Valley, fall smells like roasting chile and fresh-cut grass. Our Aggies play with that same heat, and the Organ Mountains watch every snap.

The School in 60 Seconds

New Mexico State plays FBS football in Conference USA. The road here was winding. The Aggies were independent in 2013, a football-only Sun Belt member from 2014 to 2017, and independent again from 2018. They announced in November 2021 that they would join Conference USA in all sports starting in 2023. Home is Aggie Memorial Stadium in Las Cruces, which CFBD lists as built in 1978 with a capacity of 28,853.

Here's the honest part: Wikipedia notes that NMSU has one of the longest AP poll droughts in FBS, with its last ranking in 1960. The recent highs are real, though. The Aggies went 10-5 in 2023. The last five seasons: 2-10, 7-6, 10-5, 3-9 and 4-8.

The Coach and the Scheme

Tony Sanchez is the head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 23, 2023. He's an NMSU alum and a former Aggie wide receiver. He was head coach at UNLV from 2014 to 2019, and before that at Bishop Gorman High School in Las Vegas.

The 2026 numbers say run first. NMSU averages 142.7 rushing yards per game at 4.53 yards per carry, plus 230.5 passing yards. Scoring is 23.7 points per game (97th). The defense is sturdier against the run. It allows 125.5 rushing yards (47th) and 3.50 yards per carry, and it has 15 sacks. The red-pepper warnings: a -5 turnover margin (122nd), 92.9% red-zone scoring allowed (118th), and a 27:08 time of possession (127th).

Players to Know

RB James Jones: 599 yards on 92 carries, 3 TD. He entered the FIU game leading Conference USA at 102.0 rushing yards per game, then ran for 89 there. Chile rating: Hatch hot.
QB Trey Hedden: the season passing leader, at 906 yards, 5 TD, 6 INT, 52.4%. He started the first four games.
QB Adam Damante: started at FIU, going 9 of 22 for 104 yards with an interception. Wednesday's starter isn't confirmed in my sources.
WR Tyler "TK" King: 20 catches, 286 yards, 3 TD. Terrione Graves caught two passes for 39 yards at FIU.
DE Gabe Peterson: 4.5 sacks. S Nick Session: a team-high 50 tackles.

The Conference Picture

New Mexico State is 2-4 overall and 1-1 in Conference USA. The Aggies are 2-1 at home and 0-3 on the road. They are not ranked. The highlight so far is a 34-13 win over Western Kentucky, the same WKU team that beat Sam Houston 16-3 last week. A road win Wednesday would make NMSU 2-1 in the league and earn its first road win of 2026.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

New Mexico State (2-4) at Sam Houston (1-5) · Wednesday, Oct. 21, 8:00 p.m. ET · Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville, Texas · ESPN2

Last time out. FIU beat us 22-3 in Miami on Oct. 7. Their kicker made five field goals, and we threw two interceptions. Sam Houston lost 16-3 to Western Kentucky on Oct. 14 and managed just 177 total yards. Both teams have had a week to cool off. Time to fire up the roaster again.

NMSU's offense vs. Sam Houston's defense. This is the matchup I'm roasting over an open flame. The Bearkats allow 200.3 rushing yards per game (129th). Jones against that front is my top storyline. Sam Houston's pass defense, though, allows just 137.8 yards per game (4th in FBS), so I expect the Aggies to stay on the ground. One more thing: the Bearkats hold opponents to 32.1% on third down (24th). Staying ahead of the chains is the key.

Sam Houston's offense vs. NMSU's defense. Landyn Locke has 1,418 passing yards and 11 touchdowns in Phil Longo's offense, which Wikipedia calls air raid. The Bearkats run for just 95.0 yards per game (134th), so they'll lean on Locke. Our pass defense allows 222.3 yards per game (90th), and our 15 sacks are the answer. Peterson needs a big night.

Series. New Mexico State leads 2-1, per a search summary of school records: NMSU won 27-13 in 2023, Sam Houston won 31-11 in 2024, and NMSU won 37-10 on Oct. 2, 2025. I'm marking that thin until I confirm it on the media guide.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026. Our quarterback situation is unconfirmed: Hedden started four games and Damante started the last one. I found no other confirmed injury news.

Sam Houston debuts a storyteller insider this week too, a history teacher. I'll bring the green chile stew if he brings the campfire.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Jones and the run game feast on a defense allowing 200.3 rushing yards a game?
2. Can the Aggies stop giving the ball away (-5 margin)?
3. Can our defense pressure Locke into mistakes?

Local Flavor

I'm not naming Huntsville spots I haven't checked. I'm packing my own chile, thanks. Not an ad.
