report.title: "Pull Up a Stump": Lem Coxwell Tells the Bearkats' Tale Under the Wednesday Lights
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

Evenin', folks. Pull up a stump. I'm Lemuel Coxwell, but everybody from here to the Trinity River calls me Lem, and I'm your Sam Houston insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Walker County native and a high-school history teacher, and I collect Texas folklore the way some folks collect bottle caps. My students say I can turn a fire drill into a three-part saga. They're not wrong.

Here's how I'll tell it. I'll be patient, because seasons are long and young men grow. I'll be proud, because Huntsville is a small Texas town with a big Texas name, and our Bearkats play like they're carrying it. Most of all, I'll be honest. A good storyteller never needs to stretch the truth. Every number I give you will be real. If I don't know something, I'll say so plain, then go dig through the archives.

The School in 60 Seconds

Sam Houston State fielded its first football team in 1912. Home is Elliott T. Bowers Stadium in Huntsville, which seats 14,000; CFBD lists it as built in 1986. In 2021 the Bearkats left the Southland Conference for the WAC's FCS football league, and in November 2021 they accepted an invitation to join Conference USA at the FBS level starting in 2023-24.

The last five seasons tell a tale with some hills in it: 11-1 in 2021, 5-4 in 2022, 3-9 in 2023, 10-3 in 2024 and 2-10 in 2025. That 10-3 year was the high mark of the FBS era so far. Every good story has a hard chapter before a good one.

The Coach and the Scheme

Phil Longo was named Sam Houston's 16th head coach on Dec. 18, 2024, so this is his second season. Wikipedia describes him as a practitioner of the air raid offense. He was previously offensive coordinator at Wisconsin, and before that offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at North Carolina, Ole Miss and Sam Houston.

The 2026 numbers match that reputation through the air but not on the ground. The Bearkats throw for 247.0 yards per game (51st in FBS) and run for 95.0 (134th), at 3.15 yards per carry. Scoring sits at 19.5 points per game (123rd). The defense is split. It allows just 137.8 passing yards per game (4th in FBS) but 200.3 rushing yards (129th), and opponents convert only 32.1% of third downs (24th). The Bearkats have 12 sacks and a +1 turnover margin (61st).

Players to Know

QB Landyn Locke: 129 of 205, 1,418 yards, 11 TD, 4 INT, 62.9%. He was 13 of 30 for 112 yards against Western Kentucky.
RB Alton McCaskill: 211 yards on 53 carries, 1 TD. M.J. Dowdy ran 14 times for 55 yards against WKU.
WR Chris Reed: 17 catches, 289 yards, 3 TD, including three catches for 51 yards against WKU.
LB Dean Ford: a team-high 38 tackles. LB Elijah Groves: 2.5 sacks.
K Sam Carpenter: made a 42-yard field goal against WKU and a 36-yarder at Liberty.

The Conference Picture

Sam Houston is 1-5 overall and 0-2 in Conference USA. The Bearkats are 1-2 at home and 0-3 on the road. They are not ranked. The two close losses came early, 24-21 at Troy and 23-17 to Tulsa. Since then it's been a steep climb: 49-14 at Texas Tech, 35-3 at Liberty and 16-3 to Western Kentucky. The lone win was 59-0 over Nicholls. A home win Wednesday would be the first league win of the season. In a long story, that's the chapter where the hero stands back up.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

New Mexico State (2-4) at Sam Houston (1-5) · Wednesday, Oct. 21, 8:00 p.m. ET · Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville · ESPN2

Last time out. Western Kentucky won 16-3 in Huntsville on Oct. 14. Sam Houston was held to 177 total yards and 12 first downs. WKU is now 4-1 against Sam Houston and perfect since the Bearkats joined CUSA in 2023. New Mexico State lost 22-3 at FIU on Oct. 7. FIU's kicker made five field goals, and NMSU threw two interceptions.

Sam Houston's offense vs. New Mexico State's defense. The Aggies allow 347.8 yards per game (61st) and are tougher against the run (125.5 yards, 47th) than the pass (222.3, 90th). So Locke's arm is our best path. NMSU has 15 sacks, with Gabe Peterson at 4.5, so protection matters. The Aggies rank 118th in red-zone defense, allowing scores on 92.9% of trips. Get there, and good things tend to happen.

New Mexico State's offense vs. Sam Houston's defense. The Aggies will want to run, and James Jones is the reason: 599 yards on 92 carries and three touchdowns. He entered the FIU game leading Conference USA at 102.0 rushing yards per game. Our run defense allows 200.3 yards a game. That's the whole ballgame in one sentence. Our pass defense, fourth in FBS, should make the Aggies one-dimensional if we can slow Jones.

Series. New Mexico State leads 2-1. NMSU won 27-13 in 2023, Sam Houston won 31-11 in 2024, and NMSU won 37-10 on Oct. 2, 2025. Those series details come from a search summary of the schools' pages, so I'm marking them thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026. I found no confirmed Sam Houston injury news. On the New Mexico State side, Adam Damante started at FIU after Trey Hedden started the first four games. Who starts Wednesday hasn't been confirmed.

New Mexico State brings its own debut insider, a chile-roasting storyteller from Las Cruces. Two storytellers, one ballgame. Somebody's tale gets a happy ending.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can the Bearkats slow Jones and the NMSU run game?
2. Can Sam Houston's offense get into the red zone against a defense that rarely stops anyone there?
3. Can the Bearkats keep winning the turnover battle (+1) against an NMSU team at -5?

Local Flavor

I'll tell you about my Huntsville haunts once I've confirmed them. Bring a lawn chair and a story. Not an ad.

report.text:
Thurman 'Tops' Whitsitt · Western Kentucky Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Go Tops! I'm Thurman 'Tops' Whitsitt, and I'm your Western Kentucky insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a warren County barber, three decades of Hilltopper stories told one haircut at a time. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. On the podcast, my segment is called Barbershop. The show card describes it like this: the Fanatic's weekly signature column and podcast segment. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Hilltoppers have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium in Bowling Green, KY, built in 1968 with a listed capacity of 22,113. The fight song is "Stand Up and Cheer!", per Wikipedia. The band is the Big Red Marching Band, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 9-5, 9-5, 8-5, 8-6 and 9-4, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Middle Tennessee (9-1 in 10 meetings), Florida International (6-3 in 9 meetings), Louisiana Tech (4-3 in 7 meetings), Florida Atlantic (3-4 in 7 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 81 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about Big Red; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Tyson Helton leads the Hilltoppers; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Nov. 27, 2018. Through 7 games, Western Kentucky scores 21.3 points a game and allows 30.6. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 51% of its plays, gaining 134.7 rushing yards and 218.3 passing yards a game. That's a balanced menu. On third down, Western Kentucky converts 40.7% of the time and opponents convert 31.5%. The defense has 9 sacks and 32 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 9 giveaways against 6 takeaways. Penalties cost 41.6 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 52 points against Mercyhurst on Sept. 26, 2026, and 0 of the 7 games were decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, opponents have outscored Western Kentucky by a combined 65 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB Rodney Tisdale Jr. (passing leader): 80/119, 857 yards, 4 TD, 2 INT.
RB Ajay Allen (rushing leader): 82 carries, 346 yards, 4 TD.
WR Jonathan Stafford Jr. (receiving leader): 41 catches, 369 yards, 1 TD.
On defense, DB Jaylen Lewis leads with 56 tackles; LB Westen Ard has 2.5 sacks; DB Tony Newsome Jr. has 2 interceptions.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Western Kentucky is 3-4 overall, 2-0 at home and 1-4 away. In Conference USA play the Hilltoppers are 2-1, which sorts them No. 3 of 10 by record. Jacksonville State sits on top at 3-0 in league games. Right around us: Liberty (2-0) and Florida International (1-1). The top of the table: Jacksonville State (3-0), Liberty (2-0), Western Kentucky (2-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Western Kentucky this week. The last time out, on Oct. 15, 2026, the Hilltoppers beat Sam Houston on the road, 16-3. Next up: Tuesday, Oct. 27, vs. Delaware, in Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green, with a 6 p.m. kickoff, and it is a Red Out. Delaware comes in at 2-4. After that, CFBD lists at Middle Tennessee (Nov. 7), vs. Jacksonville State (Nov. 14), at Liberty (Nov. 21), vs. Kennesaw State (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Hilltoppers come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Go Tops!

report.title: "Paint It Blue": Thatcher Bluestem Takes the Blue Turf Spirit to Pullman
report.byline: Our blue-everything Broncos evangelist introduces himself and previews No. 21 Boise State at Washington State.
report.text:
Thatcher Bluestem · Boise State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Paint it blue! Howdy, friends, I'm Thatcher Bluestem, and yes, my car is blue, my pancakes are blue and my opinions are the bluest you'll ever hear. I travel with the Broncos and I live with the Broncos, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, loud and sunny and endlessly proud. Visitors always ask me if the field really looks that blue in person. Friend, it looks bluer. Bring sunglasses and an open mind. Here's the thing about me: no matter how good this team gets, I carry myself like we're the scrappy kids from the foothills nobody invited to the party. Old habits. We earned every seat at the table, and I'll never take one of them for granted. Smurf Turf, baby, show some respect.

The School in 60 Seconds
Boise State was established in 1933 and now plays in the Pac-12. The Broncos have won 23 conference championships and six division titles in the Mountain West's Mountain Division. Home is Albertsons Stadium, on campus in Boise, listed at 36,387 seats, and yes, that's where the famous blue turf lives. The last five years: 7-5, 10-4, 8-6, a glorious 12-2 in 2024 and 9-5 in 2025, all in the Mountain West. This is our first ride through the new Pac-12, and so far we're 2-0 in league play. Blue all the way down.

The Coach and the Scheme
Spencer Danielson is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 3, 2023. Danielson's Broncos run the ball and keep it: 234.5 rushing yards a game (9th in FBS), 35 points a game (37th) and 450.5 total yards (27th). Friends, we lead the entire country in time of possession at 36:41 a game. We convert 50.6% of third downs, 16th in FBS. And we take care of the football: only 3 turnovers in six games, a plus-3 margin. The defense stops the run, 106.8 yards allowed a game (29th), and its red zone defense ranks 30th. Where we need work: the pass defense allows 261.3 yards a game, 126th in FBS. I'm loud, not blind.

Players to Know
QB Maddux Madsen: 110 of 166 for 1,296 yards, 13 touchdowns and zero interceptions. Zero! That's bluer than a cloudless October sky.
RB Dylan Riley: 835 yards on 127 carries, 6 TD. At Fresno State he ran 19 times for 150 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 64 yards and another score.
WR Rasean Jones: 23 catches, 359 yards, 1 TD. Matt Wagner had five catches for 46 yards at Fresno.
LB Boen Phelps: team-high 35 tackles. LB Max Stege: 2.5 sacks. DB Travis Anderson: 3 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Boise State is 5-1, 2-0 in the Pac-12, and ranked No. 21 by the AP and No. 22 in the coaches poll. We opened with a 34-27 loss at Oregon, then rolled: Memphis 38-20, South Dakota 38-24, at Western Michigan 32-7, Utah State 37-18 and at Fresno State 38-31. Then we had a week off to rest. After Pullman, Texas State comes to the blue turf on Oct. 31. I'm not doing standings math, friends, but an unbeaten league record keeps the dream bright and blue.
About that Oregon game: we lost by a touchdown on the road, in Week 1. I've watched that one more times than I'll admit, and I still came away proud. Since then, five straight wins.

This Week: No. 21 Boise State (5-1) at Washington State (1-6)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6 p.m. ET · Pullman, Wash. · USA Network. The venue is Gesa Field at Martin Stadium; Gesa names the playing surface. CFBD lists it at 32,952 seats.
Last time out: we beat Fresno State 38-31 on Oct. 10; Madsen went 23 of 34 for 238 yards and two scores. Washington State lost 48-30 at Oregon State on Oct. 17.
Watch out for: redshirt freshman Owen Eshelman, who made his first career start at Oregon State, threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 136 yards and a score. AP says he led three straight late touchdown drives. Friends, that kid can run, and our defense needs to keep him in the pocket. Receiver Branden Ganashamoorthy caught 11 passes for 147 yards in that game.
Our offense vs. their defense: Washington State allows 158.3 rushing yards a game (94th) and 27.1 points (101st). That's a good matchup for Riley.
Their offense vs. our defense: the Cougars average 308.3 yards a game (130th), but our pass defense ranks 126th, so I'll be watching every throw.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our ground game and our clock control. (2) Keeping Eshelman from breaking loose. (3) Ball security; Washington State is minus-7 in turnovers, 131st in FBS.
To Hank Palouse, Washington State's insider: I respect anyone who's kept cassette tapes this long. Bring Ol' Crimson. I'll bring a blue thermos of cocoa.

Why I Love This Team
I love that a team from a school founded in 1933 has become the program everybody in the West circles on the calendar. I love Madsen's zero in the interceptions column. I love that Riley got a week off after Fresno. And I love that every time a new fan sees the field, they gasp. Paint it blue.

report.title: "Thin Air, Thick Defense": Ansel Rimrock Welcomes the Aztecs to Fort Collins
report.byline: Our Front Range trail runner introduces himself and previews Colorado State vs. San Diego State.
report.text:
Ansel Rimrock · Colorado State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Thin air, thick defense. Hello, friends, I'm Ansel Rimrock. Most mornings you'll find me on a trail in the foothills west of town, and on fall Saturdays you'll find me with the Rams. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. I'm a calm guy, but don't mistake calm for quiet: I'm competitive right down to my trail shoes. I think football is just a long trail run with blocking. You pace yourself, you climb, you don't panic on the switchbacks, and you finish strong. Fort Collins on a fall Saturday is green and gold from the foothills to the stadium. Visiting teams breathe a little harder up here, and our kids love it. Ram tough, trail ready.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Colorado State Rams compete in the Pac-12. Our big rivalries are with Colorado, Wyoming and Air Force. We've played at Canvas Stadium since 2017; before that, the Rams spent 49 seasons, 1968 to 2016, at Sonny Lubick Field at Hughes Stadium. CFBD lists Canvas at 36,500 seats. The last five seasons were a steep climb: 3-9, 3-9, 5-7, a nice 8-5 in 2024 and then 2-10 in 2025. Every trail has a hard stretch. We're climbing out of one.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jim Mora was hired on Nov. 26, 2025, and this is his first season. The offense can move: 445.3 yards a game (34th), 35.7 points (29th) and 274.7 passing yards (26th). And we take care of the ball. We've turned it over only 4 times and taken it away 12 times, good for a plus-8 margin, 6th in FBS. We play disciplined, 42.3 penalty yards a game (17th). Now the hard switchback, friends. The defense is allowing 530.3 yards a game, 274.3 rushing yards and 43.2 points, all 138th in FBS. I said thick defense. I'm still waiting for the thick part. It'll come.

Players to Know
QB K'saan Farrar: 89 of 144 for 931 yards, 5 TD, 2 INT. At Texas State he went 26 of 41 for 282 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions.
RB Brown: 431 yards on just 47 carries, 3 TD. That's more than nine yards a carry. Heads-up: ESPN lists him as Mel Brown and AP as Jayden Brown; I'm showing both.
WR Reginald "RJ" Vick Jr.: 24 catches, 367 yards, 4 TD. WR Jackson Harper: five catches for 91 yards at Texas State.
LB Oumar Diomande: team-high 54 tackles. DL Jack Moran: 1.5 sacks. CB CJ Blocker: 3 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Colorado State is 2-4 and 0-2 in the Pac-12. The season started fast: Wyoming 35-13 in the rivalry, then Southern Utah 58-24. Then a tough climb: BYU 41-23, a 59-45 shootout at UTSA, Oregon State 56-26 and at Texas State 66-27. After San Diego State, we visit Utah State on Oct. 31. I don't do standings math on a trail. I just look at the next switchback.
Season so far, in trail terms: the first two miles were downhill and fast. Then came four straight climbs against BYU, UTSA, Oregon State and Texas State, and the legs got heavy. Every trail runner knows that feeling. You don't quit at mile four. You drink some water, shorten your stride and keep going.
The good news: beating Wyoming is never a small thing up here. And scoring 45 at UTSA shows how fast this offense can move.

This Week: San Diego State (3-4) at Colorado State (2-4)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6:30 p.m. ET (4:30 p.m. Mountain) · Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins · The CW.
Last week: we lost 66-27 at Texas State on Oct. 15. San Diego State beat Fresno State 26-23 on Oct. 17.
Our offense vs. their defense: San Diego State allows 449 yards a game (133rd) and 276.6 passing yards (131st). Farrar, Vick and Harper should find room up top.
Their offense vs. our defense: San Diego State averages 292.9 yards (133rd) and converts only 29.3% of third downs (135th). But it runs it, 144.4 yards a game, and Lucky Sutton ran for 110 last week. Our run defense has to win this climb.
Ball control: San Diego State's average time of possession is 24:47, 138th in FBS. We'll have the ball plenty.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our run defense against Kinnard and Sutton. (2) Farrar against a 131st-ranked pass defense. (3) Our plus-8 turnover habit.
To Kai Delgado-Sorensen, San Diego State's insider: holding your breath under a wave is one thing. Try running a mile at 5,000 feet. I'll lend you a water bottle.

Why I Love This Team
I love that this team keeps hold of the football. I love that Brown averages more than nine yards a carry. I love that this is a first-year staff building something. And I love Fort Collins in late October, when the foothills turn and the stadium fills up. Ram tough, trail ready.

report.title: "Measure twice, kick once": Juniper Ostrowski Takes the Open Week
report.byline: Our insider (archetype: forestry-school outdoorsy nerd) introduces the Oregon State Beavers during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Juniper Ostrowski · Oregon State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Measure twice, kick once! I'm Juniper Ostrowski, and I'm your Oregon State insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a forestry PhD who charts treetop weather and red-zone efficiency. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. Fair warning about my habit: corrects everyone's tree species in metaphors. On the podcast, my segment is called Tree ID. The show card describes it like this: corrects everyone's tree metaphors. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Beavers have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Reser Stadium in Corvallis, OR, built in 1953 with a listed capacity of 43,363. The fight song is "Hail to Old OSU", per Wikipedia. The band is the Oregon State University Marching Band, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 7-6, 10-3, 8-5, 5-7 and 2-10, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Washington State (3-8 in 11 meetings), California (5-5 in 10 meetings), Oregon (3-7 in 10 meetings), Washington (1-7 in 8 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 100 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about Benny the Beaver; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
JaMarcus Shephard leads the Beavers; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Nov. 28, 2025. Through 7 games, Oregon State scores 42.7 points a game and allows 23.1. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 42% of its plays, gaining 138.1 rushing yards and 371.3 passing yards a game. That's a team that wants to throw it around. On third down, Oregon State converts 46.5% of the time and opponents convert 38.3%. The defense has 17 sacks and 33 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 4 giveaways against 9 takeaways. Penalties cost 61.1 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 66 points against San Diego State on Oct. 10, 2026, and 0 of the 7 games were decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, Oregon State has outscored opponents by a combined 137 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB Braden Atkinson (passing leader): 189/273, 2604 yards, 24 TD, 2 INT.
RB AJ Newberry (rushing leader): 65 carries, 431 yards, 3 TD.
WR Jesse Legree (receiving leader): 46 catches, 1040 yards, 14 TD.
On defense, LB Aiden Sullivan leads with 53 tackles; LB Takari Hickle has 6 sacks; DB TJ Crandall has 1 interception.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Oregon State is 5-2 overall, 3-1 at home and 2-1 away. In Pac-12 play the Beavers are 3-0, which sorts them No. 1 of 8 by record. That's the top spot in the table, at least for now. Right around us: Boise State (2-0). The top of the table: Oregon State (3-0), Boise State (2-0), San Diego State (2-1). That order is a sort by record, not the official tiebreaker order. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Oregon State this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Beavers beat Washington State at home, 48-30. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, at Fresno State, in Fresno, with a 8 p.m. Pacific kickoff. Fresno State comes in at 4-3. After that, CFBD lists vs. Texas State (Nov. 7), at Boise State (Nov. 14), vs. Utah State (Nov. 21). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Beavers come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. Measure twice, kick once!

report.title: "Gnarly": Kai Delgado-Sorensen Paddles Out to Fort Collins
report.byline: Our Ocean Beach surfer introduces himself and previews San Diego State at Colorado State.
report.text:
Kai Delgado-Sorensen · San Diego State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Gnarly. Hey, dudes and dudettes, I'm Kai Delgado-Sorensen. I'm out in the water at Ocean Beach most mornings before the sun's all the way up, and I'm at every Aztecs game when it goes down. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. Fair warning: I rate defenses by swell size. A soft defense is ankle-high mush. A great one is a ten-foot wall, totally gnarly. Don't let the surfer drawl fool you, though. I've watched every snap this season, some of them twice, with a notebook full of salt stains. When we win, I yell "Gnarly!" and mime catching a wave. When we lose, it's "Wipeout, dude," and I paddle right back out.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Aztecs represent San Diego State University and began playing football in 1921. We went to our first bowl game in 1948 and won our first major bowl in 1969. The Aztecs have won 21 conference championships and are 10-10 all-time in bowl games. Now we play in the Pac-12, at Snapdragon Stadium, which opened in 2022 and seats 35,000. The last five seasons had some big waves and some flat days: 12-2 in 2021, 7-6, 4-8, 3-9 and then a 9-4 bounce back last year.

The Coach and the Scheme
Sean Lewis is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 29, 2023. Real talk, dudes: the offense has been flat water this year. We average 292.9 yards (133rd in FBS) and 23.3 points (101st). The passing game is 148.4 yards a game (132nd), and we convert 29.3% of third downs (135th). Our run game, 144.4 a game, is 87th. The defense has given up 449 yards a game (133rd) and 33.3 points (127th). But here's the thing: the pass rush is real. We have 16 sacks, and linebacker Djibril Rahman has 4. And the Aztecs have found ways to win close ones: 31-29 over Texas State and 26-23 over Fresno State.

Players to Know
QB Jayden Denegal: 83 of 151, about 900 yards (ESPN says 899, AP says 896), 7 TD, 5 INT. Against Fresno he was efficient, 7 of 10 for 112 and a score.
RB Javion Kinnard: 432 yards on 81 carries, 1 TD.
RB Lucky Sutton: 110 rushing yards on 18 carries against Fresno State. That's a set wave, dude.
WR Nathan Acevedo: 17 catches, 181 yards, 2 TD. WR Jaylon Hawkins: six catches for 84 yards and a touchdown against Fresno.
LB Sione Hala: team-high 67 tackles. LB Djibril Rahman: 4 sacks. CB Mike Lindsay: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
San Diego State is 3-4 and 2-1 in the Pac-12. We're 3-1 at home and 0-3 on the road. The season: a 53-20 win over Portland State, losses at UCLA 28-10, to James Madison 26-13 and at Toledo 41-16, a 31-29 win over Texas State, a rough 66-14 loss at Oregon State, and then a 26-23 win over Fresno State. After Fort Collins, we host Washington State on Oct. 31. Not doing table math, dude. But a winning league record is a nice place to be standing up on the board.
The road thing: we haven't won away from home yet. Every surfer knows a new break takes some figuring out. This is the one to figure out.
Why I love this team: it keeps paddling back out. After the Oregon State wipeout, these dudes came home and beat Fresno State by three. Sione Hala leads the team with 67 tackles and seems to be in on every play. That's a surfer who never gets out of the water.

This Week: San Diego State (3-4) at Colorado State (2-4)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6:30 p.m. ET · Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins · The CW.
Last week: we beat Fresno State 26-23 on Oct. 17. Colorado State lost 66-27 at Texas State on Oct. 15.
Our offense vs. their defense: Colorado State gives up 530.3 yards a game (138th) and 274.3 rushing yards (138th). Opponents convert 43.7% of third downs against them (133rd). Dudes, that's knee-high mush. Kinnard and Sutton should be paddling in.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is a real swell. Colorado State scores 35.7 points (29th) and throws for 274.7 yards a game (26th). Quarterback K'saan Farrar threw for 282 yards last week. And the Rams have a plus-8 turnover margin, 6th in FBS, while we're minus-2. Our 131st-ranked pass defense has to show up.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our run game against the 138th-ranked run defense. (2) Slowing Farrar and receiver Reginald Vick Jr. (3) Holding onto the ball against a team that takes it away.
To Ansel Rimrock, Colorado State's insider: thin air? Brah, I hold my breath under a six-foot set every morning. We'll be fine. Respect, though.

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Back in San Diego? Eureka! on La Jolla Village Drive makes a solid burger after a dawn patrol.

report.title: "Go With the Flow": Yesenia Calderwood Floats the Bobcats Into Week 8
report.byline: Our San Marcos river-float enthusiast introduces herself and previews Texas State vs. Utah State.
report.text:
Yesenia Calderwood · Texas State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Eat 'em up, Cats! Hey, y'all, I'm Yesenia Calderwood, and if you can't find me at a Bobcats game, I'm probably floating down the San Marcos River on an inner tube with a sun hat and a radio. I travel with the Bobcats and I live with the Bobcats, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, sunny and laid-back but fiercely proud. San Marcos has a clear, cold river and a hot, rising football team. Grab a tube, grab a seat, and enjoy the ride with us. My motto for life and football: go with the flow, then run it up the middle. When we win, I'm floating on air. When we lose, I let the river carry it away and get ready for next week.

The School in 60 Seconds
Texas State football began in 1904 and has an overall winning record. The program has 14 conference titles, nine of them outright. As of 2026, the Bobcats play in the Pac-12. Home games are in San Marcos at UFCU Stadium, built in 1981 and seating 28,388. (Bobcat Stadium is the former name, still used in CFBD data.) Texas State is now the fourth-largest university in Texas. And the recent current is strong: 4-8, 4-8, then 8-5, 8-5 and 7-6. That's a river rising.

The Coach and the Scheme
G.J. Kinne is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 2, 2022. His offense is a flash flood, y'all. Texas State leads all of FBS in total offense at 562.3 yards a game. We run for 303.5 a game, 3rd in the country, and score 40 points a game, 9th. We convert 56.1% of third downs, 4th. That's going with the flow, then running it up the middle, over and over. The defense is where the water gets choppy: 297.3 passing yards allowed a game, 137th, and 32.2 points (122nd). And our turnover margin is minus-5. Here's the thing, though: when an offense moves like this, every possession is a chance to put points on the board. We hold the ball 31:30 a game, 37th in FBS. Keep the defense rested, keep the river flowing, and good things happen.

Players to Know
QB Brad Jackson: 106 of 157 for 1,439 yards, 14 TD, 5 INT. Against Colorado State he went 14 of 19 for 213 yards and a touchdown, and ran 13 times for 181 yards and three more scores. Whoa, that's a waterfall.
RB Torrance Burgess Jr.: 838 yards on 108 carries, 5 TD. Against Colorado State: 224 yards and four touchdowns on 24 carries.
WR Chris Dawn Jr.: 29 catches, 348 yards, 4 TD. Beau Sparks: two catches for 57 yards against the Rams.
DB Jayden Bradley: team-high 44 tackles. DL Tymere Jackson: 2.5 sacks.

The Conference Picture
Texas State is 3-3 and 1-1 in the Pac-12, and 3-1 at home. We lost at Texas 59-7, then lost to UTSA 31-26. Then the current picked up: North Texas 49-35, Incarnate Word 63-10. We lost a 31-29 heartbreaker at San Diego State, then beat Colorado State 66-27. After Utah State, we go to No. 21 Boise State on Oct. 31. No standings math on the river, y'all. Just know a home win keeps us floating.
The close ones: five points against UTSA and two points at San Diego State. A couple of bounces, and this record looks a lot different.
Season so far, from the tube: the Texas game was cold water, a shock to the system. Since then, this offense has scored 26, 49, 63, 29 and 66. That's a river that keeps rising, and it's the most treasured part of my fall.

This Week: Utah State (2-4) at Texas State (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 p.m. Central) · San Marcos · CBS Sports Network.
Our offense vs. their defense: Utah State allows 140.8 rushing yards a game (68th) and lets opponents convert 40.4% of third downs (93rd). Burgess and Jackson should find running room.
Their offense vs. our defense: Utah State scores 14.5 points a game (136th) and gains 310 yards (129th). But our pass defense is 137th, and receiver Eli Wood has 472 receiving yards. We have to keep an eye on him.
Red zone: we've scored on just 71% of our trips, 128th in FBS. Y'all, that's where we have to finish.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Our run game against a 68th-ranked run defense. (2) Pass defense against Wood. (3) Finishing in the red zone.
To Hyrum Tolleson, Utah State's insider: ice cream and a river float? Now you're speaking my language. Come on down.

Why I Love This Team
I love an offense that leads the country. I love Burgess running like the river after a storm. I love that the Bobcats keep rising. And I love San Marcos on a fall night. Eat 'em up, Cats!

report.title: "Udderly Dominant": Hyrum Tolleson Brings Cache Valley Heart to San Marcos
report.byline: Our Cache Valley dairy philosopher introduces himself and previews Utah State at Texas State.
report.text:
Hyrum Tolleson · Utah State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Go Aggies! Well, hello there, neighbors. I'm Hyrum Tolleson, and I've spent most of my life on a dairy up in Cache Valley, which is a fancy way of saying I've been up before the sun since I was eight years old. I travel with the Aggies and I live with the Aggies, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, slow and steady, the way you'd tell a story over the fence. I'm a patient man. It takes a lot to get me riled, and a lot less to get me laughing. Logan sits in a valley so pretty it almost feels unfair. Our Aggies play with that small-town heart, and afterward, everybody goes for ice cream. I always order a double scoop of Aggie Ice Cream, win or lose. When we play well, that's udderly dominant.

The School in 60 Seconds
Utah State football was established in 1892, which makes it one of the oldest programs in the western United States. We play in the Pac-12 now. Home since 1968 has been Merlin Olsen Field at Maverik Stadium in Logan, listed at 25,513 seats. The field is named for Merlin Olsen, a Pro Football Hall of Famer who played here. The Aggies have won 13 conference championships across four different leagues, most recently in 2021, the year we went 11-3. Since then: 6-7, 6-7, 4-8 and 6-7. Steady folks. We'll get the herd back to the top.

The Coach and the Scheme
Bronco Mendenhall is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 6, 2024. Now, I'll be straight with you, neighbors, because that's the dairy way. The offense has had a hard time: 310 yards a game (129th in FBS) and 14.5 points (136th). We've allowed 19 sacks and turned it over 12 times, a minus-6 margin. The defense is the steady cow in the barn: 23.5 points allowed (66th) and 140.8 rushing yards allowed (68th). It's kept us close. Four of our six games were decided by 12 points or fewer, including a 16-14 loss at Washington and a 17-16 win over Washington State.

Players to Know
QB Grady Brosterhous: 78 of 142 for 914 yards, 7 TD, 6 INT. Against Washington State he threw for 150 yards and a touchdown.
RB Javen Jacobs: 393 yards on 70 carries, 2 TD. He ran for 62 yards and a touchdown against Washington State.
WR Eli Wood: 36 catches, 472 yards, 5 TD. Six catches for 84 yards and a touchdown last time out. Now that's a fine young man.
S Brevin Hamblin: team-high 50 tackles and an interception. LB Jordan Pendleton: 2.5 sacks.

The Conference Picture
Utah State is 2-4 and 1-1 in the Pac-12. The season: a 29-17 loss to Idaho State, a 16-14 loss at Washington, 33-0 at Utah, a 21-10 win over Troy, a 37-18 loss at Boise State and a 17-16 win over Washington State. We had last week off. After San Marcos, Colorado State comes to Logan on Oct. 31. I won't do standings math, neighbors. I'll just say a.500 league record keeps the barn lights on.
On the road: we're 0-3 away from home this year, and three of those trips were to Washington, Utah and Boise State. Tough barns.
Season so far: the Washington game still sticks with me. Two points, on the road, against a Big Ten team. That told me plenty about this team's heart. And the 17-16 win over Washington State? I had ice cream for dinner that night.

This Week: Utah State (2-4) at Texas State (3-3)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (5:30 p.m. Mountain) · San Marcos, Texas · CBS Sports Network. The venue is UFCU Stadium; CFBD data still uses the former name, Bobcat Stadium.
Last time out: we beat Washington State 17-16 on Oct. 9. Texas State beat Colorado State 66-27 on Oct. 15.
Their offense vs. our defense: here's the challenge, neighbors. Texas State leads the entire country in total offense, 562.3 yards a game, and runs for 303.5 a game (3rd). They convert 56.1% of third downs (4th). Running back Torrance Burgess Jr. has 838 yards, and quarterback Brad Jackson ran for 181 yards and three touchdowns last game. That's a stampede. Our defense has to tackle.
Our offense vs. their defense: Texas State allows 297.3 passing yards a game, 137th in FBS. Brosterhous and Eli Wood should have a chance to make plays.
One more: Texas State scores on only 71% of its red zone trips (128th). If we bend, we must not break.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18.
What decides it: (1) Tackling the run game. (2) Our passing game against the 137th-ranked pass defense. (3) Holding onto the ball; both teams are below even in turnovers.
To Yesenia Calderwood, Texas State's insider: a river float sounds lovely. Come see Logan sometime, and the ice cream's on me.

Why I Love This Team
I love that this team keeps showing up, even when the scoreboard is rough. I love Eli Wood's hands. I love that Utah State has been playing football since 1892. And I love that after every game, win or lose, Logan goes out for ice cream. Go Aggies!

report.title: "Wave the Flag": Hank Palouse Welcomes the Broncos to the Palouse
report.byline: Our wheat-farming, tape-keeping Cougar introduces himself and previews Washington State vs. No. 21 Boise State.
report.text:
Hank Palouse · Washington State Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Wave the flag. Howdy, neighbors, I'm Hank Palouse. I drive a combine for a living out in the wheat country, and I haven't missed a game in Pullman since cassette tapes. And yes, I still have the tapes. A whole shoebox of them, labeled by year, in the cab of my pickup. I travel with the Cougars and I live with the Cougars, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little dry Palouse humor and a lot of love for Ol' Crimson, the flag that shows up at every big game in the country. When we win, I wave Ol' Crimson right here in the studio. When we lose, I say "Cougs never quit," and then I tell you a 20-minute story about harvest. You've been warned.

The School in 60 Seconds
Washington State University is in Pullman, and the first Cougar football team took the field in 1894. We play in the Pac-12. Home is Gesa Field at Martin Stadium, with Gesa naming the playing surface. Martin Stadium opened in 1972; the ground there dates back to 1892, when it was called Soldier Field. CFBD lists 32,952 seats. The last five seasons were 7-6, 7-6, 5-7, 8-5 and 7-6. Steady folks out here, like the wheat: some years are a bumper crop, some years you pray for rain, but you always plant again.

The Coach and the Scheme
Kirby Moore is in his first season; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 12, 2025. I'll be honest, neighbors, because that's how we do it out here: it's been a hard first year. The offense averages 308.3 yards (130th in FBS) and 20.1 points (120th). We've allowed 22 sacks and turned it over 12 times, and our turnover margin is minus-7, 131st. The defense allows 383.1 yards a game (102nd) and 27.1 points (101st). One bright spot: we hold opponents to 37% on third down, 66th in FBS. And here's the big bright spot. Last week we found a quarterback.

Players to Know
QB Owen Eshelman: the redshirt freshman made his first career start at Oregon State and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns, ran for 136 yards on 15 carries and a touchdown, and led three straight touchdown drives late. AP says our 30 points were the most we've scored against an FBS team this season. That's a foot of fresh topsoil on a dry field, neighbors.
QB Caden Pinnick: the season passing leader, 110 of 178 for 952 yards, 3 TD, 5 INT. Who starts this week? I haven't seen it announced.
WR Branden Ganashamoorthy: 26 catches, 343 yards, 3 TD, and 11 catches for 147 yards and a score last week.
RB Kirby Vorhees: 267 yards on 54 carries, 2 TD.
LB Keith Brown: team-high 51 tackles. DT Jirah Leaupepetele: 2.5 sacks. S Jaylen Thomas: 2 interceptions.

The Conference Picture
Washington State is 1-6 and 0-3 in the Pac-12. The schedule has been a grind: at Washington 24-10, at Kansas State 34-7, a 48-7 win over Duquesne, then Arizona 34-24, Fresno State 26-6, a one-point heartbreaker at Utah State 17-16 and at Oregon State 48-30. Four of those were on the road. Next up after Boise, we head to San Diego State on Oct. 31. I'm not doing math on the standings, neighbors. I'm doing math on how loud Pullman gets for a ranked visitor.
That one-point game in Logan still sits with me like hail on a ripe field. But Cougs never quit.
Why I still love this team: because in the fourth quarter at Corvallis, down big, a redshirt freshman in his first start led three straight touchdown drives. Nobody quit. Nobody ever does out here. That's a tape I'll be labeling and keeping, right next to the good ones from the old days.

This Week: No. 21 Boise State (5-1) at Washington State (1-6)
Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6 p.m. ET (3 p.m. Pacific) · Gesa Field at Martin Stadium, Pullman · USA Network.
Their offense vs. our defense: Boise State runs for 234.5 yards a game (9th) and holds the ball 36:41 a game, first in the country. Dylan Riley has 835 rushing yards. And Maddux Madsen has 13 touchdown passes with zero interceptions. If we're going to win, the defense has to get them off the field on third down, and Boise converts 50.6%, 16th in FBS.
Our offense vs. their defense: Boise State's pass defense allows 261.3 yards a game, 126th. Eshelman just threw for 289. Now that's a crop I'd like to harvest.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source.

Colorado State (2-4 overall) is 0-2 in league play. Washington State (1-6 overall) is 0-3 in league play. That's a sort by record, not official tiebreakers. Utah State linebacker Asher Cunningham and San Diego State returner Jaylon Hawkins took the defensive and special teams honors that week. New league, who dis? report.title: "I would posit": Declan Moriarty-Chen Takes the Open Week
report.byline: Our insider (archetype: preppy history dork / CFP-résumé analyst) introduces the Notre Dame Fighting Irish during an open date on the schedule.
report.text:
Declan Moriarty-Chen · Notre Dame Insider · College Debut · Week 8

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
I would posit! I'm Declan Moriarty-Chen, and I'm your Notre Dame insider here at The Cover Window. The short version: I'm a sweater-vested grad-student type who can recite the Irish schedule back to the leather-helmet era and the CFP selection protocol by heart. I follow this team from the stands, every week, and I love it out loud. On the podcast, my segment is called The Thesis Defense. The show card describes it like this: argues one Notre Dame proposition and defends it. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me. This week the Fighting Irish have an open date, so instead of a game preview you get the full tour: the school, the coach, the players, the league and what's next.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Notre Dame Stadium in Notre Dame, IN, built in 1930 with a listed capacity of 80,795. The mascot lineup: Notre Dame Leprechaun, per Wikipedia. The fight song is "Notre Dame Victory March", per Wikipedia. The band is the Band of the Fighting Irish, per Wikipedia. The program claims national titles from 1924, 1929, 1930, 1943, 1946, 1947, 1949, 1966, 1973, 1977, 1988, per Wikipedia. The last five seasons went 11-2, 9-4, 10-3, 14-2 and 10-2, from 2021 through 2025. The most frequent opponents from 2016 through 2025 tell you who matters around here: Stanford (6-3 in 9 meetings), Navy (8-1 in 9 meetings), USC (7-2 in 9 meetings), Syracuse (5-0 in 5 meetings). That's a list of games, not an official rivalry list. The 2026 recruiting class ranked No. 5 nationally in CFBD's team rankings. And if you visit, ask somebody about 'Touchdown Jesus'; it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Marcus Freeman leads the Fighting Irish; CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 3, 2021. Through 7 games, Notre Dame scores 41.1 points a game and allows 13.4. By our math from CFBD figures, the offense runs on about 55% of its plays, gaining 183.4 rushing yards and 261.7 passing yards a game. That's a balanced menu. On third down, Notre Dame converts 44.0% of the time and opponents convert 39.1%. The defense has 15 sacks and 36 tackles for loss, and the turnover ledger reads 2 giveaways against 16 takeaways. Penalties cost 29.4 yards a game. The high-water mark so far was 58 points against Stanford on Oct. 10, 2026, and 1 of the 7 games was decided by eight points or fewer. Over the season, Notre Dame has outscored opponents by a combined 194 points. Every one of those numbers is a little homework for the open week.

Players to Know
QB CJ Carr (passing leader): 129/193, 1639 yards, 16 TD, 1 INT.
RB Jonaz Walton (rushing leader): 57 carries, 426 yards, 3 TD.
WR Jordan Faison (receiving leader): 34 catches, 451 yards, 4 TD.
On defense, LB Drayk Bowen leads with 38 tackles; DL Boubacar Traore has 3.5 sacks; S Luke Talich has 2 interceptions.
Injury news: we found no official availability report during an open week, so we're not listing any. Official reports return before the next game.

The Conference Picture
Notre Dame is 6-1 overall, 3-0 at home and 2-1 away. As an independent, Notre Dame has no league table, so every week is its own itinerary. The Fighting Irish are No. 4 in the latest AP poll in our data. Every league game from here is a chance to move up, and the open week is when the plan for that climb gets built. An open date in late October is a chance to heal up and study the stretch run.

This Week: Open Date
No game for Notre Dame this week. The last time out, on Oct. 17, 2026, the Fighting Irish lost to BYU on the road, 28-24. Next up: Saturday, Oct. 31, vs. Navy, in Gillette Stadium, Foxborough, Mass. (Navy is the designated home team), with a noon kickoff. Navy comes in at 2-4. From 2016 through 2025, Notre Dame went 8-1 against Navy in 9 meetings. After that, CFBD lists vs. Miami (Nov. 7), vs. Boston College (Nov. 14), vs. SMU (Nov. 21), at Syracuse (Nov. 28). Until then: rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub.

My Open-Week Take
Here's how I see it, friends. An open date isn't a day off; it's a deep breath. The coaches get to fix the little things, the players get their legs back, and we fans get a Saturday to call our families, clean the grill and argue happily about the depth chart. When the Fighting Irish come back, I'll be right there in the stands, same seat, same voice, and I'll bring you every sourced detail. Thanks for spending part of your open week with me. I would posit!

report.title: "Pack the Rent": Jo Ferrante Brings Fast-Break Energy to Friday Night in East Hartford
report.text:
Meet Your Insider

What's up, Husky Nation. I'm Jo Ferrante, your UConn insider at The Cover Window. I'm from the Hartford area. I played point guard in college and coached high school quarterbacks after that, so I treat football like a fast break and I know every Husky by number. I count possessions like a basketball coach, because every one matters.

Here's the deal. I'm brash and competitive, and I take "nobody watches UConn football" very personally. I also keep it honest. Every stat I give you has a source, and if I don't know something, I'll say so. Next play, next possession. I celebrate these players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I'm grateful to God for a Friday night under the lights. Pack the Rent.

The School in 60 Seconds

UConn first fielded a team in 1896 and played in Division I-AA until 1999. The Huskies began moving to Division I-A in 2000 and became a full member in 2002. They played in the Big East and then the American from 2004 through 2019. In 2019 the program went independent, since the current Big East doesn't sponsor football. CFBD lists UConn as an FBS independent this season.

Home is Pratt & Whitney Stadium in East Hartford. CFBD lists it as built in 2003 with 40,000 seats. The recent climb is real: 1-11 in 2021, 6-7 in 2022, 3-9 in 2023, then 9-4 in both 2024 and 2025. Back-to-back nine-win seasons. Say it louder for the people in the back.

The Coach and the Scheme

Jason Candle is the new head coach. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 6, 2025. He was head coach at Toledo from 2016 to 2025 and an assistant there from 2009. Before that he coached at Mount Union from 2003 to 2008, and he played wide receiver at Mount Union and Geneva.

His offense plays with pace. UConn gains 451.8 yards per game (24th in FBS) and scores 35.7 points (29th). It runs for 195.3 yards per game (33rd) and throws for 256.5 (43rd). In the 34-20 win at Temple, the Huskies scored four rushing touchdowns from four different players.

Now the honest part. The defense allows 407.5 yards per game (115th) and 290.5 passing yards per game (135th). Opponents convert 43.3% of third downs (113th). The run defense is much better, at 117.0 yards per game (39th). UConn also averages 79.0 penalty yards per game, 130th in FBS. That's like committing reach-in fouls on every possession. We have to clean it up.

Players to Know

QB Kalieb Osborne: 1,421 yards, 10 TD, 2 INT, 60.1% completions. At Temple he went 17 of 23 for 257 yards and ran for a 12-yard touchdown on the opening drive. That's a point guard pushing the ball.
RB Cyncir Bowers: 433 yards on 65 carries, six touchdowns. He ran 18 times for 84 yards at Temple and scored from 8 yards out to stretch the lead.
RB Trey Cornist: seven carries for 114 yards at Temple, including a 51-yard run and a 1-yard touchdown. Instant offense off the bench.
RB Kenji Christian: one carry at Temple, a 39-yard touchdown. Efficiency, people.
WR Shamar Porter: team-leading 235 receiving yards on 11 catches, two touchdowns. That's 21.4 yards a catch by my math.
WR Ryder Treadway: three catches for 63 yards at Temple.
LB K'Von Sherman: team-high 3.5 sacks.
LB Hayden Pegg: team-high 40 tackles.
K Jack O'Connor: field goals of 21 and 27 yards at Temple.

The Conference Picture

UConn is 3-3 and plays as an independent, so there's no conference race. The Huskies are 1-2 at home and 2-1 on the road. They beat Lafayette 56-7, then lost 38-14 to Maryland. They won 48-20 at Southern Miss and lost 24-21 at Miami (Ohio). Then came a 42-41 overtime loss to Syracuse and the 34-20 win at Temple.

Bowl eligibility is the goal, and the schedule after Friday runs at Air Force, then North Carolina, James Madison and Old Dominion at home, and a trip to Wyoming. Three of those last five are at the Rent. A home win now gets the Huskies back above.500.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

UMass (4-3) at UConn (3-3) · Friday, Oct. 23, 7:00 p.m. ET · Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field, East Hartford, Conn. · CBS Sports Network

Last time out. UConn beat Temple 34-20 in Philadelphia on Oct. 10 and then had a bye. UMass lost 25-18 in overtime at Buffalo on Oct. 17.

UConn's offense vs. UMass' defense. This is a real test. UMass allows 307.9 yards per game (30th) and 19.1 points (33rd). Its pass defense ranks 30th and its run defense 45th. UMass is +7 in turnover margin (8th) and has two interception-return touchdowns. So Osborne has to protect the ball, and the run game has to keep UMass honest. More possessions, fewer turnovers.

UMass' offense vs. UConn's defense. UMass gains 339.1 yards per game (113th) and throws for 179.0 (117th). But William Watson III completes 74% of his passes, and our pass defense ranks 135th. T.Y. Harding leads the Minutemen with 28 catches. Our run defense (39th) should handle Elijah Faulkner and Curtis Kimmons IV. Logan Inagawa played quarterback at Buffalo, so we may see two looks.

Series. CFBD has UConn 4-2 against UMass from 2016 to 2025. CollegeFootballDigest lists UConn ahead 6-4 all-time, including a 47-42 UConn win in 2024. Treat that last bit as thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report has been published. I found no confirmed UConn injury news.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can UConn's pass defense (135th) get off the field on third down?
2. Can Osborne avoid giving the ball to a +7 defense?
3. Can the Huskies cut their 79.0 penalty yards per game?

Abner, the UMass insider, will have a Revolutionary War pun ready. I'll have a box score ready.

Local Flavor

UConn is calling Friday "The Rent at Night," and it's the Huskies' Cancer Awareness game. Wear your support proudly, hug somebody who's been through the fight, and say a prayer for every family touched by it. Can't make it? The game is on the UConn Sports Network on FOX Sports 97.9 FM. Not an ad. Pack the Rent.

display.story_text:
Ten and a half points is a lot of football to give away on a Tuesday night. But Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate already has the cafecito poured, and she is not handing any of it back.

Middle Tennessee (3-3) at Florida International (3-3), Tuesday at 7:00 p.m. ET on CBSSN at Pitbull Stadium in Miami. DraftKings has Florida International Panthers −10.5 with a total of 45.5. My card: Florida International Panthers −10.5, Under 45.5, and a final of Florida International Panthers 28, Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 16.

Lourdes speaks for FIU, and she opens with the home split. "We are 3-0 at home and 0-3 on the road. Opal, sweetheart, you are not on the road tonight. You are in Abuela's living room."

Opal Stonebriar speaks for Middle Tennessee, and she brought biscuits for the press box. "Sugar, Roman Gagliano has thrown two interceptions in 188 passes. You can't slam a domino on a quarterback who never drops one."

She has a point, and it is the best case for the Blue Raiders. Gagliano is 110 of 188 for 1,204 yards and 11 touchdowns, and Middle Tennessee has only four giveaways all season. He just threw for 291 yards and three scores to beat Delaware 33-30, capping a 93-yard drive in the final minutes.

Why FIU anyway? Because the Panther defense is the best thing on this field. FIU allows 14.7 points a game, and DeeJay Holmes Jr. already has five sacks. Middle Tennessee is 0-3 away from home this year, with road losses at Marshall, Jax State and Kansas. And this series has turned lately: FIU won 35-24 in 2024 and 56-30 in 2025.

The worry is the kicking. Robert Czeremcha made five field goals against New Mexico State, then missed from 38 and 49 in a 27-24 loss at Jax State. If FIU has to settle for three, 10.5 gets heavy in a hurry.

Opal: Fourteen to seven, sugar. Grandmama's ledger never forgets.

Lourdes: And Abuela's ledger says the last two are ours. Panther pride, Miami style.

Two 2-4 teams, a Tuesday night in Newark, and a librarian who has been shushing people for a living for years. Tonight Hen Lofland gets to yell, and she plans to.

Missouri State (2-4) at Delaware (2-4), Tuesday at 7:00 p.m. ET on ESPNU at Delaware Stadium. It's a Conference USA game and Senior Day for the Blue Hens. DraftKings has Delaware Blue Hens −3 with a total of 52.5. My card: Delaware Blue Hens −3, Over 52.5, and a final of Delaware Blue Hens 29, Missouri State Bears 24.

Hen speaks for Delaware, and she has the quarterback file open. "Nick Minicucci leads us with 838 passing yards, but he has missed two straight games. So we sent in Tyler Bell, and he threw for 306 yards and then caught a touchdown pass. I've shelved him under reference."

Clementine Bilyeu speaks for Missouri State, and she paddled in from the Ozarks. "Hen, honey, Isaiah Myers has 27 catches for 554 yards and five touchdowns. He caught seven for 135 and both scores last week. When the river's low, he's the paddle."

That last week matters. The Bears beat Kennesaw State 24-21 when Yousef Obeid kicked a 20-yard field goal as time expired. It was Missouri State's first FBS win under Casey Woods. Delaware, meanwhile, led 30-26 with 9:57 left at Middle Tennessee and lost 33-30.

Why Delaware? The Blue Hens throw it for 271.0 yards a game, 29th in FBS, and Missouri State's defense gives up 430.8 yards a game, 127th. Delaware also has 18 sacks in six games, which is bad news for a Missouri State team that hasn't named its starting quarterback. My final has Delaware by five, so the home team clears the 3.

The caveat: Delaware runs for just 94.0 yards a game, 135th, so it lives and dies with the pass. And Delaware hasn't announced Minicucci's status. If the backup has an off night, a field goal decides it, and the Bears just proved they can win that way.

Why the Over? The Delaware pass defense ranks 125th, and Myers is exactly the kind of receiver who makes that number hurt. Put a good passing offense against a leaky defense on both sides and you get points. My 29-24 adds up to 53, half a point over 52.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up is all the way in, with Delaware 31-24 and the Over. Letdown Watch has Delaware 30-23 and likes the Blue Hens too. The Formula has Delaware 27-25, a two-point game, so it takes Missouri State +3 with the Under, and In The Trenches likes the Bears. Follow The Money sits this one out.

Next Man Up started it: "The Formula, you've got Delaware winning and you still took the Bears? That's not a pick, that's a coin flip."

The Formula shot back: "And you've got Delaware scoring 31 with the quarterback still a question. Read the fine print, friend."

Follow The Money just smiled. "I'm sitting this one out. Somebody has to keep score while you three argue."

Bottom of the card: the home team, a passing game that fits the matchup, and a Senior Day crowd. Clementine's float is fun, but Hen's library is open late.

Senior Night in Newark: Delaware Hunts Its First League Win as Missouri State Rides a Walk-Off High

Missouri State (2-4) at Delaware (2-4). Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7 p.m. ET, Delaware Stadium, Newark, ESPNU.

Your hosts are Hen Lofland, the Newark librarian who loves the wing-T, and Clementine Bilyeu, the Missouri State float-trip guide from the Ozarks.

Hen: Please lower your voices. Kidding. It's Senior Night, so shout all you like.

Clementine: Howdy from the Ozarks! I paddled a long way for this, Hen. Hope your library has a dock.

Players to watch

Delaware's quarterback room comes with a plot twist. Nick Minicucci leads the team with 838 passing yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions, but he missed the Middle Tennessee game, his second straight game out. Tyler Bell started in his place and threw for 306 yards and two touchdowns on 22 of 36. He also caught a 15-yard touchdown pass from Bryson Graves. Wide receiver Sean Wilson has 25 catches for 339 yards and three scores. On defense, linebacker Blake Matthews has 4.5 sacks and linebacker Colin Gallagher leads the team with 42 tackles.

Missouri State's top threat is wide receiver Isaiah Myers: 27 catches, 554 yards and five touchdowns. Skyler Locklear leads the Bears in passing with 788 yards, but Henry Belin IV threw for a career-high 300 yards in the last game. Linebacker Jared Lloyd leads the team with 71 tackles. The run game is a committee, and nobody on the roster has reached 250 rushing yards yet.

Clementine: When the river's low, you paddle harder. Isaiah Myers is our paddle.

What happened last week

Delaware led 30-26 with 9:57 left at Middle Tennessee on Oct. 13, after Bell threw a 23-yard touchdown pass to Kaderris Roberts. Then the Blue Raiders went 93 yards and won 33-30.

Missouri State had the happier ending the next night. Yousef Obeid kicked a 20-yard field goal as time expired to beat Kennesaw State 24-21. Myers caught seven passes for 135 yards and both touchdowns, tying the game twice in the second half. It was the Bears' first FBS win under Casey Woods.

Clementine: Read the current, respect the rocks, and kick it through as the clock hits zero.

Hen: Noted, and filed under "very lucky."

Injuries and availability

No official conference availability report has been published for this game. Minicucci has missed Delaware's last two games, Delaware hasn't announced his status for Tuesday, and Missouri State hasn't named a starting quarterback.

What the coaches are up to

Ryan Carty is in his fifth season at Delaware. He led the Blue Hens' move to FBS and Conference USA, and the Blue Hens are the 2025 68 Ventures Bowl champions. This year's team is a tale of two offenses: 271.0 passing yards per game, 29th in FBS, but just 94.0 rushing yards, 135th. The defense has 18 sacks in six games.

Casey Woods is in his first season at Missouri State, after serving as SMU's offensive coordinator. His defense has had a rough stretch, allowing 430.8 yards per game, 127th in FBS. But his team now has a last-second FBS win to build on.

Player storylines

Bell is the story in Newark: a backup quarterback who threw for 306 yards and also caught a touchdown pass in the same game. Hen: Versatile young man. I'd shelve him under "reference." For Missouri State, Myers against a Delaware pass defense ranked 125th is the matchup to circle.

What's happening on campus

Delaware has made Oct. 20 Senior Day, the CUSA Mental Health Game and Healthcare Appreciation night, with discounted tickets for health care professionals. Homecoming comes later, against FIU on Nov. 14. This schedule exists because of a mid-spring rework: the CUSA update after Louisiana Tech's departure moved this game from Springfield to Newark.

Clementine: So technically, Hen, this was supposed to be my party.

Hen: And now it's my Senior Night. Please sign the guest book.

Anything else fun and true

This is the first time these programs have met as FBS members. Missouri State became a full FBS member in 2026. The two schools have different gridiron roots. Delaware claims six national titles, from 1946 to 2003, and produced quarterbacks Rich Gannon and Joe Flacco. Missouri State first fielded a football team in 1909 and was known as Southwest Missouri State until 2005.

Hen: Six national titles. I keep them cross-referenced, alphabetized and dusted weekly.

Clementine: And we've got the prettiest rivers in America. Pack a snack. It's going to be a fun float.

The Cover Window

My call: Delaware Blue Hens 29, Missouri State Bears 24.

Lem speaks for Sam Houston, and he points to the pass defense. "Ma'am, we give up 137.8 passing yards a game, fourth in the nation. Only Texas Tech has topped 200 through the air against us. That's not a defense, that's a chapter in a history book."

Trey Hedden has six interceptions, and Adam Damante went 9 of 22 in a 22-3 loss at FIU. That's not an offense that pulls away from anybody. The Formula sat back: "Same score as the boss. Somebody in here knows what they're doing."

New Mexico State (2-4, 1-1 CUSA) at Sam Houston (1-5, 0-2 CUSA). Wednesday, Oct. 21, 7 p.m. CT (8 p.m. ET), Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville, Texas, ESPN2.

Your hosts are Lem Coxwell, a Walker County history teacher and Texas folklore collector, and Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, a chile farmer's daughter from Las Cruces who grades every play on a chile-pepper scale.

Lem: Evenin', folks. Pull up a stump. This chapter is called "The Hero Stands Back Up."

Esperanza: ¡Buenas noches! Lem, I brought a roaster. Your stump is about to get warm.

Players to watch

New Mexico State running back James Jones has 599 yards and three touchdowns on 92 carries. He entered the FIU game leading Conference USA at 102.0 rushing yards per game. Defensive end Gabe Peterson has a career-best 4.5 sacks, second among CUSA defenders, and safety Nick Session leads the team with 50 tackles. Wide receiver Tyler "TK" King has 286 receiving yards and three scores. Trey Hedden leads in passing with 906 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions.

Sam Houston quarterback Landyn Locke is 129 of 205 for 1,418 yards, 11 touchdowns and four interceptions. Wide receiver Chris Reed has 289 receiving yards, Alton McCaskill leads the rushers with 211 yards, and linebacker Dean Ford leads the team with 38 tackles.

Esperanza: A James Jones 40-yard run? Hatch hot.

Sam Houston lost 16-3 at home to Western Kentucky on Oct. 14. The Bearkats were held to 177 yards and 12 first downs. Locke went 13 of 30 for 112 yards. WKU is now 4-1 against Sam Houston and unbeaten against the Bearkats since they joined CUSA in 2023.

New Mexico State had a bye. Its last game was a 22-3 loss at FIU on Oct. 7, after a 34-minute lightning delay. FIU's kicker made five field goals, and NMSU's athletics department said three turnovers proved costly. Peterson had two sacks and three tackles for loss in that game. NM State says the bye gave the Aggies 13 full days off after three games in 12 days.

Tony Sanchez is an NMSU alum and former Aggie wide receiver. He coached UNLV from 2014 to 2019 and before that Bishop Gorman High School in Las Vegas. His defense has allowed fewer than 75 rushing yards three times this season, which NM State says is a first since at least 1994.

Lem: That coach of ours knows how to tell a story through the air. We just need a few more chapters on the ground.

The best matchup on paper is the Aggie pass rush against Sam Houston's protection. NM State has 15 sacks, second in CUSA, and Sam Houston has allowed 17, the second-most in the league. On the other side, Sam Houston allows just 137.8 passing yards per game, fourth in the nation, and NM State says only Texas Tech has topped 200 passing yards against the Bearkats. The Aggies have gone over 200 in four of six games.

Esperanza: Christmas-style, red and green. That's a fourth-down stop on the Bearkats.

Lem: Ma'am, that pass defense has turned better offenses than yours into folklore.

Anything else fun and true

New Mexico State leads the series 2-1. This is the fourth all-time meeting and only the Aggies' second trip to Huntsville. The common opponent is fun: NMSU beat WKU 34-13 in the Aggies' first-ever win in a CUSA opener, while WKU just beat Sam Houston 16-3.

Lem: Every Texas tale has a turn. This one's coming Wednesday.

Esperanza: Bring water, Lem, and maybe a fire extinguisher. My roaster is set to Hatch hot, and the Organ Mountains are watching.

My call: New Mexico State Aggies 24, Sam Houston Bearkats 23.

Lila Shenandoah speaks for JMU, a former cheer captain who turns every number into a chant. "Give me a 42.9! That's points per game, third in FBS. Camden Coleman has 13 touchdown passes and one interception. Give me an 8-0, y'all!"

Zeb speaks for App State, and he talks like a man who has carved a lot of porch posts. "Ma'am, App leads this series 14-6. My granddaddy carved every one of them. And we just came back from 24-14 down at halftime to beat Coastal 35-32."

That comeback was real. Jaquari Lewis ran for four touchdowns, Malachi Singleton went 12 of 14, and backup Henry Hasselbeck ran 21 times for 125 yards. App State hasn't said how it will split the quarterback snaps.

So why JMU by more than 10.5? Because the Dukes win in every way a team can win. They run for 223.6 yards a game, 14th in FBS. George Pettaway has seven touchdowns. They're 3-0 on the road. And the last meeting wasn't close: JMU won 58-10 in Harrisonburg last November. The matchup to watch is App's ground game, the thing that won it the Coastal game, against a JMU run defense allowing 3.31 yards a carry with 18 sacks.

The worry is the flags. JMU gives up 71.1 penalty yards a game, 119th in FBS.

Why the Under? It's a half-point call, and I'll own that. My 35-21 adds up to 56, just under 56.5. JMU runs the ball, and running teams burn the clock. App's two losses came with 31 and 3 points. If JMU's defense holds the Mountaineers to around three touchdowns, the number stays out of reach.

Now the room, and for once nobody wants App State. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch are all on JMU −10.5, while Follow The Money and In The Trenches sit this one out. The fight is over the total. Letdown Watch has the widest margin on the board, JMU 37-17, and that's an Under. Next Man Up has JMU 36-22, which adds to 58, and calls the Over. The Formula has 33-22 and the Under.

Letdown Watch opened: "Next Man Up, you've got App scoring 22 against a defense that allows 3.31 a carry? Who's carrying it, the mascot?"

Next Man Up fired back: "And you've got JMU at 37 and the game still staying low. Pick a lane."

Follow The Money just shrugged: "I'm sitting this one out. Somebody has to keep you two honest."

Bottom of the card: an unbeaten team that wins on the road, wins on the ground, and won the last meeting 58-10. Bring a jacket, bring a cowbell, and lay the points.

Defensive lineman Caleb Sandstrom has five sacks, and linebacker Colton Phares leads the team with 38 tackles.

Lila: Give me an N! Give me a J! Nakian Jackson, y'all!

What happened last week

App State rallied past Coastal Carolina 35-32 on Oct. 16. The Mountaineers trailed 24-14 at halftime, then came back behind four Lewis touchdown runs and ran out the clock. Singleton went 12 of 14 for 151 yards. Backup Henry Hasselbeck ran 21 times for 125 yards and threw his first college touchdown pass, a 31-yarder to Pickett.

Zeb: Steady as a mule on a ridge, that Hasselbeck.

James Madison beat Georgia State 49-22 on Oct. 17. Coleman went 13 of 19 for 185 yards and two touchdowns, and Pettaway ran for 119 yards and a score.

His first JMU team is 4-0 at home and 3-0 on the road, and its closest games were a 20-13 opening win over Liberty and a 27-24 win at Georgia Southern. One thing to fix: 71.1 penalty yards per game, 119th in FBS.

Dowell Loggains is in his second season at App State after serving as South Carolina's offensive coordinator. He was also an NFL offensive coordinator for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets, and he played quarterback at Arkansas. His offense throws for 267.7 yards per game, and his team is plus-4 in turnover margin.

Lewis's four-touchdown night is the App State story. Lila's story is the Dukes' perfect start, and a JMU win would make it 8-0 and 5-0 in the Sun Belt. App State leads the series 14-6. But last year's game went to the Dukes, 58-10 in Harrisonburg on Nov. 15, 2025. App State's two losses this year came at NC State, 41-31, and at home to Old Dominion, 10-3.

Zeb: Fourteen to six. My granddaddy carved every one of those into a porch post.

Lila: And we've chanted the 58-10 all year. Respect the history. Cheer the present.

Zeb: Steady climbing, honest footing, then a view at the top. See y'all Thursday.

Memphis turned it over six times at Tulane and lost. ECU blew a 14-0 lead at UAB and lost in overtime. Thursday night, somebody gets to stop talking about last week.

East Carolina (3-3) at Memphis (5-2), Thursday at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium. It's an American game, and SportsCenter on Campus is setting up on Tiger Lane. DraftKings has Memphis Tigers −10 with a total of 54.5. My card: Memphis Tigers −10, Under 54.5, and a final of Memphis Tigers 33, East Carolina Pirates 21.

Otis Delaney-Crum speaks for Memphis, a blues guitarist who sings bass in his gospel choir. "That Tulane game hurt like a broken string in the middle of a solo. You tune up and play the next song. And the next song is at home, where we're 3-0."

Bart Quidley speaks for ECU, in a purple tricorn hat. "Ahoy! The Pirates lead this series 18-8, Otis. I'm grading costumes on national TV, and your tiger had better be brushed."

The case for Memphis starts with the offense. The Tigers gain 512.6 yards a game, sixth in FBS. Marcus Stokes has 18 touchdown passes, Jaylin Carter has 780 rushing yards and eight scores, and even at Tulane, Stokes threw for 306 yards while Carter ran for 135. Six turnovers sank that boat. Clean that up at home and Memphis is a different team.

ECU's problem is finishing. The Pirates convert 31.3% of third downs, 125th in FBS, and they rank 125th in red-zone scoring. Memphis ranks sixth in red-zone defense. That is the matchup that decides whether this is a ten-point game or a twelve-point game, and my final says twelve.

The caveat: ECU can run. TJ Engleman Jr. carried 26 times for 104 yards at UAB, and the Pirates' pass defense allows 187.5 yards a game, 34th in FBS. If Engleman keeps the Memphis offense on the bench, the Pirates can hang around.

Why the Under? ECU's offense doesn't finish drives, and Emory Williams has 655 passing yards this season. That's not a team built to trade touchdowns. My 33-21 adds up to 54, half a point under 54.5. It's close, and I'll say so.

Now the room. Next Man Up has the biggest Memphis number, 35-20, and calls the Over. Letdown Watch has Memphis 32-20, and In The Trenches likes the Tigers. The Formula has Memphis 31-22, a nine-point game, so it goes with ECU +10. Follow The Money skips the side and calls the Over.

The Formula fired first: "Ten points? Memphis just lost 31-17 at Tulane. I'll take the Pirates and the points."

Next Man Up answered: "They lost because of six turnovers. Bart's hat isn't going to force six more."

Then Letdown Watch looked at Follow The Money: "No side, just the Over? You came to a football game to watch the scoreboard?"

Follow The Money: "Somebody has to. Family meeting after the game."

Bottom of the card: a home team that hasn't lost at home, an offense that can roll, and a visitor that struggles to finish drives. Otis plays the next song. I'll lay the ten.

Harrison Wexley-Moore IV speaks for Duke, a pre-everything overachiever with a degree for every occasion. "Nate Sheppard is a double major, Prescott. He has 820 rushing yards and eight scores, and he leads us in receiving. Summa cum laude."

Sheppard is the matchup of the night. Virginia's run defense ranks 88th at 152.7 yards a game, and he caught 11 passes against North Carolina last week on top of 77 rushing yards.

So why Virginia? Home field, mostly, and the turnover margin. The Cavaliers are plus-5, and Duke gives up 73.8 penalty yards a game, 123rd in FBS. In a game this close, free yards and extra possessions decide it. Virginia also went 8-2 against Duke from 2016 to 2025. My final has the Cavaliers by two, which clears the 1.5 by a whisker.

The caveat is real. Duke has lost two straight by four points or fewer, 24-20 to North Carolina and 28-25 at Georgia Tech. This is a team that keeps games close. And Duke's defense holds opponents to 29.2% on third down, ninth in FBS, while Virginia converts just 33.0%, 120th.

Why the Over? My 25-23 adds up to 48, a point and a half over 46.5. Sheppard against that run defense should move the chains. Da'Shawn Martin has five touchdown catches on just 15 receptions. Virginia's red-zone scoring, 124th in FBS, is the thing that could keep this Under, so watch the field goals.

Now the room, and the boss is outnumbered. Only Next Man Up is on Virginia with me, at 25-21, and it calls the Under. The Formula has Virginia 25-24, a one-point game, so it takes Duke +1.5. Letdown Watch has Virginia 26-25 and likes the Over. Follow The Money likes Duke, and In The Trenches sits this one out.

Letdown Watch opened: "Next Man Up, you're the only one in here with a four-point game. Did Duke forget how to lose close?"

Next Man Up answered: "Duke lost by four last week. I'm just reading the box score."

The Formula added: "Twenty-five to 24. That's a coin with a helmet on."

Follow The Money had the last word: "Duke and the Under. When you're right, you don't need a crowd."

Bottom of the card: the home team that hasn't lost at home, a road team that loses close, and a number small enough that two points does the job. Wear blue, Prescott says. I'll lay the 1.5.
