NC State is flying across the country for a 10:30 p.m. ET kickoff, and Ruff Pegram has measured every mile. Iggy Yamamoto-Ross has already pitched an app to make the trip shorter.

NC State (3-3) at Stanford (3-4), Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET on ESPN at Stanford Stadium. It's an ACC game, Heroes Appreciation night on The Farm, and the Wolfpack's first trip ever to Stanford. DraftKings has NC State Wolfpack −7 with a total of 55.5. My card: NC State Wolfpack −7, Over 55.5, and a final of NC State Wolfpack 33, Stanford Cardinal 24.

Ruff speaks for NC State, a Wake County engineer who grills in the same Carter-Finley lot every home game. "Wolfpack, howl! That's my one howl, engineer-approved. CJ Bailey completed his first 16 passes against Wake Forest, and we had two weeks to recalibrate."

Iggy speaks for Stanford, the founder of three failed apps. "Love the energy, Ruff. Micah Ford ran for 179 yards and four touchdowns against Elon. That tied the school record. Ship it twice."

Ford is the real deal, with 529 yards and eight touchdowns. But the NC State case is about the other side of the ball. Stanford's defense allows 452.0 yards a game, 134th in FBS, and opponents score on 96.4% of red-zone trips, 136th. NC State converts 51.1% of its third downs, 15th. Bailey has 1,507 yards and nine touchdowns, and Keenan Jackson has 27 catches for 400 yards and five scores.

The worry is how the Pack finished at Wake. NC State led 14-10 at halftime, then gave up the last 31 points and ran for only 15 yards in a 38-14 loss. Dave Doeren said afterward the team needed some injured players back, and the bye gave them time.

Why NC State by more than seven? The red zone. Stanford's offense needs Ford to answer every touchdown. All three Stanford wins have come at home, so the Cardinal won't fold, but my final has the Pack by nine.

Why the Over? The NC State defense allows 27.7 points a game, so Stanford will get its share, and NC State's offense against that red-zone defense is a scoreboard waiting to happen. My 33-24 adds up to 57, a point and a half over 55.5. The last meeting finished 59-28.

Now the room, and Stanford gets no love. The Formula has NC State 33-25 and the Over. Next Man Up has the biggest number, 35-25, and likes both NC State and the Over. Letdown Watch has 32-24 and calls the Over. Follow The Money and In The Trenches sit this one out.

Next Man Up opened: "Follow The Money, a defense that gives up 452.0 yards a game and you won't even pick a side? You fell asleep before kickoff."

Follow The Money answered: "It's 10:30 at night on the East Coast. I'm saving my energy for a game that needs me."

Letdown Watch added: "Thirty-two to 24 and the Over. That's called optimism."

Bottom of the card: a rested road team with a hot quarterback against a home defense that can't stop anybody in the red zone. Stay up late, Ruff. Lay the seven.

Heroes Night on The Farm: NC State Crosses the Country for a Late Friday Kick at Stanford

NC State (3-3, 1-2 ACC) at Stanford (3-4, 1-3 ACC). Friday, Oct. 23, 7:30 p.m. PT (10:30 p.m. ET), Stanford Stadium, Stanford, Calif., ESPN.

Your hosts are Rutherford "Ruff" Pegram, a Wake County engineer who grills in the same Carter-Finley lot every home game, and Ignatius "Iggy" Yamamoto-Ross, the founder of three failed apps and one great Cardinal model.

Ruff: Wolfpack, howl! That's my one howl for this segment. Engineer-approved.

Iggy: Love the energy, Ruff. Let's pivot to the run game.

Players to watch

NC State quarterback CJ Bailey has thrown for 1,507 yards, nine touchdowns and four interceptions while completing 66.7% of his passes. Wide receiver Keenan Jackson leads with 27 catches for 400 yards and five scores. Running back Jayden Scott has 358 yards and four touchdowns. Linebacker Popo Aguirre leads with 54 tackles, and Elijah Satchell leads with three sacks. The Wolfpack convert 51.1% of third downs, 15th in FBS.

Stanford quarterback Davis Warren has 1,630 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Running back Micah Ford has 529 yards and eight touchdowns. Wide receiver Caden High leads with 337 receiving yards. Jay Green leads with 43 tackles, and Gabe Kaminski leads with two sacks.

Iggy: Ford is pure product fit. Ship it twice.

What happened last week

Stanford beat FCS Elon 34-7 on Oct. 17. Ford ran 19 times for 179 yards and four touchdowns, including an 81-yard score, and his four touchdowns tied Stanford's single-game record. Warren went 27 of 39 for 279 yards. Coach Tavita Pritchard said he challenged the team at halftime after a flat first half.

NC State had a bye after a 38-14 loss to Wake Forest on Oct. 10. The Wolfpack led 14-10 at halftime, then gave up the game's last 31 points and ran for only 15 yards. Bailey completed his first 16 passes, which is the part Ruff keeps on the fridge. Afterward Aguirre said, "We got to be a little bit more disciplined."

Ruff: Fair quote. The thermometer dropped in the second half. We had two weeks to recalibrate.

Injuries and availability

The ACC's first availability reports post three days before kickoff. After the Wake loss, Dave Doeren said NC State needed to get some injured players back, and the bye gave them time. Check the official report before kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Dave Doeren is in his 14th season at NC State, after coaching Northern Illinois in 2011 and 2012. His team hasn't played a road game since Sept. 19, and this trip is the Wolfpack's first ever to Stanford.

Tavita Pritchard is in his first season as Stanford's head coach. He's a Stanford alum who played quarterback on the 2007 team that upset USC, then coached the Cardinal and later the Washington Commanders' quarterbacks from 2023 to 2025. All three Stanford wins have come at home.

Iggy: Founder returns to the company. Best origin story in the deck.

Player storylines

Ford's record-tying day makes him the player to watch against an NC State defense allowing 27.7 points per game. For the Pack, the matchup is Bailey and Jackson against a Stanford defense that allows 452.0 yards per game, 134th, and allows scores on 96.4% of opponents' red-zone trips, 136th.

Ruff: Engineer-approved trash talk: your red-zone defense has a 96.4% failure rate, Iggy.

Iggy: We call that a known bug. The patch ships Friday.

What's happening on The Farm

Stanford has made Friday its Heroes Appreciation game, saluting Bay Area police, fire, military and first responders. There's a 3 p.m. Heroes Appreciation tailgate on Ueland Field, plus a free reusable water bottle giveaway at Gates 2, 5 and 10 before kickoff, while supplies last. Stanford already held its Reunion Homecoming earlier in the season, against Elon.

Anything else fun and true

This is only the second meeting. NC State won the first 59-28 in Raleigh on Nov. 2, 2024. NC State opened its season with a 34-8 loss to Virginia, then beat Richmond 73-0. Stanford's 2026 recruiting class ranked 37th.

Ruff: Run with the Pack. And Iggy, I measured: it's 2,800 miles of runway for one howl. Worth it.

Iggy: Ship it. Go Card.

The Cover Window

My call: NC State Wolfpack 33, Stanford Cardinal 24.

Last November, Cal drove 75 yards in the final minutes to stun SMU 38-35 in Berkeley. SMU has not forgotten. SMU has, in fact, had it altered and tailored.

California (3-4) at No. 23 SMU (5-1), Saturday at 12:00 p.m. ET on CW at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas. It's an ACC game and Fan Appreciation day, so wear red. DraftKings has SMU Mustangs −18.5 with a total of 53.5. My card: California Golden Bears +18.5, Under 53.5, and a final of SMU Mustangs 35, California Golden Bears 18.

Tatum Delacroix-Price speaks for SMU, a Highland Park boutique owner who grades the other sideline's outfits. "Welcome to the Boulevard, darling. Kevin Jennings completes 72.9% of his passes. We're 4-0 at home and we've outscored visitors 138-63. Saddle up or sit down, sugar."

Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch speaks for Cal, a Berkeley philosophy Ph.D. student with a picket sign for every bad play call. Today's sign reads "REMEMBER NOVEMBER (RESPECTFULLY)."

Let's be honest about the last week. Cal lost 41-7 at home to Wake Forest, and Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele threw for 110 yards. SMU beat Virginia 23-13. These are not two teams heading in the same direction, and my final has SMU by 17.

So why Cal? Because 18.5 is a mountain, and SMU has a habit of leaving points on the field. The Mustangs give up 69.0 penalty yards a game, 114th in FBS, and red-zone touchdowns are the other thing Rhett Lashlee wants fixed. Cal also throws for 288.1 yards a game, 15th in FBS, so the Bears can move it through the air even when they're behind. And Sagapolutele is the same quarterback who led that drive last November.

The worry is the matchup. SMU's pass defense allows 164.8 yards a game, 11th, and SMU has 18 sacks while allowing only seven. Cal's run game ranks 137th at 90.3 yards a game, so the Bears are one-dimensional. If the Mustangs get to Sagapolutele early, this turns into the 38-6 game from 2024.

Why the Under? Cal can't run, which takes away the clock-eating drives that pile up points, and SMU's red-zone trouble trims touchdowns into field goals. My 35-18 adds up to 53, half a point under 53.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up has the exact same final as mine, 35-18, and three voices like the Under. The Formula has SMU 33-20 and likes Cal, and In The Trenches sits this one out. Letdown Watch goes big for SMU at 37-15. Follow The Money likes SMU too and is the lone voice for the Over.

Letdown Watch fired first: "Thirty-seven to 15. Cal just lost 41-7 at home. Who is taking the points here?"

The Formula answered: "Me. And the boss. And Next Man Up. Count the hands, friend."

Follow The Money waved from the other side: "SMU and the Over. I'm alone, but I'm well dressed."

Next Man Up added: "That's a lot of optimism, Money. Tatum would grade that outfit a C."

Bottom of the card: the better team, a huge number, and a home favorite that hands out penalty yards and settles for field goals. Quentin keeps the sign up. I'll take the points.

Revenge in Red: No. 23 SMU Hosts the Cal Team That Stunned It Last November

California (3-4, 2-2 ACC) at No. 23 SMU (5-1, 3-1 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 24, 11 a.m. CT (noon ET), Gerald J. Ford Stadium, Dallas, The CW.

Your hosts are Tatum Delacroix-Price, a Highland Park boutique owner who grades opponents' sideline outfits, and Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch, a Berkeley philosophy Ph.D. student with a picket sign for every bad play call.

Tatum: Welcome to the Boulevard, darling. Saddle up or sit down, sugar.

Quentin: Power to the play call! My sign today reads "WELCOME, GRACIOUS HOST (WE STILL INTEND TO WIN)."

Players to watch

SMU throws for 329.3 yards per game, fifth in FBS, and its pass defense allows only 164.8, 11th. Quarterback Kevin Jennings has completed 72.9% of his passes for more than 1,800 yards, with 16 touchdowns and five interceptions. Running back Kendrick Raphael has 542 yards and six touchdowns, and wide receiver Yamir Knight leads with 418 receiving yards. SMU has 18 sacks and has allowed only seven.

Cal throws on about 61% of its plays, for 288.1 yards per game, 15th in FBS. Quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele has 1,290 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. Wide receiver Chase Hendricks leads with 47 catches for 415 yards, and running back Adam Mohammed has 336 yards and three scores.

Tatum: Jennings at 72.9%. That's couture accuracy, darling.

What happened last week

SMU beat Virginia 23-13 on Oct. 17. Jennings went 23 of 36 for 246 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, and Raphael ran for 124 yards. Yannick Smith caught five passes for 87 yards.

Cal lost 41-7 at home to Wake Forest. Sagapolutele went 15 of 18 for 110 yards and a touchdown, and Hendricks caught eight passes.

Quentin: I painted a sign after that one. It reads "THIRD-AND-LONG IS A SOCIAL CONSTRUCT."

Injuries and availability

The first official ACC availability reports post three days before kickoff. No injury news has surfaced for either team, so check back closer to kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Tosh Lupoi was named Cal's 35th head coach on Dec. 4, 2025, replacing Justin Wilcox. His first Cal team won ACC games at Syracuse and against Virginia Tech, but its run game ranks 137th at 90.3 yards per game.

Rhett Lashlee is in his fifth season at SMU. His Mustangs are 4-0 at home and have outscored visitors 138-63 at Ford Stadium. Their only loss came at Louisville, 41-31, and they also won 27-24 at Florida State. The things to fix are 69.0 penalty yards per game, 114th in FBS, and red-zone touchdowns.

Player storylines

Sagapolutele is the central figure in this matchup's recent history. Last Nov. 29 in Berkeley, with Cal trailing then-No. 21 SMU 35-31 and just over two minutes left, he led a seven-play, 75-yard drive that ended in a go-ahead touchdown run. Cal won 38-35 when SMU's final drive ended with a missed field goal try. This week he faces a pass defense ranked 11th.

Tatum: Darling, we remember November. We've had it altered.

What's happening on campus

SMU has made Saturday Fan Appreciation and asks fans to Wear Red. Cal says this is only its second trip to Dallas to face SMU since both programs joined the ACC in 2024.

Quentin: A whole stadium in red. I'll bring a blue and gold sign for contrast. It reads "REMEMBER NOVEMBER (RESPECTFULLY)."

Tatum: I'll grade it, sugar. Gently.

Anything else fun and true

The last two meetings split: SMU won 38-6 in 2024, and Cal won 38-35 in 2025. SMU's Doak Walker won the 1948 Heisman Trophy, and Tatum would like you to know he looked fabulous doing it. Cal fans still celebrate "The Play," the five-lateral kickoff return that beat Stanford 25-20 in the 1982 Big Game.

Quentin: Five laterals. That's the people's offense.

Tatum: And this is the people's boulevard, darling. Five laterals won't get you through our gift shop. Saddle up.

The Cover Window

My call: SMU Mustangs 35, California Golden Bears 18.

Auburn just beat No. 1 Georgia on a field goal at the horn. Lacey Bellamy has reenacted that kick at every tailgate since, and she plays the kicker. Every time.

No. 18 LSU (5-2) at Auburn (4-2), Saturday at 12:00 p.m. ET on ABC at Jordan-Hare Stadium. It's an SEC game, Tiger against Tiger. DraftKings has LSU Tigers −7 with a total of 50.5. My card: Auburn Tigers +7, Under 50.5, and a final of LSU Tigers 28, Auburn Tigers 22.

Cece Thibodeaux speaks for LSU, a Baton Rouge socialite who scores every defense on a spice scale. "Bless your heart, Lacey. We just shut out Mississippi State 31-0. Sam Leavitt went 31 of 38 for four touchdowns. Our run defense allows 2.82 yards a carry. That's Saturday night in Death Valley, cher."

Both have a case, and LSU's is the stronger one to win the game. The purple Tigers score 40.4 points a game, and Princewill Umanmielen has eight sacks. My final has LSU by six.

But that's why Auburn is the pick. LSU is 0-2 on the road this year: 32-24 at Ole Miss and 35-34 at Kentucky. Auburn is 3-1 in one-score games. And there's a question on the LSU side: Jackson Harris, the team leader with 456 receiving yards, left the Mississippi State game with an apparent ankle injury in the third quarter. Watch the SEC availability report. A home team riding the biggest win of its year, getting a full touchdown, is a nice place to be.

The caveat is the pass rush. Auburn has allowed 23 sacks, and LSU's defense has 24. If Umanmielen lives in the backfield, Brown has to make plays with his legs all day.

Why the Under? Both defenses can play. LSU's run defense is nasty, and Auburn allows 21.8 points a game. The last LSU trip to Jordan-Hare, in 2022, finished 21-17. My 28-22 adds up to 50, half a point under 50.5.

Now the room, and not one voice is laying the seven. The Formula has LSU 29-23 and the Over. Next Man Up has LSU 27-21 and likes the Under. Letdown Watch has LSU 28-22, the exact same final as mine. Follow The Money and In The Trenches sit this one out.

Next Man Up opened: "Three of us picking a side, and nobody wants LSU minus seven. Somebody tell Baton Rouge."

The Formula answered: "We don't dislike LSU. We dislike seven."

Follow The Money stirred the pot: "I'm sitting this one out. Next Man Up, 27-21? Did you bring a defense or a blanket?"

Next Man Up: "Both. It's late October."

Bottom of the card: a better road team that hasn't won on the road, a home team with a fresh upset, and a full touchdown. Bring a ladder for the oaks, Lacey. I'll take the points.

Lacey: War Eagle, y'all! Cece, welcome to the Plains, sugar. Bring your beignets.

Cece: Bless your heart, Lacey. Congratulations on Georgia. Now pass the beignets.

Players to watch

LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,784 yards and 14 touchdowns. Running back Dilin Jones has 567 yards and five touchdowns. Wide receiver Jackson Harris leads LSU with 456 receiving yards and five touchdown catches. Linebacker T.J. Dottery leads with 54 tackles, and pass rusher Princewill Umanmielen leads with eight sacks. LSU averages 40.4 points per game and allows only 2.82 yards per carry.

Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown has 1,202 passing yards and eight touchdowns, and he's a real threat as a runner. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton leads with 32 catches for 367 yards. Linebacker Elijah Melendez leads with 52 tackles, plus four sacks and an interception. The Auburn defense allows 21.8 points per game and 3.56 yards per carry.

Cece: LSU's run defense? That's "Saturday night in Death Valley" on my spice scale, cher.

What happened last week

Auburn beat No. 1 Georgia 27-24 on Oct. 17 when Alex McPherson kicked a 34-yard field goal as time expired. Georgia had tied the game late, then fumbled, and Auburn recovered to set up the kick. Brown went 15 of 26 for 150 yards and a touchdown and ran 26 times for 115 yards and another score. Melendez had nine tackles, a sack and an interception. Lacey says the Toomer's oaks never stood a chance.

LSU shut out No. 16 Mississippi State 31-0. Leavitt went 31 of 38 for 289 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions. Harris had six catches for 85 yards and two touchdowns before leaving with an apparent ankle injury in the third quarter.

Lacey: I'll be reenacting that field goal at every tailgate until Christmas. I play McPherson, naturally.

Injuries and availability

The first official SEC availability reports post three days before kickoff. Watch that report for Harris after he left the Mississippi State game in the third quarter. No Auburn injury news has surfaced, so check back closer to kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Both coaches are in their first seasons. Kiffin came to LSU from Ole Miss, and Alex Golesh came to Auburn from South Florida. Bryce Underwood has six interceptions and was benched at halftime against Penn State, and true freshman Tommy Carr went 5 of 7 in relief. Michigan has lost 11 turnovers and is minus-3 in margin. Gus: Hail to the spreadsheet. Column header: "Champions of the West."

Players to watch

Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover has thrown 18 touchdown passes and no interceptions, with 1,660 yards. Wide receiver Charlie Becker has 39 catches for 694 yards and eight touchdowns, and Nick Marsh has 585 yards and seven scores. On offense, wide receiver JJ Buchanan has 27 catches for 482 yards and four scores, and Jordan Marshall leads the rushers with 293 yards. Sophomore quarterback Bryce Underwood has 924 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions.

Mallory: Zero interceptions, Gus. Bless your yards-per-play.

Indiana lost 19-15 to Ohio State, its first loss in 23 games. On the final play, Marsh caught a fourth-and-4 pass but couldn't get his left foot down inbounds. The Hoosier defense held the Buckeyes to 313 yards, only 78 on the ground. Becker caught nine passes for 165 yards. Afterward, Curt Cignetti said, "We can accomplish anything we want, all of our goals, except going undefeated".

Michigan trailed Penn State 3-0 at halftime, then scored 21 second-half points to win 21-18. Underwood was benched at halftime after throwing two interceptions, and true freshman Tommy Carr went 5 of 7 for 47 yards and ran for a touchdown. Savion Hiter ran 11 times for 78 yards.

Gus: Second-half data set: 21 points. Statistically significant. I made a pivot table to celebrate.

Hoover landed on his right shoulder against Ohio State, missed one play and finished the game. Indiana hasn't given an official status for Saturday. Cignetti's Hoosiers won the 2025 national title, beating Miami 27-21 in the CFP championship game on Jan. 19, 2026, to finish 16-0. He brought 13 transfers with him from James Madison when he arrived.

Whittingham was named Michigan's 22nd head coach on Dec. 26, 2025, after going 177-88 in 21 seasons at Utah. He replaced Sherrone Moore. His first Michigan team is 4-1 at home, and its losses came against Iowa, 20-19, and at Minnesota, 20-14.

The quarterback question in Ann Arbor is the week's biggest storyline: Underwood or Carr. On the other side, Becker and Marsh face a Michigan pass defense ranked 14th. Michigan has lost 11 turnovers and is minus-3 in turnover margin, while Indiana has lost only three.

What's happening on campus

Saturday is Michigan's Block Cancer Game and Parents Weekend, and the game is sold out. Michigan already held homecoming on Oct. 17 against Penn State. The Michigan Stadium record crowd is 115,109, set against Notre Dame in 2013.

Mallory: A sold-out Big House. I'll wear the sash on the way in, just to practice.

Gus: In Ann Arbor, darling, we call that a participation ribbon. Kindly meant.

Michigan leads the series 62-11, but Indiana won the last meeting, 20-15 in Bloomington in 2024. The teams didn't play in 2025. Michigan has the most all-time wins in college football, and Indiana's Fernando Mendoza became the 18th Heisman winner to also win a national championship.

Mallory: Miss Congeniality sash, reserved for Gus. With love.

Gus: Hail to the Victors. Off-key, as promised.

Miami scores 48.5 points a game, the most in FBS. Miami is also giving 22.5 points to the team with the best run defense in the country. Javi "The Breeze" Castillo has his sunglasses on. Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci has his whistle.

Pittsburgh (5-2) at No. 1 Miami (6-0), Saturday at 12:00 p.m. ET on ESPN at Hard Rock Stadium. It's an ACC game, and Miami is honoring its 2001 national champions on their 25th anniversary. DraftKings has Miami Hurricanes −22.5 with a total of 50.5. My card: Pittsburgh Panthers +22.5, Over 50.5, and a final of Miami Hurricanes 37, Pittsburgh Panthers 18.

Javi speaks for Miami, a former Canes defensive back who scouts in linen. "It's all about the U, baby! Darian Mensah completes 80.8% of his passes with 18 touchdowns and one interception. Malachi Toney has 758 yards. Number one in the sun, Canes get it done!"

Yinz speaks for Pitt, a steel-town linebacker who grades every tackle from "yinz" to "yikes." "Nice sunglasses. We allow 57.3 rushing yards a game, best in FBS. Opponents get 2.02 a carry. Dat's a yinz problem, not a yikes problem."

Miami wins this game. My final says by 19, and nobody in the room disagrees on the winner. The Canes have scored 30 or more in every game and they're 3-0 on the road. They just beat Florida State 43-35, with Toney catching 11 passes for 154 yards.

So why Pitt? Because 22.5 points is a cliff, and Pitt's run defense takes away half of what a big favorite uses to pull away. Miami gains 6.09 yards a carry. If Pitt holds that ground game in check, Miami has to do it all through the air.

The honest worry is Pitt's quarterback. Mason Heintschel tore his ACL and is out for the season, and Pat Narduzzi hasn't said who starts. Corey Dailey went 11 of 25 with two interceptions in his first start. Pitt's pass defense ranks 115th, allowing 249.0 yards a game, which is exactly where Mensah and Toney live.

Why the Over? Miami gets to 37 on its own in my final, and Pitt only needs a few scores to push it past 50.5. My 37-18 adds up to 55. The forecast called for a chance of storms, so watch the weather.

Now the room, and four voices are on Pitt. The Formula has Miami 36-20, Letdown Watch has 36-17, Next Man Up has the biggest number at 40-19, and all three call the Over. Follow The Money likes Pitt too, but calls the Under. In The Trenches sits it out.

Next Man Up opened: "Forty to 19. And I still take Pitt plus 22.5. That's how big this number is."

Letdown Watch answered: "Thirty-six to 17. I'm with you. Miami's going to win by plenty and still not get there."

Rice (1-6) at Florida Atlantic (4-2), Saturday at 12:00 p.m. ET on ESPNU at Flagler Credit Union Stadium. It's an American game and Homecoming in Boca. DraftKings has Florida Atlantic Owls −10 with a total of 55.5. My card: Rice Owls +10, Over 55.5, and a final of Florida Atlantic Owls 33, Rice Owls 24.

Kaia speaks for FAU, a former Boca beach volleyball player. "Surf's up on tempo, babe. We throw for 307.3 yards a game. Caden Veltkamp has 15 touchdowns. We're 3-0 at home, and we've outscored visitors 120-50."

Odalys speaks for Rice, a bioengineering Ph.D. student and self-described stats cop. "We run on about 79% of our plays, Kaia. That's not a small sample. That's an identity. Jacurri Brown ran 11 times for 154 yards against Tulsa."

FAU is the better team, and my final has it winning by nine. But the line is ten, and the matchup favors the underdog in one big way. FAU's run defense allows 5.43 yards a carry, and the Owls from Boca just got run over 56-24 at Army. Rice is a run-first team that gains 4.87 a carry with a quarterback who has 668 rushing yards. That's a bad combination for the home defense.

Rice also tends to keep it close. The Owls from Houston lost 16-14 to UTSA and 28-21 to Western Michigan. And this series is about as tight as they come: tied 3-3, with five of the six games decided by six points or fewer.

The worry for Rice is ball security. The Owls have lost 10 turnovers and forced four. Give Veltkamp a short field and this gets away fast. Even in the Army loss, he went 33 of 48 for 318 yards and three touchdowns.

Why the Over? FAU scores 35.0 points a game, and its defense struggles against the run. Rice should move the ball on the ground, and FAU will move it through the air. My 33-24 adds up to 57, a point and a half over 55.5. The forecast called for wind and a chance of rain, which Odalys says affects passing more than running.

Now the room. Letdown Watch has the exact same 33-24 final as mine, and The Formula has 31-25 and likes Rice. In The Trenches sits this one out. Next Man Up is the lone voice for FAU, at 35-24, and likes the Over. Follow The Money skips the side and takes the Under.

Next Man Up started it: "Thirty-five to 24. FAU at home on Homecoming against a 1-6 team. What are we doing?"

The Formula answered: "Watching a run defense that just gave up 56 points to Army. Rice runs on about 79% of its plays. Do the math."

Letdown Watch looked at Follow The Money: "No side and the Under? Everybody else in here has this game going Over. Bold."

Follow The Money: "I'm counting on the wind."

Rice (1-6, 0-3 American) at Florida Atlantic (4-2, 1-1 American). Saturday, Oct. 24, noon ET, Howard Schnellenberger Field at Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton, Fla., ESPNU.

Your hosts are Kaia Brightwater, a former Boca beach volleyball player who gives surf reports for offenses, and Odalys Chen-Moreau, a Rice bioengineering Ph.D. student and self-described stats cop.

Kaia: Hey, fellow Owl! Surf's up on tempo, babe.

Odalys: Lovely to meet you, Kaia. Our sample size together is small, so let's call this a pilot study.

Players to watch

FAU throws for 307.3 yards per game. Quarterback Caden Veltkamp has 1,743 yards and 15 touchdowns. Wide receiver Kelby Valsin has 47 catches for 601 yards and six scores. Linebacker Joseph Sipp Jr. leads with 41 tackles and has a sack. The Owls are 3-0 at home and have outscored visitors 120-50 there.

Rice runs on about 79% of its plays and gains 4.87 yards per carry. Quarterback Jacurri Brown leads the team with 668 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns, plus 471 passing yards. Running back Tyvonn Byars has 372 yards. Defensive end A.J. Brown leads with 52 tackles.

Odalys: Seventy-nine percent runs. That's not a small sample. That's an identity.

What happened last week

Both teams lost. FAU fell 56-24 at Army. Veltkamp still went 33 of 48 for 318 yards and three touchdowns, and Valsin caught seven passes for 89 yards and a score. Rice lost 38-17 at home to Tulsa. Jacurri Brown ran 11 times for 154 yards and two touchdowns.

Kaia: Army was a closeout wave, and we were on the wrong end of it. Choppy water, babe. Moving on.

Injuries and availability

No official conference availability report has been published for this game. No injury news has surfaced for either team, so check back closer to kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Zach Kittley was named FAU's Hagerty Family Head Football Coach on Dec. 2, 2024. His offense averages 35.0 points per game, but his defense allows 5.43 yards per carry. That matters this week, a week after Army ran all over the Owls.

Scott Abell was named Rice's head coach on Nov. 26, 2024, after seven seasons at Davidson. Several Rice losses have been close, including 16-14 to UTSA and 28-21 to Western Michigan. The variable to fix is ball security: Rice has lost 10 turnovers and forced four.

Player storylines

Jacurri Brown against an FAU run defense allowing 5.43 yards per carry is the matchup Odalys has circled. Kaia's is Veltkamp and Valsin against a Rice pass defense allowing 188.7 yards per game, if the weather cooperates. The forecast called for 81 degrees, a 52% chance of rain and a 20 mph northeast wind.

Odalys: Wind affects passing more than running. That's not my opinion. That's physics.

Kaia: Babe, I play volleyball on the beach. I know wind.

What's happening on campus

It's Homecoming in Boca Raton. FAU will celebrate with a Celebration of Champions and Youth Sports Day, and alumni are coming home. There's a Homecoming Unity Tailgate in Lot 5, and the Homecoming Court will be crowned during the game. FAU's promotion also mentions a Varsity Owls tailgate and youth sports teams from across the tri-county area.

Anything else fun and true

The series is tied 3-3, and this is the seventh meeting. Five of the six games were decided by six or fewer points. FAU won last year's meeting in Houston. FAU's field is named for Howard Schnellenberger, who founded the program and was its first head coach. And Rice Stadium has history: President Kennedy gave his "We choose to go to the moon" speech there on Sept. 12, 1962, and it hosted Super Bowl VIII in 1974.

Odalys: N equals six meetings. Still too small to call a trend. But it's a fun dataset, and five of six within a touchdown is a very caffeinated dataset.

Kaia: Surf's up, Owls. Both kinds.

West Virginia (4-3, 1-3 Big 12) at TCU (3-3, 1-2 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 24, 11 a.m. CT (noon ET), Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth, Texas, ESPN2.

Your hosts are Ryder Galloway, a Stockyards cowboy turned finance guy who explains defenses as cattle drives, and Jolene Buckhannon, a former rifle team captain who counts possessions like rounds.

Ryder: Yeehaw, and welcome to Fort Worth, where the West begins. Anything goes wrong today, I'm blaming Dallas.

Jolene: Load up. I don't miss.

Players to watch

West Virginia quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. has 1,519 passing yards and 10 touchdowns, and he leads all of FBS in rushing touchdowns. Running back Cam Cook has 833 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, fifth in FBS in rushing yards. Linebacker Isaiah Patterson leads with 44 tackles, plus a sack and an interception. The Mountaineers run on about 72% of their plays and score 37.6 points per game.

TCU quarterback Jaden Craig has 1,694 yards and 10 touchdowns. Running back Jeremy Payne leads with 429 rushing yards, and linebacker Hudson Hooper leads with 33 tackles. The defense is the herd's lead rider: TCU allows just 12.2 points and 264.2 yards per game, and opponents average 2.88 yards per carry.

Ryder: Every rider holding his spot. Nobody gets loose on my drive.

What happened last week

West Virginia beat Cincinnati 45-42 when Jack Cassidy kicked a 35-yard field goal as time expired. Hawkins threw for a career-best 464 yards and three touchdowns. Cincinnati held Cook to 40 rushing yards, but he caught a 40-yard touchdown pass to tie the game late. On the winning drive, which started at the West Virginia 2, Prince Strachan caught passes of 41 and 39 yards.

TCU won the Revivalry at Baylor 17-6 and didn't allow a touchdown, keeping the Bears scoreless in the second half. Craig went 21 of 36 for 294 yards and two touchdowns. Jordan Dwyer caught six passes for 150 yards, and Ed Small caught seven for 91 and a touchdown. Defensive end Koron Hayward had three of TCU's four sacks, and safety Jamel Johnson intercepted a pass.

Jolene: From our own 2 all the way into field goal range. I sang a verse of "Country Roads" for that one.

Injuries and availability

The first official Big 12 availability reports post three days before kickoff. No injury news has surfaced for either team, so check back closer to kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Sonny Dykes took TCU to the national championship game in his first season, 2022. His defense has carried this team, and all three of TCU's losses were by eight points or fewer: 15-10 to North Carolina, 21-13 at UCF and 17-10 to BYU.

Rich Rodriguez was named West Virginia's 36th head coach in December 2024. His Mountaineers came into last week averaging 295.5 rushing yards per game, tops in the Big 12. His defense, though, allows 34.0 points and 310.1 passing yards per game.

Jolene: I'm counting to ten on that defense. Slowly.

Player storylines

The big matchup is the West Virginia run game against a TCU defense that allows 2.88 yards per carry. On the other side, Craig and Dwyer face a Mountaineer pass defense allowing 310.1 yards per game. TCU's run game is its weak spot, at 3.27 yards per carry, and its blockers have allowed 17 sacks.

What's happening on campus

Saturday is TCU's annual Homecoming game. TCU opened this season against North Carolina in Dublin, Ireland, and earlier held Family Weekend against Arkansas State and its Block T Hall of Fame Weekend against BYU.

Ryder: Homecoming, sunshine and a defense where every rider holds his spot. My kind of Saturday.

Jolene: Your kind of Saturday has a pepperoni-roll tally waiting, cowboy. One roll per fumble.

Anything else fun and true

West Virginia leads the series 8-6. TCU's 1938 team went 11-0, beat Carnegie Tech 15-7 in the Sugar Bowl and won a national title, and quarterback Davey O'Brien won the Heisman Trophy. TCU also went 13-0 in 2010 and won the Rose Bowl.

Ryder: Yeehaw, that's a turnover. Hopefully. Probably. Dallas permitting.

Jolene: Saturday you can blame Morgantown.

My call: TCU Horned Frogs 34, West Virginia Mountaineers 22.

Baylor (4-2) at Kansas (2-4), Saturday at 1:00 p.m. ET on TNT at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium. It's a Big 12 game and KU's 114th Homecoming. DraftKings has Baylor Bears −1.5 with a total of 54.5. My card: Kansas Jayhawks +1.5, Over 54.5, and a final of Baylor Bears 28, Kansas Jayhawks 27.

Maggie speaks for Baylor, a Waco interior designer who renovates roster weaknesses live on air. "Sugar, your run defense needs new drywall. Our defense has 22 sacks, and Gavin Freeman has 49 catches for 555 yards. He's a load-bearing wall."

Fitz speaks for Kansas, a hoops-first Lawrence native who converts every stat into basketball. "Maggie, Kansas has won its last four homecoming games. Bryson Hayes just returned a kickoff 95 yards. In my world, that's a coast-to-coast fast break."

Here's the game. Baylor's defense is the best thing on the field, but Baylor's offense just went 22 of 53 through the air in a 17-6 loss to TCU, and three long first-half drives ended in field-goal tries. Dave Aranda called it "embarrassing." Kansas runs for about 5.2 yards a carry. Baylor allows about 87 rushing yards a game. Something gives.

Why Kansas? Because my final has Baylor by one, and you're getting 1.5 with the home team on Homecoming. Isaiah Marshall threw for 151 yards and ran for 116 in the loss at Kansas State, and a facemask penalty wiped out his 45-yard touchdown run. That's a quarterback who can make plays against a good defense. And this is Lawrence, with a parade the night before.

The caveat: Kansas has lost nine turnovers and forced six, and Lance Leipold said after the K-State loss that the margin for error is very small. Baylor leads the series 19-4.

Why the Over? It's a half-point call. DJ Lagway threw four touchdowns in a 55-19 win at Arizona State two weeks before TCU, and Kansas can run. My 28-27 adds up to 55, half a point over 54.5.

Now the room, and it's as close as the game. Next Man Up has Kansas 28-27 outright and likes the Jayhawks. Letdown Watch has Kansas 27-25 and likes them too, but calls the Under. The Formula has Baylor 27-24 and likes the Under. Follow The Money and In The Trenches sit this one out.

Follow The Money waved: "I'm sitting this one out. I'm not arguing with anybody today."

Homecoming on the Hill: Kansas Hosts Baylor's Brick-Wall Defense

Baylor (4-2, 2-1 Big 12) at Kansas (2-4, 0-3 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 24, noon CT / 1 p.m. ET, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence, Kan., TNT.

Your hosts are Fitz Calloway, a hoops-first Lawrence native who converts every football stat into basketball points, and Maggie Whitlock, a Waco interior designer who renovates roster weaknesses live on air.

Fitz: Maggie, welcome to Lawrence. Fair warning: Sunday it's the Blue Blood Classic, so this whole town is one day from full hoops mode.

Maggie: Sugar, I brought my tape measure. Your run defense needs new drywall.

Players to watch

Kansas quarterback Isaiah Marshall has 1,294 passing yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. Wide receiver Nik McMillan leads with 400 receiving yards and four touchdowns. Running back Dylan Edwards has 375 rushing yards and four scores. Trey Lathan leads with 41 tackles, and Leroy Harris III leads with three sacks.

Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway has 1,116 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has 49 catches for 555 yards. Running back Dawson Pendergrass leads with 327 rushing yards. Travion Barnes leads with 36 tackles, and Daniel Cobbs has three sacks.

Maggie: Freeman is a load-bearing wall. You don't knock that out.

What happened last week

Both teams lost Oct. 17. TCU beat Baylor 17-6 in Waco and ended the Bears' four-game winning run. Lagway went 22 of 53 for 256 yards, and three straight long first-half drives ended in field-goal tries. Safety Micah Gifford forced a fumble and grabbed an interception late in the first half.

Kansas led Kansas State by 10 early but lost 35-24 in Manhattan. It was K-State's 18th straight win in the series. Marshall threw for 151 yards and ran for 116, but a facemask penalty wiped out his 45-yard touchdown run. Bryson Hayes returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown.

Fitz: Ninety-five yards. In my world that's a coast-to-coast fast break.

Injuries and availability

No official conference availability report has been published for this game. No injury news has surfaced for either team, so check back closer to kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Dave Aranda called the TCU loss "frustrating," "disappointing" and "embarrassing". His defense hasn't allowed more than 19 points in any game. That's the program's longest such run to start a season since 1966, and the Bears have 22 sacks.

Lance Leipold said after the K-State loss, "our margin for error is very small, and you have to play clean". Kansas has lost nine turnovers and forced six. Leipold won six Division III national titles at Wisconsin-Whitewater.

Player storylines

Kansas runs for about 5.2 yards per carry, and Baylor allows about 87 rushing yards per game. That's the matchup. Edwards also scored against his former team, Kansas State, last week. Two weeks before TCU, Lagway threw four touchdowns in a 55-19 win at Arizona State.

Maggie: Same house, better lighting. Let's get Lagway back to that Arizona State floor plan.

What's happening on campus

It's KU's 114th Homecoming. The Homecoming Parade returns Friday at 6 p.m. on Jayhawk Boulevard, the first in seven years. Lawrence is also hosting the Big 12 Fall Tour, Oct. 22-24. Saturday brings a Big 12 tailgate on the Hill three hours before kickoff, with the Jack Wharff Band, and students in the south end get rally towels. The game is also Breast Cancer Awareness and Youth Sports Day. Homecoming weekend wraps up Sunday when KU men's basketball hosts Duke in the Blue Blood Classic exhibition.

Anything else fun and true

Kansas has won its last four homecoming games. It's also 1-0 against Baylor on homecoming, a 28-21 win in 2003. Baylor leads the all-time series 19-4, which Maggie calls "a very well-kept home."

Fitz: Homecoming magic, Maggie. That's a buzzer-beater kind of tradition.

Maggie: Cute. I'll bring paint swatches anyway. Crimson and blue is a bold palette, sugar. Green and gold is timeless.

The Cover Window

My call: Baylor Bears 28, Kansas Jayhawks 27.

Cordelia Van Doren wears a cardigan and ambushes people with Cradle of Coaches trivia. Brynn Haverkamp races snowmobiles and says "Ope." This is the most MAC sentence ever written, and it's Senior Day in Mount Pleasant.

Miami (OH) (4-3) at Central Michigan (3-4), Saturday at 1:00 p.m. ET on ESPN+ at Kelly/Shorts Stadium. It's a MAC game. DraftKings has Miami (OH) RedHawks −2.5 with a total of 42.5. My card: Central Michigan Chippewas +2.5, Over 42.5, and a final of Miami (OH) RedHawks 24, Central Michigan Chippewas 23.

Cordelia speaks for Miami. "Trivia ambush, darling. Miami has won five in a row in this series, most recently 46-7. Rodney Nelson ran for 142 yards and two touchdowns against Akron. And we hold opponents to 3.6 yards a carry. I keep a chart."

Brynn speaks for Central Michigan, a marketing grad from up north who tracks sacks like hunting-season tags. "Ope! Charts melt in the snow, Cordelia. Angel Flores has 618 rushing yards. He ran 31 times against Western Michigan. He's the whole snowmobile some weeks."

Miami should win, and my final says by one. But you're getting 2.5, and this is a coin flip with a cardigan on. Four of Miami's seven games this year were tight, including a 20-19 win at Massachusetts. And Central Michigan has a plan that makes sense: Matt Drinkall coached Army's blockers, his 2024 group won the Joe Moore Award, and the Chippewas run on about 66% of their plays.

That matchup is the game. Flores against a Miami run defense allowing 3.6 a carry. If the RedHawks stop him, Central Michigan has trouble. But Miami has allowed 16 sacks, and Central Michigan has 12, so Brynn's tags are in play when David McComb drops back.

The caveat for the Chippewas is the history. Their last win in this series came in 2014. And Central Michigan allows 4.82 yards a carry, which is an opening for Nelson.

Why the Over? Both teams have a back who can break one. Nelson had 142 on 13 carries last week. Flores keeps the chains moving. My 24-23 adds up to 47, four and a half over 42.5. That's a low number for two teams that can both run.

Now the room, and the boss is in the majority for once. The Formula has the exact same 24-23 and likes the Over. Next Man Up and Letdown Watch both have Central Michigan winning outright, 24-22, and both like the Chippewas and the Over. In The Trenches likes Central Michigan too. Follow The Money is the lone RedHawk, at 23-20.

Next Man Up opened: "Twenty-four to 22, Chippewas. Senior Day, the run game, and Brynn's sack tags. Ope."

Follow The Money answered: "Miami has won this five times running. Twenty-three to 20. History has a vote."

Letdown Watch fired back: "History lost its last vote in 2014. Same 24-22 as Next Man Up. We're a voting bloc."

The Formula sat back: "And I'm the tiebreaker with the boss. Twenty-four to 23. Pass the trivia."

Bottom of the card: a coin-flip game, a home underdog on Senior Day with a run game built by a blocking coach, and two and a half points. Pin a blue ribbon on Brynn. I'll take the points.

Miami (OH) (4-3, 2-1 MAC) at Central Michigan (3-4, 1-2 MAC). Saturday, Oct. 24, 1 p.m. ET, Mount Pleasant, Mich., ESPN+.

Your hosts are Cordelia Van Doren, a cardigan-wearing Oxford brick-campus devotee who ambushes everyone with Cradle of Coaches trivia, and Brynn Haverkamp, a snowmobile-racing marketing grad from up north who tracks sacks like hunting-season tags.

Cordelia: Trivia ambush, darling. Name a coach from Miami's Cradle of Coaches. You have until kickoff.

Brynn: Ope! Bo Schembechler? Am I right? Don't tell me. I'll be in the tailgate lot.

Cordelia: Blue ribbon, darling. Pinned to your snowsuit.

Players to watch

Miami (OH) quarterback David McComb has 1,120 passing yards and seven touchdowns. Running back Rodney Nelson has 348 yards. Linebacker Malcolm McCain leads the defense with 57 tackles. Miami holds opponents to 3.6 yards per carry.

Central Michigan quarterback Angel Flores has 618 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns, plus 475 passing yards. Running back Jayden Clerveaux has 239 yards. Linebacker Xavier White has 52 tackles. The Chippewas run on about 66% of their plays.

Brynn: Flores is the whole snowmobile some weeks. Engine, skis, the works.

What happened last week

Miami (OH) beat Akron 34-14, its second straight win. Nelson ran 13 times for 142 yards and two touchdowns, and McCain had 10 tackles.

Central Michigan lost 21-14 to Western Michigan in the Battle for the Victory Cannon. Flores ran 31 times for 117 yards and threw for 162 and a touchdown. White made 11 tackles.

Cordelia: Two blue ribbons for Mr. Nelson. One for the yards, one for style.

Injuries and availability

No official conference availability report has been published for this game. No injury news has surfaced for either team, so check back closer to kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

Chuck Martin was hired at Miami on Dec. 3, 2013, so he's one of the longest-serving coaches in the conference. Four of his team's seven games this season were tight, including a 20-19 win at Massachusetts.

Matt Drinkall was named Central Michigan's 30th head coach on Dec. 9, 2024. He spent six seasons on Army's staff, coaching the offensive front and serving as co-offensive coordinator. His 2024 Army group won the Joe Moore Award, given to the nation's best blocking group. The run-first plan in Mount Pleasant makes sense.

Player storylines

Flores against Miami's run defense is the main event. The Chippewas need yards on the ground, and the RedHawks allow only 3.6 per carry. Brynn's sack tags are in play too: Miami has allowed 16 sacks, and Central Michigan has 12. On the other side, Central Michigan allows 4.82 yards per carry, which is an opening for Nelson.

Brynn: Ope, opportunity. Sixteen sacks allowed? I've got tags.

What's happening on campus

It's Senior Day in Mount Pleasant, with the Chippewas honoring their graduating class. Fans can grab "Beat" buttons for the opponent at Fan Central near the northwest entrances. The Kids' Zone opens three hours before kickoff with bounce houses, yard games and face painting. The field is Kramer/Deromedi Field.

Anything else fun and true

Miami leads the series 17-13-1 and has won five straight, most recently 46-7 in 2024. Central Michigan's last win in the series came in 2014. The Chippewas' stadium has been home since 1972, and it's the MAC's largest on-campus stadium. Miami's Cradle of Coaches includes Paul Brown, Weeb Ewbank, Ara Parseghian and Bo Schembechler.

Cordelia: Five straight, darling. I keep a chart.

Brynn: Charts melt in the snow, Cordelia. Ope.

Oregon is the better team, and my final has it by 10. But the Ducks' quarterback situation is unsettled. Dante Moore hasn't played since his fourth game, Dan Lanning said Raiola and Brock Thomas will keep competing, and Thomas went 9 of 20 for 54 yards before Raiola came in against Nebraska.

Whoever starts for Oregon faces a defense with nine interceptions, including Matthew Bailey's 88-yard return for a score.

The caveat is the Oregon defense. Matayo Uiagalelei has five sacks, and the Ducks don't let anybody run. If Illinois can't run, it gets one-dimensional, and Oregon won the last meeting 38-9.

Follow The Money: "I'm with the Illini. The total I'll leave to you four."

Bottom of the card: the better team on the road with a quarterback question, against a rested home team with a receiver who finds the end zone. Ten out of ten for stamina, Margery. I'll take the 10.5.

Margery: Nine receiving touchdowns. Class, please take a moment to admire that number.

display.story_text:
Floyd of Rosedale is a bronze pig, he's been on the line since 1935, and Orrin Kalvelage has worn the same sweater every week hoping to bring him home again. Torvald Engebretsen owns enough coats to lend one out.

No. 15 Iowa (5-1) at Minnesota (4-2), Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on FS1 at Huntington Bank Stadium. It's a Big Ten game and Homecoming week in Minneapolis. DraftKings has Iowa Hawkeyes −7 with a total of 41.5. My card: Iowa Hawkeyes −7, Over 41.5, and a final of Iowa Hawkeyes 28, Minnesota Golden Gophers 18.

Orrin speaks for Iowa, from farm country. "Same sweater, same defense. We allow 14.5 points a game, eighth in FBS, and 84.7 rushing yards, seventh. Kamari Moulton ran for a career-high 208 at Washington. And Iowa went 9-1 against Minnesota from 2016 to 2025."

Torvald speaks for Minnesota, a ski-hill Gopher. "Orrin, I respect a man with commitment. Our pass defense ranks ninth, allowing 159.7 yards a game. And Minnesota leads the all-time series 63-54-2. Floyd's from up here originally. Well, he's a bronze pig. But still."

Why Iowa by more than seven? Because Minnesota can't run. The Gophers gain 104.8 rushing yards a game, 129th in FBS, and managed 25 at Purdue in a 41-13 loss. Against an Iowa run defense this good, that puts everything on Drake Lindsey. Iowa held Washington to minus-3 rushing yards with six sacks. And P.J. Fleck is 1-8 in his career against Iowa, which Orrin mentions roughly once per sweater. My final has Iowa by 10.

The caveat is the Iowa quarterback. Hank Brown didn't start at Washington, and Iowa hasn't announced its starter. Jeremy Hecklinski went 14 of 19 for 202 yards and three touchdowns in that game, so the backup has been good, but it's a question. And Minnesota has real wins this year: 27-24 at Washington and 20-14 over Michigan.

Why the Over? It's a low number. Iowa scored 41 at Washington and 41 against Minnesota last year. Minnesota's red-zone defense ranks 102nd, so Iowa can finish drives. My 28-18 adds up to 46, four and a half over 41.5.

Now the room, and four voices are on Iowa. Letdown Watch has the biggest number, 31-16, and likes the Hawkeyes and the Over. The Formula has 29-19, Next Man Up has 27-19, and both like the Over. Follow The Money likes the Hawkeyes but calls the Under. In The Trenches sits this one out.

Letdown Watch opened: "Thirty-one to 16. Minnesota ran for 25 yards in its last game. Twenty-five. I could run for 25 in this sweater."

Follow The Money answered: "Iowa and the Under. It's Iowa. Eventually somebody punts."

The Formula shot back: "Somebody punted for 41 points at Washington? Twenty-nine to 19, friend."

Next Man Up added: "Two weeks off for both. Minnesota spent its two weeks looking for a run game."

Bottom of the card: a top-10 run defense against an offense that can't run, a coach who keeps losing this rivalry, and a low total. Same sweater, Orrin. I'll lay the seven.

Iowa Hawkeyes 28, Minnesota Golden Gophers 18. Iowa Hawkeyes cover the 7. Over 41.5.

Homecoming for Floyd: No. 15 Iowa's Run-Stuffing Defense Visits Minnesota With the Bronze Pig Up for Grabs

No. 15 Iowa (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten) at Minnesota (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 24, 2:30 p.m. CT / 3:30 p.m. ET, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, FS1.

Your hosts are Orrin Kalvelage, an Iowa farm-country Hawkeye who wears the same sweater every week, and Torvald Engebretsen, a Minnesota ski-hill Gopher who owns enough coats to lend one out.

Orrin: Afternoon, Torvald. Same sweater. Same defense. Same pig, hopefully.

Torvald: Orrin, I respect a man with commitment. Floyd looks good in maroon, though.

Players to watch

Iowa running back Kamari Moulton has 519 yards and four touchdowns. Wide receiver Tony Diaz leads with 28 catches for 329 yards. Cam Buffington leads with 52 tackles, and Joseph Anderson has three sacks. Iowa allows 14.5 points per game, eighth in FBS, and 84.7 rushing yards, seventh.

Minnesota quarterback Drake Lindsey has 1,335 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. Wide receiver Javon Tracy leads with 32 catches for 375 yards. TJ Bush Jr. has four sacks, and Maverick Baranowski has 45 tackles. The Gophers' pass defense ranks ninth, allowing 159.7 yards per game.

Orrin: A defense built in a barn. That's a compliment where I'm from.

What happened last week

Both teams had an open week. Iowa's last game was a 41-24 win at Washington on Oct. 9. Moulton ran 26 times for a career-high 208 yards, including a 56-yard touchdown, and said he played with "a chip on my shoulder". Jeremy Hecklinski went 14 of 19 for 202 yards and three touchdowns, two to tight end DJ Vonnahme. Iowa held Washington to minus-3 rushing yards with six sacks.

Minnesota lost 41-13 at Purdue on Oct. 10. P.J. Fleck said Purdue "dominated the game in pretty much every facet". Jalen Smith caught a 42-yard touchdown.

Torvald: A rough run down the hill. Two weeks to wax the skis.

Injuries and availability

The official Big Ten report for this game has not been published yet. Iowa quarterback Hank Brown (832 yards, five touchdowns) didn't start at Washington, and Iowa hasn't announced its starter for Saturday. No Minnesota injury news has surfaced.

What the coaches are up to

Kirk Ferentz is in his 28th season at Iowa, the longest current tenure in FBS. He's the Big Ten's all-time leader in wins. The Washington win was Iowa's first in the Pacific Time Zone since the 2019 Holiday Bowl.

Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017. He is 1-8 in his career against Iowa, which Orrin mentions roughly once per sweater. His team's big Big Ten wins this year came at Washington, 27-24, and against Michigan, 20-14.

Player storylines

Moulton against a Minnesota defense allowing 288.8 yards per game is a strength-on-strength matchup. Minnesota runs for 104.8 yards per game, 129th, and managed 25 rushing yards at Purdue. That puts the load on Lindsey and Tracy against an Iowa pass defense ranked 68th. Iowa wants to finish drives: Minnesota's red-zone defense ranks 102nd.

Torvald: The pass defense is the open trail. Let's ski it.

What's happening on campus

It's Homecoming week in Minneapolis, Oct. 19-24. Comedians Sal Vulcano and Wally Baram perform at Northrop on Oct. 23. Homecoming also includes a Jr. Royalty program for young Gophers 12 and under.

Anything else fun and true

The winner takes home Floyd of Rosedale, a bronze pig trophy introduced in 1935. Minnesota leads the all-time series 63-54-2. Iowa went 9-1 against Minnesota from 2016 to 2025, and Iowa won 41-3 last year in Iowa City.

Orrin: Nine of ten, Torvald. Floyd likes it in Iowa City.

Torvald: Sixty-three wins all-time, Orrin. Floyd's from up here originally. Well, he's a bronze pig. But still.

The Cover Window

My call: Iowa Hawkeyes 28, Minnesota Golden Gophers 18.

BYU just beat Notre Dame 28-24, its first win over the Irish since 2004. Now the No. 2 Cougars are the highest-ranked visitor in Bounce House history. Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi has a dad joke ready. Knox Brevard-Stiles has a ride check.

No. 2 BYU (6-0) at UCF (3-3), Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox at the Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando. It's a Big 12 game and UCF's Homecoming week. DraftKings has BYU Cougars −6.5 with a total of 44.5. My card: BYU Cougars −6.5, Over 44.5, and a final of BYU Cougars 28, UCF Knights 21.

Bryce speaks for BYU, a superfan whose dad jokes are so clean they sparkle. "Why did the Cougar bring a ladder to Orlando? He heard the house bounces. Bear Bachmeier ran for two touchdowns, caught another and threw the go-ahead score against Notre Dame with 1:47 left. I'll see myself out."

Knox speaks for UCF, a roller-coaster devotee. "Ride check: maximum bounce requested. We're 3-0 at home, and we had a bye to get ready. Keyone Jenkins threw four touchdowns in his last game."

The Notre Dame finish comes with an asterisk. The Big 12 said afterward the final play was cleared incorrectly with time on the clock. The score stands, and BYU is still 6-0 for the third straight season under Kalani Sitake.

Why BYU by more than 6.5? The defense. BYU allows 15.2 points a game and about 86.2 rushing yards. UCF's best runner, Duke Watson, has 483 yards, and if he can't get going, the Knights turn to Jenkins, who has 806 passing yards. UCF is 0-5 at home against top-10 teams. My final has BYU by seven.

The caveat: the Bounce House is loud on Homecoming, and UCF is rested. BYU just played an emotional game. Legend Glasker, Bachmeier's top target with 444 yards, faces a UCF pass defense allowing about 236.8 yards a game, so BYU's passing game should have room.

Why the Over? Bachmeier makes plays with his arm and his legs, and UCF's pass defense gives up yards. Jenkins threw four touchdowns at Oklahoma State in a 42-28 loss. My 28-21 adds up to 49, four and a half over 44.5.

Now the room. Letdown Watch has my exact final, 28-21, and likes the Over. The Formula has BYU 30-21 and likes the Over too. In The Trenches sits this one out. Next Man Up has BYU 26-22 and takes UCF +6.5. Follow The Money picks UCF and the Under.

Next Man Up opened: "Twenty-six to 22. BYU just beat Notre Dame. Nobody plays the next week like that."

Letdown Watch answered: "Funny, coming from somebody who isn't named Letdown Watch. I'm the expert on letdowns. BYU by seven."

The Formula turned to Follow The Money: "UCF and the Under? You're on a different ride from the rest of us."

Follow The Money: "Keep your arms inside the car. It's a bumpy day."

Bottom of the card: an unbeaten team with a defense that stops the run, against a rested home team that has never beaten a top-10 team at home. Catch the duck, Bryce. I'll lay the 6.5.

Spirit Splash Week Meets No. 2: Unbeaten BYU Is the Highest-Ranked Visitor in Bounce House History

No. 2 BYU (6-0, 3-0 Big 12) at UCF (3-3, 1-2 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, Fox.

Your hosts are Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi, a BYU superfan whose dad jokes are so clean they sparkle, and Knox Brevard-Stiles, a UCF roller-coaster devotee who runs a Ride Check before every big game.

Bryce: Why did the Cougar bring a ladder to Orlando? Because he heard the house bounces. I'll see myself out.

Knox: Ride Check: maximum bounce requested. This season's had ups and downs, Bryce, but we're still strapped in.

Players to watch

BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier has 1,257 yards, nine touchdowns and two interceptions. Wide receiver Legend Glasker has 444 receiving yards, and AP writers named him the Big 12's top first-year freshman at midseason. Running back LJ Martin has 344 yards. Tausili Akana has 3.5 sacks, and Cade Uluave has 35 tackles. BYU allows 15.2 points per game.

UCF quarterback Keyone Jenkins has 806 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. Running back Duke Watson leads with 483 rushing yards. Wide receiver Josh Derry has 28 catches for 304 yards. Isaiah Nixon has 2.5 sacks, and Tackett Curtis has 39 tackles.

Bryce: Glasker's numbers are like my jokes. They just keep landing.

What happened last week

BYU beat No. 2 Notre Dame 28-24, its first win over the Irish since 2004 and its first over a top-10 team since 2018. Bachmeier threw for 224 yards, ran for two touchdowns and caught another. He threw the go-ahead 6-yard touchdown to Walker Lyons with 1:47 left. Afterward the Big 12 said time remained on the clock when the final pass hit the ground and the play was cleared incorrectly. The score stands, and the conference will review its end-of-game process.

UCF had an open date. Its last game was a 42-28 loss at Oklahoma State, where Jenkins threw for 265 yards and four touchdowns.

Knox: Bye week means the ride got a full safety inspection.

Injuries and availability

The official Big 12 report for this game has not been published yet, and no injury news has surfaced for BYU. Check the report before kickoff for UCF's quarterback room, too.

What the coaches are up to

Kalani Sitake played fullback at BYU under LaVell Edwards and is the first Tongan head coach in college football. This is the third straight season his team has started 6-0.

Scott Frost is in his second stint at UCF; he coached the Knights in 2016 and 2017. As a player, he led Nebraska to the 1997 national championship. His Knights are 3-0 at home this season.

Player storylines

Watson against a BYU run defense allowing about 86.2 yards per game is the key matchup for UCF. Bachmeier and Glasker face a UCF pass defense allowing about 236.8 yards per game. History is the subplot. BYU is the highest-ranked opponent ever to play at UCF, and the Knights are 0-5 at home against top-10 teams.

What's happening on campus

It's UCF Homecoming Week, Oct. 18-25. Spirit Splash returns to the Reflecting Pond on Oct. 23, with thousands of students running into the water after a custom rubber duck. Concert Knight brings Soulja Boy and Waka Flocka Flame, and Jay Pharoah headlines Comedy Knight. McKenzie Milton is in the 2026 UCF Athletics Hall of Fame class. Alumni tailgates open three hours before kickoff at the FAIRWINDS Alumni Center.

Anything else fun and true

UCF's first homecoming was in 1971, and football didn't start until 1979. After BYU, UCF hosts Baylor on Oct. 30 for the annual Space Game.

Bryce: Spirit Splash? I'd catch that duck. Then I'd make a pun about it. Something about a quack defense. I'm workshopping.

Knox: Keep your arms and legs inside the ride at all times, Bryce. The Bounce House doesn't do refunds on the loops.

The Cover Window

My call: BYU Cougars 28, UCF Knights 21.

Homecoming at the Capstone: Alabama Tries to Stop a Skid Against Texas A&M's Stingy Defense

Texas A&M (4-3, 1-3 SEC) at No. 13 Alabama (5-2, 3-2 SEC). Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:30 p.m. ET, Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium, Tuscaloosa, ABC.

Your hosts are MK Strickland, a former Tide equestrian rider who reads blitz pickups like Southern Living, and Colt Wendeborn, a petroleum engineer who reports with his whole chest and explains every Aggie tradition, then explains the explanation.

Colt: HOWDY! I've brought you a tradition, explained. It's long.

MK: Howdy right back, sugar. Bryant-Denny is lovely this time of year. Roll Tide, and I mean that as a greeting. Mostly.

Players to watch

Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell has 1,746 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions. Running back Trae'shawn Brown has 313 yards and five touchdowns. Linebacker Caleb Woodson leads with 53 tackles, Yhonzae Pierre has 3.5 sacks, and Bray Hubbard has two interceptions. Alabama scores 39.3 points per game, 12th in FBS.

Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed has 1,227 yards, seven touchdowns and six interceptions. Running back K.J. Edwards has 317 yards. Wide receiver Isaiah Horton has 280 receiving yards and three touchdowns. Linebacker Ray Coney leads with 36 tackles. The Aggies allow 17.1 points per game (27th) and 164.1 passing yards (10th).

Colt: Tenth in pass defense! Let me yell that again!

What happened last week

Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10. The Tide managed 201 yards, turned it over four times and went 2 for 13 on third down. It was their first back-to-back regular-season losses since 2007. "The key was they were able to run the football," Kalen DeBoer said. Russell said afterward, "It was just a lack of a plan that I had. Just wasn't playing my game today."

Texas A&M beat The Citadel 41-0. Edwards ran 13 times for 116 yards, and Aaron Gregory caught six passes for 94 yards and two touchdowns.

MK: We straighten our pearls and move on, darling. Two in a row stings, but this barn has seen bad weather before.

Injuries and availability

The SEC's first official report for this game is due Oct. 21. Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams (415 receiving yards) missed the Tennessee game. Check the official report for his status and for both teams' lists before kickoff.

What the coaches are up to

DeBoer was hired Jan. 12, 2024, and went 9-4 and 11-4 in his first two seasons. His team opened 2026 scoring 48, 45, 50, 49 and 56 points before managing 17 against Georgia and 10 at Tennessee. After this game comes an open date, then LSU on Nov. 7.

Mike Elko was hired at Texas A&M on Nov. 27, 2023. His team is disciplined, 14th in FBS at 41.7 penalty yards per game. Opponents convert only 29.8% of third downs. The puzzle is the road: A&M scored six points in each of its two SEC road games.

Player storylines

Russell against a top-10 pass defense is the headline matchup. Reed's opening is in the red zone: Alabama allows a score on 95.7% of opponents' trips inside the 20, 134th in FBS. A&M's pass rush has only five sacks, which could give Russell time to get his plan back.

Colt: Red zone, Mary-Kathryn. That's where we'll yell loudest.

What's happening on campus

It's Homecoming in Tuscaloosa. Friday brings a pep rally, the queen announcement and a bonfire on the Quad. The alumni tent hosts Rock the Quad on Friday evening with the band Boomerang. Saturday's parade starts at 10 a.m. on Greensboro Avenue and travels down University Boulevard to the Quad. The Elephant Stomp, with the Million Dollar Band and Big Al, starts about an hour before kickoff outside Gorgas Library.

Anything else fun and true

Alabama leads the series 13-3. The last meeting was a 26-20 Alabama win in College Station on Oct. 7, 2023. Texas A&M's last win in Tuscaloosa was 29-24 in 2012, and Alabama has won five straight home meetings since. Alabama's elephant mascot, Big Al, debuted in 1980.

MK: Five straight at home, sugar. It's practically a family heirloom.

Colt: Heirlooms get passed down, ma'am! Gig 'em!

The Cover Window

My call: Alabama Crimson Tide 33, Texas A&M Aggies 20.

Kansas State ran for 359 yards last week. Arizona State gave up six sacks. Hattie Brandvold names every drive after a crop. Skylar Vanterpool's motto is "Hydrate and Dominate." It's going to be a long, warm afternoon in Tempe.

Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3), Saturday at 3:45 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at Mountain America Stadium. It's a Big 12 game and ASU's Blackout, so wear black. DraftKings has Kansas State Wildcats −3.5 with a total of 56.5. My card: Kansas State Wildcats −3.5, Over 56.5, and a final of Kansas State Wildcats 32, Arizona State Sun Devils 27.

Hattie speaks for K-State, an agronomy grad. "You still can't rush a harvest, darlin'. Avery Johnson just became the school's all-time leader in combined passing and rushing yards. Joe Jackson ran for 159. That's a bumper crop."

Skylar speaks for Arizona State. "Bring sunscreen, Hattie. Mikey Keene threw for 256 yards and two touchdowns in one half at Texas Tech. And Arizona State leads this series 6-1. Hydrate and dominate."

Why K-State? Because the Wildcats run the ball, and Arizona State can't stop the run. The Sun Devils allow 4.80 yards a carry and 32.0 points a game. K-State trailed Kansas 17-7 and still won 35-24, piling up 568 yards. Kicker Luis Rodriguez made four field goals, including a 51-yarder, so even stalled drives come away with points. My final has the Wildcats by five.

Arizona State also has a quarterback decision to make. Kenny Dillingham pulled Cutter Boley for Keene at halftime of the 53-25 loss in Lubbock and hasn't named a starter. ASU's blockers have allowed 15 sacks, and K-State has 13.

The caveat is Johnson's shoulder. He went down after a 59-yard run against Kansas, pointing to his right shoulder, but he returned and said he just had the wind knocked out of him. Watch the Big 12 report. Arizona State also throws for 276.7 yards a game, so the Sun Devils can answer.

Why the Over? K-State's ground game should move at will, and Arizona State's passing game can keep pace. My 32-27 adds up to 59, two and a half over 56.5.

Now the room, and four voices call the Over. The Formula has the exact same 32-27 and stays with K-State. Next Man Up has the biggest number, 33-29, and likes the Over most. Letdown Watch has 31-26. In The Trenches likes K-State's ground game and the Wildcats. Follow The Money sits this one out.

Next Man Up opened: "Thirty-three to 29. Sixty-two points. Avery Johnson in the desert. Somebody hydrate the scoreboard operator."

Follow The Money answered: "I'm sitting this one out. But Arizona State leads the series six and one, friend."

In The Trenches shot back: "Three hundred fifty-nine rushing yards last week. Your series history doesn't tackle anybody."

The Formula added: "Same score as the boss. Plant in the spring, harvest in the fall, lay the 3.5."

Bottom of the card: a road team that runs it against a defense that can't stop the run, with a home quarterback question. Saturday's forecast, Hattie says, is sunny with a chance of Avery Johnson. I'll lay the 3.5.

Kansas State Wildcats 32, Arizona State Sun Devils 27. Kansas State Wildcats cover the 3.5. Over 56.5.

Blackout in Tempe: Collin Klein's Wildcats Bring the Ground Game to the Desert

Kansas State (4-2, 1-2 Big 12) at Arizona State (3-3). Saturday, Oct. 24, 3:45 p.m. ET (12:45 p.m. in Arizona), Mountain America Stadium, Tempe, ESPN2.

Your hosts are Hattie Brandvold, a Kansas State fan with an agronomy degree who names every drive after a crop, and Skylar Vanterpool, an Arizona State fan whose motto is "Hydrate and Dominate."

Hattie: I'll bring the shade hat and the water jug, darlin'. Hydrate all you like. You still can't rush a harvest.

Skylar: Bring sunscreen, Hattie. It's a Blackout, and the desert doesn't do sweater weather.

Players to watch

K-State quarterback Avery Johnson leads the team with 1,301 passing yards and 462 rushing yards. Against Kansas he became the school's all-time leader in combined passing and rushing yards. Running back Joe Jackson ran for a season-high 159 yards and a touchdown against the Jayhawks. Jaron Tibbs leads the receivers with 268 yards. Kicker Luis Rodriguez made four field goals last week, including a 51-yarder.

Arizona State has two quarterbacks to think about. Cutter Boley started last week, and backup Mikey Keene threw for 256 yards and two touchdowns in the second half. Receiver Reed Harris is the deep threat Skylar watches first.

Skylar: Harris catches deep balls like I catch rays. Effortlessly.

What happened last week

K-State trailed Kansas 17-7 in the first quarter, then won 35-24. The Wildcats piled up 568 yards, 359 of them on the ground. Logan Bartley made an end-zone interception. The win extended K-State's run over Kansas to 18 straight.

Arizona State lost 53-25 at Texas Tech. Kenny Dillingham replaced Boley with Keene at halftime. Texas Tech gained 7.8 yards a play, and ASU allowed a season-high six sacks.

Hattie: Three hundred fifty-nine rushing yards. That's a bumper crop.

Injuries and availability

The official Big 12 availability report for this game hasn't been published yet. Johnson went down after a 59-yard run against Kansas and pointed to his right shoulder, but he returned, and he said afterward he had just had the wind knocked out of him. Dillingham hasn't named a starting quarterback for this game.

What the coaches are up to

Collin Klein is in his first season as K-State's 36th head coach. He was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and Johnny Unitas Award winner as the Wildcats' quarterback. He's the first K-State alum to lead the program since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77.

Dillingham became ASU's 26th head coach on Nov. 27, 2022, and won the Big 12 title in 2024. This week brings his quarterback decision.

Player storylines

K-State's running game meets an ASU defense allowing 4.80 yards a carry and 32.0 points a game. ASU throws for 276.7 yards a game, but its blockers have allowed 15 sacks. K-State has 13 sacks of its own. The Big 12's top two teams meet in the championship game, so a 1-2 league start means every week matters for K-State.

What's happening on campus

This is ASU's Blackout game, so wear black. Homecoming comes later, on Nov. 21 against Oklahoma State. K-State hasn't played in Tempe since the 1989 season opener. Its last game in this stadium was a 31-14 bowl win over Michigan in 2013.

Anything else fun and true

Arizona State leads the series 6-1 and won the last meeting 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024. K-State's only win came 34-27 on Dec. 27, 2002. One famous Sun Devil day came in Pasadena, when ASU beat Michigan 22-15 in the Rose Bowl on Jan. 1, 1987.

Skylar: Six and one, Hattie. Hydrate and dominate.

Hattie: Farmers are patient, sugar. One year we'll get two. Plant in the spring, harvest in the fall, and Saturday's forecast says sunny with a chance of Avery Johnson.

The Cover Window

My call: Kansas State Wildcats 32, Arizona State Sun Devils 27.

display.story_text:
Ohio is 3-0 in the MAC and has won four in a row. Penny Trautman builds every argument brick by brick. Imogen Tremblay builds hers cell by cell, color-coded. Saturday in Athens, the spreadsheet meets the wall.

Eastern Michigan (4-4) at Ohio (5-2), Saturday at 4:00 p.m. ET on ESPNU at Peden Stadium. It's a MAC game, Senior Day and Heroes Day, and Ohio's last Saturday home game of 2026. DraftKings has Ohio Bobcats −10.5 with a total of 49.5. My card: Ohio Bobcats −10.5, Over 49.5, and a final of Ohio Bobcats 31, Eastern Michigan Eagles 19.

Penny speaks for Ohio. "We run for 207 yards a game, 24th in FBS. Nick Poulos has five touchdown passes and no interceptions. We beat Sacramento State 48-7. That's a sturdy wall, Imogen."

Imogen speaks for Eastern Michigan, with a spreadsheet tab devoted to the gray turf. "Noah Kim has 1,678 yards and 11 touchdowns, Penny. Joshua Long, a tight end, leads us with 38 catches. Highlight that cell in green. And we've already won three road games."

Why Ohio by more than 10.5? The run game against the pass game. Eastern Michigan throws for 215 yards a game and runs for 105, which ranks 128th. A one-dimensional offense on the road against a team that runs it 207 a game is how you lose the clock and the game. Kim went 16 of 36 in last week's 34-14 loss to Toledo. Ohio has also won the last four meetings, including 35-10 in Athens in 2024. My final has the Bobcats by 12.

The caveat is Ohio's third-down defense. Opponents convert 42.1%, 106th in FBS, and Eastern Michigan converts 41.9% of its own, 56th. If the Eagles keep moving the chains, they keep it inside the number. Eastern Michigan's run defense is also middle of the pack, allowing 142.3 yards a game, so this won't be a total wipeout either way.

Why the Over? Ohio's ground game should roll, and Kim will throw enough to put up points late. My 31-19 adds up to 50, half a point over 49.5. Tight, and every voice in the room agrees with it.

Now the room. Next Man Up has the biggest Ohio number, 34-18, and likes the Bobcats. Letdown Watch has my exact final, 31-19. Follow The Money has 30-20 and likes Ohio, and In The Trenches likes the Bobcats too. The Formula has the same 30-20 as Follow The Money and takes Eastern Michigan +10.5.

Next Man Up opened: "Thirty-four to 18. Senior Day, Heroes Day, last Saturday home game. Ohio rolls."

The Formula answered: "Thirty to 20. That's ten. The line is 10.5. I'll take the half point and Imogen's spreadsheet."

Then The Formula turned to Follow The Money: "You're laying 10.5 with Ohio and you won't even touch the total? Your spreadsheet has a typo."

Follow The Money: "I don't use spreadsheets. I use instincts. And snacks."

Bottom of the card: a home team that runs it, a road team that can't, and the last Saturday crowd at Peden. Bring a hard hat, Penny says. I'll lay the 10.5.

Ohio Bobcats 31, Eastern Michigan Eagles 19. Ohio Bobcats cover the 10.5. Over 49.5.
