Senior Day in Athens: Unbeaten-in-MAC Ohio Hosts Eastern Michigan's Spreadsheet Squad

Eastern Michigan (4-4, 3-1 MAC) at Ohio (5-2, 3-0 MAC). Saturday, Oct. 24, 4 p.m. ET, Peden Stadium, Athens, Ohio, ESPNU.

Your hosts are Imogen Tremblay, an Eastern Michigan fan with a color-coded spreadsheet tab devoted to the gray turf, and Penny Trautman, an Ohio fan who builds every argument brick by brick.

Imogen: Penny, I hear you build things brick by brick. I build them cell by cell. Let's compare blueprints.

Penny: Deal. Just know my blueprint has a four-game winning run penciled in.

Players to watch

Ohio quarterback Nick Poulos has completed 38 of 68 passes for 503 yards and five touchdowns with no interceptions. Receiver Riley Neer has 32 catches for 441 yards and five touchdowns. Running back Duncan Brune has 330 yards on 73 carries. Linebacker Michael Molnar leads with 52 tackles, and defensive end Ike Ackerman has 4.5 sacks.

Eastern Michigan quarterback Noah Kim has 1,678 yards, 11 touchdowns and four interceptions. Tight end Joshua Long leads the team with 38 catches for 366 yards. Running back Amareon Blue has 338 yards. Linebacker Zach Mowchan has 58 tackles, Quincy Byas has four sacks and Caleb Dobbs has two interceptions.

Imogen: A tight end leading the team in catches. Highlight that cell in green.

What happened last week

Ohio beat Sacramento State 48-7. Poulos went 11 of 14 for 165 yards and a touchdown and ran five times for 48 yards. Irving Brown ran eight times for 87 yards and a score, and Preston Bowman caught three passes for 94 yards and a touchdown.

Eastern Michigan lost 34-14 to Toledo on homecoming. Kim threw for 214 yards and two touchdowns, but he went 16 of 36. Long caught seven passes for 84 yards and a score.

Penny: Four straight wins. That's a sturdy wall.

Injuries and availability

The MAC doesn't publish an official availability report, and no injury news had surfaced for either team as of Oct. 18. Check the schools' channels on game day.

What the coaches are up to

John Hauser is in his first season as Ohio's head coach, hired Dec. 26, 2025. His Bobcats run for 207 yards a game, 24th in FBS.

Chris Creighton has led Eastern Michigan since being hired on Dec. 11, 2013. His teams went 7-6 in 2021 and 9-4 in 2022. This year's offense loves to throw it. EMU throws for 215 yards a game and runs for 105, which ranks 128th.

Player storylines

Ohio's ground game meets an EMU run defense allowing 142.3 yards a game, 71st in FBS. Third downs could flip it. Ohio's defense allows opponents to convert 42.1%, which ranks 106th. EMU converts 41.9% of its own third downs, 56th in FBS. Poulos's clean sheet is worth watching too: no interceptions all season.

What's happening on campus

It's Senior Day and Heroes Day at Peden Stadium, and Ohio's last Saturday home game of 2026. After this, the Bobcats visit Akron on Nov. 3. Eastern Michigan hosts Central Michigan on Nov. 4. MAC weeknight football season is almost here.

Anything else fun and true

Ohio leads the series 22-12-1 in 35 meetings since 1976. The Bobcats have won four straight, including 28-21 in Ypsilanti last year and 35-10 in Athens in 2024. EMU's last win in the series was 27-20 in Athens in 2016. In last year's game, Ohio quarterback Parker Navarro threw for a career-high 315 yards. EMU has already won three road games this season.

Imogen: Ten years since our last win in Athens. My model would like a word.

Penny: Your model is welcome at Peden anytime, Imogen. Bring a hard hat.

The Cover Window

My call: Ohio Bobcats 31, Eastern Michigan Eagles 19.

Kentucky's quarterback has thrown one interception all season. Vanderbilt's has thrown seven, against a defense that has taken the ball away 16 times. Rhett Abernathy-Coyle, a Kentucky fan raised on a horse farm out past Keeneland, grades teams like bloodlines. Pippa Ashcroft, a Vanderbilt economics student, writes a country song about every game.

Vanderbilt (3-4) at No. 12 Kentucky (6-1), Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on SEC Network at Kroger Field in Lexington. It's an SEC game and a Blue Out under the lights. DraftKings has Kentucky Wildcats −11.5 with a total of 51.5. My card: Vanderbilt Commodores +11.5, Over 51.5, and a final of Kentucky Wildcats 33, Vanderbilt Commodores 22.

Rhett speaks for Kentucky. "Kenny Minchey has 13 touchdown passes and just one interception. We're plus-11 in turnover margin, third in FBS, and 3-0 on the road. Five straight wins since Alabama. A thoroughbred that never breaks stride."

Pippa speaks for Vanderbilt. "Sugar, I grade hooks. Junior Sherrill has 628 receiving yards and caught eight passes for 99 yards and a score last week. Jared Curtis threw for 274. We went 10-3 last season. Every great album saves the anthem for the end."

Why Vanderbilt with 11.5? Kentucky wins, but it doesn't always win big. It won back-to-back one-point games, at South Carolina and against LSU, and won 21-13 at Oklahoma last week. Kentucky converts 29.1% of its third downs, last in FBS, and drives that stall don't build big leads. Sherrill also gets a Kentucky pass defense ranked 116th. My final has Kentucky by 11, half a point inside the number.

The caveat is the turnovers. Curtis has seven interceptions, and Jordan Castell has four picks for Kentucky. If Vanderbilt gives the ball away twice, this one gets long. Vanderbilt's run defense allowed 196 yards to Ole Miss and 170 to Arkansas, so the Wildcats can run. Vanderbilt is 0-4 in the SEC. C.J. Baxter, with eight touchdowns, didn't lead Kentucky's backs at Oklahoma, so watch for his name when the report posts.

Why the Over? Kentucky's takeaways create short fields, and Sherrill should find room against that pass defense. My 33-22 adds up to 55, three and a half over 51.5.

Now the room, and four of five back Kentucky. Next Man Up has 36-20 and likes the Wildcats and the Over. The Formula has 34-22 and likes the Over. Follow The Money likes Kentucky but calls the Under. In The Trenches likes Kentucky. Letdown Watch has 29-26 and likes Vanderbilt and the Over.

Letdown Watch opened: "Twenty-nine to 26. Both teams have a week off after this. Kentucky goes to Tennessee next. This is a Blue Out with one eye on the bye."

Next Man Up answered: "Thirty-six to 20. One interception versus seven. That's not a song, that's a ballad with a sad ending."

The Formula turned on Follow The Money: "Kentucky and the Under? Sherrill gets a pass defense ranked 116th, and you want it low?"

Follow The Money: "Every great horse saves its kick for the stretch."

Bottom of the card: a home team that wins close, a road receiver who can make plays against a soft pass defense, and 11.5 points of cushion. Sing it, Pippa. I'll take the 11.5.

Kentucky Wildcats 33, Vanderbilt Commodores 22. Vanderbilt Commodores cover the 11.5. Over 51.5.

display.story_text:
Utah has never beaten Houston. Houston leads the series 5-0. Utah also has the longest active winning run in FBS, 12 games. Something has to give, late Saturday night in Salt Lake City. Yolanda "Yo" Pacheco, a Houston fan who breaks down every game like a launch countdown, says Houston, we have liftoff. Aspen Mortensen, a Utah fan and skier, says the mountain's steep at night.

No. 14 Houston (6-1) at No. 10 Utah (6-0), Saturday at 10:15 p.m. ET on ESPN at Rice-Eccles Stadium. It's a Big 12 night game and Utah's Homecoming. DraftKings has Utah Utes −6.5 with a total of 56.5. My card: Utah Utes −6.5, Over 56.5, and a final of Utah Utes 34, Houston Cougars 25.

Aspen speaks for Utah. "Send it, no fear, Yo. We've scored a touchdown on our opening drive in every game. We've outscored opponents 75-3 in the first quarter. Six for six, our first 6-0 start since 2015."

Yo speaks for Houston. "Conner Weigman has 20 touchdown passes and two interceptions. That's a clean launch every time. He threw five touchdown passes against No. 18 Oklahoma State. Four straight wins, and Willie Fritz says he just keeps getting a little bit better every single week."

Why Utah by a touchdown? The first quarter. Utah has outscored people 75-3 in the opening quarter, and Houston has to survive that on the road, late at night, at Homecoming. Utah's defense allows 14.8 points a game and has allowed only 25 conversions on 81 third downs. Devon Dampier has 15 touchdown passes, and Wayshawn Parker has seven rushing scores. My final has Utah by nine.

The caveats are real. Weigman is the best quarterback on the field, and Houston has converted 54 of 88 third downs. Houston's run defense allows 82.6 yards a game, which could take away Parker. Utah's last win was 27-24 at Colorado, with two Dampier interceptions. "It's not always pretty, but we did enough," Morgan Scalley said. And 5-0 is 5-0.

Why the Over? Weigman's offense gained 505 yards last week, and Utah scores early in every game. My 34-25 adds up to 59, two and a half over 56.5.

Now the room, and it's split on the side, but four voices call the Over. Next Man Up has Utah 35-26 and likes the Over. Letdown Watch has 36-21 and likes the Utes. Follow The Money skips the side and likes the Over. The Formula has Utah 31-27 and takes Houston, and In The Trenches sits this one out.

The Formula opened: "Thirty-one to 27. Houston has never lost to Utah. Never. And you want to lay a touchdown?"

Letdown Watch answered: "Thirty-six to 21. Utah's been waiting at the lift for this one a long time. Homecoming at night."

Next Man Up turned on The Formula: "You've got Utah winning and you're still on Houston? Never is a long time, friend."

Follow The Money: "No side for me. But the countdown says points."

Bottom of the card: a home team that scores first every week, a road quarterback who's playing great, and a series history that's begging to be broken. Every ski run has a bottom. I'll lay the 6.5.

Utah Utes 34, Houston Cougars 25. Utah Utes cover the 6.5. Over 56.5.
